Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Saṃyuttanikāyo

The Connected Discourses

Saḷāyatanavaggo

The Chapter on the Six Sense Bases

1. Saḷāyatanasaṃyuttaṃ

1. The Connected Discourses on the Six Sense Bases

1. Aniccavaggo

1. The Chapter on Impermanence

1. Ajjhattāniccasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Internal Impermanence

1. Evaṃ [T 4.0001][V 2.0001][M 2.0236][P 4.0001] me sutaṃ. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

1. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There, the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks!” “Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Cakkhuṃ[V 2.0002], bhikkhave, aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā. Yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sotaṃ aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ…pe… ghānaṃ aniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ…pe… jivhā aniccā. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā. Yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kāyo anicco. Yadaniccaṃ…pe… mano anicco. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā. Yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya [T 4.0002] daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ [P 4.0002] passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, sotasmimpi nibbindati, ghānasmimpi nibbindati, jivhāyapi nibbindati, kāyasmimpi nibbindati[M 2.0237], manasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Monks, the eye is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ The ear is impermanent… The nose is impermanent… The tongue is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ The body is impermanent… The mind is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus, monks, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye, becomes disenchanted with the ear, becomes disenchanted with the nose, becomes disenchanted with the tongue, becomes disenchanted with the body, and becomes disenchanted with the mind. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises, ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’” The first.

2. Ajjhattadukkhasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Internal Suffering

2. “Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ. Yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sotaṃ dukkhaṃ…pe… ghānaṃ dukkhaṃ… jivhā dukkhā… kāyo dukkho… mano dukkho. Yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

2. “Monks, the eye is suffering. What is suffering is not-self; what is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ The ear is suffering… the nose is suffering… the tongue is suffering… the body is suffering… the mind is suffering. What is suffering is not-self; what is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is no more for this state of being.’” The second.

3. Ajjhattānattasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Internal Not-Self

3. “Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, anattā. Yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sotaṃ anattā…pe… ghānaṃ anattā… jivhā anattā… kāyo anattā… mano anattā. Yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

3. “Monks, the eye is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ The ear is not-self… the nose is not-self… the tongue is not-self… the body is not-self… the mind is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is no more for this state of being.’” The third.

4. Bāhirāniccasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on External Impermanence

4. “Rūpā[T 4.0003][V 2.0003], bhikkhave, aniccā. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā. Yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi[P 4.0003], na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saddā… gandhā… rasā… phoṭṭhabbā… dhammā aniccā. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ; yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā. Yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpesupi nibbindati, saddesupi nibbindati, gandhesupi nibbindati, rasesupi nibbindati, phoṭṭhabbesupi nibbindati, dhammesupi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

4. “Monks, forms are impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Sounds… smells… tastes… tangibles… mental objects are impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering; what is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus, monks, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with forms, disenchanted with sounds, disenchanted with smells, disenchanted with tastes, disenchanted with tangibles, and disenchanted with mental objects. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’” The fourth.

5. Bāhiradukkhasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on External Suffering

5. “Rūpā[M 2.0238], bhikkhave, dukkhā. Yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā; yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saddā… gandhā… rasā… phoṭṭhabbā… dhammā dukkhā. Yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadanattā. Yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

5. “Monks, forms are suffering. What is suffering is not-self; what is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Sounds… smells… tastes… tangibles… mental objects are suffering. What is suffering is not-self; what is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is no more for this state of being.’” The fifth.

6. Bāhirānattasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on External Not-Self

6. “Rūpā, bhikkhave, anattā. Yadanattā taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saddā… gandhā… rasā… phoṭṭhabbā… dhammā anattā. Yadanattā taṃ [T 4.0004] ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ…pe… nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

6. “Monks, forms are not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Sounds… smells… tastes… tangibles… mental objects are not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus… he understands: ‘…there is no more for this state of being.’” The sixth.

7. Ajjhattāniccātītānāgatasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Impermanence of the Internal in the Past and Future

7. “Cakkhuṃ[V 2.0004][P 4.0004], bhikkhave, aniccaṃ atītānāgataṃ; ko pana vādo paccuppannassa! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītasmiṃ cakkhusmiṃ anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ cakkhuṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannassa cakkhussa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Sotaṃ aniccaṃ… ghānaṃ aniccaṃ… jivhā aniccā atītānāgatā; ko pana vādo paccuppannāya! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītāya jivhāya anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ jivhaṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannāya jivhāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Kāyo anicco…pe… mano anicco atītānāgato; ko pana vādo paccuppannassa! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītasmiṃ manasmiṃ anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ manaṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannassa manassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hotī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

7. “Bhikkhus, the past and future eye is impermanent; what then is to be said of the present? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with the past eye, does not delight in the future eye, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of the present eye. The ear is impermanent… the nose is impermanent… the past and future tongue is impermanent; what then is to be said of the present? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with the past tongue, does not delight in the future tongue, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of the present tongue. The body is impermanent… the past and future mind is impermanent; what then is to be said of the present? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with the past mind, does not delight in the future mind, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of the present mind.” Seventh.

8. Ajjhattadukkhātītānāgatasuttaṃ

8. Discourse on the Internal, Suffering, Past and Future

8. “Cakkhuṃ[M 2.0239], bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ atītānāgataṃ; ko pana vādo paccuppannassa! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītasmiṃ cakkhusmiṃ anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ cakkhuṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannassa cakkhussa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Sotaṃ dukkhaṃ…pe… ghānaṃ dukkhaṃ…pe… jivhā [T 4.0005] dukkhā atītānāgatā; ko pana vādo paccuppannāya! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītāya jivhāya anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ jivhaṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannāya jivhāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Kāyo dukkho…pe… mano dukkho atītānāgato; ko pana vādo paccuppannassa! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītasmiṃ manasmiṃ anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ manaṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannassa manassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hotī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

8. “Bhikkhus, the past and future eye is suffering; what then is to be said of the present? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with the past eye, does not delight in the future eye, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of the present eye. The ear is suffering… The nose is suffering… The past and future tongue is suffering; what then is to be said of the present? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with the past tongue, does not delight in the future tongue, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of the present tongue. The body is suffering… The past and future mind is suffering; what then is to be said of the present? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with the past mind, does not delight in the future mind, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of the present mind.” Eighth.

9. Ajjhattānattātītānāgatasuttaṃ

9. Discourse on the Internal, Not-Self, Past and Future

9. “Cakkhuṃ[V 2.0005], bhikkhave, anattā atītānāgataṃ; ko pana vādo paccuppannassa! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako [P 4.0005] atītasmiṃ cakkhusmiṃ anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ cakkhuṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannassa cakkhussa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Sotaṃ anattā…pe… ghānaṃ anattā…pe… jivhā anattā atītānāgatā; ko pana vādo paccuppannāya! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītāya jivhāya anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ jivhaṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannāya jivhāya nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Kāyo anattā…pe… mano anattā atītānāgato; ko pana vādo paccuppannassa! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītasmiṃ manasmiṃ anapekkho hoti; anāgataṃ manaṃ nābhinandati; paccuppannassa manassa nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hotī”ti. Navamaṃ.

9. “Bhikkhus, the past and future eye is not-self; what then is to be said of the present? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with the past eye, does not delight in the future eye, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of the present eye. The ear is not-self… The nose is not-self… The past and future tongue is not-self; what then is to be said of the present? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with the past tongue, does not delight in the future tongue, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of the present tongue. The body is not-self… The past and future mind is not-self; what then is to be said of the present? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with the past mind, does not delight in the future mind, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of the present mind.” Ninth.

10. Bāhirāniccātītānāgatasuttaṃ

10. Discourse on the External, Impermanence, Past and Future

10. “Rūpā[T 4.0006], bhikkhave, aniccā atītānāgatā; ko pana vādo paccuppannānaṃ! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītesu rūpesu [M 2.0240] anapekkho hoti; anāgate rūpe nābhinandati; paccuppannānaṃ rūpānaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Saddā… gandhā… rasā… phoṭṭhabbā… dhammā aniccā atītānāgatā; ko pana vādo paccuppannānaṃ! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītesu dhammesu anapekkho hoti; anāgate dhamme nābhinandati; paccuppannānaṃ dhammānaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hotī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

10. “Bhikkhus, past and future forms are impermanent; what then is to be said of present ones? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with past forms, does not delight in future forms, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of present forms. Sounds… smells… tastes… touches… past and future mental phenomena are impermanent; what then is to be said of present ones? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with past mental phenomena, does not delight in future mental phenomena, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of present mental phenomena.” Tenth.

11. Bāhiradukkhātītānāgatasuttaṃ

11. Discourse on the External, Suffering, Past and Future

11. “Rūpā, bhikkhave, dukkhā atītānāgatā; ko pana vādo paccuppannānaṃ! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītesu rūpesu anapekkho hoti; anāgate rūpe nābhinandati[V 2.0006]; paccuppannānaṃ rūpānaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hotī”ti…pe. [P 4.0006]…. Ekādasamaṃ.

11. “Bhikkhus, past and future forms are suffering; what then is to be said of present ones? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with past forms, does not delight in future forms, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of present forms… and so on.” Eleventh.

12. Bāhirānattātītānāgatasuttaṃ

12. Discourse on the External, Not-Self, Past and Future

12. “Rūpā, bhikkhave, anattā atītānāgatā; ko pana vādo paccuppannānaṃ! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako atītesu rūpesu anapekkho hoti; anāgate rūpe nābhinandati; paccuppannānaṃ rūpānaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti. Saddā… gandhā… rasā… phoṭṭhabbā… dhammā anattā atītānāgatā; ko pana vādo paccuppannānaṃ! Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave[T 4.0007], sutavā ariyasāvako atītesu dhammesu anapekkho hoti; anāgate dhamme nābhinandati; paccuppannānaṃ dhammānaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hotī”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

12. “Bhikkhus, past and future forms are not-self; what then is to be said of present ones? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with past forms, does not delight in future forms, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of present forms. Sounds… smells… tastes… touches… past and future mental phenomena are not-self; what then is to be said of present ones? Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the learned noble disciple is unconcerned with past mental phenomena, does not delight in future mental phenomena, and practices for disenchantment, for dispassion, for the cessation of present mental phenomena.” Twelfth.

Aniccavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Impermanence.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā ca, tayo ajjhattabāhirā;

Yadaniccena tayo vuttā, te te ajjhattabāhirāti.

Impermanence, Suffering, and Not-self—three internal and external. By ‘Whatever is impermanent,’ three are taught; those very ones are internal and external.

2. Yamakavaggo

2. 2. The Chapter of Pairs

1. Paṭhamapubbesambodhasuttaṃ

1. 1. The First Discourse on Prior to Awakening

13. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0241]. “Pubbeva [T 4.0008] me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva [P 4.0007] sato etadahosi – ‘ko nu kho cakkhussa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko sotassa…pe… ko ghānassa… ko jivhāya… ko kāyassa… ko manassa [V 2.0007] assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇa’nti? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘yaṃ kho cakkhuṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ cakkhussa assādo. Yaṃ cakkhuṃ aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, ayaṃ cakkhussa ādīnavo. Yo cakkhusmiṃ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ cakkhussa nissaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ sotaṃ…pe… yaṃ ghānaṃ…pe… yaṃ jivhaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ jivhāya assādo. Yaṃ yā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) jivhā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṃ jivhāya ādīnavo. Yo jivhāya chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ jivhāya nissaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ kāyaṃ…pe… yaṃ manaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ manassa assādo. Yaṃ yo (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.) mano anicco dukkho vipariṇāmadhammo, ayaṃ manassa ādīnavo. Yo manasmiṃ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ manassa nissaraṇa’”nti.

13. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, before my awakening, while I was still an unawakened Bodhisatta, this thought occurred to me: ‘What, I wonder, is the gratification in the eye, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in the ear… nose… tongue… body… mind, what is the danger, what is the escape?’ Then, monks, this thought occurred to me: ‘The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on the eye—this is the gratification in the eye. That the eye is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in the eye. The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust for the eye—this is the escape from the eye. The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on the ear… nose… tongue… this is the gratification in the tongue. That the tongue is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in the tongue. The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust for the tongue—this is the escape from the tongue. The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on the body… mind… this is the gratification in the mind. That the mind is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in the mind. The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust for the mind—this is the escape from the mind.’”

“Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ channaṃ ajjhattikānaṃ āyatanānaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ, neva tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake [T 4.0009] sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti sabbatthāpi evameva itisaddena saha dissati paccaññāsiṃ. Yato ca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ channaṃ ajjhattikānaṃ āyatanānaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca [P 4.0008] pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti cetovimutti (sī. pī. ka.) evamuparipi, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Monks, for as long as I did not directly know these six internal sense bases in this way, as they really are—the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape—for so long, monks, I did not claim to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. But when, monks, I did directly know these six internal sense bases in this way, as they really are—the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape—then, monks, I claimed to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘Unshakable is my liberation of mind. This is the final birth. Now there is no further becoming.’” The first.

2. Dutiyapubbesambodhasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on What Preceded Enlightenment

14. “Pubbeva [M 2.0242] me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi – ‘ko nu kho rūpānaṃ assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ? Ko saddānaṃ…pe… ko gandhānaṃ… ko rasānaṃ… ko phoṭṭhabbānaṃ… ko dhammānaṃ assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇa’nti? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘yaṃ kho rūpe paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ rūpānaṃ assādo. Yaṃ rūpā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā, ayaṃ rūpānaṃ ādīnavo. Yo rūpesu chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ rūpānaṃ [V 2.0008] nissaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… yaṃ dhamme paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ dhammānaṃ assādo. Yaṃ dhammā aniccā dukkhā vipariṇāmadhammā[T 4.0010], ayaṃ dhammānaṃ ādīnavo. Yo dhammesu chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ dhammānaṃ nissaraṇa’”nti.

14. “Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment, while I was still an unenlightened Bodhisatta, this thought occurred to me: ‘What, I wonder, is the gratification in forms, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in sounds… in odors… in tastes… in tangibles… What is the gratification in mental phenomena, what is the danger, what is the escape?’ Then, Bhikkhus, this thought occurred to me: ‘The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on forms—this is the gratification in forms. That forms are impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in forms. The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust for forms—this is the escape from forms. The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on sounds… odors… tastes… tangibles… The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on mental phenomena—this is the gratification in mental phenomena. That mental phenomena are impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in mental phenomena. The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust for mental phenomena—this is the escape from mental phenomena.’”

“Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ channaṃ bāhirānaṃ āyatanānaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ, neva tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ. Yato ca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ channaṃ bāhirānaṃ āyatanānaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for as long as I did not directly know these six external sense bases in this way, as they really are—the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape—for so long, Bhikkhus, I did not claim to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, its Māra, and its Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. But when, Bhikkhus, I did directly know these six external sense bases in this way, as they really are—the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape—then, Bhikkhus, I claimed to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, its Māra, and its Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘Unshakable is my liberation of mind. This is the final birth. Now there is no further becoming.’”

3. Paṭhamaassādapariyesanasuttaṃ

3. The First Discourse on the Search for Gratification

15. “Cakkhussāhaṃ, bhikkhave, assādapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo cakkhussa assādo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā cakkhussa assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Cakkhussāhaṃ, bhikkhave[P 4.0009], ādīnavapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo cakkhussa ādīnavo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā cakkhussa ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Cakkhussāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nissaraṇapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yaṃ cakkhussa nissaraṇaṃ tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā cakkhussa nissaraṇaṃ[T 4.0011], paññāya me taṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ. Sotassāhaṃ[M 2.0243], bhikkhave… ghānassāhaṃ, bhikkhave… jivhāyāhaṃ bhikkhave, assādapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo jivhāya assādo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā jivhāya assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Jivhāyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādīnavapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo jivhāya ādīnavo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā jivhāya ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Jivhāyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nissaraṇapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yaṃ jivhāya nissaraṇaṃ tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā jivhāya nissaraṇaṃ, paññāya me taṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ. Manassāhaṃ, bhikkhave, assādapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo manassa assādo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā manassa assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Manassāhaṃ, bhikkhave[V 2.0009], ādīnavapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo manassa ādīnavo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā manassa ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Manassāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nissaraṇapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yaṃ manassa nissaraṇaṃ tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā manassa nissaraṇaṃ, paññāya me taṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ.

15. “Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the gratification in the eye. Whatever gratification there is in the eye, that I found. To whatever extent there is gratification in the eye, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the danger in the eye. Whatever danger there is in the eye, that I found. To whatever extent there is danger in the eye, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the escape from the eye. Whatever escape there is from the eye, that I found. To whatever extent there is escape from the eye, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I… for the ear… Bhikkhus, I… for the nose… Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the gratification in the tongue. Whatever gratification there is in the tongue, that I found. To whatever extent there is gratification in the tongue, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the danger in the tongue. Whatever danger there is in the tongue, that I found. To whatever extent there is danger in the tongue, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the escape from the tongue. Whatever escape there is from the tongue, that I found. To whatever extent there is escape from the tongue, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the gratification in the mind. Whatever gratification there is in the mind, that I found. To whatever extent there is gratification in the mind, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the danger in the mind. Whatever danger there is in the mind, that I found. To whatever extent there is danger in the mind, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the escape from the mind. Whatever escape there is from the mind, that I found. To whatever extent there is escape from the mind, that has been well seen by me with wisdom.”

“Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ channaṃ ajjhattikānaṃ āyatanānaṃ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ…pe… paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for as long as I did not yet directly know, as it really is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape in these six internal sense bases… I declared it. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘My liberation of mind is unshakable; this is the final birth; now there is no more renewed existence.’” The Third.

4. Dutiyaassādapariyesanasuttaṃ

4. The Second Discourse on the Search for Gratification

16. “Rūpānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, assādapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo rūpānaṃ assādo [T 4.0012] tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā rūpānaṃ assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Rūpānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādīnavapariyesanaṃ [P 4.0010] acariṃ. Yo rūpānaṃ ādīnavo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā rūpānaṃ ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Rūpānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nissaraṇapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yaṃ rūpānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā rūpānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ, paññāya me taṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ. Saddānāhaṃ, bhikkhave… gandhānāhaṃ, bhikkhave… rasānāhaṃ, bhikkhave… phoṭṭhabbānāhaṃ, bhikkhave… dhammānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, assādapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo dhammānaṃ assādo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā dhammānaṃ assādo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Dhammānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādīnavapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yo dhammānaṃ ādīnavo tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā dhammānaṃ ādīnavo paññāya me so sudiṭṭho. Dhammānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nissaraṇapariyesanaṃ acariṃ. Yaṃ dhammānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ tadajjhagamaṃ. Yāvatā dhammānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ, paññāya [M 2.0244] me taṃ sudiṭṭhaṃ.

16. “Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the gratification in forms. Whatever gratification there is in forms, that I found. To whatever extent there is gratification in forms, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the danger in forms. Whatever danger there is in forms, that I found. To whatever extent there is danger in forms, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the escape from forms. Whatever escape there is from forms, that I found. To whatever extent there is escape from forms, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I… in sounds… Bhikkhus, I… in odors… Bhikkhus, I… in tastes… Bhikkhus, I… in tactile objects… Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the gratification in mental phenomena. Whatever gratification there is in mental phenomena, that I found. To whatever extent there is gratification in mental phenomena, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the danger in mental phenomena. Whatever danger there is in mental phenomena, that I found. To whatever extent there is danger in mental phenomena, that has been well seen by me with wisdom. Bhikkhus, I undertook the search for the escape from mental phenomena. Whatever escape there is from mental phenomena, that I found. To whatever extent there is escape from mental phenomena, that has been well seen by me with wisdom.”

“Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ channaṃ bāhirānaṃ āyatanānaṃ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ…pe… paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for as long as I did not yet directly know, as it really is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape in these six external sense bases… I declared it. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘My liberation of mind is unshakable. This is my final birth. Now there is no more renewed existence.’” The Fourth.

5. Paṭhamanoceassādasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on ‘If There Were No Gratification’

17. “No [V 2.0010] cedaṃ, bhikkhave, cakkhussa assādo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā cakkhusmiṃ sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi cakkhussa assādo [T 4.0013] tasmā sattā cakkhusmiṃ sārajjanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, cakkhussa ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā cakkhusmiṃ nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi cakkhussa ādīnavo tasmā sattā cakkhusmiṃ nibbindanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, cakkhussa nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā cakkhusmā nissareyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi cakkhussa nissaraṇaṃ tasmā sattā cakkhusmā nissaranti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, sotassa assādo abhavissa… no [P 4.0011] cedaṃ, bhikkhave, ghānassa assādo abhavissa… no cedaṃ, bhikkhave, jivhāya assādo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā jivhāya sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi jivhāya assādo, tasmā sattā jivhāya sārajjanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, jivhāya ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā jivhāya nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi jivhāya ādīnavo, tasmā sattā jivhāya nibbindanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, jivhāya nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā jivhāya nissareyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi jivhāya nissaraṇaṃ, tasmā sattā jivhāya nissaranti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, kāyassa assādo abhavissa… no cedaṃ, bhikkhave, manassa assādo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā manasmiṃ sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi manassa assādo, tasmā sattā manasmiṃ sārajjanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, manassa ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā manasmiṃ nibbindeyyuṃ[T 4.0014]. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi manassa ādīnavo, tasmā sattā manasmiṃ nibbindanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, manassa nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā manasmā nissareyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi manassa nissaraṇaṃ, tasmā sattā manasmā nissaranti.

17. “Bhikkhus, if there were no gratification in the eye, beings would not be attached to the eye. But because there is gratification in the eye, beings are attached to the eye. Bhikkhus, if there were no danger in the eye, beings would not become disenchanted with the eye. But because there is danger in the eye, beings become disenchanted with the eye. Bhikkhus, if there were no escape from the eye, beings would not escape from the eye. But because there is an escape from the eye, beings escape from the eye. Bhikkhus, if there were no gratification in the ear… Bhikkhus, if there were no gratification in the nose… Bhikkhus, if there were no gratification in the tongue, beings would not be attached to the tongue. But because there is gratification in the tongue, beings are attached to the tongue. Bhikkhus, if there were no danger in the tongue, beings would not become disenchanted with the tongue. But because there is danger in the tongue, beings become disenchanted with the tongue. Bhikkhus, if there were no escape from the tongue, beings would not escape from the tongue. But because there is an escape from the tongue, beings escape from the tongue. Bhikkhus, if there were no gratification in the body… Bhikkhus, if there were no gratification in the mind, beings would not be attached to the mind. But because there is gratification in the mind, beings are attached to the mind. Bhikkhus, if there were no danger in the mind, beings would not become disenchanted with the mind. But because there is danger in the mind, beings become disenchanted with the mind. Bhikkhus, if there were no escape from the mind, beings would not escape from the mind. But because there is an escape from the mind, beings escape from the mind.”

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṃ channaṃ ajjhattikānaṃ āyatanānaṃ [M 2.0245] assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññaṃsu, neva tāva, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaññuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena vipariyādikatena (sī. pī.), vipariyādikatena (syā. kaṃ. ka.) cetasā vihariṃsu. Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṃ channaṃ ajjhattikānaṃ āyatanānaṃ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca [V 2.0011] ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññaṃsu[P 4.0012], atha, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaññuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for as long as beings did not directly know, as it really is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape in these six internal sense bases, for so long, bhikkhus, beings did not dwell released, disjoined, and liberated, with a mind that has overcome the boundaries, from this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, from this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. But when, bhikkhus, beings directly knew, as it really is, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape in these six internal sense bases, then, bhikkhus, beings dwell released, disjoined, and liberated, with a mind that has overcome the boundaries, from this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, from this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans.”

6. Dutiyanoceassādasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on 'If There Were No Gratification'

18. “No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpānaṃ assādo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā rūpesu sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpānaṃ assādo, tasmā sattā rūpesu sārajjanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpānaṃ ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā rūpesu nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā [T 4.0015] ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpānaṃ ādīnavo, tasmā sattā rūpesu nibbindanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā rūpehi nissareyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi rūpānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ, tasmā sattā rūpehi nissaranti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, saddānaṃ… gandhānaṃ… rasānaṃ… phoṭṭhabbānaṃ… dhammānaṃ assādo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā dhammesu sārajjeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi dhammānaṃ assādo, tasmā sattā dhammesu sārajjanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ ādīnavo abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā dhammesu nibbindeyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi dhammānaṃ ādīnavo, tasmā sattā dhammesu nibbindanti. No cedaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ abhavissa, nayidaṃ sattā dhammehi nissareyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi dhammānaṃ nissaraṇaṃ, tasmā sattā dhammehi nissaranti.

18. “Bhikkhus, if there were no gratification in forms, beings would not be attached to forms. But because there is gratification in forms, beings are attached to forms. If there were no danger in forms, beings would not become disenchanted with forms. But because there is danger in forms, beings become disenchanted with forms. If there were no escape from forms, beings would not escape from forms. But because there is an escape from forms, beings escape from forms. If there were no gratification in sounds… aromas… flavors… tactile sensations… mental phenomena, beings would not be attached to mental phenomena. But because there is gratification in mental phenomena, beings are attached to mental phenomena. If there were no danger in mental phenomena, beings would not become disenchanted with mental phenomena. But because there is danger in mental phenomena, beings become disenchanted with mental phenomena. If there were no escape from mental phenomena, beings would not escape from mental phenomena. But because there is an escape from mental phenomena, beings escape from mental phenomena.”

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṃ channaṃ bāhirānaṃ āyatanānaṃ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññaṃsu[P 4.0013], neva tāva, bhikkhave, sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā [M 2.0246] pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaññuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā vihariṃsu. Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, sattā imesaṃ channaṃ bāhirānaṃ āyatanānaṃ assādañca assādato, ādīnavañca ādīnavato, nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññaṃsu, atha, bhikkhave[T 4.0016], sattā sadevakā lokā samārakā sabrahmakā sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya nissaṭā visaññuttā vippamuttā vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharantī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

For as long as, bhikkhus, beings had not truly understood the gratification in these six external sense bases as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape, for so long, bhikkhus, beings in the world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, had not yet escaped, were not disjoined, were not liberated, and did not dwell with a mind without boundaries. But when, bhikkhus, beings had truly understood the gratification in these six external sense bases as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape, then, bhikkhus, beings in the world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, have escaped, are disjoined, are liberated, and dwell with a mind without boundaries.

7. Paṭhamābhinandasuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse on Delighting

19. “Yo[V 2.0012], bhikkhave, cakkhuṃ abhinandati, dukkhaṃ so abhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ abhinandati, aparimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo sotaṃ…pe… yo ghānaṃ…pe… yo jivhaṃ abhinandati, dukkhaṃ so abhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ abhinandati, aparimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo kāyaṃ…pe… yo manaṃ abhinandati, dukkhaṃ so abhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ abhinandati, aparimutto so dukkhasmā”ti vadāmi.

19. Bhikkhus, whoever delights in the eye delights in suffering. Whoever delights in suffering, I say, is not released from suffering. Whoever delights in the ear... the nose... the tongue delights in suffering. Whoever delights in suffering, I say, is not released from suffering. Whoever delights in the body... the mind delights in suffering. Whoever delights in suffering, I say, is not released from suffering.

“Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, cakkhuṃ nābhinandati, dukkhaṃ so nābhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ nābhinandati, parimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo sotaṃ…pe… yo ghānaṃ…pe… yo jivhaṃ nābhinandati, dukkhaṃ so nābhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ nābhinandati, parimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo kāyaṃ…pe… yo manaṃ nābhinandati, dukkhaṃ so nābhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ nābhinandati, parimutto so dukkhasmā”ti vadāmi. Sattamaṃ.

But, bhikkhus, whoever does not delight in the eye does not delight in suffering. Whoever does not delight in suffering, I say, is released from suffering. Whoever does not delight in the ear... the nose... the tongue does not delight in suffering. Whoever does not delight in suffering, I say, is released from suffering. Whoever does not delight in the body... the mind does not delight in suffering. Whoever does not delight in suffering, I say, is released from suffering.

8. Dutiyābhinandasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse on Delighting

20. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpe abhinandati, dukkhaṃ so abhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ abhinandati, aparimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Yo sadde…pe… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… dhamme abhinandati, dukkhaṃ so abhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ abhinandati, aparimutto so dukkhasmā”ti vadāmi.

20. Bhikkhus, whoever delights in visible forms, delights in suffering. Whoever delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Whoever delights in sounds… in odors… in tastes… in tangibles… in mental objects, delights in suffering. Whoever delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering.

“Yo [P 4.0014] ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpe nābhinandati, dukkhaṃ so nābhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ nābhinandati, parimutto so dukkhasmāti vadāmi[T 4.0017]. Yo sadde…pe… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… dhamme nābhinandati, dukkhaṃ so nābhinandati. Yo dukkhaṃ nābhinandati, parimutto so dukkhasmā”ti vadāmi. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

But, bhikkhus, whoever does not delight in visible forms does not delight in suffering. Whoever does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. Whoever does not delight in sounds… in odors… in tastes… in tangibles… in mental objects does not delight in suffering. Whoever does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.

9. Paṭhamadukkhuppādasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on the Arising of Suffering

21. “Yo[M 2.0247][V 2.0013], bhikkhave, cakkhussa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo sotassa…pe… yo ghānassa… yo jivhāya… yo kāyassa… yo manassa uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo.

21. Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, persistence, reproduction, and manifestation of the eye, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. Whatever is the arising, persistence, reproduction, and manifestation of the ear… of the nose… of the tongue… of the body… of the mind, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.

“Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, cakkhussa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo. Yo sotassa… yo ghānassa… yo jivhāya… yo kāyassa… yo manassa nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Navamaṃ.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation, pacification, and disappearance of the eye, that is the cessation of suffering, the pacification of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death. Whatever is the cessation, pacification, and disappearance of the ear… of the nose… of the tongue… of the body… of the mind, that is the cessation of suffering, the pacification of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death.

10. Dutiyadukkhuppādasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on the Arising of Suffering

22. “Yo, bhikkhave, rūpānaṃ uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo. Yo saddānaṃ…pe… yo gandhānaṃ… yo rasānaṃ… yo phoṭṭhabbānaṃ… yo dhammānaṃ uppādo ṭhiti abhinibbatti pātubhāvo, dukkhasseso uppādo, rogānaṃ ṭhiti, jarāmaraṇassa pātubhāvo.

22. Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, persistence, reproduction, and manifestation of visible forms, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death. So it is for sounds… odors… tastes… tangibles… and for mental objects, their arising, persistence, reproduction, and manifestation is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.

“Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpānaṃ nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo. Yo [T 4.0018] saddānaṃ…pe… yo gandhānaṃ… yo rasānaṃ… yo phoṭṭhabbānaṃ… yo [P 4.0015] dhammānaṃ nirodho vūpasamo atthaṅgamo, dukkhasseso nirodho, rogānaṃ vūpasamo, jarāmaraṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, whatever is the cessation, pacification, and disappearance of visible forms, that is the cessation of suffering, the pacification of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death. So it is for sounds… odors… tastes… tangibles… and for mental objects, their cessation, pacification, and disappearance is the cessation of suffering, the pacification of diseases, and the disappearance of aging and death.

Yamakavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter of Pairs.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Sambodhena [V 2.0014] duve vuttā, assādena apare duve;

No cetena duve vuttā, abhinandena apare duve;

Uppādena duve vuttā, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

Two were taught on enlightenment, and another two on gratification; two were taught with ‘If not for this,’ and another two on delight; two were taught on arising; for that reason, it is called a chapter.

3. Sabbavaggo

3. The Chapter on the All

1. Sabbasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the All

23. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 2.0248]. “Sabbaṃ [T 4.0019] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha. Kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ? Cakkhuñceva rūpā ca, sotañca sotañceva (?) evamitarayugalesupi saddā ca, ghānañca gandhā ca, jivhā ca rasā ca, kāyo ca phoṭṭhabbā ca, mano ca dhammā ca – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ. Yo, bhikkhave, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ahametaṃ sabbaṃ paccakkhāya aññaṃ sabbaṃ paññāpessāmī’ti, tassa vācāvatthukamevassa vācāvatthurevassa (sī. pī.), vācāvatthudevassa (syā. kaṃ.); puṭṭho ca na sampāyeyya, uttariñca vighātaṃ āpajjeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yathā taṃ, bhikkhave, avisayasmi”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

23. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the All. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the All? The eye and forms, the ear and sounds, the nose and odors, the tongue and tastes, the body and tangible objects, the mind and mental objects—this is called the All, bhikkhus. If anyone, bhikkhus, should say thus: ‘Having rejected this All, I will declare another All,’ for him it would be a matter of words only. When questioned, he would not be able to answer, and further, he would come to vexation. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, it is beyond his domain.”

2. Pahānasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Abandonment

24. “Sabbappahānāya sabbaṃ pahānāya (syā. kaṃ. ka.) vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sabbappahānāya dhammo? Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, pahātabbaṃ, rūpā pahātabbā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ pahātabbaṃ, cakkhusamphasso pahātabbo[P 4.0016], yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi pahātabbaṃ…pe… yampidaṃ sotasamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi pahātabbaṃ… yampidaṃ ghānasamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi pahātabbaṃ. Jivhā pahātabbā, rasā pahātabbā, jivhāviññāṇaṃ pahātabbaṃ, jivhāsamphasso pahātabbo, yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā [V 2.0015] tampi pahātabbaṃ. Kāyo pahātabbo… mano pahātabbo, dhammā pahātabbā, manoviññāṇaṃ [T 4.0020] pahātabbaṃ, manosamphasso pahātabbo, yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi pahātabbaṃ. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sabbappahānāya dhammo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

24. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma for the abandoning of all. Listen to it. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma for the abandoning of all? The eye, bhikkhus, is to be abandoned. Forms are to be abandoned. Eye-consciousness is to be abandoned. Eye-contact is to be abandoned. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is to be abandoned. … The ear is to be abandoned… The nose is to be abandoned… The tongue is to be abandoned; tastes are to be abandoned; tongue-consciousness is to be abandoned; tongue-contact is to be abandoned; and whatever feeling arises conditioned by tongue-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is to be abandoned. The body is to be abandoned… The mind is to be abandoned; mental objects are to be abandoned; mind-consciousness is to be abandoned; mind-contact is to be abandoned; and whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is to be abandoned. This, indeed, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma for the abandoning of all.” Second.

3. Abhiññāpariññāpahānasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Abandoning through Direct Knowledge and Full Understanding

25. “Sabbaṃ abhiññā pariññā pahānāya vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ abhiññā pariññā pahānāya dhammo? Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṃ, rūpā abhiññā pariññā pahātabbā[M 2.0249], cakkhuviññāṇaṃ abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṃ, cakkhusamphasso abhiññā pariññā pahātabbo, yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṃ…pe… jivhā abhiññā pariññā pahātabbā, rasā abhiññā pariññā pahātabbā, jivhāviññāṇaṃ abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṃ, jivhāsamphasso abhiññā pariññā pahātabbo, yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṃ. Kāyo abhiññā pariññā pahātabbo… mano abhiññā pariññā pahātabbo, dhammā abhiññā pariññā [P 4.0017] pahātabbā, manoviññāṇaṃ abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṃ, manosamphasso abhiññā pariññā pahātabbo, yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā [T 4.0021] tampi abhiññā pariññā pahātabbaṃ. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ abhiññā pariññā pahānāya dhammo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

25. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma for abandoning all through direct knowledge and full understanding. Listen to it. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma for abandoning all through direct knowledge and full understanding? The eye, bhikkhus, is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. Forms are to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. Eye-consciousness is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. Eye-contact is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. … The tongue is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. Tastes are to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. Tongue-consciousness is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. Tongue-contact is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by tongue-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. The body is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding… The mind is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. Mental objects are to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. Mind-consciousness is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. Mind-contact is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is to be abandoned through direct knowledge and full understanding. This, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma for abandoning all through direct knowledge and full understanding.” Third.

4. Paṭhamaaparijānanasuttaṃ

4. The First Discourse on Not Fully Comprehending

26. “Sabbaṃ[V 2.0016], bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Kiñca, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya? Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Rūpe anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Cakkhusamphassaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya…pe… jivhaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Rase…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ…pe… jivhāsamphassaṃ…pe… yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Kāyaṃ…pe… manaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Dhamme…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ…pe… manosamphassaṃ…pe… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ [M 2.0250] appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.

26. “Bhikkhus, by not directly knowing all, not fully comprehending all, not becoming dispassionate towards all, and not abandoning all, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. And what, bhikkhus, is the all that, by not directly knowing, not fully comprehending, not becoming dispassionate towards, and not abandoning, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering? Bhikkhus, by not directly knowing the eye, not fully comprehending it, not becoming dispassionate towards it, and not abandoning it, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. By not directly knowing forms… one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. By not directly knowing eye-consciousness… one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. By not directly knowing eye-contact… one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—by not directly knowing that too, not fully comprehending it, not becoming dispassionate towards it, and not abandoning it, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. … By not directly knowing the tongue… one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. Tastes… Tongue-consciousness… Tongue-contact… And whatever feeling arises conditioned by tongue-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—by not directly knowing that too, not fully comprehending it, not becoming dispassionate towards it, and not abandoning it, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. The body… By not directly knowing the mind... one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. Mental objects… Mind-consciousness… Mind-contact… And whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—by not directly knowing that too, not fully comprehending it, not becoming dispassionate towards it, and not abandoning it, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. This, indeed, bhikkhus, is the all that, by not directly knowing, not fully comprehending, not becoming dispassionate towards, and not abandoning, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering.”

“Sabbañca kho, bhikkhave, abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo [T 4.0022] dukkhakkhayāya. Kiñca[P 4.0018], bhikkhave, sabbaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya? Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Rūpe abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Cakkhusamphassaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya…pe… [V 2.0017] jivhaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Rase…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ…pe… jivhāsamphassaṃ…pe… yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Kāyaṃ…pe… manaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Dhamme…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ…pe… manosamphassaṃ…pe… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāyā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“And Bhikkhus, by directly knowing the all, fully comprehending it, developing dispassion for it, and abandoning it, one is capable of ending suffering. And what, Bhikkhus, is the all that, by directly knowing, fully comprehending, developing dispassion for, and abandoning, one is capable of ending suffering? Bhikkhus, by directly knowing the eye, fully comprehending it, developing dispassion for it, and abandoning it, one is capable of ending suffering. By directly knowing forms… one is capable of ending suffering. By directly knowing eye-consciousness… one is capable of ending suffering. By directly knowing eye-contact… one is capable of ending suffering. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—by directly knowing that too, fully comprehending it, developing dispassion for it, and abandoning it, one is capable of ending suffering. … By directly knowing the tongue… one is capable of ending suffering. Tastes… Tongue-consciousness… Tongue-contact… And whatever feeling arises conditioned by tongue-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—by directly knowing that too, fully comprehending it, developing dispassion for it, and abandoning it, one is capable of ending suffering. The body… By directly knowing the mind... one is capable of ending suffering. Mental objects… Mind-consciousness… Mind-contact… And whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—by directly knowing that too, fully comprehending it, developing dispassion for it, and abandoning it, one is capable of ending suffering. Bhikkhus, it is by directly knowing this all, fully comprehending it, developing dispassion for it, and abandoning it, that one is capable of ending suffering.”

5. Dutiyaaparijānanasuttaṃ

5. The Second Discourse on Not Fully Comprehending

27. “Sabbaṃ[M 2.0251], bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya? Yañca, bhikkhave[V 2.0018], cakkhu, ye [T 4.0023] ca rūpā, yañca cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, ye ca cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā…pe… yā [P 4.0019] ca jivhā, ye ca rasā, yañca jivhāviññāṇaṃ, ye ca jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā; yo ca kāyo, ye ca phoṭṭhabbā, yañca kāyaviññāṇaṃ, ye ca kāyaviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā; yo ca mano, ye ca dhammā, yañca manoviññāṇaṃ, ye ca manoviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā – idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya.

27. “Bhikkhus, by not directly knowing the all, not fully comprehending it, not developing dispassion for it, and not abandoning it, one is incapable of the exhaustion of suffering. And what, Bhikkhus, is the all that, by not directly knowing, not fully comprehending, not developing dispassion for, and not abandoning, one is incapable of the exhaustion of suffering? The eye, Bhikkhus, and forms, and eye-consciousness, and those dhammas cognizable by eye-consciousness… the tongue, and tastes, and tongue-consciousness, and those dhammas cognizable by tongue-consciousness; the body, and tangible objects, and body-consciousness, and those dhammas cognizable by body-consciousness; the mind, and mental objects, and mind-consciousness, and those dhammas cognizable by mind-consciousness. Bhikkhus, it is by not directly knowing this all, not fully comprehending it, not developing dispassion for it, and not abandoning it, that one is incapable of the exhaustion of suffering.”

“Sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya? Yañca, bhikkhave, cakkhu, ye ca rūpā, yañca cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, ye ca cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā…pe… yā ca jivhā, ye ca rasā, yañca jivhāviññāṇaṃ, ye ca jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā; yo ca kāyo, ye ca phoṭṭhabbā, yañca kāyaviññāṇaṃ, ye ca kāyaviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā; yo ca mano, ye ca dhammā, yañca manoviññāṇaṃ, ye ca manoviññāṇaviññātabbā dhammā – idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāyā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, by directly knowing the all, fully comprehending it, developing dispassion for it, and abandoning it, one is capable of the exhaustion of suffering. And what, Bhikkhus, is the all that, by directly knowing, fully comprehending, developing dispassion for, and abandoning, one is capable of the exhaustion of suffering? The eye, Bhikkhus, and forms, and eye-consciousness, and those dhammas cognizable by eye-consciousness… the tongue, and tastes, and tongue-consciousness, and those dhammas cognizable by tongue-consciousness; the body, and tangible objects, and body-consciousness, and those dhammas cognizable by body-consciousness; the mind, and mental objects, and mind-consciousness, and those dhammas cognizable by mind-consciousness. Bhikkhus, it is by directly knowing this all, fully comprehending it, developing dispassion for it, and abandoning it, that one is capable of the exhaustion of suffering.” The fifth.

6. Ādittasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Burning

28. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā gayāyaṃ viharati gayāsīse saddhiṃ bhikkhusahassena. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, ādittaṃ. Kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ ādittaṃ? Cakkhu cakkhuṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), bhikkhave, ādittaṃ, rūpā ādittā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ, cakkhusamphasso āditto. Yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ [T 4.0024] sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? ‘Rāgagginā, dosagginā, mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi āditta’nti vadāmi…pe… jivhā ādittā, rasā ādittā, jivhāviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ, jivhāsamphasso āditto[P 4.0020]. Yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? ‘Rāgagginā, dosagginā, mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi āditta’nti vadāmi…pe… mano āditto, dhammā ādittā, manoviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ, manosamphasso āditto. Yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? ‘Rāgagginā, dosagginā, mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi āditta’nti vadāmi. Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati, yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati [M 2.0252] vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi nibbindati [V 2.0019] …pe… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā [T 4.0025] vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanduṃ. Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne tassa bhikkhusahassassa anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsūti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

28. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Gayā, on Gayā Head, together with a thousand bhikkhus. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, the all is burning. And what, bhikkhus, is the all that is burning? The eye, bhikkhus, is burning; forms are burning; eye-consciousness is burning; eye-contact is burning. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is burning. Burning with what? It is burning with the fire of lust, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion. It is burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs, and despairs, I say. ... The tongue is burning; tastes are burning; tongue-consciousness is burning; tongue-contact is burning. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by tongue-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is burning. Burning with what? It is burning with the fire of lust, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion. It is burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs, and despairs, I say. ... The mind is burning; mental objects are burning; mind-consciousness is burning; mind-contact is burning. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is burning. Burning with what? It is burning with the fire of lust, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion. It is burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs, and despairs, I say. Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye, disenchanted with forms, disenchanted with eye-consciousness, disenchanted with eye-contact. And whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—with that too he becomes disenchanted. ... And whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—with that too he becomes disenchanted. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’” This is what the Blessed One said. Delighted, those bhikkhus rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words. And while this exposition was being spoken, the minds of that thousand of bhikkhus were liberated from the taints through non-clinging. The sixth.

7. Addhabhūtasuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on the Afflicted

29. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, addhabhūtaṃ andhabhūtaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.). Kiñca[P 4.0021], bhikkhave, sabbaṃ addhabhūtaṃ? Cakkhu, bhikkhave, addhabhūtaṃ, rūpā addhabhūtā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ addhabhūtaṃ, cakkhusamphasso addhabhūto, yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi addhabhūtaṃ. Kena addhabhūtaṃ? ‘Jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi addhabhūta’nti vadāmi…pe… jivhā addhabhūtā, rasā addhabhūtā, jivhāviññāṇaṃ addhabhūtaṃ, jivhāsamphasso addhabhūto, yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi addhabhūtaṃ. Kena addhabhūtaṃ? ‘Jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi addhabhūta’nti vadāmi. Kāyo addhabhūto…pe… mano addhabhūto, dhammā addhabhūtā, manoviññāṇaṃ addhabhūtaṃ, manosamphasso addhabhūto, yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā [T 4.0026] tampi addhabhūtaṃ. Kena addhabhūtaṃ? ‘Jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi addhabhūta’nti vadāmi. Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati…pe… [V 2.0020] yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati[M 2.0253], virāgā vimuccati, vimuttasmiṃ ‘vimutta’miti ñāṇaṃ hoti, ‘khīṇā jāti vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

29. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, the all is afflicted. And what, bhikkhus, is the all that is afflicted? The eye, bhikkhus, is afflicted; forms are afflicted; eye-consciousness is afflicted; eye-contact is afflicted; and whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is afflicted. By what is it afflicted? ‘It is afflicted by birth, by aging, by death, by sorrow, by lamentation, by pain, by displeasure, and by despair,’ I say. ... The tongue is afflicted; tastes are afflicted; tongue-consciousness is afflicted; tongue-contact is afflicted; and whatever feeling arises with tongue-contact as condition—pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is afflicted. By what is it afflicted? ‘It is afflicted by birth, by aging, by death, by sorrow, by lamentation, by pain, by displeasure, and by despair,’ I say. The body is afflicted. ... The mind is afflicted; mental phenomena are afflicted; mind-consciousness is afflicted; mind-contact is afflicted; and whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition—pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is afflicted. By what is it afflicted? ‘It is afflicted by birth, by aging, by death, by sorrow, by lamentation, by pain, by displeasure, and by despair,’ I say. Seeing thus, bhikkhus, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye, disenchanted with forms, disenchanted with eye-consciousness, disenchanted with eye-contact. ... And with whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition—pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—with that too he becomes disenchanted. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’” Seventh.

8. Samugghātasāruppasuttaṃ

8. The Sutta on What is Suitable for Uprooting

30. “Sabbamaññitasamugghātasāruppaṃ vo, bhikkhave, paṭipadaṃ [P 4.0022] desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmīti. Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, sabbamaññitasamugghātasāruppā paṭipadā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhuṃ na maññati, cakkhusmiṃ na maññati, cakkhuto na maññati, cakkhuṃ meti na maññati. Rūpe na maññati, rūpesu na maññati, rūpato na maññati, rūpā meti na maññati. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na maññati, cakkhuviññāṇasmiṃ na maññati, cakkhuviññāṇato na maññati, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ meti na maññati. Cakkhusamphassaṃ na maññati, cakkhusamphassasmiṃ na maññati, cakkhusamphassato na maññati, cakkhusamphasso meti na maññati. Yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi na maññati[T 4.0027], tasmimpi na maññati, tatopi na maññati, taṃ meti na maññati…pe… jivhaṃ na maññati, jivhāya na maññati, jivhāto na maññati, jivhā meti na maññati. Rase na maññati, rasesu na maññati, rasato na maññati, rasā meti na maññati. Jivhāviññāṇaṃ na maññati, jivhāviññāṇasmiṃ na maññati, jivhāviññāṇato na maññati, jivhāviññāṇaṃ meti na maññati. Jivhāsamphassaṃ na maññati, jivhāsamphassasmiṃ na maññati, jivhāsamphassato na maññati, jivhāsamphasso meti na maññati. Yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi na maññati, tasmimpi na maññati, tatopi na maññati, taṃ meti na maññati…pe… manaṃ na maññati, manasmiṃ na maññati, manato na maññati, mano meti na maññati. Dhamme na maññati, dhammesu na maññati, dhammato na maññati, dhammā meti [V 2.0021] na maññati. Manoviññāṇaṃ na maññati, manoviññāṇasmiṃ na maññati, manoviññāṇato na maññati, manoviññāṇaṃ meti na maññati. Manosamphassaṃ na maññati, manosamphassasmiṃ na maññati, manosamphassato na maññati, manosamphasso meti na maññati[P 4.0023]. Yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi na maññati, tasmimpi na maññati, tatopi na maññati, taṃ meti na [T 4.0028] maññati. Sabbaṃ na maññati, sabbasmiṃ na maññati, sabbato na maññati, sabbaṃ meti na maññati. So evaṃ amaññamāno [M 2.0254] na ca kiñci loke upādiyati. Anupādiyaṃ na paritassati. Aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Ayaṃ kho sā, bhikkhave, sabbamaññitasamugghātasāruppā paṭipadā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

30. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the practice suitable for uprooting all conceivings. Listen to that, attend carefully, and I will speak.” “And what, bhikkhus, is that practice suitable for uprooting all conceivings? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not conceive the eye, does not conceive in the eye, does not conceive from the eye, does not conceive, ‘The eye is mine.’ He does not conceive forms, does not conceive in forms, does not conceive from forms, does not conceive, ‘Forms are mine.’ He does not conceive eye-consciousness, does not conceive in eye-consciousness, does not conceive from eye-consciousness, does not conceive, ‘Eye-consciousness is mine.’ He does not conceive eye-contact, does not conceive in eye-contact, does not conceive from eye-contact, does not conceive, ‘Eye-contact is mine.’ He does not conceive whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—does not conceive in it, does not conceive from it, does not conceive, ‘That is mine.’ … He does not conceive the tongue, does not conceive in the tongue, does not conceive from the tongue, does not conceive, ‘The tongue is mine.’ He does not conceive tastes, does not conceive in tastes, does not conceive from tastes, does not conceive, ‘Tastes are mine.’ He does not conceive tongue-consciousness, does not conceive in tongue-consciousness, does not conceive from tongue-consciousness, does not conceive, ‘Tongue-consciousness is mine.’ He does not conceive tongue-contact, does not conceive in tongue-contact, does not conceive from tongue-contact, does not conceive, ‘Tongue-contact is mine.’ He does not conceive whatever feeling arises with tongue-contact as condition—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—does not conceive in it, does not conceive from it, does not conceive, ‘That is mine.’ … He does not conceive the mind, does not conceive in the mind, does not conceive from the mind, does not conceive, ‘The mind is mine.’ He does not conceive mental phenomena, does not conceive in mental phenomena, does not conceive from mental phenomena, does not conceive, ‘Mental phenomena are mine.’ He does not conceive mind-consciousness, does not conceive in mind-consciousness, does not conceive from mind-consciousness, does not conceive, ‘Mind-consciousness is mine.’ He does not conceive mind-contact, does not conceive in mind-contact, does not conceive from mind-contact, does not conceive, ‘Mind-contact is mine.’ He does not conceive whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—does not conceive in it, does not conceive from it, does not conceive, ‘That is mine.’ He does not conceive the all, does not conceive in the all, does not conceive from the all, does not conceive, ‘The all is mine.’ Not conceiving thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. Not clinging, he is not agitated. Being unagitated, he personally attains Nibbāna. He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’ This, bhikkhus, is that practice suitable for uprooting all conceivings.” Eighth.

9. Paṭhamasamugghātasappāyasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on What Is Conducive to Uprooting
