Nisajja kho bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “kacci te, bhikkhu, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti no abhikkamanti, paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no abhikkamo”ti?

Then the Blessed One, having heard the words about the new and sick bhikkhu, and knowing, “This is an unknown bhikkhu,” approached that bhikkhu. That bhikkhu saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Seeing him, he made to rise from his cot. Then the Blessed One said to that bhikkhu: “Enough, bhikkhu, do not rise from your cot. These seats are prepared; I shall sit there.” The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said to that bhikkhu: “I hope you are enduring, bhikkhu, I hope you are managing. I hope your painful feelings are subsiding and not increasing, and that their subsiding is apparent and not their increasing.”

“Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ, bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti no paṭikkamanti, abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no paṭikkamo”ti.

“Venerable sir, I am not enduring, I am not managing. My strong painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding. Their increase is apparent, not their subsiding.”

“Kacci te, bhikkhu, na kiñci kukkuccaṃ, na koci vippaṭisāro”ti?

“I hope, bhikkhu, you have no worry, no remorse.”

“Taggha me, bhante, anappakaṃ [T 4.0057] kukkuccaṃ, anappako vippaṭisāro”ti.

“Indeed, venerable sir, my worry is not small, and my remorse is not small.”

“Kacci [P 4.0047] pana taṃ tvaṃ (sī.), te (syā. kaṃ. ka.), bhikkhu, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti?

“But, bhikkhu, does your self reproach you with regard to virtue?”

“Na kho maṃ, bhante, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti no hetaṃ bhante (pī. ka.).

“Venerable sir, my self does not reproach me with regard to virtue.”

“No ce kira te, bhikkhu, attā sīlato upavadati, atha kiñca atha kismiñca (sī.), atha bhikkhu kismiñca (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) te kukkuccaṃ ko ca vippaṭisāro”ti?

“If, bhikkhu, your self does not reproach you with regard to virtue, then what is your worry and what is your remorse?”

“Na khvāhaṃ[V 2.0051], bhante, sīlavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmī”ti[M 2.0273].

“Venerable sir, I do not understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One to be for the purpose of the purification of virtue.”

“No ce kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, sīlavisuddhatthaṃ mayā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi, atha kimatthaṃ carahi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsī”ti?

“If, bhikkhu, you do not understand the Dhamma taught by me to be for the purpose of the purification of virtue, then for what purpose do you understand the Dhamma taught by me?”

“Rāgavirāgatthaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“Venerable sir, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One to be for the purpose of the fading away of passion.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, rāgavirāgatthaṃ mayā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi. Rāgavirāgattho hi, bhikkhu, mayā dhammo desito. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi bhikkhu, cakkhu niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good, bhikkhu, that you understand the Dhamma taught by me to be for the purpose of the fading away of passion. For the fading away of passion, bhikkhu, the Dhamma has been taught by me. What do you think, bhikkhu, is the eye permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ…pe… sotaṃ… ghānaṃ… jivhā… kāyo… mano nicco vā anicco vā”ti?

“…the ear… the nose… the tongue… the body… the mind—is it permanent or impermanent?”

“Anicco, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Certainly not, venerable sir.”

“Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, sotasmimpi nibbindati…pe… manasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.

“Seeing thus, bhikkhu, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye, disenchanted with the ear… disenchanted with the mind. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When he is liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He knows distinctly: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’”

Idamavoca [T 4.0058] bhagavā. Attamano so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandi. Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne tassa bhikkhuno virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

The Blessed One said this. Delighted, that bhikkhu rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words. And while this exposition was being spoken, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in that bhikkhu: “Whatever has the nature to arise, all that has the nature to cease.”

2. Dutiyagilānasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on the Sick

75. Atha [V 2.0052] kho aññataro bhikkhu…pe… bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “amukasmiṃ, bhante, vihāre aññataro bhikkhu navo appaññāto ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā”ti.

75. Then a certain bhikkhu…pe… approached the Blessed One and said this: “Venerable sir, in such-and-such a monastery there is a certain bhikkhu who is new, unknown, afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would visit that bhikkhu out of compassion.”

Atha kho bhagavā navavādañca sutvā gilānavādañca, “appaññāto bhikkhū”ti iti viditvā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna mañcake samadhosi. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā tvaṃ mañcake samadhosi. Santimāni āsanāni paññattāni, tatthāhaṃ nisīdissāmī”ti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “kacci te, bhikkhu, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti no abhikkamanti, paṭikkamosānaṃ [M 2.0274] paññāyati no abhikkamo”ti?

Then the Blessed One, having heard the word about the new one and the word about the sick one, and knowing, “The bhikkhu is unknown,” approached that bhikkhu. That bhikkhu saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, he stirred on his couch. Then the Blessed One said this to that bhikkhu: “Enough, bhikkhu, do not stir on your couch. These seats are prepared; I will sit there.” The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to that bhikkhu: “Are you enduring, bhikkhu? Are you managing? Are your painful feelings subsiding and not increasing? Is their subsiding apparent, and not their increase?”

“Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ…pe… na kho maṃ me (sabbattha), bhante, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti.

“Venerable sir, it is not endurable for me, it is not manageable…pe… Venerable sir, my self does not reproach me with regard to virtue.”

“No ce kira te, bhikkhu, attā sīlato upavadati, atha kiñca te kukkuccaṃ ko ca vippaṭisāro”ti?

“If indeed, bhikkhu, your self does not reproach you with regard to virtue, then what is your worry, and what is your remorse?”

“Na khvāhaṃ, bhante, sīlavisuddhatthaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“Venerable sir, I do not understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One to be for the purpose of the purification of virtue.”

“No [P 4.0048] ce kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, sīlavisuddhatthaṃ mayā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi, atha [T 4.0059] kimatthaṃ carahi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mayā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsī”ti?

“If indeed, bhikkhu, you do not understand the Dhamma taught by me to be for the purpose of the purification of virtue, then for what purpose, bhikkhu, do you understand the Dhamma taught by me?”

“Anupādāparinibbānatthaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmī”ti.

“Venerable sir, I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One to be for the purpose of final Nibbāna without clinging.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, anupādāparinibbānatthaṃ mayā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi. Anupādāparinibbānattho hi, bhikkhu, mayā dhammo desito.

“Excellent, excellent, bhikkhu! It is indeed good, bhikkhu, that you understand the Dhamma taught by me to be for the purpose of final Nibbāna without clinging. For the Dhamma taught by me is indeed for the purpose of final Nibbāna without clinging.

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, bhikkhu, cakkhu niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“What do you think of this, bhikkhu: is the eye permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ[V 2.0053], bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ…pe… sotaṃ… ghānaṃ… jivhā… kāyo… mano… manoviññāṇaṃ… manosamphasso… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“…pe… the ear… the nose… the tongue… the body… the mind… mind-consciousness… mind-contact… and whatever feeling—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that arises conditioned by mind-contact, is that also permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“Now, that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“Now, that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Indeed, it is not, venerable sir.”

“Evaṃ passaṃ, bhikkhu, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati…pe… manasmimpi… manoviññāṇepi… manosamphassepi nibbindati. Yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.

“Seeing thus, bhikkhu, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye…pe… with the mind… with mind-consciousness… with mind-contact. He becomes disenchanted also with whatever feeling—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that arises conditioned by mind-contact. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When he is liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandi. Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne tassa bhikkhussa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccīti vimuccatīti (sabbattha). Dutiyaṃ.

The Blessed One said this. Delighted, that bhikkhu rejoiced in the Blessed One’s utterance. And while this exposition was being delivered, the mind of that bhikkhu was liberated from the taints through non-clinging.

3. Rādhaaniccasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse to Rādha on Impermanence

76. Atha [T 4.0060] kho āyasmā rādho…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu[M 2.0275], yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Yaṃ kho, rādha, aniccaṃ tatra te chando pahātabbo. Kiñca, rādha, aniccaṃ tatra te chando pahātabbo? Cakkhu aniccaṃ[V 2.0054], rūpā aniccā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ… cakkhusamphasso… yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi aniccaṃ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… jivhā… kāyo… mano anicco. Tatra te chando pahātabbo. Dhammā… manoviññāṇaṃ… manosamphasso… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi aniccaṃ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo. Yaṃ [P 4.0049] kho, rādha, aniccaṃ tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

76. Then the Venerable Rādha…pe… sat to one side and said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma briefly, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute.” “Rādha, whatever is impermanent, you should abandon desire for it. And what, Rādha, is impermanent, that you should abandon desire for? The eye is impermanent, forms are impermanent, eye-consciousness… eye-contact… whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is impermanent. You should abandon desire for it…pe… the tongue… the body… the mind is impermanent. You should abandon desire for it. Mental phenomena… mind-consciousness… mind-contact… whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is impermanent. You should abandon desire for it. Rādha, whatever is impermanent, you should abandon desire for it.”

4. Rādhadukkhasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse to Rādha on Suffering

77. “Yaṃ kho, rādha, dukkhaṃ tatra te chando pahātabbo. Kiñca, rādha, dukkhaṃ? Cakkhu kho, rādha, dukkhaṃ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo. Rūpā… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ… cakkhusamphasso… yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassa…pe… adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi dukkhaṃ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo…pe… mano dukkho… dhammā… manoviññāṇaṃ… manosamphasso… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ [T 4.0061] sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi dukkhaṃ. Tatra te chando pahātabbo. Yaṃ kho, rādha, dukkhaṃ tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

77. “Rādha, whatever is suffering, there your desire should be abandoned. And what, Rādha, is suffering? The eye, Rādha, is suffering. There your desire should be abandoned. Forms… eye-consciousness… eye-contact… whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—be it pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is suffering. There your desire should be abandoned… The mind is suffering… mental phenomena… mind-consciousness… mind-contact… whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—be it pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is suffering. There your desire should be abandoned. Rādha, whatever is suffering, there your desire should be abandoned.” The fourth.

5. Rādhaanattasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse to Rādha on Not-self

78. “Yo kho, rādha, anattā tatra te chando pahātabbo. Ko ca, rādha, anattā? Cakkhu kho, rādha, anattā. Tatra te chando pahātabbo. Rūpā… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ… cakkhusamphasso… yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā…pe… mano anattā… dhammā… manoviññāṇaṃ… manosamphasso… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi anattā. Tatra te chando pahātabbo. Yo kho, rādha, anattā tatra te chando pahātabbo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

78. “Rādha, whatever is not-self, you should abandon desire for it. And what, Rādha, is not-self? The eye, Rādha, is not-self. You should abandon desire for it. Forms… eye-consciousness… eye-contact… whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is not-self. You should abandon desire for it. … The mind is not-self… mental phenomena… mind-consciousness… mind-contact… whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is not-self. You should abandon desire for it. Rādha, whatever is not-self, you should abandon desire for it.” The fifth.

6. Paṭhamaavijjāpahānasuttaṃ

6. The First Discourse on the Abandonment of Ignorance

79. Atha [M 2.0276][V 2.0055] kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “atthi nu kho, bhante, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?

79. Then a certain monk approached the Blessed One… Having sat down to one side, that monk said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, is there one thing, by the abandoning of which ignorance is abandoned in a monk and true knowledge arises?”

“Atthi kho, bhikkhu, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.

“Monk, there is one thing, by the abandoning of which ignorance is abandoned in a monk and true knowledge arises.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?

“But, venerable sir, what is that one thing, by the abandoning of which ignorance is abandoned in a monk and true knowledge arises?”

“Avijjā [P 4.0050] kho, bhikkhu, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.

“Monk, ignorance is that one thing, by the abandoning of which ignorance is abandoned in a monk and true knowledge arises.”

“Kathaṃ pana, bhante, jānato, kathaṃ passato bhikkhuno avijjā [T 4.0062] pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?

“But, venerable sir, for a monk knowing in what way, seeing in what way, is ignorance abandoned and does true knowledge arise?”

“Cakkhuṃ kho, bhikkhu, aniccato jānato passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati. Rūpe… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ… cakkhusamphassaṃ… yampidaṃ, cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi aniccato jānato passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati…pe… manaṃ aniccato jānato passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati. Dhamme… manoviññāṇaṃ… manosamphassaṃ… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi aniccato jānato passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, jānato evaṃ passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Monk, for a monk knowing and seeing the eye as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Forms… eye-consciousness… eye-contact… and whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—for a monk knowing and seeing that too as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises… The mind… for a monk knowing and seeing it as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Mental phenomena… mind-consciousness… mind-contact… and whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—for a monk knowing and seeing that too as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Thus, monk, for a monk knowing in this way and seeing in this way, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises.” The sixth.

7. Dutiyaavijjāpahānasuttaṃ

7. The Second Discourse on the Abandonment of Ignorance

80. Atha [V 2.0056] kho aññataro bhikkhu…pe… etadavoca – “atthi nu kho, bhante, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?

80. Then a certain monk… said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, is there one thing, by the abandoning of which ignorance is abandoned in a monk and true knowledge arises?”

“Atthi kho, bhikkhu, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.

“Monk, there is one thing, by the abandoning of which ignorance is abandoned in a monk and true knowledge arises.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?

“But, venerable sir, what is that one thing, by the abandoning of which ignorance is abandoned in a monk and true knowledge arises?”

“Avijjā kho, bhikkhu, eko dhammo yassa pahānā bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti.

“Ignorance, monk, is that one thing, by the abandoning of which ignorance is abandoned in a monk and true knowledge arises.”

“Kathaṃ pana, bhante, jānato, kathaṃ passato avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti?

“But, venerable sir, for a monk knowing in what way, seeing in what way, is ignorance abandoned and does true knowledge arise?”

“Idha, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti – ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. Evañcetaṃ, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti – ‘sabbe dhammā [M 2.0277] nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. So sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhiññāya sabbaṃ dhammaṃ parijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ pariññāya sabbanimittāni aññato passati, cakkhuṃ aññato passati[T 4.0063], rūpe… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ… cakkhusamphassaṃ… yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi aññato passati…pe… manaṃ aññato passati, dhamme… manoviññāṇaṃ… manosamphassaṃ… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi aññato passati. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, jānato evaṃ passato bhikkhuno avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjatī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Here, monk, a monk has heard: ‘All phenomena are not to be clung to.’ And when a monk has heard this, monk—that ‘All phenomena are not to be clung to’—he directly knows every phenomenon. Having directly known every phenomenon, he fully comprehends every phenomenon. Having fully comprehended every phenomenon, he sees all signs as other. He sees the eye as other, forms… eye-consciousness… eye-contact… and whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too he sees as other… He sees the mind as other, mental phenomena… mind-consciousness… mind-contact… and whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too he sees as other. Thus, monk, for a monk knowing in this way and seeing in this way, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises.” The seventh.

8. Sambahulabhikkhusuttaṃ

8. The Discourse to Many Monks

81. Atha [V 2.0057] kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ [P 4.0051] – “idha no, bhante, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā amhe evaṃ pucchanti – ‘kimatthiyaṃ, āvuso, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhā mayaṃ, bhante, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākaroma – ‘dukkhassa kho, āvuso, pariññatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti. Kacci mayaṃ, bhante, evaṃ puṭṭhā evaṃ byākaramānā vuttavādino ceva bhagavato homa, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhāma, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaroma, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī”ti?

81. Then many monks approached the Blessed One… and sat down to one side. Seated there, those monks said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, here wanderers of other sects ask us: ‘For what purpose, friends, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?’ When asked thus, venerable sir, we answer those wanderers of other sects: ‘Friends, it is for the full understanding of suffering that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’ When we answer thus, venerable sir, are we stating what has been said by the Blessed One, and not misrepresenting the Blessed One with what is untrue? Do we explain in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no legitimate, consequential statement gives grounds for censure?”

“Taggha tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ puṭṭhā evaṃ byākaramānā vuttavādino ceva me hotha, na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhatha, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākarotha, na ca [T 4.0064] koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati. Dukkhassa hi, bhikkhave, pariññatthaṃ mayi brahmacariyaṃ vussati. Sace pana vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘katamaṃ pana taṃ, āvuso, dukkhaṃ, yassa pariññāya samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘cakkhu kho, āvuso, dukkhaṃ, tassa pariññāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussati. Rūpā…pe… yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi dukkhaṃ. Tassa pariññāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussati…pe… mano dukkho…pe… yampidaṃ [M 2.0278] manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi dukkhaṃ. Tassa pariññāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussati. Idaṃ kho taṃ, āvuso, dukkhaṃ, tassa pariññāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti. Evaṃ [P 4.0052] puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyāthā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Indeed, monks, when you are asked thus and answer thus, you are stating what has been said by me, and not misrepresenting me with what is untrue. You explain in accordance with the Dhamma, and no legitimate, consequential statement gives grounds for censure. For, monks, it is for the full understanding of suffering that the holy life is lived under me. But if, monks, wanderers of other sects should ask you: ‘And what, friends, is that suffering for the full understanding of which the holy life is lived under the ascetic Gotama?’—being asked thus, monks, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: ‘The eye, friends, is suffering; it is for the full understanding of this that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One. Forms… Whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is suffering. It is for the full understanding of this that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One… The mind is suffering… Whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is suffering. It is for the full understanding of this that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One. This, friends, is that suffering for the full understanding of which the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’ Being asked thus, monks, you should answer those wanderers of other sects in this way.”

9. Lokapañhāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Question about the World

82. Atha [V 2.0058] kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

82. Then a certain monk approached the Blessed One… and sat down to one side. Seated there, that monk said to the Blessed One:

“‘Loko, loko’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, lokoti vuccatī”ti? “‘Lujjatī’ti kho, bhikkhu, tasmā lokoti vuccati. Kiñca lujjati? Cakkhu kho, bhikkhu, lujjati. Rūpā lujjanti, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ lujjati, cakkhusamphasso lujjati[T 4.0065], yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi lujjati…pe… jivhā lujjati…pe… mano lujjati, dhammā lujjanti, manoviññāṇaṃ lujjati, manosamphasso lujjati, yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi lujjati. Lujjatīti kho, bhikkhu, tasmā lokoti vuccatī”ti. Navamaṃ.

“‘The world, the world,’ venerable sir, it is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is it called ‘the world’?” “It perishes, monk, therefore it is called ‘the world.’ And what perishes? The eye, monk, perishes. Forms perish, eye-consciousness perishes, eye-contact perishes, and whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too perishes… The tongue perishes… The mind perishes, mental objects perish, mind-consciousness perishes, mind-contact perishes, and whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too perishes. It perishes, monk, therefore it is called ‘the world.’”

10. Phaggunapañhāsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Phagguna's Question

83. Atha kho āyasmā phagguno…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā phagguno bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

83. Then the Venerable Phagguna approached the Blessed One... and sat down to one side. Seated there, the Venerable Phagguna said this to the Blessed One:

“Atthi nu kho, bhante, taṃ cakkhu, yena cakkhunā atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya…pe… atthi nu kho, bhante, sā jivhā, yāya jivhāya atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya…pe… atthi nu kho so, bhante, mano, yena manena atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyyā”ti?

“Venerable sir, is there that eye by which one could make known the Buddhas of the past who have attained final Nibbāna, who have cut off mental proliferation, severed the round of kamma, whose round of suffering is exhausted, and have transcended all suffering? ... Is there, venerable sir, that tongue...? ... Is there, venerable sir, that mind...?”

“Natthi kho taṃ, phagguna, cakkhu, yena cakkhunā atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya [M 2.0279] …pe… natthi kho sā[V 2.0059], phagguna, jivhā, yāya jivhāya atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno [T 4.0066] paññāpeyya…pe… natthi [P 4.0053] kho so, phagguna, mano, yena manena atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivaṭṭe paññāpayamāno paññāpeyyā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“There is no such eye, Phagguna, by which one could make known the Buddhas of the past who have attained final Nibbāna, who have cut off mental proliferation, severed the round of kamma, whose round of suffering is exhausted, and have transcended all suffering. ... There is no such tongue, Phagguna... ... There is no such mind, Phagguna...”

Gilānavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Chapter on the Sick, the Eighth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Gilānena duve vuttā, rādhena apare tayo;

Avijjāya ca dve vuttā, bhikkhu loko ca phaggunoti.

Two suttas were spoken concerning the sick, and three others concerning Rādhā; two were also spoken on ignorance, and also the suttas on the Bhikkhu, the World, and Phagguna.

9. Channavaggo

9. The Chapter on Channa

1. Palokadhammasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on What Is Subject to Dissolution

84. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha [T 4.0067] kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

84. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One... and sat down to one side. Seated there, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:

“‘Loko, loko’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, lokoti vuccatī”ti? “Yaṃ kho, ānanda, palokadhammaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati ariyassa vinaye loko. Kiñca, ānanda, palokadhammaṃ? Cakkhu kho, ānanda, palokadhammaṃ, rūpā palokadhammā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ palokadhammaṃ, cakkhusamphasso palokadhammo, yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā…pe… tampi palokadhammaṃ…pe… jivhā palokadhammā, rasā palokadhammā, jivhāviññāṇaṃ palokadhammaṃ, jivhāsamphasso palokadhammo, yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā…pe… tampi palokadhammaṃ…pe… [V 2.0060] mano palokadhammo, dhammā palokadhammā, manoviññāṇaṃ palokadhammaṃ, manosamphasso palokadhammo, yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi palokadhammaṃ. Yaṃ kho, ānanda, palokadhammaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati ariyassa vinaye loko”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“‘The world, the world,’ it is said, venerable sir. To what extent, venerable sir, is it called ‘the world’?” “That which is subject to dissolution, Ānanda, is called ‘the world’ in the Noble One’s Discipline. And what, Ānanda, is subject to dissolution? The eye, Ānanda, is subject to dissolution; forms are subject to dissolution; eye-consciousness is subject to dissolution; eye-contact is subject to dissolution; and whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact… that too is subject to dissolution.… The tongue is subject to dissolution; flavors are subject to dissolution; tongue-consciousness is subject to dissolution; tongue-contact is subject to dissolution; and whatever feeling arises dependent on tongue-contact… that too is subject to dissolution.… The mind is subject to dissolution; mental objects are subject to dissolution; mind-consciousness is subject to dissolution; mind-contact is subject to dissolution; and whatever feeling—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—arises dependent on mind-contact, that too is subject to dissolution. That which is subject to dissolution, Ānanda, is called ‘the world’ in the Noble One’s Discipline.”

2. Suññatalokasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Empty World

85. Atha [M 2.0280][P 4.0054] kho āyasmā ānando…pe… bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘suñño loko, suñño loko’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, suñño lokoti vuccatī”ti? “Yasmā ca kho, ānanda, suññaṃ [T 4.0068] attena vā attaniyena vā tasmā suñño lokoti vuccati. Kiñca, ānanda, suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā? Cakkhu kho, ānanda, suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā. Rūpā suññā attena vā attaniyena vā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā, cakkhusamphasso suñño attena vā attaniyena vā…pe… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā. Yasmā ca kho, ānanda, suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā, tasmā suñño lokoti vuccatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

85. Then the Venerable Ānanda… addressed the Blessed One, saying: “‘Empty is the world, empty is the world,’ it is said, venerable sir. To what extent, venerable sir, is the world said to be empty?” “Because, Ānanda, it is empty of self or of what belongs to self, therefore it is said, ‘The world is empty.’ And what, Ānanda, is empty of self or of what belongs to self? The eye, Ānanda, is empty of self or of what belongs to self. Forms are empty of self or of what belongs to self. Eye-consciousness is empty of self or of what belongs to self. Eye-contact is empty of self or of what belongs to self.… Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is empty of self or of what belongs to self. Because, Ānanda, it is empty of self or of what belongs to self, therefore it is said, ‘The world is empty.’” The Second.

3. Saṃkhittadhammasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Dhamma in Brief

86. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti.

86. Having sat down to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute.’

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, ānanda, cakkhu niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“What do you think, Ānanda, is the eye permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“But that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ[V 2.0061], bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“But that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Surely not, venerable sir.”

“Rūpā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti?

“Are forms permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccā, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”…

“Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ [P 4.0055] vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“Eye-consciousness… and whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—is that too permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ [T 4.0069] vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“But that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso [M 2.0281] me attā’”ti?

“But that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”…pe….

“Surely not, venerable sir.”…

“Jivhā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti?

“Is the tongue permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccā, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”…

“Jivhāviññāṇaṃ… jivhāsamphasso…pe… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“Tongue-consciousness… tongue-contact… and whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—is that too permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ [V 2.0062] panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“But that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“But that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”…pe….

“Surely not, venerable sir.”…

“Evaṃ passaṃ, ānanda, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati…pe… cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati…pe… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Seeing thus, Ānanda, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye… becomes disenchanted with eye-contact… becomes disenchanted with whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant. Being disenchanted, one becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, one is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘Liberated!’ One understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’” The Third.

4. Channasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse to Channa

87. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahācundo āyasmā ca channo gijjhakūṭe pabbate viharanti. Tena kho pana samayena yena āyasmā channo ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno[T 4.0070]. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā [P 4.0056] vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahācundo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahācundaṃ etadavoca – “āyāmāvuso cunda, yenāyasmā channo tenupasaṅkamissāma gilānapucchakā”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā mahācundo āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosi.

87. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Veḷuvana, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Now at that time, the Venerable Sāriputta, the Venerable Mahācunda, and the Venerable Channa were dwelling on the mountain Gijjhakūṭa. At that time, the Venerable Channa was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta arose from solitary abiding and approached the Venerable Mahācunda. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable Mahācunda: “Come, friend Cunda, let us go to the Venerable Channa to inquire about his illness.” “So be it, friend,” the Venerable Mahācunda replied in assent to the Venerable Sāriputta.

Atha kho āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahācundo yenāyasmā channo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṃsu. Nisajja kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ channaṃ etadavoca – “kacci te, āvuso channa, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti no abhikkamanti, paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no abhikkamo”ti?

Then the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahācunda approached the Venerable Channa; having approached, they sat down on a seat that had been prepared. Having sat down, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Venerable Channa: 'Friend Channa, are you enduring? Are you managing? Are your painful feelings receding and not increasing? Is their subsiding apparent, and not their increasing?'

“Na [V 2.0063] me, āvuso sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ, bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti no paṭikkamanti, abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena khaggena (ka.) muddhani muddhānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) abhimattheyya abhimantheyya (sī.); evameva kho, āvuso, adhimattā vātā muddhani muddhānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ūhananti upahananti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), uhananti (ka.). Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ…pe… no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi[M 2.0282], āvuso, balavā puriso daḷhena varattakkhaṇḍena sīse sīsaveṭhaṃ dadeyya; evameva kho, āvuso, adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā. Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṃ[T 4.0071], na yāpanīyaṃ…pe… no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā tiṇhena govikantanena kucchiṃ parikanteyya; evameva kho adhimattā vātā kucchiṃ parikantanti. Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ…pe… no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, dve balavanto purisā dubbalataraṃ purisaṃ nānābāhāsu gahetvā aṅgārakāsuyā santāpeyyuṃ [P 4.0057] samparitāpeyyuṃ; evameva kho, āvuso, adhimatto kāyasmiṃ ḍāho. Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ, bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti no paṭikkamanti, abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati no paṭikkamo. Satthaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, āharissāmi, nāvakaṅkhāmi nāpi kaṅkhāmi (ka.) jīvita”nti.

“Friend Sāriputta, I am not enduring, I am not managing. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not receding; their increase is apparent, not their receding. Friend, just as if a strong man were to cleave the head with a sharp sword, even so, exceedingly severe winds pierce my head. I am not enduring, I am not managing... their receding is not apparent. Friend, just as if a strong man were to apply a headband with a stout leather strap, even so, there are exceedingly severe headaches in my head. I am not enduring, I am not managing... their receding is not apparent. Friend, just as if a skilled butcher or a butcher's apprentice were to carve the belly with a sharp butcher's knife, even so, exceedingly severe winds carve my belly. I am not enduring, I am not managing... their receding is not apparent. Friend, just as if two strong men, having seized a weaker man by the arms, were to heat and scorch him over a pit of embers, even so, there is an exceedingly severe burning in my body. I am not enduring, I am not managing. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not receding; their increase is apparent, not their receding. Friend Sāriputta, I shall take up the knife; I have no desire for this life.”

“Mā āyasmā channo satthaṃ āharesi. Yāpetāyasmā channo, yāpentaṃ mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ channaṃ icchāma. Sace āyasmato channassa natthi sappāyāni bhojanāni, ahaṃ āyasmato channassa sappāyāni bhojanāni pariyesissāmi. Sace āyasmato channassa natthi sappāyāni bhesajjāni, ahaṃ āyasmato channassa sappāyāni bhesajjāni pariyesissāmi. Sace āyasmato channassa natthi patirūpā upaṭṭhākā, ahaṃ āyasmantaṃ channaṃ upaṭṭhahissāmi. Mā āyasmā channo satthaṃ āharesi. Yāpetāyasmā channo, yāpentaṃ mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ channaṃ icchāmā”ti.

“Let the Venerable Channa not take up the knife. Let the Venerable Channa live on; we wish for the Venerable Channa to live on. If the Venerable Channa has no suitable foods, I will search for suitable foods for the Venerable Channa. If the Venerable Channa has no suitable medicines, I will search for suitable medicines for the Venerable Channa. If the Venerable Channa has no suitable attendants, I will attend upon the Venerable Channa. Let the Venerable Channa not take up the knife. Let the Venerable Channa live on; we wish for the Venerable Channa to live on.”

“Na me, āvuso sāriputta, natthi sappāyāni bhojanāni; atthi me sappāyāni [T 4.0072] bhojanāni. Napi me natthi sappāyāni bhesajjāni; atthi me sappāyāni bhesajjāni. Napi me natthi patirūpā upaṭṭhākā; atthi me patirūpā upaṭṭhākā. Api ca me, āvuso, satthā pariciṇṇo dīgharattaṃ manāpeneva, no amanāpena. Etañhi, āvuso, sāvakassa patirūpaṃ yaṃ satthāraṃ [V 2.0064] paricareyya manāpeneva, no amanāpena. ‘Anupavajjaṃ taṃ anupavajjaṃ (bahūsu) channo bhikkhu satthaṃ āharissatī’ti – evametaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, dhārehī”ti.

“Friend Sāriputta, it is not that I have no suitable foods; I do have suitable foods. It is not that I have no suitable medicines; I do have suitable medicines. It is not that I have no suitable attendants; I do have suitable attendants. Moreover, Friend, the Teacher has been served by me for a long time with what is pleasing, not with what is displeasing. For this, Friend, is fitting for a disciple: that he should serve the Teacher with what is pleasing, not with what is displeasing. ‘The monk Channa will take up the knife blamelessly’—thus, Friend Sāriputta, should you bear this in mind.”

“Puccheyyāma [M 2.0283] mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ channaṃ kañcideva kiñcideva (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) desaṃ, sace āyasmā channo okāsaṃ karoti pañhassa veyyākaraṇāyā”ti. “Pucchāvuso [P 4.0058] sāriputta, sutvā vedissāmā”ti.

“We would ask the Venerable Channa a certain question, if the Venerable Channa would grant an opportunity for the answering of a question.” “Ask, Friend Sāriputta; having heard, we shall know.”

“Cakkhuṃ, āvuso channa, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasi…pe… jivhaṃ, āvuso channa, jivhāviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasi…pe… manaṃ, āvuso channa, manoviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassasī”ti?

“Friend Channa, do you regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’? … Do you regard the tongue, tongue-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by tongue-consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’? … Do you regard the mind, mind-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“Cakkhuṃ, āvuso sāriputta, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmi…pe… jivhaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, jivhāviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ [T 4.0073] mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmi…pe… manaṃ, āvuso sāriputta, manoviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmī”ti.

“Friend Sāriputta, I regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ … I regard the tongue, tongue-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by tongue-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ … I regard the mind, mind-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

“Cakkhusmiṃ, āvuso channa, cakkhuviññāṇe cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu kiṃ disvā kiṃ abhiññāya cakkhuṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassasi… jivhāya, āvuso channa, jivhāviññāṇe jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu kiṃ disvā kiṃ abhiññāya jivhaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassasi… manasmiṃ, āvuso channa, manoviññāṇe manoviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu kiṃ disvā kiṃ abhiññāya manaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassasī”ti?

“Friend Channa, in the eye, in eye-consciousness, and in phenomena cognizable by eye-consciousness, seeing what, directly knowing what, do you regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’? … In the tongue, Friend Channa, in tongue-consciousness, and in phenomena cognizable by tongue-consciousness, seeing what, directly knowing what, do you regard the tongue, tongue-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by tongue-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’? … In the mind, Friend Channa, in mind-consciousness, and in phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness, seeing what, directly knowing what, do you regard the mind, mind-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’?”

“Cakkhusmiṃ[V 2.0065], āvuso sāriputta, cakkhuviññāṇe cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu nirodhaṃ disvā nirodhaṃ abhiññāya cakkhuṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti [M 2.0284] samanupassāmi…pe… jivhāya, āvuso sāriputta, jivhāviññāṇe jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu nirodhaṃ disvā nirodhaṃ abhiññāya jivhaṃ jivhāviññāṇaṃ jivhāviññāṇaviññātabbe [P 4.0059] dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti [T 4.0074] samanupassāmi…pe… manasmiṃ, āvuso sāriputta, manoviññāṇe manoviññāṇaviññātabbesu dhammesu nirodhaṃ disvā nirodhaṃ abhiññāya manaṃ manoviññāṇaṃ manoviññāṇaviññātabbe dhamme ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassāmī”ti.

“Friend Sāriputta, in the eye, in eye-consciousness, and in phenomena cognizable by eye-consciousness, seeing cessation, directly knowing cessation, I regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ … In the tongue, friend Sāriputta, in tongue-consciousness, and in phenomena cognizable by tongue-consciousness, seeing cessation, directly knowing cessation, I regard the tongue, tongue-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by tongue-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ … In the mind, friend Sāriputta, in mind-consciousness, and in phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness, seeing cessation, directly knowing cessation, I regard the mind, mind-consciousness, and phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā mahācundo āyasmantaṃ channaṃ etadavoca – “tasmātiha, āvuso channa, idampi tassa bhagavato sāsanaṃ niccakappaṃ sādhukaṃ manasi kātabbaṃ – ‘nissitassa calitaṃ, anissitassa calitaṃ natthi. Calite asati passaddhi hoti. Passaddhiyā sati nati na hoti. Natiyā asati āgatigati na hoti. Āgatigatiyā asati cutūpapāto na hoti. Cutūpapāte asati nevidha na huraṃ na ubhayamantarena. Esevanto dukkhassā’”ti.

When this was said, the Venerable Mahācunda said this to the Venerable Channa: “Therefore, friend Channa, this instruction of the Blessed One should be constantly and carefully borne in mind here: ‘For one who is dependent, there is agitation; for one who is independent, there is no agitation. When there is no agitation, there is tranquility. When there is tranquility, there is no inclination. When there is no inclination, there is no coming and going. When there is no coming and going, there is no passing away and reappearing. When there is no passing away and reappearing, there is neither here, nor hereafter, nor in between the two. This itself is the end of suffering.’”

Atha kho āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahācundo āyasmantaṃ channaṃ iminā ovādena ovaditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā channo acirapakkantesu tesu āyasmantesu satthaṃ āharesi.

Then the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahācunda, having instructed the Venerable Channa with this admonition, rose from their seats and departed. Then, not long after those venerable ones had departed, the Venerable Channa took up a knife.

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “āyasmatā, bhante, channena satthaṃ āharitaṃ. Tassa kā gati ko abhisamparāyo”ti? “Nanu te, sāriputta, channena bhikkhunā sammukhāyeva anupavajjatā byākatā”ti[T 4.0075]? “Atthi, bhante, pubbavijjanaṃ pubbaviciraṃ (sī.), pubbavijjhanaṃ (pī.), pubbajiraṃ (ma. ni. 3.394 nāma vajjigāmo. Tatthāyasmato channassa mittakulāni suhajjakulāni upavajjakulānī”ti. “Honti hete, sāriputta, channassa bhikkhuno mittakulāni suhajjakulāni upavajjakulāni. Na kho panāhaṃ, sāriputta[P 4.0060], ettāvatā saupavajjoti vadāmi. Yo kho, sāriputta, tañca kāyaṃ nikkhipati, aññañca kāyaṃ [V 2.0066] upādiyati, tamahaṃ saupavajjoti vadāmi. Taṃ channassa bhikkhuno natthi. ‘Anupavajjaṃ channena bhikkhunā satthaṃ āharita’nti – evametaṃ, sāriputta, dhārehī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, and having approached, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the Venerable Channa has taken up a knife. What is his destination? What is his future course?” “Sāriputta, was it not declared by the monk Channa in your presence that he is without a basis for rebirth?” “Venerable sir, there is a Vajjian village named Pubbavijjana. There the Venerable Channa has friendly families, cordial families, and families that may be visited.” “Sāriputta, the monk Channa does indeed have these friendly families, cordial families, and families that may be visited. However, Sāriputta, I do not say that one has a basis for rebirth to that extent. Sāriputta, whoever lays down this body and grasps another body, him I call one with a basis for rebirth. That does not exist for the monk Channa. The monk Channa, being without a basis for rebirth, took up the knife. Thus, Sāriputta, should you remember this.”

5. Puṇṇasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse to Puṇṇa

88. Atha [M 2.0285] sāvatthinidānaṃ. atha (?) ma. ni. 3.395 passitabbaṃ kho āyasmā puṇṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā puṇṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti.

88. Then the Venerable Puṇṇa approached the Blessed One; having approached, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Puṇṇa said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute.”

“Santi kho, puṇṇa, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī. ‘Nandisamudayā dukkhasamudayo, puṇṇā’ti vadāmi…pe… santi kho, puṇṇa, jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… santi kho, puṇṇa, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce [T 4.0076] bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī. ‘Nandisamudayā dukkhasamudayo, puṇṇā’ti vadāmi.

“Puṇṇa, there are forms cognizable by eye-consciousness that are desirable, agreeable, pleasing, lovely, connected with sensual pleasure, and enticing. If a bhikkhu delights in them, welcomes them, and remains attached to them, delight arises in him. ‘From the arising of delight, Puṇṇa, comes the arising of suffering,’ I say… There are tastes cognizable by the tongue… There are mental objects cognizable by the mind that are desirable, agreeable, pleasing, lovely, connected with sensual pleasure, and enticing. If a bhikkhu delights in them, welcomes them, and remains attached to them, delight arises in him. ‘From the arising of delight, Puṇṇa, comes the arising of suffering,’ I say.”

“Santi kho, puṇṇa, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, tassa taṃ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato nirujjhati nandī. ‘Nandinirodhā dukkhanirodho, puṇṇā’ti vadāmi…pe… santi kho, puṇṇa, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu [P 4.0061] nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, tassa taṃ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato nirujjhati nandī. ‘Nandinirodhā dukkhanirodho, puṇṇā’ti vadāmi.

“Puṇṇa, there are forms cognizable by eye-consciousness that are desirable, agreeable, pleasing, lovely, connected with sensual pleasure, and enticing. If a bhikkhu does not delight in them, does not welcome them, and does not remain attached to them, then for him who does not delight in, welcome, or remain attached to them, delight ceases. ‘From the cessation of delight, Puṇṇa, comes the cessation of suffering,’ I say… There are mental objects cognizable by the mind that are desirable, agreeable, pleasing, lovely, connected with sensual pleasure, and enticing. If a bhikkhu does not delight in them, does not welcome them, and does not remain attached to them, then for him who does not delight in, welcome, or remain attached to them, delight ceases. ‘From the cessation of delight, Puṇṇa, comes the cessation of suffering,’ I say.”

“Iminā [V 2.0067] tvaṃ iminā ca tvaṃ, puṇṇa, mayā saṃkhittena ovādena ovadito katamasmiṃ katarasmiṃ (ma. ni. 3.395) janapade viharissasī”ti? “Atthi, bhante, sunāparanto nāma janapado, tatthāhaṃ viharissāmī”ti.

“Puṇṇa, having been instructed by me with this brief instruction, in which country will you dwell?” “Venerable sir, there is a country named Sunāparanta. I will dwell there.”

“Caṇḍā [T 4.0077] kho, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā; pharusā kho, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā. Sace taṃ, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā akkosissanti paribhāsissanti, tatra te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?

“Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta are fierce; Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta are harsh. If, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta were to abuse and revile you, how would it be for you then?”

“Sace maṃ, bhante, sunāparantakā [M 2.0286] manussā akkosissanti paribhāsissanti, tatra me evaṃ bhavissati – ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṃ me maṃ (sabbattha) nayime pāṇinā pahāraṃ dentī’ti. Evamettha evammettha (?), bhagavā, bhavissati; evamettha, sugata, bhavissatī”ti.

“If, venerable sir, the people of Sunāparanta were to abuse and revile me, then it would occur to me: ‘Truly, these people of Sunāparanta are good, truly, these people of Sunāparanta are very good, in that they do not strike me with their hands.’ That is how it would be for me then, Blessed One; that is how it would be for me then, Sugata.”

“Sace pana te, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā pāṇinā pahāraṃ dassanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?

“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta were to strike you with their hands, what would you think then?”

“Sace me, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā pāṇinā pahāraṃ [T 4.0078] dassanti, tatra me evaṃ bhavissati – ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṃ me evammettha (?) nayime leḍḍunā pahāraṃ dentī’ti. Evamettha, bhagavā, bhavissati; evamettha, sugata, bhavissatī”ti.

“If, venerable sir, the people of Sunāparanta were to strike me with their hands, then it would occur to me: ‘Truly, these people of Sunāparanta are good, truly, these people of Sunāparanta are very good, in that they do not strike me with a clod.’ That is how it would be for me then, Blessed One; that is how it would be for me then, Sugata.”

“Sace pana te, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā leḍḍunā pahāraṃ dassanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?

“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta were to strike you with a clod, what would you think then?”

“Sace me, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā leḍḍunā pahāraṃ dassanti, tatra me evaṃ bhavissati – ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṃ me nayime daṇḍena pahāraṃ dentī’ti[P 4.0062]. Evamettha, bhagavā, bhavissati; evamettha, sugata, bhavissatī”ti.

“If, venerable sir, the people of Sunāparanta were to strike me with a clod, then it would occur to me: ‘Truly, these people of Sunāparanta are good, truly, these people of Sunāparanta are very good, in that they do not strike me with a stick.’ That is how it would be for me then, Blessed One; that is how it would be for me then, Sugata.”

“Sace [V 2.0068] pana puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā daṇḍena pahāraṃ dassanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?

“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta were to strike you with a stick, what would you think then?”

“Sace me, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā daṇḍena pahāraṃ dassanti, tatra me evaṃ bhavissati – ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṃ me nayime satthena pahāraṃ dentī’ti. Evamettha, bhagavā, bhavissati; evamettha, sugata, bhavissatī”ti.

“If, venerable sir, the people of Sunāparanta were to strike me with a stick, then it would occur to me: ‘Truly, these people of Sunāparanta are good, truly, these people of Sunāparanta are very good, in that they do not strike me with a weapon.’ That is how it would be for me then, Blessed One; that is how it would be for me then, Sugata.”

“Sace pana te, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā satthena pahāraṃ dassanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?

“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta were to strike you with a weapon, what would you think then?”

“Sace me, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā satthena pahāraṃ dassanti, tatra me evaṃ bhavissati – ‘bhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, subhaddakā vatime sunāparantakā manussā, yaṃ maṃ nayime [T 4.0079] tiṇhena satthena jīvitā voropentī’ti. Evamettha, bhagavā, bhavissati; evamettha, sugata, bhavissatī”ti.

“If, venerable sir, the people of Sunāparanta were to strike me with a weapon, then it would occur to me: ‘Truly, these people of Sunāparanta are good, truly, these people of Sunāparanta are very good, in that they do not deprive me of life with a sharp weapon.’ That is how it would be for me then, Blessed One; that is how it would be for me then, Sugata.”

“Sace [M 2.0287] pana taṃ, puṇṇa, sunāparantakā manussā tiṇhena satthena jīvitā voropessanti, tatra pana te, puṇṇa, kinti bhavissatī”ti?

“But if, Puṇṇa, the people of Sunāparanta were to deprive you of life with a sharp weapon, what would you think then?”

“Sace maṃ, bhante, sunāparantakā manussā tiṇhena satthena jīvitā voropessanti, tatra me evaṃ bhavissati – ‘santi kho tassa bhagavato sāvakā kāyena ca jīvitena ca aṭṭīyamānā harāyamānā jigucchamānā satthahārakaṃ pariyesanti, taṃ me idaṃ apariyiṭṭhaññeva satthahārakaṃ laddha’nti. Evamettha, bhagavā, bhavissati; evamettha, sugata, bhavissatī”ti.

“Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta were to deprive me of life with a sharp weapon, this thought would occur to me: ‘There are disciples of the Blessed One who, being weary of, ashamed of, and disgusted with the body and with life, seek a life-taking weapon. I have obtained this life-taking weapon without having sought it.’ Thus it will be for me in this matter, Blessed One; thus it will be for me in this matter, Sugata.”

“Sādhu sādhu, puṇṇa! Sakkhissasi kho tvaṃ, puṇṇa, iminā damūpasamena samannāgato sunāparantasmiṃ janapade vatthuṃ. Yassa dāni tvaṃ, puṇṇa, kālaṃ maññasī”ti.

“Good, good, Puṇṇa! Being endowed with this self-control and calm, you will be able, Puṇṇa, to dwell in the Sunāparanta country. Now, Puṇṇa, you may do that for which you deem it is time.”

Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇo bhagavato vacanaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ [V 2.0069] abhivādetvā [P 4.0063] padakkhiṇaṃ katvā senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sunāparanto janapado tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sunāparanto janapado tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ āyasmā puṇṇo sunāparantasmiṃ janapade viharati. Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇo tenevantaravassena pañcamattāni upāsakasatāni paṭivedesi paṭipādesi (sī. pī.), paṭidesesi (syā. kaṃ.). Tenevantaravassena pañcamattāni upāsikāsatāni paṭivedesi. Tenevantaravassena tisso vijjā [T 4.0080] sacchākāsi. Tenevantaravassena parinibbāyi.

Then the Venerable Puṇṇa, having delighted in and rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, set his lodging in order, took his bowl and robe, and set out on a journey to the Sunāparanta country. Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at the Sunāparanta country. There the Venerable Puṇṇa dwelled in the Sunāparanta country. And the Venerable Puṇṇa, within that same rains-retreat, caused five hundred male lay followers to understand the truth. Within that same rains-retreat, he caused five hundred female lay followers to understand the truth. Within that same rains-retreat, he realized the three true knowledges. Within that same rains-retreat, he attained final Nibbāna.

Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “yo so, bhante, puṇṇo nāma kulaputto bhagavatā saṃkhittena ovādena ovadito, so kālaṅkato. Tassa kā gati ko abhisamparāyo”ti?

Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One... Seated to one side, those bhikkhus said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, that clansman named Puṇṇa, who was admonished by the Blessed One with a brief instruction, has passed away. What is his destination? What is his future state?”

“Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, puṇṇo kulaputto kulaputto ahosi (sabbattha), paccapādi saccavādī (syā. kaṃ. ka.) dhammassānudhammaṃ, na ca maṃ dhammādhikaraṇaṃ vihesesi viheṭhesi (sī. syā. kaṃ.). Parinibbuto, bhikkhave, puṇṇo kulaputto”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, the clansman Puṇṇa was wise. He practiced the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and he did not trouble me on account of matters of the Dhamma. The clansman Puṇṇa, bhikkhus, has attained final Nibbāna.”

6. Bāhiyasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Bāhiya

89. Atha [M 2.0288] kho āyasmā bāhiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā bāhiyo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti.

89. Then the Venerable Bāhiya approached the Blessed One… Seated to one side, the Venerable Bāhiya said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, bāhiya, cakkhu niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“What do you think, Bāhiya: is the eye permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“And that which is impermanent, suffering, and of a nature to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No [V 2.0070][P 4.0064] hetaṃ, bhante”.

Indeed not, venerable sir.

“Rūpā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti?

Are forms permanent or impermanent?

“Aniccā, bhante”…pe… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… cakkhusamphasso…pe… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“Impermanent, venerable sir.” … “Is eye-consciousness … is eye-contact … and whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—is that also permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

Impermanent, venerable sir.

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

Suffering, venerable sir.

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu [T 4.0081] taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

And that which is impermanent, suffering, and of a nature to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?

“No hetaṃ, bhante”.

Indeed not, venerable sir.

“Evaṃ passaṃ, bāhiya, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati…pe… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.

Seeing thus, Bāhiya, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye, disenchanted with forms, disenchanted with eye-consciousness, disenchanted with eye-contact… and with whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—with that also one becomes disenchanted. Being disenchanted, one becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, one is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ One understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’”

Atha kho āyasmā bāhiyo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmā bāhiyo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ[V 2.0071], nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā bāhiyo arahataṃ ahosīti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

Then the Venerable Bāhiya, having rejoiced and delighted in the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed. Then the Venerable Bāhiya, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, before long, in this very life, realized for himself with higher knowledge and attained that supreme culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. He understood: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’ And the Venerable Bāhiya became one of the arahants. The sixth.

7. Paṭhamaejāsuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse on Agitation

90. “Ejā[M 2.0289], bhikkhave, rogo, ejā gaṇḍo, ejā sallaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tathāgato anejo viharati vītasallo. Tasmātiha[P 4.0065], bhikkhave, bhikkhu cepi ākaṅkheyya ‘anejo vihareyyaṃ vihareyya (sī. pī. ka.) vītasallo’ti, cakkhuṃ na maññeyya, cakkhusmiṃ na maññeyya, cakkhuto na maññeyya, cakkhu [T 4.0082] meti na maññeyya; rūpe na maññeyya, rūpesu na maññeyya, rūpato na maññeyya, rūpā meti na maññeyya; cakkhuviññāṇaṃ na maññeyya, cakkhuviññāṇasmiṃ na maññeyya, cakkhuviññāṇato na maññeyya, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ meti na maññeyya; cakkhusamphassaṃ na maññeyya, cakkhusamphassasmiṃ na maññeyya, cakkhusamphassato na maññeyya, cakkhusamphasso meti na maññeyya. Yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṃ meti na maññeyya.

90. “Bhikkhus, agitation is a disease, agitation is a boil, agitation is a dart. Therefore, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata dwells without agitation, with the dart removed. Therefore, bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish, ‘May I dwell without agitation, with the dart removed,’ he should not conceive the eye, he should not conceive in the eye, he should not conceive from the eye, he should not conceive, ‘The eye is mine.’ He should not conceive forms, he should not conceive in forms, he should not conceive from forms, he should not conceive, ‘Forms are mine.’ He should not conceive eye-consciousness, he should not conceive in eye-consciousness, he should not conceive from eye-consciousness, he should not conceive, ‘Eye-consciousness is mine.’ He should not conceive eye-contact, he should not conceive in eye-contact, he should not conceive from eye-contact, he should not conceive, ‘Eye-contact is mine.’ And whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—he should not conceive that, he should not conceive in that, he should not conceive from that, he should not conceive, ‘That is mine.’”

“Sotaṃ na maññeyya…pe… ghānaṃ na maññeyya…pe… jivhaṃ na maññeyya, jivhāya na maññeyya, jivhāto na maññeyya, jivhā meti na maññeyya; rase na maññeyya…pe… jivhāviññāṇaṃ na maññeyya…pe… jivhāsamphassaṃ na maññeyya…pe… yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṃ meti na maññeyya.

“He should not conceive the ear… and so on… He should not conceive the nose… and so on… He should not conceive the tongue, he should not conceive in the tongue, he should not conceive from the tongue, he should not conceive, ‘The tongue is mine.’ He should not conceive tastes… and so on… He should not conceive tongue-consciousness… and so on… He should not conceive tongue-contact… and so on… And whatever feeling arises conditioned by tongue-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—he should not conceive that, he should not conceive in that, he should not conceive from that, he should not conceive, ‘That is mine.’”

“Kāyaṃ na maññeyya…pe… manaṃ na maññeyya, manasmiṃ na maññeyya, manato na maññeyya, mano meti na maññeyya; dhamme na maññeyya…pe… mano viññāṇaṃ…pe… manosamphassaṃ…pe… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṃ meti na maññeyya; sabbaṃ na maññeyya, sabbasmiṃ [T 4.0083] na maññeyya, sabbato na maññeyya, sabbaṃ meti na maññeyya.

“He should not conceive the body… and so on… He should not conceive the mind, he should not conceive in the mind, he should not conceive from the mind, he should not conceive, ‘The mind is mine.’ He should not conceive mental phenomena… and so on… He should not conceive mind-consciousness… and so on… He should not conceive mind-contact… and so on… And whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—he should not conceive that, he should not conceive in that, he should not conceive from that, he should not conceive, ‘That is mine.’ He should not conceive the all, he should not conceive in the all, he should not conceive from the all, he should not conceive, ‘The all is mine.’”

“So [V 2.0072] evaṃ amaññamāno na kiñcipi loke upādiyati. Anupādiyaṃ na paritassati. Aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati[P 4.0066]. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Not conceiving thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. Not clinging, he is not agitated. Being unagitated, he personally attains Nibbāna. He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’” Seventh.

8. Dutiyaejāsuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse on Agitation

91. “Ejā[M 2.0290], bhikkhave, rogo, ejā gaṇḍo, ejā sallaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tathāgato anejo viharati vītasallo. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cepi ākaṅkheyya ‘anejo vihareyyaṃ vītasallo’ti, cakkhuṃ na maññeyya, cakkhusmiṃ na maññeyya, cakkhuto na maññeyya, cakkhu meti na maññeyya; rūpe na maññeyya… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ… cakkhusamphassaṃ… yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṃ meti na maññeyya. Yañhi, bhikkhave, maññati, yasmiṃ maññati, yato maññati, yaṃ meti maññati, tato taṃ hoti aññathā. Aññathābhāvī bhavasatto loko bhavameva abhinandati…pe….

91. “Agitation, bhikkhus, is a disease, agitation is a boil, agitation is a dart. Therefore, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata dwells without agitation, with the dart removed. Therefore, bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish, ‘May I dwell without agitation, with the dart removed,’ he should not conceive the eye, should not conceive in the eye, should not conceive from the eye, he should not conceive, ‘The eye is mine.’ He should not conceive forms… eye-consciousness… eye-contact… and whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—he should not conceive that, should not conceive in that, should not conceive from that, he should not conceive, ‘That is mine.’ For, bhikkhus, whatever one conceives, whatever one conceives in, whatever one conceives from, whatever one conceives as ‘mine’—that becomes otherwise. The world, attached to becoming and subject to becoming otherwise, delights only in becoming… and so on…”

“Jivhaṃ na maññeyya, jivhāya na maññeyya, jivhāto na maññeyya, jivhā meti na maññeyya; rase na maññeyya… jivhāviññāṇaṃ… jivhāsamphassaṃ… yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṃ meti na maññeyya. Yañhi, bhikkhave, maññati, yasmiṃ maññati, yato maññati, yaṃ meti maññati, tato taṃ hoti aññathā. Aññathābhāvī bhavasatto loko bhavameva abhinandati…pe….

“He should not conceive the tongue, should not conceive in the tongue, should not conceive from the tongue, should not conceive, ‘The tongue is mine.’ He should not conceive tastes… tongue-consciousness… tongue-contact… and whatever feeling arises with tongue-contact as condition—whether pleasant, painful, or neither pleasant nor painful—he should not conceive that, should not conceive in that, should not conceive from that, should not conceive, ‘That is mine.’ For, Bhikkhus, whatever one conceives, whatever one conceives in, whatever one conceives from, whatever one conceives as ‘mine’—that becomes otherwise. The world, attached to becoming and subject to becoming otherwise, delights only in becoming…and so on….”

“Manaṃ na maññeyya, manasmiṃ na maññeyya, manato na maññeyya, mano meti na maññeyya… manoviññāṇaṃ… manosamphassaṃ… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi [T 4.0084] na maññeyya, taṃ meti na maññeyya. Yañhi, bhikkhave, maññati, yasmiṃ maññati[V 2.0073], yato [P 4.0067] maññati, yaṃ meti maññati, tato taṃ hoti aññathā. Aññathābhāvī bhavasatto loko bhavameva abhinandati.

“He should not conceive the mind, should not conceive in the mind, should not conceive from the mind, should not conceive, ‘Mind is mine.’… mind-consciousness… mind-contact… and whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition—whether pleasant, painful, or neither pleasant nor painful—he should not conceive that, should not conceive in that, should not conceive from that, should not conceive, ‘That is mine.’ For, Bhikkhus, whatever one conceives, whatever one conceives in, whatever one conceives from, whatever one conceives as ‘mine’—that becomes otherwise. The world, attached to becoming and subject to becoming otherwise, delights only in becoming.”

“Yāvatā, bhikkhave, khandhadhātuāyatanā tampi na maññeyya, tasmimpi na maññeyya, tatopi na maññeyya, taṃ meti na maññeyya. So evaṃ amaññamāno na kiñci loke upādiyati. Anupādiyaṃ na paritassati. Aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, whatever aggregates, elements, and sense bases there are, he should not conceive them, should not conceive in them, should not conceive from them, should not conceive, ‘They are mine.’ Not conceiving thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. Not clinging, he is not agitated. Being unagitated, he personally attains Parinibbāna. He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’” The Eighth.

9. Paṭhamadvayasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on the Pair
