110. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the things that are bases for clinging, and clinging itself. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, are the things that are bases for clinging, and what is clinging? The eye, Bhikkhus, is a thing that is a basis for clinging. Whatever desire and lust there is in relation to it, that is the clinging there... the tongue is a thing that is a basis for clinging... the mind is a thing that is a basis for clinging. Whatever desire and lust there is in relation to it, that is the clinging there. These, Bhikkhus, are called the things that are bases for clinging, and this is clinging.” Seventh.

8. Ajjhattikāyatanaparijānanasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Comprehending the Internal Sense Bases

111. “Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Sotaṃ… ghānaṃ… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ… manaṃ anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Cakkhuñca kho, bhikkhave, abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya…pe… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ… manaṃ abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāyā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

111. “Bhikkhus, without directly knowing the eye, without fully understanding it, without becoming dispassionate towards it, without abandoning it, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. The ear… the nose… the tongue… the body… the mind—without directly knowing it, without fully understanding it, without becoming dispassionate towards it, without abandoning it, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. But, Bhikkhus, by directly knowing the eye, by fully understanding it, by becoming dispassionate towards it, and by abandoning it, one is capable of the destruction of suffering… the tongue… the body… the mind—by directly knowing it, by fully understanding it, by becoming dispassionate towards it, and by abandoning it, one is capable of the destruction of suffering.” Eighth.

9. Bāhirāyatanaparijānanasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Comprehending the External Sense Bases

112. “Rūpe[M 2.0310][P 4.0090], bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… dhamme anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ [V 2.0097] avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Rūpe ca kho, bhikkhave, abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāya. Sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… dhamme abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāyā”ti. Navamaṃ.

112. “Bhikkhus, without directly knowing forms, without fully understanding them, without becoming dispassionate towards them, without abandoning them, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. Sounds… smells… tastes… tactile objects… mental objects—without directly knowing them, without fully understanding them, without becoming dispassionate towards them, without abandoning them, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering. But, Bhikkhus, by directly knowing forms, by fully understanding them, by becoming dispassionate towards them, and by abandoning them, one is capable of the destruction of suffering. Sounds… smells… tastes… tactile objects… mental objects—by directly knowing them, by fully understanding them, by becoming dispassionate towards them, and by abandoning them, one is capable of the destruction of suffering.” Ninth.

10. Upassutisuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Overhearing

113. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā nātike ñātike (sī. syā. kaṃ.) viharati giñjakāvasathe. Atha kho bhagavā rahogato paṭisallīno imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ abhāsi – “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṃ. Tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso. Phassapaccayā vedanā; vedanāpaccayā taṇhā; taṇhāpaccayā [T 4.0112] upādānaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo; bhavapaccayā jāti; jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati…pe… manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṃ. Tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso. Phassapaccayā vedanā; vedanāpaccayā taṇhā; taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ; upādānapaccayā bhavo; bhavapaccayā jāti; jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti”.

113. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Nātika in the brick hall. Then, while in seclusion and solitude, the Blessed One spoke this exposition of the Dhamma: “Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as a condition, feeling arises; with feeling as a condition, craving arises; with craving as a condition, clinging arises; with clinging as a condition, becoming arises; with becoming as a condition, birth arises; with birth as a condition, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come into being. Such is the origin of this entire mass of suffering. Dependent on the tongue and tastes… Dependent on the mind and mental objects, mind-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as a condition, feeling arises; with feeling as a condition, craving arises; with craving as a condition, clinging arises; with clinging as a condition, becoming arises; with becoming as a condition, birth arises; with birth as a condition, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come into being. Such is the origin of this entire mass of suffering.”

“Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṃ. Tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso. Phassapaccayā vedanā; vedanāpaccayā taṇhā. Tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodhā upādānanirodho; upādānanirodhā bhavanirodho; bhavanirodhā jātinirodho; jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hoti…pe… jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati…pe… manañca paṭicca dhamme ca uppajjati manoviññāṇaṃ. Tiṇṇaṃ saṅgati phasso. Phassapaccayā vedanā; vedanāpaccayā taṇhā. Tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodhā upādānanirodho[M 2.0311]; upādānanirodhā…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti.

“Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as a condition, feeling arises; with feeling as a condition, craving arises. Through the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving, clinging ceases. With the cessation of clinging, becoming ceases. With the cessation of becoming, birth ceases. With the cessation of birth, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Such is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering… Dependent on the tongue and tastes… Dependent on the mind and mental objects, mind-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as a condition, feeling arises; with feeling as a condition, craving arises. Through the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving, clinging ceases. With the cessation of clinging… such is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering.”

Tena [T 4.0113][P 4.0091] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu bhagavato upassuti upassutiṃ (sī. ka.) ṭhito hoti. Addasā kho [V 2.0098] bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ upassuti ṭhitaṃ. Disvāna taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “assosi no tvaṃ, bhikkhu, imaṃ dhammapariyāya”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Uggaṇhāhi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ. Pariyāpuṇāhi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ. Dhārehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ. Atthasaṃhitoyaṃ, bhikkhu, dhammapariyāyo ādibrahmacariyako”ti. Dasamaṃ.

Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu was standing nearby, listening to the Blessed One. The Blessed One saw that bhikkhu standing there listening. Having seen him, the Blessed One said to that bhikkhu: “Bhikkhu, did you hear this exposition of the Dhamma?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhu, you should learn this exposition of the Dhamma. Bhikkhu, you should master this exposition of the Dhamma. Bhikkhu, you should bear in mind this exposition of the Dhamma. Bhikkhu, this exposition of the Dhamma is beneficial and fundamental to the holy life.” Tenth.

Yogakkhemivaggo ekādasamo.

The Eleventh Chapter on Security from Bondage.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Yogakkhemi upādāya, dukkhaṃ loko ca seyyo ca;

Saṃyojanaṃ upādānaṃ, dve parijānaṃ upassutīti.

Security from Bondage, Agitation from Clinging, Suffering, the World, and ‘I Am Better’; The Fetter, Bases for Clinging, the two on Comprehension, and Overhearing.

12. Lokakāmaguṇavaggo

12. The Chapter on Worldly Sensual Pleasures

1. Paṭhamamārapāsasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on Māra's Snare

114. “Santi[T 4.0114], bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce, bhikkhu, abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āvāsagato mārassa, mārassa vasaṃ gato vasagato (sī. aṭṭha. syā. aṭṭha.), paṭimukkassa mārapāso. Baddho so mārabandhanena yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato…pe….

114. “Bhikkhus, there are forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a lovely nature, connected with sensual desire, and passion-arousing. If a bhikkhu delights in it, speaks of it, and remains attached to it, this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is said to be one who has gone to Māra's abode, one who has come under Māra's power. Māra's snare is fastened upon him. He is bound by Māra's fetter, at the disposal of the Evil One….

“Santi, bhikkhave, jivhāviññeyyā rasā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āvāsagato mārassa, mārassa vasaṃ gato, paṭimukkassa mārapāso. Baddho so mārabandhanena…pe….

“Bhikkhus, there are tastes cognizable by the tongue—desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a lovely nature, connected with sensual desire, and passion-arousing. If a bhikkhu delights in it, speaks of it, and remains attached to it, this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is said to be one who has gone to Māra's abode, one who has come under Māra's power. Māra's snare is fastened upon him. He is bound by Māra's fetter….

“Santi[M 2.0312], bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āvāsagato mārassa, mārassa vasaṃ gato, paṭimukkassa [P 4.0092] mārapāso. Baddho so mārabandhanena yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato.

“Bhikkhus, there are mental objects cognizable by the mind—desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a lovely nature, connected with sensual desire, and passion-arousing. If a bhikkhu delights in it, speaks of it, and remains attached to it, this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is said to be one who has gone to Māra's abode, one who has come under Māra's power. Māra's snare is fastened upon him. He is bound by Māra's fetter, at the disposal of the Evil One.

“Santi ca kho, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave[V 2.0099], bhikkhu nāvāsagato mārassa, na mārassa vasaṃ gato, ummukkassa mārapāso. Mutto so mārabandhanena na yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato…pe….

“Indeed, bhikkhus, there are forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a lovely nature, connected with sensual desire, and passion-arousing. If a bhikkhu does not delight in it, does not speak of it, and does not remain attached to it, this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is said to be one who has not gone to Māra's abode, one who has not come under Māra's power. Māra's snare is released from him. He is freed from Māra's fetter, not at the disposal of the Evil One….

“Santi, bhikkhave, jivhāviññeyyā rasā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nāvāsagato [T 4.0115] mārassa, na mārassa vasaṃ gato, ummukkassa mārapāso. Mutto so mārabandhanena na yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato…pe….

“Bhikkhus, there are tastes cognizable by the tongue—desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a lovely nature, connected with sensual desire, and passion-arousing. If a bhikkhu does not delight in it, does not speak of it, and does not remain attached to it, this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is said to be one who has not gone to Māra's abode, one who has not come under Māra's power. Māra's snare is released from him. He is freed from Māra's fetter, not at the disposal of the Evil One….

“Santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nāvāsagato mārassa, na mārassa vasaṃ gato, ummukkassa mārapāso. Mutto so mārabandhanena na yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, there are mental objects cognizable by the mind—desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a lovely nature, connected with sensual desire, and passion-arousing. If a bhikkhu does not delight in it, does not speak of it, and does not remain attached to it, this bhikkhu, bhikkhus, is said to be one who has not gone to Māra's abode, one who has not come under Māra's power. Māra's snare is released from him. He is freed from Māra's fetter, not at the disposal of the Evil One.” First.

2. Dutiyamārapāsasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on Māra's Snare

115. “Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu baddho cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu, āvāsagato mārassa, mārassa vasaṃ gato, paṭimukkassa mārapāso. Baddho so mārabandhanena yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato…pe….

115. “Bhikkhus, there are forms cognizable by eye-consciousness that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, endearing, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. If a bhikkhu delights in them, welcomes them, and remains holding to them, this, bhikkhus, is called a bhikkhu who is bound in regard to forms cognizable by eye-consciousness. He has gone to Māra's abode, has come under Māra's power; Māra's snare is fastened upon him. He is bound by Māra's bond, to be dealt with as the Evil One wishes… and so on….”

“Santi, bhikkhave, jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati [M 2.0313] abhivadati [V 2.0100] ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu baddho manoviññeyyesu dhammesu, āvāsagato mārassa, mārassa vasaṃ gato, paṭimukkassa mārapāso. Baddho so mārabandhanena yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato…pe….

“Bhikkhus, there are tastes cognizable by tongue-consciousness… and so on…. Bhikkhus, there are mental phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, endearing, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. If a bhikkhu delights in them, welcomes them, and remains holding to them, this, bhikkhus, is called a bhikkhu who is bound in regard to mental phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness. He has gone to Māra's abode, has come under Māra's power; Māra's snare is fastened upon him. He is bound by Māra's bond, to be dealt with as the Evil One wishes… and so on….”

“Santi ca kho, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave[T 4.0116], bhikkhu mutto cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi, nāvāsagato mārassa, na mārassa vasaṃ gato, ummukkassa mārapāso. Mutto so mārabandhanena na yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato…pe….

“Bhikkhus, there are forms cognizable by eye-consciousness that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, endearing, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. If a bhikkhu does not delight in them, does not welcome them, and does not remain holding to them, this, bhikkhus, is called a bhikkhu who is freed from forms cognizable by eye-consciousness. He has not gone to Māra's abode, has not come under Māra's power; Māra's snare is cast off from him. He is freed from Māra's bond, not to be dealt with as the Evil One wishes… and so on….”

“Santi, bhikkhave, jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce [P 4.0093] bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mutto manoviññeyyehi dhammehi, nāvāsagato mārassa, na mārassa vasaṃ gato, ummukkassa mārapāso. Mutto so mārabandhanena na yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, there are tastes cognizable by tongue-consciousness… and so on…. Bhikkhus, there are mental phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, endearing, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. If a bhikkhu does not delight in them, does not welcome them, and does not remain holding to them, this, bhikkhus, is called a bhikkhu who is freed from mental phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness. He has not gone to Māra's abode, has not come under Māra's power; Māra's snare is cast off from him. He is freed from Māra's bond, not to be dealt with as the Evil One wishes.”

3. Lokantagamanasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Going to the End of the World

116. “Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ, daṭṭheyyaṃ diṭṭheyyaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.), patteyyanti vadāmi. Na ca panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyaṃ vadāmī”ti. Idaṃ vatvā bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – “idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ, daṭṭheyyaṃ, patteyyanti vadāmi. Na ca panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyaṃ vadāmī’ti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā”ti?

116. “Bhikkhus, I do not say that by traveling, the end of the world can be known, seen, or reached. And yet, bhikkhus, I do not say that one can make an end of suffering without having reached the end of the world.” Having said this, the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered the dwelling. Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: “Friends, the Blessed One, having given this summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, has risen from his seat and entered the dwelling, saying: ‘Bhikkhus, I do not say that by traveling, the end of the world can be known, seen, or reached. And yet, bhikkhus, I do not say that one can make an end of suffering without having reached the end of the world.’ Now who might analyze in detail the meaning of this summary stated in brief by the Blessed One without it having been analyzed?”

Atha [M 2.0314] kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito[V 2.0101], sambhāvito ca [T 4.0117] viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā”ti.

Then this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: “This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary stated in brief by the Blessed One without it having been analyzed. What if we were to approach the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, we could question the Venerable Ānanda about this matter.”

Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ [P 4.0094] etadavocuṃ –

Then those bhikkhus approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, they exchanged greetings with the Venerable Ānanda. Having concluded their pleasant and memorable conversation, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Venerable Ānanda:

“Idaṃ kho no, āvuso ānanda, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ, daṭṭheyyaṃ, patteyyanti vadāmi. Na ca panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyaṃ vadāmī’ti. Tesaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ, daṭṭheyyaṃ, patteyyanti vadāmi. Na ca panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyaṃ vadāmīti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’ti[T 4.0118]? Tesaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho, āvuso, āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti. Vibhajatāyasmā ānando”ti.

“Friend Ānanda, the Blessed One, having given this summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, has risen from his seat and entered the dwelling, saying: ‘Bhikkhus, I do not say that by traveling, the end of the world can be known, seen, or reached. And yet, bhikkhus, I do not say that one can make an end of suffering without having reached the end of the world.’ For us, friend, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred: ‘Friends, the Blessed One, having given this summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, has risen from his seat and entered the dwelling, saying: “Bhikkhus, I do not say that by traveling, the end of the world can be known, seen, or reached. And yet, bhikkhus, I do not say that one can make an end of suffering without having reached the end of the world.” Now who might analyze in detail the meaning of this summary stated in brief by the Blessed One without it having been analyzed?’ For us, friend, this thought occurred: ‘This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary stated in brief by the Blessed One without it having been analyzed. What if we were to approach the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, we could question the Venerable Ānanda about this matter.’ May the Venerable Ānanda please analyze it.”

“Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṃ caramāno mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato atikkammeva, mūlaṃ atikkammeva, khandhaṃ sākhāpalāse sāraṃ pariyesitabbaṃ maññeyya; evaṃ sampadamidaṃ āyasmantānaṃ satthari sammukhībhūte taṃ bhagavantaṃ atisitvā [M 2.0315] amhe etamatthaṃ paṭipucchitabbaṃ maññatha maññetha (pī. ka.). So hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti, passaṃ [V 2.0102] passati – cakkhubhūto, ñāṇabhūto, dhammabhūto, brahmabhūto, vattā, pavattā, atthassa ninnetā, amatassa dātā, dhammassāmī, tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha[P 4.0095]. Yathā vo bhagavā byākareyya tathā vo dhāreyyāthā”ti.

“Friends, it is as if a man needing heartwood, seeking heartwood, wandering in search of heartwood, were to pass over the root and the trunk of a great, standing tree possessing heartwood, thinking that heartwood should be sought among its branches and leaves. So it is with you, venerable ones. With the Teacher present before you, you pass over that Blessed One and think that we are to be questioned about this matter. For, friends, that Blessed One knows what is to be known and sees what is to be seen. He has become the eye, become knowledge, become the Dhamma, become Brahmā. He is the speaker, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the giver of the deathless, the Lord of the Dhamma, the Tathāgata. And that was the very time when you should have questioned the Blessed One himself about this matter. As the Blessed One would have explained it to you, so you should have remembered it.”

“Addhāvuso ānanda, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti, passaṃ passati – cakkhubhūto, ñāṇabhūto, dhammabhūto, brahmabhūto, vattā, pavattā, atthassa ninnetā, amatassa dātā, dhammassāmī, tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma[T 4.0119]. Yathā no bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāma. Api cāyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Vibhajatāyasmā ānando agaruṃ karitvā”ti.

“Certainly, friend Ānanda, the Blessed One knows what is to be known and sees what is to be seen. He has become the eye, become knowledge, become the Dhamma, become Brahmā. He is the speaker, the proclaimer, the elucidator of meaning, the giver of the deathless, the Lord of the Dhamma, the Tathāgata. And that was the very time when we should have questioned the Blessed One himself about this matter. As the Blessed One would have explained it to us, so we would have remembered it. Moreover, the Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise fellow practitioners in the holy life. The Venerable Ānanda is capable of explaining in detail the meaning of this brief summary stated by the Blessed One, of which the meaning was not analyzed in detail. Let the Venerable Ānanda explain, not taking it as a burden.”

“Tenahāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā ānando etadavoca –

“Then, friends, listen and apply your minds well; I will speak.” “Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda said this:

“Yaṃ kho vo, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ, daṭṭheyyaṃ, patteyyanti vadāmi. Na ca panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyaṃ vadāmī’ti, imassa khvāhaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Yena kho, āvuso, lokasmiṃ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī – ayaṃ vuccati ariyassa vinaye loko. Kena cāvuso, lokasmiṃ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī? Cakkhunā kho, āvuso, lokasmiṃ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī. Sotena kho, āvuso… ghānena kho, āvuso… jivhāya kho, āvuso, lokasmiṃ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī[M 2.0316]. Kāyena kho, āvuso… manena kho, āvuso, lokasmiṃ lokasaññī hoti lokamānī. Yena kho, āvuso, lokasmiṃ lokasaññī [T 4.0120] hoti lokamānī – ayaṃ vuccati ariyassa vinaye loko. Yaṃ [P 4.0096] kho vo, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ[V 2.0103], daṭṭheyyaṃ, patteyyanti vadāmi. Na ca panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyaṃ vadāmī’ti, imassa khvāhaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe āyasmanto bhagavantaṃyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha. Yathā vo bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti.

“Friends, as for the brief statement that the Blessed One pointed out, and without analyzing its meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the dwelling—‘Monks, I do not say that by traveling one can know, see, or reach the end of the world. And yet, monks, I do not say that one makes an end of suffering without having reached the end of the world’—of this brief statement pointed out by the Blessed One, of which the meaning was not analyzed in detail, I understand the detailed meaning thus: Friends, that by which one perceives the world and conceives the world—this is called ‘the world’ in the discipline of the Noble One. And by what, friends, does one perceive the world and conceive the world? By the eye, friends, one perceives the world and conceives the world. By the ear... by the nose... by the tongue... by the body... by the mind, friends, one perceives the world and conceives the world. That by which one perceives the world and conceives the world—this is called ‘the world’ in the discipline of the Noble One. As for the brief statement that the Blessed One pointed out, and without analyzing its meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the dwelling—‘Monks, I do not say that by traveling one can know, see, or reach the end of the world. And yet, monks, I do not say that one makes an end of suffering without having reached the end of the world’—this, friends, is how I understand in detail the meaning of this brief statement pointed out by the Blessed One, of which the meaning was not analyzed in detail. But if you venerable ones wish, you may approach the Blessed One himself and question him about this matter. As he explains it to you, so you should remember it.”

“Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ –

“Very well, friend,” those monks replied to Venerable Ānanda. Having risen from their seats, they approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said this to the Blessed One:

“Yaṃ kho no, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ, daṭṭheyyaṃ, patteyyanti vadāmi. Na ca panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyaṃ vadāmī’ti. Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā [T 4.0121] vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ, daṭṭheyyaṃ, patteyyanti vadāmi. Na ca panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, appatvā lokassa antaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyaṃ vadāmī’ti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyāti? Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho [P 4.0097] āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti. Atha kho mayaṃ[M 2.0317], bhante, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipucchimha. Tesaṃ no, bhante, āyasmatā ānandena imehi ākārehi imehi padehi imehi byañjanehi attho vibhatto”ti.

“Venerable sir, the Blessed One, having stated a brief summary for us without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: ‘Bhikkhus, I do not say that by traveling one can know, see, or reach the end of the world. And, bhikkhus, I do not say that one can make an end of suffering without reaching the end of the world.’ Venerable sir, for us, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought arose: ‘Friends, the Blessed One, having stated this brief summary for us without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: “Bhikkhus, I do not say that by traveling one can know, see, or reach the end of the world. And, bhikkhus, I do not say that one can make an end of suffering without reaching the end of the world.” Who, indeed, could analyze in detail the meaning of this brief summary stated by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail?’ Venerable sir, for us, this thought arose: ‘This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this brief summary stated by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. It would be good if we were to approach the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, we could question the Venerable Ānanda about this matter.’ Then, venerable sir, we approached the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, we questioned the Venerable Ānanda about this matter. For us, venerable sir, the meaning was analyzed by the Venerable Ānanda with these reasons, with these terms, and with these phrases.”

“Paṇḍito[V 2.0104], bhikkhave, ānando; mahāpañño, bhikkhave, ānando! Maṃ cepi tumhe, bhikkhave, etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha, ahampi taṃ evamevaṃ byākareyyaṃ yathā taṃ ānandena byākataṃ. Eso cevetassa attho, evañca naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, Ānanda is wise; bhikkhus, Ānanda has great wisdom. Bhikkhus, if you were to question me about this matter, I too would explain it in the very same way that it has been explained by Ānanda. This is its meaning, and thus should you remember it.”

4. Kāmaguṇasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Strands of Sensual Pleasure

117. “Pubbeva me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva [T 4.0122] sato etadahosi – ‘yeme pañca kāmaguṇā cetaso samphuṭṭhapubbā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā, tatra me cittaṃ bahulaṃ gacchamānaṃ gaccheyya paccuppannesu vā appaṃ vā anāgatesu’. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘yeme pañca kāmaguṇā cetaso samphuṭṭhapubbā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā, tatra me attarūpena appamādo sati cetaso ārakkho karaṇīyo’. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhākampi ye te pañca kāmaguṇā cetaso samphuṭṭhapubbā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā, tatra vo cittaṃ bahulaṃ gacchamānaṃ gaccheyya paccuppannesu vā appaṃ vā anāgatesu. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, tumhākampi ye te pañca kāmaguṇā cetaso samphuṭṭhapubbā [P 4.0098] atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā, tatra vo attarūpehi appamādo sati cetaso ārakkho karaṇīyo. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati, rasasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe”ti. Idaṃ vatvā bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

117. “Bhikkhus, before my awakening, while I was still an unawakened Bodhisatta, this thought occurred to me: ‘Regarding these five strands of sensual pleasure which have been previously experienced by the mind—which are past, ceased, and altered—my mind might frequently incline towards them, or towards those in the present, or to a lesser extent, towards those in the future.’ Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to me: ‘Regarding these five strands of sensual pleasure which have been previously experienced by the mind—which are past, ceased, and altered—for my own benefit, heedfulness and mindfulness as a guard for the mind should be undertaken.’ Therefore, bhikkhus, for you also, regarding those five strands of sensual pleasure which have been previously experienced by the mind—which are past, ceased, and altered—your minds might frequently incline towards them, or towards those in the present, or to a lesser extent, towards those in the future. Therefore, bhikkhus, for you also, regarding those five strands of sensual pleasure which have been previously experienced by the mind—which are past, ceased, and altered—for your own benefit, heedfulness and mindfulness as a guard for the mind should be undertaken. Therefore, bhikkhus, that base should be known wherein the eye ceases and the perception of forms ceases; that base should be known… and so on… wherein the tongue ceases and the perception of tastes ceases; that base should be known… and so on… wherein the mind ceases and the perception of mental objects ceases; that base should be known.’ Having said this, the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered the monastery.

Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – “idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe [T 4.0123] yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati, rasasaññā ca nirujjhati, se [M 2.0318] āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā [V 2.0105] saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā”ti?

Then, for those bhikkhus, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought arose: ‘Friends, the Blessed One, having stated this brief summary for us without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: “Therefore, bhikkhus, that base should be known wherein the eye ceases and the perception of forms ceases; that base should be known… and so on… wherein the tongue ceases and the perception of tastes ceases; that base should be known… and so on… wherein the mind ceases and the perception of mental objects ceases; that base should be known.” Who, indeed, could analyze in detail the meaning of this brief summary stated by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail?’”

Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā”ti.

Then this thought arose for those bhikkhus: ‘This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this brief summary stated by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. It would be good if we were to approach the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, we could question the Venerable Ānanda about this matter.’”

Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu[P 4.0099]. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ –

Then those bhikkhus approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, they exchanged courteous greetings with the Venerable Ānanda. Having concluded their courteous and memorable talk, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Venerable Ānanda:

“Idaṃ kho no, āvuso ānanda, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati[T 4.0124], rasasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti. Tesaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati, rasasaññā ca nirujjhati se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyāti? Tesaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena [M 2.0319] uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā ānando [V 2.0106] tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti. Vibhajatāyasmā ānando”ti.

“Friend Ānanda, the Blessed One, having given us this brief exposition, without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered his dwelling, saying: ‘Therefore, bhikkhus, that sphere should be known where the eye ceases and the perception of forms ceases. That sphere should be known… where the tongue ceases and the perception of tastes ceases. That sphere should be known… where the mind ceases and the perception of mental phenomena ceases.’

Soon after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred to us: ‘Friends, the Blessed One, having given us this brief exposition, without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered his dwelling, saying: “Therefore, bhikkhus, that sphere should be known where the eye ceases and the perception of forms ceases. That sphere should be known… where the tongue ceases and the perception of tastes ceases. That sphere should be known… where the mind ceases and the perception of mental phenomena ceases.” Now who could analyze in detail the meaning of this brief exposition given by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail?’

Then this thought occurred to us: ‘This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this brief exposition given by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. What if we were to approach the Venerable Ānanda and ask him about this matter?’ May the Venerable Ānanda please analyze it.”

“Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṃ caramāno mahato rukkhassa…pe… vibhajatāyasmā ānando agaruṃ karitvāti.

“Just as, friends, a man needing heartwood, seeking heartwood, wandering in search of heartwood, would approach a great, stable, heartwood tree… May the Venerable Ānanda please analyze it, without treating it as a heavy matter.”

“Tenahāvuso[T 4.0125], suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti [P 4.0100] kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā ānando etadavoca –

“Well then, friends, listen and pay close attention; I will speak.” “Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda said this:

“Yaṃ kho vo, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti. Imassa khvāhaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Saḷāyatananirodhaṃ no etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe, yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti. Imassa khvāhaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa [T 4.0126] evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe āyasmanto bhagavantaṃyeva upasaṅkamatha; upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ puccheyyātha. Yathā vo bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti.

“Friends, as to that brief exposition which the Blessed One gave, without analyzing the meaning in detail, before rising from his seat and entering his dwelling—‘Therefore, bhikkhus, that sphere should be known where the eye ceases and the perception of forms ceases. That sphere should be known… where the mind ceases and the perception of mental phenomena ceases’—of this brief exposition given by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail, I understand the detailed meaning thus. Friends, this was spoken by the Blessed One in reference to the cessation of the six sense spheres: ‘Therefore, bhikkhus, that sphere should be known where the eye ceases and the perception of forms ceases. That sphere should be known… where the mind ceases and the perception of mental phenomena ceases.’

Friends, as to that brief exposition which the Blessed One gave, without analyzing the meaning in detail, before rising from his seat and entering his dwelling—‘Therefore, bhikkhus, that sphere should be known where the eye ceases and the perception of forms ceases. That sphere should be known… where the mind ceases and the perception of mental phenomena ceases’—of this brief exposition given by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail, I understand the detailed meaning in this way. However, venerable ones, if you wish, you may approach the Blessed One himself and ask him about this matter. As the Blessed One explains it to you, so should you bear it in mind.”

“Evamāvuso”ti [M 2.0320] kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā [V 2.0107] tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ –

“Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. Having risen from their seats, they approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:

“Yaṃ kho no, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha jivhā ca nirujjhati, rasasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti, tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso[P 4.0101], bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – tasmātiha, bhikkhave, se āyatane veditabbe yattha cakkhu ca nirujjhati, rūpasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe…pe… yattha mano ca nirujjhati, dhammasaññā ca nirujjhati, se āyatane veditabbe’ti. ‘Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena [T 4.0127] uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’ti? Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāmā’ti. Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipucchimha. Tesaṃ no, bhante, āyasmatā ānandena imehi ākārehi, imehi padehi, imehi byañjanehi attho vibhatto”ti.

“Venerable sir, the Blessed One, having pointed out a summary to us in brief, and without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: ‘Therefore, monks, that sphere should be known wherein the eye and perception of forms cease; that sphere should be known… and so on… where the tongue and perception of tastes cease; that sphere should be known… and so on… where the mind and perception of mental phenomena cease; that sphere should be known.’ Venerable sir, to us, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred: ‘Friends, the Blessed One, having pointed out this summary to us in brief, and without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: “Therefore, monks, that sphere should be known wherein the eye and perception of forms cease; that sphere should be known… and so on… where the mind and perception of mental phenomena cease; that sphere should be known.” Who, indeed, could analyze in detail the meaning of this summary pointed out in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail?’ Venerable sir, this thought occurred to us: ‘This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary pointed out in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. What if we were to approach Venerable Ānanda and ask him about this matter?’ Then, venerable sir, we approached Venerable Ānanda and asked him about this matter. Venerable sir, for us, the meaning has been analyzed by Venerable Ānanda with these reasons, with these phrases, and with these syllables.”

“Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, ānando; mahāpañño, bhikkhave, ānando! Maṃ cepi tumhe, bhikkhave, etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha, ahampi taṃ evamevaṃ byākareyyaṃ yathā taṃ ānandena byākataṃ. Eso cevetassa attho. Evañca naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Monks, Ānanda is wise; monks, Ānanda has great wisdom! Monks, if you were to ask me about this matter, I too would explain it just as it has been explained by Ānanda. This indeed is its meaning. And you should bear it in mind thus.”

5. Sakkapañhasuttaṃ

5. The Sutta on the Questions of Sakka

118. Ekaṃ [M 2.0321][V 2.0108] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Atha kho sakko devānamindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante[T 4.0128], hetu, ko paccayo yena [P 4.0102] midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti? Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?

118. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagaha on the Gijjhakūṭa mountain. Then Sakka, lord of the devas, approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Sakka, lord of the devas, said this to the Blessed One: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition by which some beings here do not attain final Nibbāna in this very life? And what, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition by which some beings here do attain final Nibbāna in this very life?”

“Santi kho, devānaminda, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti tadupādānaṃ. Saupādāno, devānaminda, bhikkhu no parinibbāyati…pe….

“Sakka, lord of the devas, there are forms cognizable by eye-consciousness that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, endearing, connected with sensual pleasure, and arousing of passion. If a monk delights in them, speaks in praise of them, and remains attached to them, for him who delights in them, speaks in praise of them, and remains attached to them, consciousness dependent on that arises, and clinging to that arises. Sakka, lord of the devas, a monk with clinging does not attain final Nibbāna… and so on.

“Santi kho, devānaminda, jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… santi kho, devānaminda, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti tadupādānaṃ. Saupādāno, devānaminda, bhikkhu no parinibbāyati. Ayaṃ kho, devānaminda, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti.

“Sakka, lord of the devas, there are tastes cognizable by tongue-consciousness… and so on… Sakka, lord of the devas, there are mental phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, endearing, connected with sensual pleasure, and arousing of passion. If a monk delights in them, speaks in praise of them, and remains attached to them, for him who delights in them, speaks in praise of them, and remains attached to them, consciousness dependent on that arises, and clinging to that arises. Sakka, lord of the devas, a monk with clinging does not attain final Nibbāna. This, Sakka, lord of the devas, is the cause, this is the condition by which some beings here do not attain final Nibbāna in this very life.

“Santi ca kho, devānaminda, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti, na tadupādānaṃ. Anupādāno, devānaminda, bhikkhu parinibbāyati…pe…[T 4.0129].

“And, Sakka, lord of the devas, there are forms cognizable by eye-consciousness that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, endearing, connected with sensual pleasure, and arousing of passion. If a monk does not delight in them, does not speak in praise of them, and does not remain attached to them, for him who does not delight in them, does not speak in praise of them, and does not remain attached to them, consciousness dependent on that does not arise, and clinging to that does not arise. Without clinging, Sakka, lord of the devas, a monk attains final Nibbāna… and so on.

“Santi kho, devānaminda, jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… santi kho, devānaminda, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato [V 2.0109] na tannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti na tadupādānaṃ. Anupādāno, devānaminda, bhikkhu [M 2.0322] parinibbāyati. Ayaṃ kho, devānaminda, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Sakka, lord of the devas, there are tastes cognizable by tongue-consciousness… and so on… Sakka, lord of the devas, there are mental phenomena cognizable by mind-consciousness that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, endearing, connected with sensual pleasure, and arousing of passion. If a monk does not delight in them, does not speak in praise of them, and does not remain attached to them, for him who does not delight in them, does not speak in praise of them, and does not remain attached to them, consciousness dependent on that does not arise, and clinging to that does not arise. Without clinging, Sakka, lord of the devas, a monk attains final Nibbāna. This, Sakka, lord of the devas, is the cause, this is the condition by which some beings here attain final Nibbāna in this very life.”

6. Pañcasikhasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Pañcasikha

119. Ekaṃ [P 4.0103] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Atha kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti? Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti? “Santi kho, pañcasikha, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā…pe… santi kho, pañcasikha, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti tadupādānaṃ. Saupādāno, pañcasikha[T 4.0130], bhikkhu no parinibbāyati. Ayaṃ kho, pañcasikha, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti”.

119. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on Gijjhakūṭa Mountain. Then Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva, approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva, said to the Blessed One: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition why some beings here do not attain final Nibbāna in this very life? And what, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition why some beings here do attain final Nibbāna in this very life?” “There are, Pañcasikha, forms cognizable by the eye… There are, Pañcasikha, mental phenomena cognizable by the mind, which are desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a lovable nature, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of passion. If a bhikkhu delights in them, extols them, and remains engrossed in them, for him who delights in them, extols them, and remains engrossed in them, consciousness dependent on that arises, and with it, clinging. A bhikkhu with clinging, Pañcasikha, does not attain final Nibbāna. This, Pañcasikha, is the cause, this is the condition why some beings here do not attain final Nibbāna in this very life.”

“Santi ca kho, pañcasikha, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā…pe… santi kho, pañcasikha, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati, tassa taṃ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti, na tadupādānaṃ. Anupādāno, pañcasikha, bhikkhu parinibbāyati. Ayaṃ kho, pañcasikha, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“There are, Pañcasikha, forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, pleasing, delightful… There are, Pañcasikha, mental phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a lovable nature, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of passion. If a bhikkhu does not delight in them, does not extol them, and does not remain engrossed in them, then for him who does not delight in them, does not extol them, and does not remain engrossed in them, consciousness dependent on that does not arise, nor does clinging. Without clinging, Pañcasikha, a bhikkhu attains final Nibbāna. This, Pañcasikha, is the cause, this is the condition why some beings here do attain final Nibbāna in this very life.”

7. Sāriputtasaddhivihārikasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Sāriputta's Co-resident

120. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme[V 2.0110]. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “saddhivihāriko[M 2.0323], āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto”ti.

120. On one occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Venerable Sāriputta and exchanged greetings with him. When the joyful and memorable talk was over, he sat down to one side and said to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Friend Sāriputta, a co-resident bhikkhu of yours has abandoned the training and returned to the lower life.”

“Evametaṃ, āvuso, hoti indriyesu aguttadvārassa, bhojane amattaññuno, jāgariyaṃ ananuyuttassa. ‘So vatāvuso, bhikkhu indriyesu aguttadvāro bhojane amattaññū jāgariyaṃ [P 4.0104] ananuyutto yāvajīvaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ santānessatī’ti [T 4.0131] netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. ‘So vatāvuso, bhikkhu indriyesu guttadvāro, bhojane mattaññū, jāgariyaṃ anuyutto yāvajīvaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ santānessatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Indeed, friend, it is so for one whose sense faculties are unguarded, who is immoderate in eating, and who is not devoted to wakefulness. Friend, it is impossible that a bhikkhu whose sense faculties are unguarded, who is immoderate in eating, and who is not devoted to wakefulness will carry on the completely fulfilled and purified holy life for his entire life. Friend, it is possible that a bhikkhu whose sense faculties are guarded, who is moderate in eating, and who is devoted to wakefulness will carry on the completely fulfilled and purified holy life for his entire life.”

“Kathañcāvuso, indriyesu guttadvāro hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, indriyesu guttadvāro hoti.

“And how, friend, is one guarded in the sense faculties? Here, friend, a bhikkhu, having seen a form with the eye, does not grasp the sign, does not grasp the secondary characteristics. Because if he were to dwell with the eye faculty unrestrained, evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might assail him, he practices for its restraint, guards the eye faculty, and undertakes restraint in the eye faculty. Having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled an odor with the nose… having tasted a flavor with the tongue… having touched a tangible with the body… having cognized a mental phenomenon with the mind, he does not grasp the sign, does not grasp the secondary characteristics. Because if he were to dwell with the mind faculty unrestrained, evil, unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might assail him, he practices for its restraint, guards the mind faculty, and undertakes restraint in the mind faculty. It is in this way, friend, that one is guarded in the sense faculties.”

“Kathañcāvuso, bhojane mattaññū hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso āhāraṃ āhāreti – ‘neva davāya, na madāya, na maṇḍanāya, na vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya, vihiṃsūparatiyā, brahmacariyānuggahāya. Iti purāṇañca vedanaṃ paṭihaṅkhāmi, navañca vedanaṃ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me bhavissati[T 4.0132], anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro cā’ti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, bhojane mattaññū hoti.

“And how, friend, is one moderate in eating? Here, friend, a bhikkhu reflects wisely and partakes of food: ‘Not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for adornment, not for beautification, but only for the maintenance and sustenance of this body, for the cessation of discomfort, for the support of the holy life, thinking: “Thus I shall ward off old feelings and not give rise to new feelings, and there will be sustenance for me, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.”’ In this way, friend, one is moderate in eating.”

“Kathañcāvuso, jāgariyaṃ anuyutto hoti? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu divasaṃ caṅkamena nisajjāya [V 2.0111] āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṃ parisodheti. Rattiyā paṭhamaṃ yāmaṃ caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṃ parisodheti[P 4.0105]. Rattiyā majjhimaṃ yāmaṃ dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappeti pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno, uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā. Rattiyā pacchimaṃ yāmaṃ paccuṭṭhāya caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṃ parisodheti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso, jāgariyaṃ [M 2.0324] anuyutto hoti. Tasmātihāvuso, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘indriyesu guttadvārā bhavissāma, bhojane mattaññuno, jāgariyaṃ anuyuttā’ti. Evañhi vo, āvuso, sikkhitabba”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“And how, friend, is one devoted to wakefulness? Here, friend, a bhikkhu purifies his mind from obstructive states by walking and sitting during the day. During the first watch of the night, he purifies his mind from obstructive states by walking and sitting. During the middle watch of the night, he lies down in the lion’s posture on his right side, placing one foot slightly over the other, mindful and fully aware, having established in his mind the perception of rising. During the last watch of the night, he gets up and purifies his mind from obstructive states by walking and sitting. In this way, friend, one is devoted to wakefulness. Therefore, friend, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will be guarded in the sense faculties, moderate in eating, and devoted to wakefulness.’ Thus, friend, should you train yourselves.”

8. Rāhulovādasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse of Advice to Rāhula

121. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “paripakkā kho rāhulassa vimuttiparipācaniyā dhammā; yaṃnūnāhaṃ rāhulaṃ uttariṃ āsavānaṃ khaye vineyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ āmantesi – “gaṇhāhi, rāhula, nisīdanaṃ. Yena andhavanaṃ tenupasaṅkamissāma divāvihārāyā”ti[T 4.0133]. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavato paṭissutvā nisīdanaṃ ādāya bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi.

121. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then, while the Blessed One was in solitude and seclusion, this thought arose in his mind: “The qualities that ripen toward liberation are now mature in Rāhula. What if I were to instruct Rāhula further in the destruction of the taints?” Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and outer robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms. Having walked for alms in Sāvatthī and returned from the alms round, after his meal he addressed the Venerable Rāhula: “Take a sitting cloth, Rāhula. Let us go to Andhavana for the day’s abiding.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Rāhula replied to the Blessed One. Taking a sitting cloth, he followed closely behind the Blessed One.

Tena kho pana samayena anekāni devatāsahassāni bhagavantaṃ anubandhāni honti – “ajja bhagavā āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ uttariṃ āsavānaṃ khaye vinessatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā andhavanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle paññatte āsane nisīdi. Āyasmāpi kho rāhulo bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [P 4.0106] nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

At that time, many thousands of deities were following the Blessed One, thinking, “Today the Blessed One will instruct the Venerable Rāhula further in the destruction of the taints.” Then the Blessed One entered Andhavana and sat down on a prepared seat at the foot of a certain tree. The Venerable Rāhula also, having paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Rāhula who was seated to one side:

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rāhula, cakkhu niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“What do you think, Rāhula, is the eye permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ [V 2.0112] panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard that as: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”. ( ) (taṃ kiṃ maññasi) evamitaresupi (ma. ni. 3.416-417)

“No, venerable sir.”

“Rūpā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti?

“Are forms permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccā, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.” …

“Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“Is eye-consciousness permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.” …

“Cakkhusamphasso nicco vā anicco vā”ti?

“Is eye-contact permanent or impermanent?”

“Anicco, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.” …

“Yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṃ, saññāgataṃ, saṅkhāragataṃ, viññāṇagataṃ, tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“And also this, whatever feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness arises conditioned by eye-contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi[M 2.0325], eso [T 4.0134] me attā’”ti?

“And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard that as: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”…pe….

“No, venerable sir.” …

“Jivhā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti?

“Is the tongue permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccā, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.” …

“Jivhāviññāṇaṃ [V 2.0113] niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“Is tongue-consciousness permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.” …

“Jivhāsamphasso nicco vā anicco vā”ti?

“Is tongue-contact permanent or impermanent?”

“Anicco, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.” …

“Yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṃ, saññāgataṃ, saṅkhāragataṃ, viññāṇagataṃ, tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“And also this, whatever feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness arises conditioned by tongue-contact: is that permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard that as: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”…pe….

“No, venerable sir.” …

“Mano nicco vā anicco vā”ti?

“Is the mind permanent or impermanent?”

“Anicco, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vāti?

“And what is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“And what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard that as: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“No, venerable sir.”

“Dhammā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti?

“Are mental objects permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccā, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.” …

“Manoviññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“Is mind-consciousness permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Manosamphasso nicco vā anicco vā”ti?

“Is mind-contact permanent or impermanent?”

“Anicco, bhante”…pe….

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yampidaṃ [V 2.0114] manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṃ, saññāgataṃ, saṅkhāragataṃ, viññāṇagataṃ, tampi niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“And whatever feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness arises conditioned by mind-contact, is that also permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“And that which is impermanent, is that suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“It is suffering, venerable sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ [T 4.0135] mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard that as: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“No, venerable sir.”

“Evaṃ passaṃ, rāhula, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati, yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ tasmimpi nibbindati…pe… jivhāyapi nibbindati, rasesupi nibbindati, jivhāviññāṇepi nibbindati, jivhāsamphassepi nibbindati, yampidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ tasmimpi nibbindati…pe….

“Seeing thus, Rāhula, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye, disenchanted with forms, disenchanted with eye-consciousness, disenchanted with eye-contact, and also disenchanted with whatever feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness arises conditioned by eye-contact… and so on… becomes disenchanted with the tongue, disenchanted with tastes, disenchanted with tongue-consciousness, disenchanted with tongue-contact, and also disenchanted with whatever feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness arises conditioned by tongue-contact… and so on.

“Manasmimpi nibbindati, dhammesupi nibbindati, manoviññāṇepi nibbindati, manosamphassepi nibbindati, yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ tasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.

“He becomes disenchanted with the mind, disenchanted with mental objects, disenchanted with mind-consciousness, disenchanted with mind-contact, and also disenchanted with whatever feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness arises conditioned by mind-contact. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’”

Idamavoca [V 2.0115] bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā rāhulo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandi. Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne āyasmato rāhulassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimucci. Anekānañca [M 2.0326] devatāsahassānaṃ virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Blessed One said this. Delighted, the Venerable Rāhula rejoiced in the Blessed One’s statement. And while this exposition was being spoken, the mind of the Venerable Rāhula was liberated from the taints through non-clinging. And for many thousands of deities, the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma arose: “Whatever has the nature to arise, all that has the nature to cease.” The Eighth.

9. Saṃyojaniyadhammasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Things Conducive to Fetters

122. “Saṃyojaniye ca, bhikkhave, dhamme desessāmi saṃyojanañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katame [P 4.0108] ca, bhikkhave, saṃyojaniyā dhammā, katamañca saṃyojanaṃ? Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā [T 4.0136] piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, saṃyojaniyā dhammā. Yo tattha chandarāgo, taṃ tattha saṃyojanaṃ…pe… santi, bhikkhave, jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, saṃyojaniyā dhammā. Yo tattha chandarāgo taṃ tattha saṃyojana”nti. Navamaṃ.

122. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the things conducive to fetters and the fetter itself. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, are the things conducive to fetters, and what is the fetter? There are, bhikkhus, forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, agreeable, pleasing, of a lovable nature, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. These, bhikkhus, are called the things conducive to fetters. Whatever desire and lust there is for them, that is the fetter in that regard. … There are, bhikkhus, tastes cognizable by the tongue… There are, bhikkhus, mental phenomena cognizable by the mind—desirable, agreeable, pleasing, of a lovable nature, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. These, bhikkhus, are called the things conducive to fetters. Whatever desire and lust there is for them, that is the fetter in that regard.” The Ninth.

10. Upādāniyadhammasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Things Conducive to Clinging

123. “Upādāniye ca, bhikkhave, dhamme desessāmi upādānañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katame ca, bhikkhave, upādāniyā dhammā, katamañca upādānaṃ? Santi, bhikkhave, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, upādāniyā dhammā. Yo tattha chandarāgo, taṃ tattha upādānaṃ…pe… santi, bhikkhave, jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… santi, bhikkhave, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, upādāniyā dhammā. Yo tattha chandarāgo taṃ tattha upādāna”nti. Dasamaṃ.

123. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the things conducive to clinging and clinging itself. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, are the things conducive to clinging, and what is clinging? There are, bhikkhus, forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, agreeable, pleasing, of a lovable nature, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. These, bhikkhus, are called the things conducive to clinging. Whatever desire and lust there is for them, that is the clinging in that regard. … There are, bhikkhus, tastes cognizable by the tongue… There are, bhikkhus, mental phenomena cognizable by the mind—desirable, agreeable, pleasing, of a lovable nature, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. These, bhikkhus, are called the things conducive to clinging. Whatever desire and lust there is for them, that is the clinging in that regard.” The Tenth.

Lokakāmaguṇavaggo dvādasamo.

The Chapter on Worldly Sensual Pleasures, the Twelfth.

Tassuddānaṃ [V 2.0116] –

The summary verse is:

Mārapāsena dve vuttā, lokakāmaguṇena ca;

Sakko pañcasikho ceva, sāriputto ca rāhulo;

Saṃyojanaṃ upādānaṃ, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

Two are taught concerning Māra's Snare, and two concerning Worldly Sensual Pleasures; Sakka, Pañcasikha, Sāriputta, and Rāhula; The Fetter and Clinging—by these the chapter is declared.

13. Gahapativaggo

13. The Chapter on the Householder

1. Vesālīsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse at Vesālī

124. Ekaṃ [T 4.0137][M 2.0327][P 4.0109] samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Atha kho uggo gahapati vesāliko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho uggo gahapati vesāliko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti? Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?

124. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Then the householder Ugga of Vesālī approached the Blessed One; having approached, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the householder Ugga of Vesālī said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby some beings here do not attain final extinguishment in this very life? And what, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby some beings here do attain final extinguishment in this very life?”

“Santi kho, gahapati, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti tadupādānaṃ. Saupādāno, gahapati, bhikkhu no parinibbāyati…pe… santi kho, gahapati, jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… santi kho, gahapati, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati. Tassa taṃ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti tadupādānaṃ. Saupādāno, gahapati, bhikkhu no parinibbāyati. Ayaṃ kho, gahapati, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo yena midhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti.

“Householder, there are forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, agreeable, pleasing, of a lovable nature, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. If a bhikkhu delights in them, welcomes them, and remains adhering to them, his consciousness becomes dependent on them, with that as its object of clinging.
