Patirūpe kule jāyitvā patirūpaṃ kulaṃ gaccheyyanti – idaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṃ ṭhānaṃ sulabhaṃ katapuññena mātugāmena. Patirūpe kule jāyitvā patirūpaṃ kulaṃ gantvā asapatti agāraṃ ajjhāvaseyyanti – idaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṃ ṭhānaṃ sulabhaṃ katapuññena mātugāmena. Patirūpe kule jāyitvā patirūpaṃ kulaṃ gantvā asapatti agāraṃ ajjhāvasantī puttavatī assanti – idaṃ, bhikkhave, catutthaṃ ṭhānaṃ sulabhaṃ katapuññena mātugāmena. Patirūpe kule [P 4.0250] jāyitvā patirūpaṃ kulaṃ gantvā asapatti agāraṃ ajjhāvasantī [M 2.0446] puttavatī samānā sāmikaṃ abhibhuyya vatteyyanti – idaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcamaṃ ṭhānaṃ sulabhaṃ katapuññena mātugāmena. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca ṭhānāni sulabhāni katapuññena mātugāmenā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, these five possibilities are easy to obtain for a woman who has made merit. What five? ‘May I be born in a suitable family’—this, bhikkhus, is the first possibility that is easy for a woman who has made merit to obtain. ‘Having been born in a suitable family, may I go to a suitable family’—this, bhikkhus, is the second possibility that is easy for a woman who has made merit to obtain. ‘Having been born in a suitable family and gone to a suitable family, may I dwell at home without a co-wife’—this, bhikkhus, is the third possibility that is easy for a woman who has made merit to obtain. ‘Having been born in a suitable family, gone to a suitable family, and dwelling at home without a co-wife, may I have children’—this, bhikkhus, is the fourth possibility that is easy for a woman who has made merit to obtain. ‘Having been born in a suitable family, gone to a suitable family, dwelling at home without a co-wife, and having children, may I live having prevailed over my husband’—this, bhikkhus, is the fifth possibility that is easy for a woman who has made merit to obtain. These, bhikkhus, are the five possibilities that are easy for a woman who has made merit to obtain.”

9. Pañcasīlavisāradasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Confidence in the Five Precepts

312. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo visārado agāraṃ ajjhāvasati. Katamehi pañcahi? Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato ca hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato ca hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato ca hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato ca hoti[T 4.0309], surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato ca hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo visārado agāraṃ ajjhāvasatī”ti. Navamaṃ.

312. “Bhikkhus, a woman endowed with five qualities dwells at home with confidence. With what five? She abstains from the destruction of life, she abstains from taking what is not given, she abstains from sexual misconduct, she abstains from false speech, and she abstains from liquor, wine, and intoxicants, which are the basis for heedlessness. A woman endowed with these five qualities, bhikkhus, dwells at home with confidence.”

10. Vaḍḍhīsuttaṃ

10. The Growth Discourse

313. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, vaḍḍhīhi vaḍḍhamānā ariyasāvikā ariyāya vaḍḍhiyā vaḍḍhati sārādāyinī ca hoti varādāyinī ca kāyassa. Katamehi pañcahi? Saddhāya vaḍḍhati, sīlena vaḍḍhati, sutena vaḍḍhati, cāgena vaḍḍhati, paññāya vaḍḍhati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi [V 2.0245] vaḍḍhīhi vaḍḍhamānā ariyasāvikā ariyāya vaḍḍhiyā vaḍḍhati, sārādāyinī ca hoti, varādāyinī ca kāyassā”ti.

313. “Bhikkhus, growing with these five growths, a noble female disciple grows with a noble growth; she takes the essence and the best for herself. With which five? She grows in faith, she grows in virtue, she grows in learning, she grows in generosity, she grows in wisdom. Growing with these five growths, bhikkhus, a noble female disciple grows with a noble growth; she takes the essence and the best for herself.”

“Saddhāya sīlena ca yādha vaḍḍhati,

Paññāya cāgena sutena cūbhayaṃ;

Sā tādisī sīlavatī upāsikā,

Ādīyati sāramidheva attano”ti. dasamaṃ;

“She who grows here in faith and virtue, in wisdom, generosity, and learning—such a virtuous noble disciple, a female lay follower, takes the essence for herself right here in this life.” Tenth.

Balavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on Strength, the Third.

Tassuddānaṃ [P 4.0251] –

The summary thereof:

Visāradā pasayha abhibhuyya, ekaṃ aṅgena pañcamaṃ;

Nāsenti hetu ṭhānañca, visārado vaḍḍhinā dasāti.

Confident, oppressing, and overwhelming; the one, the limb as the fifth; destruction, cause, and state; confident, and with growth—these are the ten.

Mātugāmasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Women is concluded.

4. Jambukhādakasaṃyuttaṃ

4. The Connected Discourses with Jambukhādaka

1. Nibbānapañhāsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Question about Nibbāna

314. Ekaṃ [T 4.0310][V 2.0246][M 2.0447] samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto magadhesu viharati nālakagāmake. Atha kho jambukhādako paribbājako yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jambukhādako paribbājako āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca –

314. On one occasion, the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling among the Magadhans in the village of Nālaka. Then the wanderer Jambukhādaka approached the Venerable Sāriputta; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta. When he had concluded this courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Jambukhādaka said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“‘Nibbānaṃ, nibbāna’nti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso, nibbāna”nti? “Yo kho, āvuso, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – idaṃ vuccati nibbāna”nti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti. “Katamo [P 4.0252] panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“‘Nibbāna, Nibbāna,’ it is said, friend Sāriputta. Now what, friend, is Nibbāna?” “Friend, the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion—this is called Nibbāna.” “But is there, friend, a path, is there a practice for the realization of this Nibbāna?” “There is, friend, a path, there is a practice for the realization of this Nibbāna.” “And what, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the realization of this Nibbāna?” “It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the realization of this Nibbāna; that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the realization of this Nibbāna.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the realization of this Nibbāna. It is indeed fitting, friend Sāriputta, for the sake of being diligent.” First.

2. Arahattapañhāsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Question about Arahantship

315. “‘Arahattaṃ, arahatta’nti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu [T 4.0311] kho, āvuso[V 2.0247], arahatta”nti? “Yo kho, āvuso, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – idaṃ vuccati arahatta”nti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa arahattassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa arahattassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti. “Katamo [M 2.0448] panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā etassa arahattassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo etassa arahattassa sacchikiriyāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho āvuso, maggo, ayaṃ paṭipadā etassa arahattassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā etassa arahattassa sacchikiriyāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

315. “‘Arahantship, Arahantship,’ it is said, friend Sāriputta. Now what, friend, is Arahantship?” “Friend, the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion—this is called Arahantship.” “But is there a path, friend, is there a practice for the realization of this Arahantship?” “There is a path, friend, there is a practice for the realization of this Arahantship.” “And what, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the realization of this Arahantship?” “It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the realization of this Arahantship; that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the realization of this Arahantship.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the realization of this Arahantship. It is indeed fitting, friend Sāriputta, to be diligent.” Second.

3. Dhammavādīpañhāsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Question about a Speaker of the Dhamma

316. “Ke nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, loke dhammavādino, ke loke suppaṭipannā, ke loke sugatā”ti? “Ye kho, āvuso, rāgappahānāya dhammaṃ desenti, dosappahānāya [P 4.0253] dhammaṃ desenti, mohappahānāya dhammaṃ desenti, te loke dhammavādino. Ye kho, āvuso, rāgassa pahānāya paṭipannā, dosassa pahānāya paṭipannā, mohassa pahānāya paṭipannā, te loke suppaṭipannā. Yesaṃ kho, āvuso, rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo, doso pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo, moho pahīno ucchinnamūlo [T 4.0312] tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo, te loke sugatā”ti.

316. “Friend Sāriputta, who in the world are speakers of the Dhamma, who in the world are those practicing well, who in the world are the well-farers?” “Friend, those who teach the Dhamma for the abandoning of lust, for the abandoning of hatred, for the abandoning of delusion—they are the speakers of the Dhamma in the world. Friend, those who are practicing for the abandoning of lust, for the abandoning of hatred, for the abandoning of delusion—they are those practicing well in the world. Friend, those for whom lust is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, of a nature not to arise again in the future; for whom hatred is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, of a nature not to arise again in the future; for whom delusion is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, of a nature not to arise again in the future—they are the well-farers in the world.”

“Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti. “Katamo, panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo [V 2.0248] bhaddikā paṭipadā, etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“But is there a path, friend, is there a practice for the abandoning of this lust, this hatred, and this delusion?” “There is a path, friend, there is a practice for the abandoning of this lust, this hatred, and this delusion.” “And what, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the abandoning of this lust, this hatred, and this delusion?” “It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the abandoning of this lust, this hatred, and this delusion; that is: right view... right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the abandoning of this lust, this hatred, and this delusion.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the abandoning of this lust, this hatred, and this delusion. It is indeed fitting, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” Third.

4. Kimatthiyasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Purpose

317. “Kimatthiyaṃ[M 2.0449], āvuso sāriputta, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti? “Dukkhassa kho, āvuso, pariññatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa pariññāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etassa dukkhassa pariññāyā”ti? “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etassa dukkhassa pariññāyā”ti?

317. “Friend Sāriputta, for what purpose is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?” “Friend, it is for the full understanding of suffering that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.” “But friend, is there a path, is there a practice for the full understanding of this suffering?” “Indeed, friend, there is a path, there is a practice for the full understanding of this suffering.” “And what, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the full understanding of this suffering?”

“Ayameva [P 4.0254] kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, etassa dukkhassa pariññāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo [T 4.0313] ayaṃ paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa pariññāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etassa dukkhassa pariññāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Friend, this very Noble Eightfold Path is for the full understanding of this suffering; that is: right view... right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the full understanding of this suffering.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the full understanding of this suffering. It is indeed fitting, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” Fourth.

5. Assāsappattasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Attaining Comfort

318. “‘Assāsappatto, assāsappatto’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, assāsappatto hotī”ti? “Yato kho, āvuso, bhikkhu channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ettāvatā kho, āvuso, assāsappatto hotī”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etassa assāsassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etassa assāsassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti. “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etassa assāsassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo etassa assāsassa sacchikiriyāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso[V 2.0249], maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etassa assāsassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etassa assāsassa sacchikiriyāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

318. “Friend Sāriputta, it is said, ‘one who has attained comfort, one who has attained comfort.’ To what extent, friend, is one who has attained comfort?” “Friend, when a bhikkhu knows as it really is the origin and the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to the six bases for contact, to that extent, friend, one has attained comfort.” “But friend, is there a path, is there a practice for the realization of this comfort?” “Indeed, friend, there is a path, there is a practice for the realization of this comfort.” “And what, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the realization of this comfort?” “Friend, this very Noble Eightfold Path is for the realization of this comfort; that is: right view... right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the realization of this comfort.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the realization of this comfort. It is indeed fitting, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” Fifth.

6. Paramassāsappattasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Attaining Supreme Comfort

319. “‘Paramassāsappatto, paramassāsappatto’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, paramassāsappatto hotī”ti? “Yato [M 2.0450] kho, āvuso, bhikkhu channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ samudayañca [P 4.0255] atthaṅgamañca assādañca [T 4.0314] ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādāvimutto hoti, ettāvatā kho, āvuso, paramassāsappatto hotī”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etassa paramassāsassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etassa paramassāsassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti. “Katamo pana, āvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etassa paramassāsassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo etassa paramassāsassa sacchikiriyāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etassa paramassāsassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etassa paramassāsassa sacchikiriyāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

319. “Friend Sāriputta, it is said, ‘one who has attained supreme comfort, one who has attained supreme comfort.’ To what extent, friend, is one who has attained supreme comfort?” “Friend, when a bhikkhu, having understood as it really is the origin and the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to the six bases for contact, is liberated through non-clinging, to that extent, friend, one has attained supreme comfort.” “But, friend, is there a path, is there a practice for the realization of this supreme comfort?” “There is, friend, a path, there is a practice for the realization of this supreme comfort.” “What, friend, is the path, what is the practice for the realization of this supreme comfort?” “This very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, is for the realization of this supreme comfort; that is: right view... right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the realization of this supreme comfort.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the realization of this supreme comfort. It is indeed fitting, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” Sixth.

7. Vedanāpañhāsuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Question of Feeling

320. “‘Vedanā, vedanā’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, āvuso, vedanā”ti? “Tisso imāvuso, vedanā. Katamā tisso? Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā – imā kho, āvuso, tisso vedanā”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etāsaṃ tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etāsaṃ tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāyā”ti. “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etāsaṃ tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko [T 4.0315] maggo, etāsaṃ tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo [V 2.0250] sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etāsaṃ tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etāsaṃ tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

320. “‘Feeling, feeling,’ friend Sāriputta, it is said. What now, friend, are feelings?” “There are, friend, these three feelings. Which three? Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These, friend, are the three feelings.” “But, friend, is there a path, is there a practice for the full understanding of these three feelings?” “There is, friend, a path, there is a practice for the full understanding of these three feelings.” “What now, friend, is the path, what is the practice for the full understanding of these three feelings?” “This very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, is for the full understanding of these three feelings, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the full understanding of these three feelings.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the full understanding of these three feelings. And it is sufficient, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” The seventh.

8. Āsavapañhāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Question of the Taints

321. “‘Āsavo[P 4.0256], āsavo’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, āvuso, āsavo”ti? “Tayo me, āvuso, āsavā[M 2.0451]. Kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, avijjāsavo – ime kho, āvuso, tayo āsavā”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etesaṃ āsavānaṃ pahānāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etesaṃ āsavānaṃ pahānāyā”ti. “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā etesaṃ āsavānaṃ pahānāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo etesaṃ āsavānaṃ pahānāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etesaṃ āsavānaṃ pahānāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etesaṃ āsavānaṃ pahānāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

321. “‘Taint, taint,’ friend Sāriputta, it is said. What, friend, is a taint?” “There are, friend, these three taints: the taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance. These, friend, are the three taints.” “But is there, friend, a path, is there a practice for the abandoning of these taints?” “There is, friend, a path, there is a practice for the abandoning of these taints.” “And what, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the abandoning of these taints?” “It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the abandoning of these taints, that is to say: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the abandoning of these taints.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, and excellent is the practice for the abandoning of these taints. And it is sufficient, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” The eighth.

9. Avijjāpañhāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Question of Ignorance

322. “‘Avijjā, avijjā’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, āvuso, avijjā”ti? “Yaṃ kho, āvuso, dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya [T 4.0316] aññāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccatāvuso, avijjā”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etissā avijjāya pahānāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etissā avijjāya pahānāyā”ti. “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etissā avijjāya pahānāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, etissā avijjāya pahānāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo [V 2.0251] sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etissā avijjāya pahānāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etissā avijjāya [P 4.0257] pahānāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Navamaṃ.

322. “‘Ignorance, ignorance,’ friend Sāriputta, it is said. What, friend, is ignorance?” “Whatever ignorance there is, friend, concerning suffering, concerning the origin of suffering, concerning the cessation of suffering, and concerning the practice leading to the cessation of suffering—this, friend, is called ignorance.” “But is there, friend, a path, is there a practice for the abandoning of this ignorance?” “There is, friend, a path, there is a practice for the abandoning of this ignorance.” “And what, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the abandoning of this ignorance?” “It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the abandoning of this ignorance, that is to say: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the abandoning of this ignorance.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, and excellent is the practice for the abandoning of this ignorance. And it is sufficient, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” The ninth.

10. Taṇhāpañhāsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Question of Craving

323. “‘Taṇhā, taṇhā’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, āvuso, taṇhā”ti? “Tisso imā, āvuso, taṇhā. Kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā – imā kho, āvuso, tisso taṇhā”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etāsaṃ taṇhānaṃ pahānāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etāsaṃ taṇhānaṃ pahānāyā”ti. “Katamo [M 2.0452] panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etāsaṃ taṇhānaṃ pahānāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, etāsaṃ taṇhānaṃ pahānāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etāsaṃ taṇhānaṃ pahānāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā[T 4.0317], etāsaṃ taṇhānaṃ pahānāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

323. “‘Craving, craving,’ friend Sāriputta, it is said. What, friend, is craving?” “Friend, there are these three cravings: craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence. These, friend, are the three cravings.” “But is there, friend, a path and a practice for the abandoning of these cravings?” “There is, friend, a path and a practice for the abandoning of these cravings.” “And what, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the abandoning of these cravings?” “It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the abandoning of these cravings; that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, friend, is the path, and this is the practice for the abandoning of these cravings.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the abandoning of these cravings. And it is sufficient, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” The tenth.

11. Oghapañhāsuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on the Question of the Floods

324. “‘Ogho, ogho’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, āvuso, ogho”ti? “Cattārome, āvuso, oghā. Kāmogho, bhavogho, diṭṭhogho, avijjogho – ime kho, āvuso, cattāro oghā”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etesaṃ oghānaṃ pahānāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etesaṃ oghānaṃ pahānāyā”ti. “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etesaṃ oghānaṃ pahānāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, etesaṃ oghānaṃ pahānāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi[P 4.0258]. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etesaṃ oghānaṃ pahānāyā”ti. “Bhaddako[V 2.0252], āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etesaṃ oghānaṃ pahānāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

324. “‘Flood, flood,’ friend Sāriputta, it is said. What, friend, is the flood?” “There are, friend, these four floods: the flood of sensual desire, the flood of existence, the flood of views, and the flood of ignorance. These, friend, are the four floods.” “Is there, friend, a path, is there a practice for the abandoning of these floods?” “There is, friend, a path, there is a practice for the abandoning of these floods.” “What, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the abandoning of these floods?” “It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the abandoning of these floods, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the abandoning of these floods.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the abandoning of these floods. And it is sufficient, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” Eleventh.

12. Upādānapañhāsuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on the Question about Clinging

325. “‘Upādānaṃ, upādāna’nti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso, upādāna”nti? “Cattārimāni, āvuso, upādānāni. Kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhupādānaṃ sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ – imāni kho, āvuso, cattāri upādānānī”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etesaṃ upādānānaṃ pahānāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etesaṃ upādānānaṃ pahānāyā”ti[T 4.0318]. “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etesaṃ upādānānaṃ pahānāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, etesaṃ upādānānaṃ pahānāya, seyyathidaṃ [M 2.0453] – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etesaṃ upādānānaṃ pahānāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etesaṃ upādānānaṃ pahānāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

325. “‘Clinging, clinging,’ friend Sāriputta, it is said. What, friend, is clinging?” “There are, friend, these four clingings: clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to a doctrine of self. These, friend, are the four clingings.” “Is there, friend, a path, is there a practice for the abandoning of these clingings?” “There is, friend, a path, there is a practice for the abandoning of these clingings.” “What, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the abandoning of these clingings?” “It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the abandoning of these clingings, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the abandoning of these clingings.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the abandoning of these clingings. And it is sufficient, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” Twelfth.

13. Bhavapañhāsuttaṃ

13. The Discourse on the Question about Becoming

326. “‘Bhavo, bhavo’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, āvuso, bhavo”ti? “Tayo me, āvuso, bhavā. Kāmabhavo, rūpabhavo, arūpabhavo – ime kho, āvuso, tayo bhavā”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etesaṃ bhavānaṃ pariññāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etesaṃ bhavānaṃ pariññāyā”ti. “Katamo, panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etesaṃ bhavānaṃ pariññāyā”ti? “Ayameva [P 4.0259] kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, etesaṃ bhavānaṃ pariññāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etesaṃ bhavānaṃ pariññāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etesaṃ bhavānaṃ pariññāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Terasamaṃ.

326. “‘Becoming, becoming,’ friend Sāriputta, it is said. What, friend, is becoming?” “There are, friend, these three becomings: sense-sphere becoming, fine-material-sphere becoming, and immaterial-sphere becoming. These, friend, are the three becomings.” “Is there, friend, a path, is there a practice for the full understanding of these becomings?” “There is, friend, a path, there is a practice for the full understanding of these becomings.” “What, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the full understanding of these becomings?” “It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the full understanding of these becomings, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the full understanding of these becomings.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the full understanding of these becomings. And it is sufficient, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” Thirteenth.

14. Dukkhapañhāsuttaṃ

14. The Discourse on the Question about Suffering

327. “‘Dukkhaṃ[V 2.0253], dukkha’nti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso, dukkha”nti? “Tisso imā, āvuso, dukkhatā. Dukkhadukkhatā, saṅkhāradukkhatā[T 4.0319], vipariṇāmadukkhatā – imā kho, āvuso, tisso dukkhatā”ti. “Atthi panāvuso maggo atthi paṭipadā, etāsaṃ dukkhatānaṃ pariññāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etāsaṃ dukkhatānaṃ pariññāyā”ti. “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etāsaṃ dukkhatānaṃ pariññāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, etāsaṃ dukkhatānaṃ pariññāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etāsaṃ dukkhatānaṃ pariññāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etāsaṃ dukkhatānaṃ pariññāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Cuddasamaṃ.

327. “‘Suffering, suffering,’ friend Sāriputta, it is said. What, friend, is suffering?” “There are, friend, these three kinds of suffering: the suffering of pain, the suffering due to formations, and the suffering due to change. These, friend, are the three kinds of suffering.” “Is there, friend, a path, is there a practice for the full understanding of these kinds of suffering?” “There is, friend, a path, there is a practice for the full understanding of these kinds of suffering.” “What, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the full understanding of these kinds of suffering?” “It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the full understanding of these kinds of suffering, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the full understanding of these kinds of suffering.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the full understanding of these kinds of suffering. And it is sufficient, friend Sāriputta, for heedfulness.” Fourteenth.

15. Sakkāyapañhāsuttaṃ

15. The Discourse on the Question about Identity

328. “‘Sakkāyo[M 2.0454], sakkāyo’ti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, āvuso, sakkāyo”ti? “Pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā sakkāyo vutto bhagavatā, seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho[P 4.0260]. Ime kho, āvuso, pañcupādānakkhandhā sakkāyo vutto bhagavatā”ti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etassa sakkāyassa pariññāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etassa sakkāyassa pariññāyā”ti. “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā, etassa sakkāyassa pariññāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, etassa sakkāyassa pariññāya[T 4.0320], seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etassa sakkāyassa pariññāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etassa sakkāyassa pariññāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Pannarasamaṃ.

328. “‘Identity, identity,’ friend Sāriputta, it is said. What, friend, is identity?” “These five aggregates subject to clinging, friend, have been called identity by the Blessed One, namely: the aggregate of form subject to clinging, the aggregate of feeling subject to clinging, the aggregate of perception subject to clinging, the aggregate of volitional formations subject to clinging, the aggregate of consciousness subject to clinging. These five aggregates subject to clinging, friend, have been called identity by the Blessed One.” “But, friend, is there a path, is there a way for the full understanding of this identity?” “There is, friend, a path, a way for the full understanding of this identity.” “And what, friend, is that path, what is that way for the full understanding of this identity?” “It is this Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the full understanding of this identity, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the way for the full understanding of this identity.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the way for the full understanding of this identity. And it is indeed fitting, friend Sāriputta, to be heedful.”

16. Dukkarapañhāsuttaṃ

16. The Discourse on the Question of What is Difficult

329. “Kiṃ [V 2.0254] nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye dukkara”nti? “Pabbajjā kho, āvuso, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye dukkarā”ti. “Pabbajitena panāvuso, kiṃ dukkara”nti? “Pabbajitena kho, āvuso, abhirati dukkarā”ti. “Abhiratena panāvuso, kiṃ dukkara”nti? “Abhiratena kho, āvuso, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti dukkarā”ti. “Kīvaciraṃ panāvuso, dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhu arahaṃ assā”ti? “Naciraṃ, āvuso”ti. Soḷasamaṃ.

329. “What, friend Sāriputta, is difficult to do in this Dhamma and Discipline?” “Going forth, friend, is difficult to do in this Dhamma and Discipline.” “And for one who has gone forth, friend, what is difficult to do?” “For one who has gone forth, friend, delight is difficult to do.” “And for one who has delight, friend, what is difficult to do?” “For one who has delight, friend, the practice in accordance with the supramundane Dhamma is difficult to do.” “And how long, friend, would a monk who practices in accordance with the supramundane Dhamma take to become an arahant?” “Not long, friend.”

Jambukhādakasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses with Jambukhādaka is complete.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Nibbānaṃ arahattañca, dhammavādī [P 4.0261] kimatthiyaṃ;

Assāso paramassāso, vedanā āsavāvijjā;

Taṇhā oghā upādānaṃ, bhavo dukkhañca sakkāyo.

Imasmiṃ dhammavinaye dukkaranti.

Nibbāna and arahantship; the speaker on Dhamma; for what purpose; assurance; the highest assurance; feeling; taints; ignorance; craving; floods; clinging; existence; suffering; identity; and what is difficult to do in this Dhamma and Discipline.

5. Sāmaṇḍakasaṃyuttaṃ

5. The Connected Discourses with Sāmaṇḍaka

1. Sāmaṇḍakasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse with Sāmaṇḍaka

330. Ekaṃ [T 4.0321][V 2.0255][M 2.0455] samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto vajjīsu viharati ukkacelāyaṃ gaṅgāya nadiyā tīre. Atha kho sāmaṇḍako sāmaṇḍakāni (sī.) paribbājako yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho sāmaṇḍako paribbājako āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca –

330. At one time the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling among the Vajjis, at Ukkacelā on the bank of the river Ganges. Then the wanderer Sāmaṇḍaka approached the Venerable Sāriputta. Having approached, he exchanged joyful greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta. When the joyful and memorable talk was concluded, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the wanderer Sāmaṇḍaka said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“‘Nibbānaṃ, nibbāna’nti, āvuso sāriputta, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso, nibbāna”nti? “Yo kho, āvuso, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – idaṃ vuccati nibbāna”nti. “Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, āvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā, etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.

“‘Nibbāna, Nibbāna,’ it is said, friend Sāriputta. What, friend, is Nibbāna?” “Friend, whatever is the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion—this is called Nibbāna.” “But is there a path, friend, is there a practice for the realization of this Nibbāna?” “There is indeed a path, friend, there is indeed a practice for the realization of this Nibbāna.”

“Katamo [P 4.0262] panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti? “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā, etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti. “Bhaddako, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā, etassa nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya. Alañca panāvuso sāriputta, appamādāyā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And what, friend, is that path, what is that practice for the realization of this Nibbāna?” “It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, friend, for the realization of this Nibbāna, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. This, friend, is the path, this is the practice for the realization of this Nibbāna.” “Excellent, friend, is the path, excellent is the practice for the realization of this Nibbāna. And it is indeed fitting, friend Sāriputta, to be heedful.”

(Yathā jambukhādakasaṃyuttaṃ, tathā vitthāretabbaṃ).

(As with the Connected Discourses with Jambukhādaka, so should this be elaborated in detail.)

2. Dukkarasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on What is Difficult

331. “Kiṃ [V 2.0256][M 2.0456] nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye dukkara”nti[T 4.0322]? “Pabbajjā kho, āvuso, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye dukkarā”ti. “Pabbajitena panāvuso, kiṃ dukkara”nti? “Pabbajitena kho, āvuso, abhirati dukkarā”ti. “Abhiratena panāvuso, kiṃ dukkara”nti? “Abhiratena kho, āvuso, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti dukkarā”ti. “Kīvaciraṃ panāvuso, dhammānudhammappaṭipanno bhikkhu arahaṃ assā”ti? “Naciraṃ, āvuso”ti. Soḷasamaṃ.

331. “Friend Sāriputta, what is difficult to do in this Dhamma and Discipline?” “Friend, in this Dhamma and Discipline, the going forth is difficult to do.” “But for one who has gone forth, friend, what is difficult to do?” “Friend, for one who has gone forth, delight is difficult to do.” “But for one who has delight, friend, what is difficult to do?” “Friend, for one who has delight, the practice in accordance with the supramundane Dhamma is difficult to do.” “But how long, friend, until a bhikkhu who practices in accordance with the supramundane Dhamma would become an Arahant?” “Not long, friend.”

(Purimakasadisaṃ uddānaṃ.)

(The summary is similar to the previous one.)

Sāmaṇḍakasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses with Sāmaṇḍaka is complete.

6. Moggallānasaṃyuttaṃ

6. The Connected Discourses with Moggallāna

1. Paṭhamajhānapañhāsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Question of the First Jhāna

332. Ekaṃ [T 4.0323][V 2.0257][M 2.0457] samayaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra [P 4.0263] kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso, bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

332. At one time, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. There, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna addressed the bhikkhus: “Friends, bhikkhus!” “Friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this:

“Idha mayhaṃ, āvuso, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ, paṭhamaṃ jhāna’nti vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho paṭhamaṃ jhānanti? Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘idha bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ vuccati paṭhamaṃ jhāna’nti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato kāmasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.

“Friends, while I was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in my mind: ‘The first jhāna, the first jhāna,’ it is said. Now what is the first jhāna? Then, friends, it occurred to me: ‘Here, a bhikkhu, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. This is called the first jhāna.’ So I, friends, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enter and abide in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. While I am abiding in this state, friends, perceptions and instances of attention connected with sensual pleasures arise in me.”

“Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna! Mā, brāhmaṇa, paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ pamādo, paṭhame jhāne cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, paṭhame jhāne cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi ekodikarohi (pī.), paṭhame jhāne cittaṃ samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi [T 4.0324] savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṃ patto’ti, mamaṃ taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṃ patto’”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by means of psychic power and said this: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna! Brahmin, do not be heedless regarding the first jhāna. Settle your mind in the first jhāna, unify your mind in the first jhāna, concentrate your mind in the first jhāna.’ So I, friends, on a later occasion, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, entered and abode in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. Friends, if one speaking rightly were to say, ‘A disciple favored by the Teacher has attained great direct knowledge,’ it is of me that one, speaking rightly, would say: ‘A disciple favored by the Teacher has attained great direct knowledge.’” The first.

2. Dutiyajhānapañhāsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Question of the Second Jhāna

333. “‘Dutiyaṃ [V 2.0258][M 2.0458] jhānaṃ, dutiyaṃ jhāna’nti vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho dutiyaṃ jhānanti? Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘idha bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ [P 4.0264] vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ vuccati dutiyaṃ jhāna’nti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato vitakkasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.

333. “‘The second jhāna, the second jhāna,’ it is said. What is the second jhāna? Then, friends, it occurred to me: ‘Here, a bhikkhu, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, enters and abides in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and has rapture and pleasure born of concentration. This is called the second jhāna.’ So I, friends, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, enter and abide in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and has rapture and pleasure born of concentration. While I am abiding in this state, friends, perceptions and instances of attention accompanied by applied thought arise in me.”

“Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna! Mā, brāhmaṇa, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ pamādo, dutiye jhāne cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, dutiye jhāne cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, dutiye jhāne cittaṃ samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṃ patto’ti, mamaṃ taṃ [T 4.0325] sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṃ patto’”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by means of psychic power and said this: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna! Brahmin, do not be heedless regarding the second jhāna. Settle your mind in the second jhāna, unify your mind in the second jhāna, concentrate your mind in the second jhāna.’ So I, friends, on a later occasion, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, entered and abode in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and has rapture and pleasure born of concentration. Friends, if one speaking rightly were to say, ‘A disciple favored by the Teacher has attained great direct knowledge,’ it is of me that one, speaking rightly, would say: ‘A disciple favored by the Teacher has attained great direct knowledge.’” The second.

3. Tatiyajhānapañhāsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Question of the Third Jhāna

334. “‘Tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ, tatiyaṃ jhāna’nti vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho tatiyaṃ jhānanti? Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – idha bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ vuccati tatiyaṃ jhānanti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharāmi sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedemi. Yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato pītisahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.

334. “‘The third jhāna, the third jhāna,’ it is said. What is the third jhāna? Then, friends, it occurred to me: ‘Here, a bhikkhu, with the fading away of rapture, abides equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and experiences pleasure with the body; he enters and abides in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: “Equanimous and mindful, one has a pleasant abiding.” This is called the third jhāna.’ So I, friends, with the fading away of rapture, abide equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and experience pleasure with the body; I enter and abide in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: “Equanimous and mindful, one has a pleasant abiding.” While I am abiding in this state, friends, perceptions and instances of attention accompanied by rapture arise in me.”

“Atha [V 2.0259][M 2.0459][P 4.0265] kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna! Mā, brāhmaṇa, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ pamādo, tatiye jhāne cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, tatiye jhāne cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, tatiye jhāne cittaṃ samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharāmi sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedemi, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Yañhi taṃ āvuso sammā vadamāno vadeyya…pe… mahābhiññataṃ patto”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by means of psychic power and said this: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna! Brahmin, do not be heedless regarding the third jhāna. Settle your mind in the third jhāna, unify your mind in the third jhāna, concentrate your mind in the third jhāna.’ So I, friends, on a later occasion, with the fading away of rapture, abode equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and experienced pleasure with the body; I entered and abode in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: “Equanimous and mindful, one has a pleasant abiding.” Friends, if one speaking rightly were to say, ‘A disciple favored by the Teacher has attained great direct knowledge,’ it is of me that one, speaking rightly, would say: ‘A disciple favored by the Teacher has attained great direct knowledge.’” The third.

4. Catutthajhānapañhāsuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Question of the Fourth Jhāna

335. “‘Catutthaṃ jhānaṃ[T 4.0326], catutthaṃ jhāna’nti vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho catutthaṃ jhānanti? Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘idha bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ vuccati catutthaṃ jhāna’nti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato sukhasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.

335. “‘The fourth jhāna, the fourth jhāna,’ it is said. What, then, is the fourth jhāna? Friends, this thought occurred to me: ‘Here, a bhikkhu, with the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain, and with the previous passing away of joy and grief, enters and abides in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. This is called the fourth jhāna.’ And so, friends, with the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain, and with the previous passing away of joy and grief, I enter and abide in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. Friends, as I was dwelling in this abiding, perceptions and acts of attention accompanied by pleasure assailed me.

“Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna! Mā, brāhmaṇa, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ pamādo, catutthe jhāne cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, catutthe jhāne cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, catutthe jhāne cittaṃ samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ [P 4.0266] atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya…pe… mahābhiññataṃ patto”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by his psychic power and said this: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna! Brahmin, do not be negligent regarding the fourth jhāna. Settle your mind in the fourth jhāna, make your mind one-pointed in the fourth jhāna, concentrate your mind in the fourth jhāna.’ And so, friends, at a later time, with the abandoning of pleasure and the abandoning of pain, and with the previous passing away of joy and grief, I entered and abided in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. Friends, if anyone, speaking rightly, were to say of someone that he has attained the state of great direct knowledge, it is of me that he would rightly speak.” The fourth.

5. Ākāsānañcāyatanapañhāsuttaṃ

5. The Sutta on the Question of the Sphere of Infinite Space

336. “‘Ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ, ākāsānañcāyatana’nti vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho ākāsānañcāyatananti[V 2.0260]? Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘idha [M 2.0460] bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ [T 4.0327] amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ vuccati ākāsānañcāyatana’nti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato rūpasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.

336. “‘The sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite space,’ it is said. What, then, is the sphere of infinite space? Then, friends, this thought occurred to me: ‘Here, a bhikkhu, with the complete transcending of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impingement, and not attending to perceptions of diversity, (thinking) “Space is infinite,” enters and abides in the sphere of infinite space. This is called the sphere of infinite space.’ And so, friends, with the complete transcending of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impingement, and not attending to perceptions of diversity, (thinking) ‘Space is infinite,’ I enter and abide in the sphere of infinite space. Friends, as I was dwelling in this abiding, perceptions and acts of attention accompanied by form assailed me.

“Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna! Mā, brāhmaṇa, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ pamādo, ākāsānañcāyatane cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, ākāsānañcāyatane cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, ākāsānañcāyatane cittaṃ samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya…pe… mahābhiññataṃ patto”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by his psychic power and said: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna! Brahmin, do not be negligent regarding the sphere of infinite space. Settle your mind in the sphere of infinite space, make your mind one-pointed in the sphere of infinite space, concentrate your mind in the sphere of infinite space.’ And so, friends, at a later time, with the complete transcending of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impingement, and not attending to perceptions of diversity, (thinking) ‘Space is infinite,’ I entered and abided in the sphere of infinite space. Friends, if anyone, speaking rightly, were to say of someone that he has attained the state of great direct knowledge, it is of me that he would rightly speak.” The fifth.

6. Viññāṇañcāyatanapañhāsuttaṃ

6. The Sutta on the Question of the Sphere of Infinite Consciousness

337. “‘Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ, viññāṇañcāyatana’nti vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho viññāṇañcāyatananti? Tassa [P 4.0267] mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘idha bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma anantaṃ viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ vuccati viññāṇañcāyatana’nti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma anantaṃ viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi[T 4.0328]. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato ākāsānañcāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.

337. “‘The sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of infinite consciousness,’ it is said. What, then, is the sphere of infinite consciousness? Then, friends, this thought occurred to me: ‘Here, a bhikkhu, having entirely transcended the sphere of infinite space, (perceiving) “Consciousness is infinite,” enters and abides in the sphere of infinite consciousness. This is called the sphere of infinite consciousness.’ And so, friends, having entirely transcended the sphere of infinite space, (perceiving) ‘Consciousness is infinite,’ I enter and abide in the sphere of infinite consciousness. Friends, as I was dwelling in this abiding, perceptions and acts of attention associated with the sphere of infinite space assailed me.

“Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna! Mā, brāhmaṇa, viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ pamādo, viññāṇañcāyatane [V 2.0261] cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, viññāṇañcāyatane cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, viññāṇañcāyatane cittaṃ samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma anantaṃ viññāṇanti [M 2.0461] viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya…pe… mahābhiññataṃ patto”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by his psychic power and said: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna! Brahmin, do not be negligent regarding the sphere of infinite consciousness. Settle your mind in the sphere of infinite consciousness, make your mind one-pointed in the sphere of infinite consciousness, concentrate your mind in the sphere of infinite consciousness.’ And so, friends, at a later time, having entirely transcended the sphere of infinite space, (perceiving) ‘Consciousness is infinite,’ I entered and abided in the sphere of infinite consciousness. Friends, if anyone, speaking rightly, were to say of someone that he has attained the state of great direct knowledge, it is of me that he would rightly speak.” Sixth.

7. Ākiñcaññāyatanapañhāsuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on the Question of the Base of Nothingness

338. “‘Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ, ākiñcaññāyatana’nti vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho ākiñcaññāyatananti? Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘idha bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma natthi kiñcīti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ vuccati ākiñcaññāyatana’nti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma natthi kiñcīti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato viññāṇañcāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.

338. “‘The base of nothingness, the base of nothingness,’ it is said. What, then, is the base of nothingness? Then, friends, this thought occurred to me: ‘Here, a bhikkhu, having completely transcended the base of infinite consciousness, (thinking) “There is nothing,” enters and abides in the base of nothingness. This is called the base of nothingness.’ And so, friends, having completely transcended the base of infinite consciousness, (thinking) ‘There is nothing,’ I enter and abide in the base of nothingness. Friends, as I was dwelling in this abiding, perceptions and acts of attention associated with the base of infinite consciousness assailed me.

“Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna! Mā, brāhmaṇa, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ pamādo, ākiñcaññāyatane cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, ākiñcaññāyatane [P 4.0268] cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, ākiñcaññāyatane [T 4.0329] cittaṃ samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma natthi kiñcīti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya…pe… mahābhiññataṃ patto”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by psychic power and said this: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna! Brahmin, do not be heedless regarding the base of nothingness. Establish your mind in the base of nothingness, make your mind one-pointed in the base of nothingness, concentrate your mind in the base of nothingness.’ So, friends, at a later time, having completely transcended the base of infinite consciousness, thinking ‘There is nothing,’ I entered and abided in the base of nothingness. Friends, if one speaking rightly were to say… and so on… ‘he has attained great direct knowledge,’ it is of me that they would be speaking.” Seventh.

8. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanapañhāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Question of the Base of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-Perception

339. “‘Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatana’nti vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho nevasaññānāsaññāyatananti? Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘idha bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ vuccati nevasaññānāsaññāyatana’nti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ [V 2.0262] upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato ākiñcaññāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.

339. “‘The base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception’—so it is said. What, friends, is the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception? Then, friends, this thought occurred to me: ‘Here, a monk, having completely transcended the base of nothingness, enters and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. This is called the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.’ So, friends, having completely transcended the base of nothingness, I enter and abide in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. To me, friends, while abiding in this abiding, perceptions and attentions associated with the base of nothingness arise.

“Atha [M 2.0462] kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna! Mā, brāhmaṇa, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ pamādo, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṃ samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya…pe… mahābhiññataṃ patto”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by psychic power and said this: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna! Brahmin, do not be heedless regarding the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Establish your mind in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, make your mind one-pointed in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, concentrate your mind in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.’ So, friends, at a later time, having completely transcended the base of nothingness, I entered and abided in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Friends, if one speaking rightly were to say… and so on… ‘he has attained great direct knowledge,’ it is of me that they would be speaking.” Eighth.

9. Animittapañhāsuttaṃ

9. The Sutta on the Question of the Signless

340. “‘Animitto [T 4.0330] cetosamādhi, animitto cetosamādhī’ti vuccati. Katamo nu kho animitto cetosamādhīti? Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – ‘idha bhikkhu sabbanimittānaṃ [P 4.0269] amanasikārā animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati animitto cetosamādhī’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbanimittānaṃ amanasikārā animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato nimittānusāri viññāṇaṃ hoti.

340. “‘The signless concentration of mind, the signless concentration of mind’—so it is said. What, friends, is the signless concentration of mind? To me, friends, this thought occurred: ‘Here, a monk, by not attending to all signs, enters and abides in the signless concentration of mind. This is called the signless concentration of mind.’ So I, friends, by not attending to all signs, enter and abide in the signless concentration of mind. For me, friends, while abiding in this state, consciousness that follows after signs arises.

“Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘moggallāna, moggallāna! Mā, brāhmaṇa, animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ pamādo, animitte cetosamādhismiṃ cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, animitte cetosamādhismiṃ cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, animitte cetosamādhismiṃ cittaṃ samādahā’ti. So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena sabbanimittānaṃ amanasikārā animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṃ patto’ti, mamaṃ taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṃ patto’”ti. Navamaṃ.

“Then, friends, the Blessed One approached me by means of psychic power and said this: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna! Brahmin, be not negligent regarding the signless concentration of mind. In the signless concentration of mind, establish your mind; in the signless concentration of mind, make your mind one-pointed; in the signless concentration of mind, concentrate your mind.’ So I, friends, at a later time, by not attending to all signs, entered and abided in the signless concentration of mind. Friends, if one were to speak rightly, one would say: ‘A disciple supported by the Teacher has attained to great direct knowledge.’ Speaking rightly, one would say this of me: ‘A disciple supported by the Teacher has attained to great direct knowledge.’” The ninth.

10. Sakkasuttaṃ

10. The Sutta on Sakka

341. Atha [V 2.0263] kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya; evameva – jetavane antarahito devesu tāvatiṃsesu pāturahosi[M 2.0463]. Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ [T 4.0331] yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [P 4.0270] āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

341. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—vanished from the Jeta Grove and reappeared among the Tāvatiṃsa devas. Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna with five hundred devas. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and stood to one side. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to Sakka, the lord of the devas, who was standing to one side:

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhasaraṇagamanaṃ buddhaṃ saraṇagamanaṃ (sī.) hoti. Buddhasaraṇagamanahetu buddhaṃ saraṇagamanahetu (sī.) kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sādhu kho, devānaminda, dhammasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Dhammasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sādhu kho, devānaminda, saṅghasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Saṅghasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

“Good indeed, lord of the devas, is going for refuge to the Buddha. Because of going for refuge to the Buddha, lord of the devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, lord of the devas, is going for refuge to the Dhamma. Because of going for refuge to the Dhamma, lord of the devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, lord of the devas, is going for refuge to the Saṅgha. Because of going for refuge to the Saṅgha, lord of the devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Buddhasaraṇagamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhammasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Dhammasaraṇagamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, saṅgha…pe… sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

“Good indeed, venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Buddha. Because of going for refuge to the Buddha, venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Dhamma. Because of going for refuge to the Dhamma, venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Saṅgha… are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

Atha kho sakko devānamindo chahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe… atha kho sakko devānamindo sattahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe… atha [T 4.0332] kho sakko devānamindo aṭṭhahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe… atha kho sakko devānamindo asītiyā devatāsahassehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā [V 2.0264] ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā [P 4.0271] mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, together with six hundred devas… and so on… Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, together with seven hundred devas… and so on… Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, together with eight hundred devas… and so on… Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, together with eighty thousand devas, approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and stood to one side. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to Sakka, the lord of the devas, who was standing to one side:

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Buddhasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sādhu kho, devānaminda, dhammasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Dhammasaraṇagamanahetu [M 2.0464] kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sādhu kho, devānaminda, saṅghasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Saṅghasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

“Good indeed, lord of the devas, is going for refuge to the Buddha. Because of going for refuge to the Buddha, lord of the devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, lord of the devas, is going for refuge to the Dhamma. Because of going for refuge to the Dhamma, lord of the devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, lord of the devas, is going for refuge to the Saṅgha. Because of going for refuge to the Saṅgha, lord of the devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Buddhasaraṇagamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhammasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti…pe… sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, saṅghasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Saṅghasaraṇagamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

“Good indeed, venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Buddha. Because of going for refuge to the Buddha, venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Dhamma… and so on… Good indeed, venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Saṅgha. Because of going for refuge to the Saṅgha, venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

Atha [T 4.0333] kho sakko devānamindo pañcahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, together with five hundred devas, approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, he stood to one side. To Sakka, the lord of the devas, who was standing to one side, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this:

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“It is indeed good, lord of the devas, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, a Sublime One, a Knower of the World, an Unsurpassed Trainer of persons to be tamed, a Teacher of devas and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ It is, lord of the devas, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘svākkhāto [P 4.0272] bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti[V 2.0265]. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“It is indeed good, lord of the devas, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One, visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be realized for oneself by the wise.’ It is, lord of the devas, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho[M 2.0465], ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ [T 4.0334] lokassā’ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“It is indeed good, lord of the devas, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is of good conduct, of upright conduct, of wise conduct, of proper conduct. That is, the four pairs of persons, the eight types of individuals—this Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ It is, lord of the devas, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

“It is indeed good, lord of the devas, to be endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken, unpierced, unspotted, unstained, liberating, praised by the wise, unmisapprehended, and conducive to concentration. It is, lord of the devas, precisely because of being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘itipi so…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“It is indeed good, venerable Moggallāna, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is… and so on… a Teacher of devas and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ It is, venerable Moggallāna, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“It is indeed good, venerable Moggallāna, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One… and so on… to be realized for oneself by the wise.’ It is, venerable Moggallāna, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ [P 4.0273] lokassā’ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena [V 2.0266] samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce [T 4.0335] sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“It is indeed good, venerable Moggallāna, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is of good conduct… and so on… an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ It is, venerable Moggallāna, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.
