“It is indeed good, Venerable Moggallāna, to be endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken... conducive to concentration. It is, Venerable Moggallāna, precisely because of being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.”

Atha [M 2.0466] kho sakko devānamindo chahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe…. Atha kho sakko devānamindo sattahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe…. Atha kho sakko devānamindo aṭṭhahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe…. Atha kho sakko devānamindo asītiyā devatāsahassehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

Then Sakka, the ruler of the devas, together with six hundred devas... and so on.... Then Sakka, the ruler of the devas, together with seven hundred devas... and so on.... Then Sakka, the ruler of the devas, together with eight hundred devas... and so on.... Then Sakka, the ruler of the devas, together with eighty thousand devas, approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, he stood to one side. To Sakka, the ruler of the devas, who was standing to one side, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this:

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“It is indeed good, ruler of the devas, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is... a Teacher of devas and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ It is, ruler of the devas, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… paccattaṃ [T 4.0336] veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“It is indeed good, ruler of the devas, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One... to be realized for oneself by the wise.’ It is, ruler of the devas, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu [V 2.0267] kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti[P 4.0274].

“It is indeed good, ruler of the devas, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha, thus: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples has practiced well... the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ It is, ruler of the devas, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

“It is indeed good, ruler of the devas, to be endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken... conducive to concentration. It is, ruler of the devas, precisely because of being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“It is indeed good, Venerable Moggallāna, to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, thus: ‘For this reason, too, the Blessed One is... a teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ It is, Venerable Moggallāna, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.

“Sādhu [M 2.0467] kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma: ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One... to be realized for oneself by the wise.’ It is, Venerable Moggallāna, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa [T 4.0337] moggallāna, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

“Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples has practiced well... the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ It is, Venerable Moggallāna, precisely because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

“Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken... conducive to concentration. It is, Venerable Moggallāna, precisely because of being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami [V 2.0268] …pe… ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

Then Sakka, ruler of the devas, together with five hundred devas, approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna... Then, while Sakka, ruler of the devas, was standing to one side, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to him:

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Buddhasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā [P 4.0275] paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena, dibbena yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena, dibbehi rūpehi, dibbehi saddehi, dibbehi gandhehi, dibbehi rasehi, dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

“Good indeed, ruler of the devas, is going for refuge to the Buddha. It is, ruler of the devas, precisely because of going for refuge to the Buddha that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan, divine beauty, divine happiness, divine glory, divine dominion, divine forms, divine sounds, divine smells, divine tastes, and divine tangibles.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, dhammasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Dhammasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa [T 4.0338] bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena, dibbena yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena, dibbehi rūpehi, dibbehi saddehi, dibbehi gandhehi, dibbehi rasehi, dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

“Good indeed, ruler of the devas, is going for refuge to the Dhamma. It is, ruler of the devas, precisely because of going for refuge to the Dhamma that some beings here, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan, divine beauty, divine happiness, divine glory, divine dominion, divine forms, divine sounds, divine smells, divine tastes, and divine tangibles.

“Sādhu [M 2.0468] kho, devānaminda, saṅghasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Saṅghasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena, dibbena yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena, dibbehi rūpehi, dibbehi saddehi, dibbehi gandhehi, dibbehi rasehi, dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehī”ti.

Good indeed, lord of the devas, is going for refuge to the Saṅgha. Because of going for refuge to the Saṅgha, lord of the devas, some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan, divine beauty, divine happiness, divine retinue, divine dominion, divine forms, divine sounds, divine scents, and divine tangibles.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Buddhasaraṇagamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Buddha. Because of going for refuge to the Buddha, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan... and in divine tangibles.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhammasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti…pe….

Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Dhamma...

“Sādhu [V 2.0269] kho, mārisa moggallāna, saṅghasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Saṅghasaraṇagamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena, dibbena [T 4.0339] yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena, dibbehi rūpehi, dibbehi saddehi, dibbehi gandhehi, dibbehi rasehi, dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehī”ti.

Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Saṅgha. Because of going for refuge to the Saṅgha, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan, divine beauty, divine happiness, divine retinue, divine dominion, divine forms, divine sounds, divine scents, and divine tangibles.

Atha kho sakko devānamindo chahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe… atha kho sakko devānamindo sattahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe… atha [P 4.0276] kho sakko devānamindo aṭṭhahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe… atha kho sakko devānamindo asītiyā devatāsahassehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

Then Sakka, lord of the devas, together with six hundred devas... Then Sakka, lord of the devas, together with seven hundred devas... Then Sakka, lord of the devas, together with eight hundred devas... Then Sakka, lord of the devas, together with eighty thousand devas, approached the Venerable Mahā Moggallāna; having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahā Moggallāna and stood at one side. While Sakka, lord of the devas, was standing at one side, the Venerable Mahā Moggallāna said this to him:

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Buddhasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

Good indeed, lord of the devas, is going for refuge to the Buddha. Because of going for refuge to the Buddha, lord of the devas, some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan... and in divine tangibles.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, dhammasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti…pe….

Good indeed, lord of the devas, is going for refuge to the Dhamma...

“Sādhu [M 2.0469] kho, devānaminda, saṅghasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Saṅghasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena, dibbena yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena, dibbehi rūpehi, dibbehi saddehi[T 4.0340], dibbehi gandhehi, dibbehi rasehi, dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehī”ti.

They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan, divine beauty, divine happiness, divine retinue, divine dominion, divine forms, divine sounds, divine scents, and divine tangibles.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti…pe… sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhammasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti…pe… sādhu kho mārisa moggallāna, saṅghasaraṇagamanaṃ hoti. Saṅghasaraṇagamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā [V 2.0270] sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena, dibbena yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena, dibbehi rūpehi, dibbehi saddehi, dibbehi gandhehi, dibbehi rasehi, dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehī”ti.

Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Buddha… Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Dhamma… Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Saṅgha. Because of going for refuge to the Saṅgha, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan, divine beauty, divine happiness, divine retinue, divine dominion, divine forms, divine sounds, divine scents, and divine tangibles.

Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ [P 4.0277] ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, together with five hundred devas, approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and stood to one side. To Sakka, the lord of the devas, who was standing to one side, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this:

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

Good indeed, O lord of the devas, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Thus is the Blessed One… Teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, O lord of the devas, some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan… and in divine tangibles.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda[T 4.0341], dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti…pe….

Good indeed, O lord of the devas, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma: ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One… to be realized for oneself by the wise.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma, O lord of the devas, some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world…

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… lokassā’ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena [M 2.0470] samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti…pe….

Good indeed, O lord of the devas, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples has practiced well… an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha, O lord of the devas, some beings here, on the dissolution of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world…

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehī”ti.

“Good indeed, lord of devas, is being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. Indeed, lord of devas, it is for the reason of being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones that some beings here, upon the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: with divine lifespan… with divine tangible objects.”

“Sādhu [V 2.0271] kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

“Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ Indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, it is for the reason of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha that some beings here, upon the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: with divine lifespan… with divine tangible objects.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

They surpass other devas in ten respects: with divine lifespan… with divine tangible objects.

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. “Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. Indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, it is for the reason of being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones that some beings here, upon the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: with divine lifespan… with divine tangible objects.”

Atha [M 2.0471] kho sakko devānamindo chahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe… atha kho sakko devānamindo sattahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe… atha kho sakko devānamindo aṭṭhahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ…pe… atha kho sakko devānamindo asītiyā devatāsahassehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā [V 2.0272] ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca [T 4.0343] –

Then Sakka, lord of devas, together with six hundred devas… Then Sakka, lord of devas, together with seven hundred devas… Then Sakka, lord of devas, together with eight hundred devas… Then Sakka, lord of devas, together with eighty thousand devas, approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and stood to one side. While Sakka, lord of devas, was standing to one side, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to him:

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena, dibbena yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena, dibbehi rūpehi, dibbehi saddehi, dibbehi gandhehi, dibbehi rasehi, dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

“Good indeed, lord of devas, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-gone One, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, lord of devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan, in divine beauty, in divine happiness, in divine fame, in divine influence, in divine forms, in divine sounds, in divine scents, in divine tastes, and in divine tangible objects.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā [P 4.0279] dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

“Good indeed, lord of devas, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma: ‘The Dhamma is well proclaimed by the Blessed One, directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be personally experienced by the wise.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma, lord of devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan…in divine tangible objects.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo [T 4.0344] añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te [M 2.0472] aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

“Good indeed, lord of devas, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way, practicing the straight way, practicing the right way, practicing the proper way; that is, the four pairs of persons, the eight individuals—this Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha, lord of devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan…in divine tangible objects.

“Sādhu kho, devānaminda, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evamidhekacce sattā [V 2.0273] kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena, dibbena yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena, dibbehi rūpehi, dibbehi saddehi, dibbehi gandhehi, dibbehi rasehi, dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehī”ti.

“Good indeed, lord of devas, is the attainment of virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken, without flaws, unblemished, unmottled, liberating, praised by the wise, not wrongly grasped, and conducive to concentration. Because of the attainment of virtues dear to the noble ones, lord of devas, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan, in divine beauty, in divine happiness, in divine glory, in divine sovereignty, in divine forms, in divine sounds, in divine scents, in divine tastes, and in divine tactile objects.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

“Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is the attainment of unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… a teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ Because of the attainment of unwavering confidence in the Buddha, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan… in divine tactile objects.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘svākkhāto [T 4.0345] bhagavatā dhammo…pe… paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce [P 4.0280] sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

“Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is the attainment of unwavering confidence in the Dhamma: ‘Well proclaimed by the Blessed One is the Dhamma… to be personally realized by the wise.’ Because of the attainment of unwavering confidence in the Dhamma, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan… in divine tactile objects.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā…pe… dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi.

“Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is the attainment of unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way… the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ Because of the attainment of unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas in ten respects: in divine lifespan… in divine tactile objects.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu [M 2.0473] kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti – dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena[V 2.0274], dibbena yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena, dibbehi rūpehi, dibbehi saddehi, dibbehi gandhehi, dibbehi rasehi, dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“It is indeed good, venerable Moggallāna, to be endowed with virtues beloved by the noble ones, which are unbroken... conducive to concentration. It is because of being endowed with virtues beloved by the noble ones, venerable Moggallāna, that some beings here, on the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. They surpass other devas on ten grounds: with divine lifespan, with divine complexion, with divine happiness, with divine retinue, with divine dominion, with divine forms, with divine sounds, with divine scents, with divine tastes, and with divine tactile objects.” The Tenth.

11. Candanasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on Candana

342. Atha kho candano nandano (sī.) devaputto…pe….

342. Then the devaputta Candana…

Atha kho suyāmo devaputto…pe…[T 4.0346].

Then the devaputta Suyāma…

Atha kho santusito devaputto…pe….

Then the devaputta Santusita…

Atha kho sunimmito devaputto…pe….

Then the devaputta Sunimmita…

Atha kho vasavatti devaputto…pe….

Then the devaputta Vasavatti…

(Yathā sakkasuttaṃ tathā ime pañca peyyālā vitthāretabbā). Ekādasamaṃ.

(These five summaries should be expanded in the same way as the Discourse on Sakka). The Eleventh.

Moggallānasaṃyuttaṃ [P 4.0281] samattaṃ.

The Moggallāna Saṃyutta is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Savitakkāvitakkañca, sukhena ca upekkhako;

Ākāsañceva viññāṇaṃ, ākiñcaṃ nevasaññinā;

Animitto ca sakko ca, candanekādasena cāti.

With Thought and Without Thought, with Happiness and Equanimity; Space and Consciousness, Nothingness and Neither-Perception; The Signless and Sakka, and Candana as the eleventh.

7. Cittasaṃyuttaṃ

7. The Connected Discourses with Citta

1. Saṃyojanasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Fetters

343. Ekaṃ [T 4.0347][V 2.0275][M 2.0474] samayaṃ sambahulā therā bhikkhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharanti ambāṭakavane. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulānaṃ therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṃ maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – “‘saṃyojana’nti vā, āvuso, ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti? Tatrekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṃ byākataṃ hoti – “‘saṃyojana’nti vā, āvuso, ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā cā”ti. Ekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṃ byākataṃ hoti – “‘saṃyojana’nti vā, āvuso, ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti.

343. On one occasion, a number of elder monks were dwelling at Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Ambāṭaka Grove. Then, at that time, after the meal, on returning from their alms-round, as the elder monks were sitting together assembled in the circular hall, this discussion arose among them: ‘Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as “a fetter” and as “fettering phenomena”—are they different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different?’ Thereupon, some elder monks answered thus: ‘Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as “a fetter” and as “fettering phenomena” are different in meaning and different in phrasing.’ Other elder monks answered thus: ‘Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as “a fetter” and as “fettering phenomena” are one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different.’”

Tena kho pana samayena citto gahapati migapathakaṃ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Assosi [P 4.0282] kho citto gahapati sambahulānaṃ kira therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṃ maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnānaṃ [V 2.0276] sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – “‘saṃyojana’nti vā, āvuso, ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti? Tatrekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṃ byākataṃ – “‘saṃyojana’nti vā, āvuso[T 4.0348], ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā cā”ti. Ekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṃ byākataṃ ‘saṃyojana’nti vā, āvuso ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nānanti. Atha kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho citto gahapati there bhikkhū etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, sambahulānaṃ kira therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantānaṃ maṇḍalamāḷe sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – ‘saṃyojana’nti vā, āvuso, ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti? Ekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi [M 2.0475] evaṃ byākataṃ – “‘saṃyojana’nti vā, āvuso, ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā cā”ti. Ekaccehi therehi bhikkhūhi evaṃ byākataṃ “‘saṃyojana’nti vā, āvuso, ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti. “Evaṃ, gahapatī”ti.

At that time, the householder Citta had arrived at Migapathaka on some business. The householder Citta heard that for many elder monks who had returned from the alms-round after the meal and were sitting together, assembled in the meeting hall, this discussion had arisen among them: ‘Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as “fetter” and as “fettering phenomena”—are they different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different?’ There, some elder monks answered thus: ‘Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as “fetter” and as “fettering phenomena” are different in meaning and different in phrasing.’ Other elder monks answered thus: ‘Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as “fetter” and as “fettering phenomena” are one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different.’ Then the householder Citta approached the elder monks; having approached, he paid homage to the elder monks and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder Citta said this to the elder monks: “Venerable sirs, I have heard that for many elder monks who had returned from the alms-round after the meal and were sitting together, assembled in the meeting hall, this discussion arose among them: ‘Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as “fetter” and as “fettering phenomena”—are they different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different?’ Some elder monks answered thus: ‘Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as “fetter” and as “fettering phenomena” are different in meaning and different in phrasing.’ Other elder monks answered thus: ‘Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as “fetter” and as “fettering phenomena” are one in meaning, with only the phrasing being different.’” “So it is, householder.”

“‘Saṃyojana’nti vā, bhante, ‘saṃyojaniyā dhammā’ti vā ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca. Tena hi, bhante, upamaṃ vo karissāmi. Upamāyapidhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānanti. Seyyathāpi, bhante, kāḷo ca balībaddo odāto ca balībaddo [T 4.0349] ekena dāmena vā yottena vā saṃyuttā assu. Yo nu kho evaṃ vadeyya – ‘kāḷo balībaddo odātassa balībaddassa saṃyojanaṃ[P 4.0283], odāto balībaddo kāḷassa balībaddassa saṃyojana’nti, sammā nu kho so vadamāno vadeyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, gahapati! Na kho, gahapati, kāḷo balībaddo odātassa balībaddassa saṃyojanaṃ, napi odāto balībaddo kāḷassa baḷībaddassa saṃyojanaṃ; yena kho te ekena dāmena vā yottena vā saṃyuttā taṃ tattha saṃyojana”nti. “Evameva kho, bhante, na cakkhu rūpānaṃ saṃyojanaṃ, na rūpā cakkhussa saṃyojanaṃ; yañca tattha tadubhayaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandarāgo taṃ tattha saṃyojanaṃ. Na sotaṃ saddānaṃ… na ghānaṃ gandhānaṃ… na jivhā rasānaṃ… na kāyo phoṭṭhabbānaṃ saṃyojanaṃ, na phoṭṭhabbā kāyassa saṃyojanaṃ; yañca tattha tadubhayaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandarāgo taṃ tattha saṃyojanaṃ. Na mano dhammānaṃ saṃyojanaṃ, na dhammā manassa saṃyojanaṃ; yañca tattha tadubhayaṃ paṭicca uppajjati chandarāgo taṃ tattha saṃyojana”nti. “Lābhā te, gahapati, suladdhaṃ te, gahapati, yassa te gambhīre buddhavacane paññācakkhu kamatī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, these phenomena spoken of as ‘fetter’ and as ‘fettering phenomena’ are different in meaning and different in phrasing. Well then, venerable sirs, I will make a simile for you. For by means of a simile, some wise persons here understand the meaning of what has been said. Suppose, venerable sirs, a black bull and a white bull were joined together with a single tether or yoke. If someone were to say, ‘The black bull is the fetter of the white bull, and the white bull is the fetter of the black bull,’ would that person be speaking rightly?” “No, householder. The black bull is not the fetter of the white bull, nor is the white bull the fetter of the black bull. Rather, that single tether or yoke by which they are joined—that is the fetter there.” “In the same way, venerable sirs, the eye is not the fetter of forms, nor are forms the fetter of the eye. Rather, that desire and lust which arises in dependence on both—that is the fetter there. The ear is not the fetter of sounds… the nose is not the fetter of odors… the tongue is not the fetter of tastes… the body is not the fetter of tangible objects, nor are tangible objects the fetter of the body. Rather, that desire and lust which arises in dependence on both—that is the fetter there. The mind is not the fetter of mental phenomena, nor are mental phenomena the fetter of the mind. Rather, that desire and lust which arises in dependence on both—that is the fetter there.” “It is a gain for you, householder, a great gain for you, that your eye of wisdom penetrates the profound word of the Buddha.” First.

2. Paṭhamaisidattasuttaṃ

2. The First Isidatta Sutta

344. Ekaṃ samayaṃ sambahulā therā bhikkhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharanti ambāṭakavane. Atha kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [T 4.0350] nisinno kho citto gahapati there bhikkhū etadavoca [V 2.0277] – “adhivāsentu me, bhante, therā svātanāya bhatta”nti. Adhivāsesuṃ kho therā bhikkhū tuṇhībhāvena[M 2.0476]. Atha kho citto gahapati therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha [P 4.0284] kho therā bhikkhū tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena cittassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṃsu.

344. At one time, many elder monks were dwelling at Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Ambāṭaka Grove. Then the householder Citta approached the elder monks; having approached, he paid homage to the elder monks and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder Citta said to the elder monks: 'Venerable sirs, may the elder monks consent to a meal from me tomorrow.' The elder monks consented by their silence. Then the householder Citta, knowing of the elder monks' consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the elder monks, circumambulated them to the right, and departed. Then, at the passing of that night, the elder monks dressed in the morning, and taking their bowls and robes, went to the residence of the householder Citta. Having arrived, they sat down on the seats prepared for them.

Atha kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “‘dhātunānattaṃ, dhātunānatta’nti, bhante thera, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā”ti? Evaṃ vutte āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “‘dhātunānattaṃ, dhātunānatta’nti, bhante thera, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā”ti? Dutiyampi kho āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi. Tatiyampi kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “‘dhātunānattaṃ, dhātunānatta’nti, bhante thera, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā”ti? Tatiyampi kho āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi.

Then the householder Citta approached the senior monks. Having approached, he paid homage to the senior monks and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the householder Citta said to the venerable elder: '“Diversity of elements, diversity of elements,” venerable elder, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, has the Blessed One spoken of the diversity of elements?' When this was said, the venerable elder remained silent. A second time, the householder Citta said to the venerable elder: '“Diversity of elements, diversity of elements,” venerable elder, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, has the Blessed One spoken of the diversity of elements?' A second time, the venerable elder remained silent. A third time, the householder Citta said to the venerable elder: '“Diversity of elements, diversity of elements,” venerable elder, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, has the Blessed One spoken of the diversity of elements?' A third time, the venerable elder remained silent.

Tena [T 4.0351] kho pana samayena āyasmā isidatto tasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe sabbanavako hoti. Atha kho āyasmā isidatto āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “byākaromahaṃ, bhante thera, cittassa gahapatino etaṃ pañha”nti? “Byākarohi tvaṃ, āvuso isidatta, cittassa gahapatino etaṃ pañha”nti. “Evañhi tvaṃ, gahapati, pucchasi – ‘dhātunānattaṃ, dhātunānattanti, bhante thera, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, dhātunānattaṃ, vuttaṃ bhagavatā’”ti? “Evaṃ[P 4.0285], bhante”. “Idaṃ kho, gahapati, dhātunānattaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā – cakkhudhātu, rūpadhātu, cakkhuviññāṇadhātu…pe… manodhātu, dhammadhātu, manoviññāṇadhātu. Ettāvatā kho, gahapati, dhātunānattaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā”ti.

Now at that time, the venerable Isidatta was the most junior in that community of monks. Then the venerable Isidatta said to the venerable elder: 'Venerable elder, I will answer this question of the householder Citta.' 'Answer, friend Isidatta, this question of the householder Citta.' 'Is this what you are asking, householder: “Diversity of elements, diversity of elements,” venerable elder, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, has the diversity of elements been spoken of by the Blessed One?”' 'Yes, venerable sir.' 'This, householder, is the diversity of elements spoken of by the Blessed One: the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element… the mind-element, the dhamma-element, the mind-consciousness-element. To this extent, householder, has the diversity of elements been spoken of by the Blessed One.'

Atha kho citto gahapati āyasmato isidattassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā there bhikkhū paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho therā bhikkhū bhuttāvino onītapattapāṇino uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā thero āyasmantaṃ [V 2.0278] isidattaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu kho taṃ, āvuso isidatta[M 2.0477], eso pañho paṭibhāsi, neso pañho maṃ paṭibhāsi. Tenahāvuso isidatta, yadā aññathāpi yadā aññadāpi (sī. pī.) aññadāpi (?) evarūpo pañho āgaccheyya, taññevettha paṭibhāseyyā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

Then the householder Citta, delighting and rejoicing in the words of the venerable Isidatta, personally served and satisfied the senior monks with choice hard and soft foods. Then the senior monks, having eaten and withdrawn their hands from their bowls, rose from their seats and departed. Then the venerable elder said to the venerable Isidatta: 'It is good, friend Isidatta, that this question occurred to you; this question did not occur to me. Therefore, friend Isidatta, whenever another such question arises, you yourself should answer it.' The second.

3. Dutiyaisidattasuttaṃ

3. The Second Isidatta Sutta

345. Ekaṃ samayaṃ sambahulā therā bhikkhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharanti ambāṭakavane. Atha kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū [T 4.0352] tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho citto gahapati there bhikkhū etadavoca – “adhivāsentu me, bhante therā, svātanāya bhatta”nti. Adhivāsesuṃ kho therā bhikkhū tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho citto gahapati therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho therā bhikkhū tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena cittassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṃsu.

345. At one time many elder bhikkhus were dwelling at Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Ambāṭaka Grove. Then the householder Citta approached those elder bhikkhus, and after approaching, he paid homage to them and sat down to one side. While sitting to one side, the householder Citta said to the elder bhikkhus: “Venerable sirs, may the elders accept tomorrow’s meal from me.” The elder bhikkhus consented by their silence. Then the householder Citta, understanding the elder bhikkhus’ consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to them, circumambulated them respectfully, and departed. Then, when that night had passed, in the morning, having dressed and taken their bowls and robes, the elder bhikkhus went to the residence of the householder Citta. Having gone there, they sat down on the seats prepared for them.

Atha [P 4.0286] kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “yā imā, bhante thera, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti – ‘sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā. Yāni cimāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle bhaṇitāni; imā nu kho, bhante, diṭṭhiyo kismiṃ sati honti, kismiṃ asati na hontī”ti?

Then the householder Citta approached the elder bhikkhus, and after approaching, he paid homage to them and sat down to one side. While sitting to one side, the householder Citta said to the venerable elder: “Venerable elder, these various kinds of views that arise in the world—‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’; ‘the world is finite’ or ‘the world is infinite’; ‘the soul is the same as the body’ or ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’; ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ or ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’; ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ or ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’—and these sixty-two speculative views that are stated in the Brahmajāla: Venerable sir, when what exists do these views arise, and when what does not exist do they not arise?”

Evaṃ [T 4.0353] vutte, āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho citto gahapati…pe… tatiyampi kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “yā imā, bhante thera, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke [M 2.0478] uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā [V 2.0279] lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā. Yāni cimāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle bhaṇitāni; imā nu kho, bhante, diṭṭhiyo kismiṃ sati honti, kismiṃ asati na hontī”ti? Tatiyampi kho āyasmā thero tuṇhī ahosi.

When this was said, the venerable elder remained silent. A second time the householder Citta... A third time the householder Citta said to the venerable elder: “Venerable elder, these various kinds of views that arise in the world—‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’; ‘the world is finite’ or ‘the world is infinite’; ‘the soul is the same as the body’ or ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’; ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ or ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’; ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ or ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’—and these sixty-two speculative views that are stated in the Brahmajāla: Venerable sir, when what exists do these views arise, and when what does not exist do they not arise?” A third time, the venerable elder remained silent.

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā isidatto tasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe sabbanavako hoti. Atha kho āyasmā isidatto āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “byākaromahaṃ, bhante thera, cittassa gahapatino etaṃ pañha”nti? “Byākarohi tvaṃ, āvuso isidatta, cittassa gahapatino etaṃ pañha”nti. “Evañhi [P 4.0287] tvaṃ, gahapati, pucchasi – ‘yā imā, bhante thera, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti – sassato lokoti vā…pe…; imā nu kho, bhante, diṭṭhiyo kismiṃ [T 4.0354] sati honti, kismiṃ asati na hontī’”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Yā imā, gahapati, anekavihitā diṭṭhiyo loke uppajjanti – ‘sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā. Yāni cimāni dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhigatāni brahmajāle bhaṇitāni; imā kho, gahapati, diṭṭhiyo sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā sati honti, sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā asati na hontī’”ti.

Now on that occasion, the Venerable Isidatta was the youngest in that assembly of bhikkhus. Then the Venerable Isidatta said to the venerable elder: “Venerable sir, I shall answer this question of the householder Citta.” “Answer this question of the householder Citta, friend Isidatta.” “Householder, did you not ask thus: ‘Venerable sir, these various views that arise in the world… when what exists do these views come to be, and when what does not exist do they not come to be?’” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Householder, these various views that arise in the world—‘the world is eternal’ or ‘the world is not eternal’; ‘the world is finite’ or ‘the world is infinite’; ‘the soul is the same as the body’ or ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’; ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ or ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’; ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ or ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’—and these sixty-two views that are spoken of in the Brahmajāla: these views, householder, come to be when there is identity view, and they do not come to be when there is no identity view.”

“Kathaṃ pana, bhante, sakkāyadiṭṭhi hotī”ti? “Idha, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ; vedanaṃ attato samanupassati…pe… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani [M 2.0479] vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Evaṃ kho, gahapati, sakkāyadiṭṭhi hotī”ti.

“But how, venerable sir, does identity view come to be?” “Here, householder, an uninstructed ordinary person, who is not a seer of the noble ones, not skilled in the Noble Dhamma, not disciplined in the Noble Dhamma; who is not a seer of true men, not skilled in the Dhamma of true men, not disciplined in the Dhamma of true men: he regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. He regards feeling as self… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. It is in this way, householder, that identity view comes to be.”

“Kathaṃ [V 2.0280] pana, bhante, sakkāyadiṭṭhi na hotī”ti? “Idha, gahapati, sutavā [T 4.0355] ariyasāvako ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto na rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā rūpaṃ, na rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ; na vedanaṃ… na saññaṃ… na saṅkhāre… na viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā viññāṇaṃ, na viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Evaṃ kho, gahapati, sakkāyadiṭṭhi na hotī”ti.

“But how, venerable sir, does identity view not come to be?” “Here, householder, an instructed noble disciple, who is a seer of the noble ones, skilled in the Noble Dhamma, well-disciplined in the Noble Dhamma; who is a seer of true men, skilled in the Dhamma of true men, well-disciplined in the Dhamma of true men: he does not regard form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. He does not regard feeling… perception… formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness. It is in this way, householder, that identity view does not come to be.”

“Kuto[P 4.0288], bhante, ayyo isidatto āgacchatī”ti? “Avantiyā kho, gahapati, āgacchāmī”ti. “Atthi, bhante, avantiyā isidatto nāma kulaputto amhākaṃ adiṭṭhasahāyo pabbajito? Diṭṭho so āyasmatā”ti? “Evaṃ, gahapatī”ti. “Kahaṃ nu kho so, bhante, āyasmā etarahi viharatī”ti? Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā isidatto tuṇhī ahosi. “Ayyo no, bhante, isidatto”ti? “Evaṃ, gahapatī”ti. “Abhiramatu, bhante, ayyo isidatto macchikāsaṇḍe. Ramaṇīyaṃ ambāṭakavanaṃ. Ahaṃ ayyassa isidattassa ussukkaṃ karissāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna”nti. “Kalyāṇaṃ vuccati, gahapatī”ti.

“Venerable sir, from where does the Venerable Isidatta come?” “I come from Avanti, householder.” “Venerable sir, is there in Avanti a clansman named Isidatta, our unseen friend, who has gone forth? Has he been seen by the venerable one?” “Yes, householder.” “But where, venerable sir, does that venerable one now dwell?” When this was said, the Venerable Isidatta remained silent. “Venerable sir, are you our Isidatta?” “Yes, householder.” “May the Venerable Isidatta delight in Macchikāsaṇḍa, venerable sir. The Ambāṭaka Grove is delightful. I will make an effort to provide for the Venerable Isidatta’s robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick.” “That is well spoken, householder.”

Atha kho citto gahapati āyasmato isidattassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā there bhikkhū paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho therā bhikkhū bhuttāvino onītapattapāṇino [T 4.0356] uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā thero āyasmantaṃ isidattaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu kho taṃ, āvuso isidatta, eso pañho paṭibhāsi. Neso pañho maṃ paṭibhāsi. Tenahāvuso isidatta, yadā aññathāpi evarūpo pañho āgaccheyya, taññevettha paṭibhāseyyā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā isidatto senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya macchikāsaṇḍamhā pakkāmi. Yaṃ macchikāsaṇḍamhā pakkāmi, tathā pakkantova ahosi, na puna paccāgacchīti. Tatiyaṃ.

Then the householder Citta, having rejoiced in and approved of the Venerable Isidatta’s words, personally served and satisfied the elder bhikkhus with choice hard and soft food. When the elder bhikkhus had finished eating and had withdrawn their hands from their bowls, they rose from their seats and departed. Then the venerable elder said this to the Venerable Isidatta: “It is good, friend Isidatta, that this question occurred to you. This question did not occur to me. Therefore, friend Isidatta, whenever another such question should arise, you yourself should answer it.” Then the Venerable Isidatta, having put his lodging in order and taken his bowl and robe, departed from Macchikāsaṇḍa. And having departed from Macchikāsaṇḍa, he remained so departed; he did not return again. The third.

4. Mahakapāṭihāriyasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Marvel of Mahaka

346. Ekaṃ [V 2.0281][M 2.0480] samayaṃ sambahulā therā bhikkhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharanti ambāṭakavane. Atha [P 4.0289] kho citto gahapati yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho citto gahapati there bhikkhū etadavoca – “adhivāsentu me, bhante therā, svātanāya gokule bhatta”nti. Adhivāsesuṃ kho therā bhikkhū tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho citto gahapati therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā there bhikkhū abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho therā bhikkhū tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena cittassa gahapatino gokulaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṃsu.

346. On one occasion, a number of elder bhikkhus were dwelling at Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Ambāṭaka Grove. Then the householder Citta approached the elder bhikkhus; having approached, he paid homage to the elder bhikkhus and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder Citta said this to the elder bhikkhus: “Venerable sirs, may the elders consent to a meal from me tomorrow at the cow pen.” The elder bhikkhus consented by their silence. Then the householder Citta, having understood the elder bhikkhus’s consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the elder bhikkhus, circumambulated them with his right side, and departed. Then, when that night had passed, in the morning, the elder bhikkhus dressed, took their bowls and robes, and went to the cow pen of the householder Citta; having gone there, they sat down on the seats that had been prepared.

Atha kho citto gahapati there bhikkhū paṇītena sappipāyāsena sahatthā santappesi [T 4.0357] sampavāresi. Atha kho therā bhikkhū bhuttāvino onītapattapāṇino uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃsu. Cittopi kho gahapati ‘sesakaṃ vissajjethā’ti vatvā there bhikkhū piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi. Tena kho pana samayena uṇhaṃ hoti kuthitaṃ kuṭṭhitaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.); te ca therā bhikkhū paveliyamānena maññe kāyena gacchanti, yathā taṃ bhojanaṃ bhuttāvino.

Then the householder Citta, with his own hands, served and satisfied the elder bhikkhus with choice milk-rice with ghee until they declined more. When the elder bhikkhus had finished eating and had withdrawn their hands from their bowls, they rose from their seats and departed. The householder Citta, saying, “Please distribute what is left,” followed closely behind the elder bhikkhus. Now at that time it was hot and sultry, and those elder bhikkhus walked with bodies that seemed heavy, as is the case for those who have just eaten a meal.

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahako tasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe sabbanavako hoti. Atha kho āyasmā mahako āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “sādhu khvassa, bhante thera, sītako ca vāto vāyeyya, abbhasampilāpo abbhasaṃbilāpo (sī.), abbhasaṃvilāpo (pī.) ca assa, devo ca ekamekaṃ phusāyeyyā”ti.

At that time, the Venerable Mahaka was the most junior in that community of bhikkhus. Then the Venerable Mahaka said this to the venerable elder: “It would be good, venerable sir, if a cool wind were to blow, there were an overcast sky, and the rain would fall drop by drop.”

“Sādhu khvassa, āvuso mahaka, yaṃ sītako ca vāto vāyeyya, abbhasampilāpo ca assa, devo ca ekamekaṃ phusāyeyyā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahako tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ [P 4.0290] abhisaṅkhari abhisaṅkhāsi (sī.) yathā sītako ca vāto vāyi, abbhasampilāpo ca assa āsi (?), devo ca ekamekaṃ phusi. Atha kho cittassa gahapatino etadahosi – “yo kho imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe sabbanavako bhikkhu tassāyaṃ evarūpo iddhānubhāvo”ti[M 2.0481]. Atha kho āyasmā mahako ārāmaṃ sampāpuṇitvā āyasmantaṃ theraṃ etadavoca – “alamettāvatā, bhante therā”ti? “Alamettāvatā, āvuso mahaka! Katamettāvatā, āvuso mahaka! Pūjitamettāvatā, āvuso mahakā”ti[V 2.0282]. Atha kho therā bhikkhū yathāvihāraṃ agamaṃsu. Āyasmāpi mahako sakaṃ vihāraṃ agamāsi.

“It would be good indeed, friend Mahaka, if a cool wind were to blow, there were an overcast sky, and the rain would fall drop by drop.” Then the Venerable Mahaka performed such a feat of psychic power that a cool wind blew, there was an overcast sky, and the rain fell drop by drop. Then this thought occurred to the householder Citta: “The psychic power of the most junior bhikkhu in this community of bhikkhus is of such a kind!” Then, the Venerable Mahaka, having reached the monastery, said this to the venerable elder: “Is this much enough, venerable sirs?” “This much is enough, friend Mahaka! This much has been done, friend Mahaka! This much has been offered in homage, friend Mahaka!” Then the elder bhikkhus went to their respective dwellings. The Venerable Mahaka also went to his own dwelling.

Atha kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā mahako [T 4.0358] tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahakaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṃ mahakaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, ayyo mahako uttarimanussadhammaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetū”ti. “Tena hi tvaṃ, gahapati, ālinde uttarāsaṅgaṃ paññapetvā tiṇakalāpaṃ okāsehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho citto gahapati āyasmato mahakassa paṭissutvā ālinde uttarāsaṅgaṃ paññapetvā tiṇakalāpaṃ okāsesi. Atha kho āyasmā mahako vihāraṃ pavisitvā sūcighaṭikaṃ datvā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhari yathā tālacchiggaḷena ca aggaḷantarikāya ca acci nikkhamitvā tiṇāni jhāpesi, uttarāsaṅgaṃ na jhāpesi. Atha kho citto gahapati uttarāsaṅgaṃ papphoṭetvā saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho āyasmā mahako vihārā nikkhamitvā cittaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “alamettāvatā, gahapatī”ti?

Then the householder Citta approached the Venerable Mahaka. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahaka and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder Citta said this to the Venerable Mahaka: "Venerable sir, it would be good if the noble Mahaka would show me a superhuman state, a miracle of psychic power." "In that case, householder, spread your upper robe on the porch and scatter a bundle of grass on it." "Yes, venerable sir," replied the householder Citta to the Venerable Mahaka, and having spread his upper robe on the porch, he scattered a bundle of grass on it. Then the Venerable Mahaka entered his dwelling, fastened the bolt, and performed such a feat of psychic power that a flame issued forth through the keyhole and the space around the bolt, burning the grass but not burning the upper robe. Then the householder Citta, shaking out his upper robe, stood to one side, struck with awe and with his hair standing on end. Then the Venerable Mahaka came out of his dwelling and said to the householder Citta: "Is this much sufficient, householder?"

“Alamettāvatā[P 4.0291], bhante mahaka! Katamettāvatā, bhante, mahaka! Pūjitamettāvatā, bhante mahaka! Abhiramatu, bhante, ayyo mahako macchikāsaṇḍe. Ramaṇīyaṃ ambāṭakavanaṃ. Ahaṃ ayyassa mahakassa ussukkaṃ karissāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna”nti. “Kalyāṇaṃ vuccati, gahapatī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahako senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya macchikāsaṇḍamhā pakkāmi. Yaṃ macchikāsaṇḍamhā pakkāmi, tathā pakkantova ahosi; na puna paccāgacchīti. Catutthaṃ.

"This is sufficient, Venerable Mahaka! With this, my request has been fulfilled, venerable sir! With this, homage has been paid, Venerable Mahaka! May the noble Mahaka delight in Macchikāsaṇḍa. The Ambāṭaka Grove is delightful. I will endeavor to provide the noble Mahaka with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick." "You have spoken well, householder." Then the Venerable Mahaka, having set his lodging in order and taken his bowl and robes, departed from Macchikāsaṇḍa. And when he departed from Macchikāsaṇḍa, he departed for good; he never returned again.

5. Paṭhamakāmabhūsuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse with Kāmabhū

347. Ekaṃ [T 4.0359] samayaṃ āyasmā kāmabhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharati ambāṭakavane. Atha kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā kāmabhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ kāmabhuṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi[M 2.0482]. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho cittaṃ gahapatiṃ āyasmā kāmabhū etadavoca –

347. On one occasion, the Venerable Kāmabhū was dwelling at Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Ambāṭaka Grove. Then the householder Citta approached the Venerable Kāmabhū; having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Kāmabhū and sat down to one side. As he was seated to one side, the Venerable Kāmabhū said this to the householder Citta:

“Vuttamidaṃ[V 2.0283], gahapati –

"This was said, householder:

“Nelaṅgo setapacchādo, ekāro vattatī ratho;

Anīghaṃ passa āyantaṃ appattaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.), chinnasotaṃ abandhana”nti.

‘With stainless parts, a white canopy, the single-axled chariot rolls on. Behold him coming, free from distress, with stream cut, and unbound.’”

“Imassa nu kho, gahapati, saṃkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti? “Kiṃ nu kho etaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā bhāsita”nti? “Evaṃ, gahapatī”ti. “Tena hi, bhante, muhuttaṃ āgamehi yāvassa atthaṃ pekkhāmī”ti. Atha kho citto gahapati muhuttaṃ tuṇhī hutvā āyasmantaṃ kāmabhuṃ etadavoca –

"Householder, how is the meaning of this, which was stated in brief, to be understood in detail?" "Venerable sir, was this spoken by the Blessed One?" "Yes, householder." "In that case, venerable sir, please wait a moment while I consider its meaning." Then the householder Citta, after remaining silent for a moment, said this to the Venerable Kāmabhū:

“‘Nelaṅga’nti [P 4.0292] kho, bhante, sīlānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. ‘Setapacchādo’ti kho, bhante, vimuttiyā etaṃ adhivacanaṃ. ‘Ekāro’ti kho, bhante, satiyā etaṃ adhivacanaṃ. ‘Vattatī’ti kho, bhante, abhikkamapaṭikkamassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. ‘Ratho’ti kho, bhante, imassetaṃ cātumahābhūtikassa kāyassa adhivacanaṃ mātāpettikasambhavassa odanakummāsūpacayassa aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammassa. Rāgo kho, bhante, nīgho, doso nīgho, moho nīgho. Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Tasmā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu ‘anīgho’ti vuccati. ‘Āyanta’nti [T 4.0360] kho, bhante, arahato etaṃ adhivacanaṃ. ‘Soto’ti kho, bhante, taṇhāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Sā khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Tasmā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu ‘chinnasoto’ti vuccati. Rāgo kho, bhante, bandhanaṃ, doso bandhanaṃ, moho bandhanaṃ. Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Tasmā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu ‘abandhano’ti vuccati. Iti kho, bhante, yaṃ taṃ bhagavatā vuttaṃ –

“Venerable sir, ‘blemishless’ is indeed a designation for virtue. Venerable sir, ‘white canopy’ is indeed a designation for liberation. Venerable sir, ‘single pole’ is indeed a designation for mindfulness. Venerable sir, ‘rolls on’ is indeed a designation for moving forward and backward. Venerable sir, ‘chariot’ is indeed a designation for this body, composed of the four great elements, originating from mother and father, built up from rice and gruel, subject to impermanence, anointing, massaging, breaking up, and destruction. Venerable sir, passion is a source of distress, aversion is a source of distress, delusion is a source of distress. For a monk whose taints are destroyed, these have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and are not subject to future arising. Therefore, a monk whose taints are destroyed is called ‘one without distress.’ Venerable sir, ‘the one who is coming’ is indeed a designation for the Arahant. Venerable sir, ‘stream’ is indeed a designation for craving. For a monk whose taints are destroyed, this has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and is not subject to future arising. Therefore, a monk whose taints are destroyed is called ‘one with the stream cut.’ Venerable sir, passion is a bond, aversion is a bond, delusion is a bond. For a monk whose taints are destroyed, these have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and are not subject to future arising. Therefore, a monk whose taints are destroyed is called ‘one without bonds.’ Thus, venerable sir, regarding what was said by the Blessed One:—

“Nelaṅgo setapacchādo, ekāro vattatī ratho;

Anīghaṃ passa āyantaṃ, chinnasotaṃ abandhana”nti.

‘The blemishless, white-canopied, single-poled chariot rolls on. Behold the one who is coming, free from distress, with stream cut, and unbound.’”

“Imassa [M 2.0483] kho, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmī”ti[V 2.0284]. “Lābhā te, gahapati, suladdhaṃ te, gahapati! Yassa te gambhīre buddhavacane paññācakkhu kamatī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Venerable sir, this is how I understand in detail the meaning of what was stated in brief by the Blessed One.” “It is a gain for you, householder, a great gain for you, that your eye of wisdom penetrates the profound word of the Buddha!” The Fifth.

6. Dutiyakāmabhūsuttaṃ

6. 6. The Second Discourse with Kāmabhū

348. Ekaṃ [P 4.0293] samayaṃ āyasmā kāmabhū macchikāsaṇḍe viharati ambāṭakavane. Atha kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā kāmabhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho citto gahapati āyasmantaṃ kāmabhuṃ etadavoca – “kati nu kho, bhante, saṅkhārā”ti? “Tayo kho, gahapati, saṅkhārā – kāyasaṅkhāro, vacīsaṅkhāro, cittasaṅkhāro”ti. “Sādhu, bhante”ti kho citto gahapati āyasmato kāmabhussa bhāsitaṃ [T 4.0361] abhinanditvā anumoditvā āyasmantaṃ kāmabhuṃ uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “katamo pana, bhante, kāyasaṅkhāro, katamo vacīsaṅkhāro, katamo cittasaṅkhāro”ti? “Assāsapassāsā kho, gahapati, kāyasaṅkhāro, vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro, saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti.

348. At one time, the Venerable Kāmabhū was dwelling at Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Ambāṭaka Grove. Then Citta the householder approached the Venerable Kāmabhū; having approached, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Citta the householder said this to the Venerable Kāmabhū: “Venerable sir, how many fabrications are there?” “Householder, there are three fabrications: the bodily fabrication, the verbal fabrication, and the mental fabrication.” “Good, venerable sir,” said Citta the householder. Delighting in and rejoicing at the words of the Venerable Kāmabhū, he asked a further question: “Venerable sir, what is the bodily fabrication, what is the verbal fabrication, and what is the mental fabrication?” “Householder, in-breaths and out-breaths are the bodily fabrication; thinking and pondering are the verbal fabrication; perception and feeling are the mental fabrication.”

“Sādhu, bhante”ti kho citto gahapati…pe… uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “kasmā pana, bhante, assāsapassāsā kāyasaṅkhāro, kasmā vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro, kasmā saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti? “Assāsapassāsā kho, gahapati, kāyikā. Ete dhammā kāyappaṭibaddhā, tasmā assāsapassāsā kāyasaṅkhāro. Pubbe kho, gahapati, vitakketvā vicāretvā pacchā vācaṃ bhindati, tasmā vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhāro. Saññā ca vedanā ca cetasikā. Ete dhammā cittappaṭibaddhā, tasmā saññā ca vedanā ca cittasaṅkhāro”ti.

“Good, venerable sir,” said Citta the householder... and asked a further question: “But why, venerable sir, are in-breaths and out-breaths the bodily fabrication? Why are thinking and pondering the verbal fabrication? Why are perception and feeling the mental fabrication?” “Householder, in-breaths and out-breaths are bodily. These phenomena are bound up with the body; therefore, in-breaths and out-breaths are the bodily fabrication. Householder, having first thought and pondered, one afterwards breaks into speech; therefore, thinking and pondering are the verbal fabrication. Perception and feeling are mental. These phenomena are bound up with the mind; therefore, perception and feeling are the mental fabrication.”

Sādhu…pe… uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “kathaṃ pana, bhante, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti hotī”ti? “Na kho, gahapati, saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjantassa bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjissa’nti vā ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno’ti vā[P 4.0294]. Atha khvassa pubbeva tathā cittaṃ bhāvitaṃ hoti yaṃ taṃ tathattāya upanetī”ti.

“Good...” he asked a further question: “Venerable sir, how does the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling come to be?” “Householder, for a monk who is entering the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, it does not occur to him: ‘I will enter the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling,’ or ‘I am entering the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling,’ or ‘I have entered the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.’ Rather, his mind has previously been so developed that it leads him to that state.”

Sādhu [M 2.0484] …pe… uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjantassa [T 4.0362] pana, bhante[V 2.0285], bhikkhuno katame dhammā paṭhamaṃ nirujjhanti, yadi vā kāyasaṅkhāro, yadi vā vacīsaṅkhāro, yadi vā cittasaṅkhāro”ti? “Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjantassa kho, gahapati, bhikkhuno vacīsaṅkhāro paṭhamaṃ nirujjhati, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato cittasaṅkhāro”ti.

“Good...” he asked a further question: “Venerable sir, for a monk who is entering the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, which phenomena cease first: the bodily fabrication, the verbal fabrication, or the mental fabrication?” “Householder, for a monk who is entering the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, the verbal fabrication ceases first, then the bodily fabrication, then the mental fabrication.”

Sādhu…pe… uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “yvāyaṃ, bhante, mato kālaṅkato, yo cāyaṃ bhikkhu saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno, imesaṃ kiṃ nānākaraṇa”nti? “Yvāyaṃ gahapati, mato kālaṅkato tassa kāyasaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, vacīsaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, cittasaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, āyu parikkhīṇo, usmā vūpasantā, indriyāni viparibhinnāni. Yo ca khvāyaṃ, gahapati, bhikkhu saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno, tassapi kāyasaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, vacīsaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, cittasaṅkhāro niruddho paṭippassaddho, āyu aparikkhīṇo, usmā avūpasantā, indriyāni vippasannāni. Yvāyaṃ, gahapati, mato kālaṅkato, yo cāyaṃ bhikkhu saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno, idaṃ nesaṃ nānākaraṇa”nti.

'Good...' ...pe... he asked a further question: 'Venerable sir, what is the difference between one who is dead and has passed away, and a bhikkhu who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling?' 'Householder, in the case of one who is dead and has passed away, their bodily fabrication has ceased and is stilled, their verbal fabrication has ceased and is stilled, their mental fabrication has ceased and is stilled, their life-force is exhausted, their heat is quenched, and their faculties are broken up. In the case of a bhikkhu who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, their bodily fabrication has also ceased and is stilled, their verbal fabrication has ceased and is stilled, their mental fabrication has ceased and is stilled, but their life-force is not exhausted, their heat is not quenched, and their faculties are clear. This, householder, is the difference between one who is dead and has passed away, and a bhikkhu who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling.'

Sādhu…pe… uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “kathaṃ pana, bhante, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ hotī”ti? “Na kho, gahapati, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahantassa bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahissa’nti vā ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahāmī’ti vā ‘ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā [T 4.0363] vuṭṭhito’ti vā. Atha khvassa pubbeva tathā cittaṃ bhāvitaṃ hoti, yaṃ taṃ tathattāya upanetī”ti.

'Good...' ...pe... he asked a further question: 'Venerable sir, how does emergence from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling come to be?' 'Householder, for a bhikkhu who is emerging from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, it does not occur to him: “I will emerge from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling,” or “I am emerging from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling,” or “I have emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.” Rather, his mind has previously been so developed that it leads him to that state.'

Sādhu[P 4.0295], bhante…pe… uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahantassa pana, bhante, bhikkhuno katame dhammā paṭhamaṃ uppajjanti, yadi vā kāyasaṅkhāro, yadi vā vacīsaṅkhāro, yadi vā cittasaṅkhāro”ti? “Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahantassa, gahapati, bhikkhuno cittasaṅkhāro paṭhamaṃ uppajjati, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato vacīsaṅkhāro”ti.

'Good, venerable sir...' ...pe... he asked a further question: 'Venerable sir, for a bhikkhu emerging from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, which phenomena arise first: the bodily fabrication, the verbal fabrication, or the mental fabrication?' 'Householder, for a bhikkhu emerging from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, the mental fabrication arises first, then the bodily fabrication, then the verbal fabrication.'

Sādhu…pe… uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitaṃ pana, bhante[V 2.0286], bhikkhuṃ kati phassā phusanti”? “Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitaṃ [M 2.0485] kho, gahapati, bhikkhuṃ tayo phassā phusanti – suññato phasso, animitto phasso, appaṇihito phasso”ti.

'Good...' ...pe... he asked a further question: 'Venerable sir, how many contacts touch a bhikkhu who has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling?' 'Householder, three contacts touch a bhikkhu who has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling: the emptiness contact, the signless contact, and the undirected contact.'

Sādhu…pe… uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitassa pana, bhante, bhikkhuno kiṃninnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, kiṃpoṇaṃ, kiṃpabbhāra”nti? “Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhitassa kho, gahapati, bhikkhuno vivekaninnaṃ cittaṃ hoti vivekapoṇaṃ vivekapabbhāra”nti.

'Good...' ...pe... he asked a further question: 'Venerable sir, when a bhikkhu has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, to what is his mind inclined, to what does it tend, to what does it gravitate?' 'Householder, when a bhikkhu has emerged from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, his mind is inclined to seclusion, it tends towards seclusion, it gravitates to seclusion.'

“Sādhu, bhante”ti kho citto gahapati āyasmato kāmabhussa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā āyasmantaṃ kāmabhuṃ uttariṃ pañhaṃ apucchi [T 4.0364] – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā pana, bhante, kati dhammā bahūpakārā”ti? “Addhā kho tvaṃ, gahapati, yaṃ paṭhamaṃ pucchitabbaṃ taṃ pucchasi. Api ca tyāhaṃ byākarissāmi. Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā kho, gahapati, dve dhammā bahūpakārā – samatho ca vipassanā cā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

'Excellent, venerable sir,' said Citta the householder.
