Delighting in and approving of the Venerable Kāmabhū’s words, he asked the Venerable Kāmabhū a further question: 'But, venerable sir, how many things are very helpful for the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling?' 'Indeed, householder, you are asking later what should have been asked first. Nevertheless, I will explain it to you. For the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, householder, two things are very helpful: serenity and insight.' Sixth.

7. Godattasuttaṃ

7. The Godatta Sutta

349. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā godatto macchikāsaṇḍe viharati ambāṭakavane. Atha [P 4.0296] kho citto gahapati yenāyasmā godatto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ godattaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho cittaṃ gahapatiṃ āyasmā godatto etadavoca – “yā cāyaṃ, gahapati, appamāṇā cetovimutti, yā ca ākiñcaññā cetovimutti, yā ca suññatā cetovimutti, yā ca animittā cetovimutti, ime dhammā nānatthā nānābyañjanā udāhu ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti? “Atthi, bhante, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca. Atthi pana, bhante, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti.

349. On one occasion, the Venerable Godatta was dwelling at Macchikāsaṇḍa in the Ambāṭaka Grove. Then Citta the householder approached the Venerable Godatta; having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Godatta and sat down to one side. As Citta the householder was sitting to one side, the Venerable Godatta said this to him: 'Householder, regarding the immeasurable liberation of mind, the nothingness liberation of mind, the emptiness liberation of mind, and the signless liberation of mind—are these states different in meaning and different in phrasing, or are they one in meaning and only different in phrasing?' 'Venerable sir, there is a way in which these states are different in both meaning and phrasing. And, venerable sir, there is also a way in which these states are one in meaning, and only the phrasing is different.'

“Katamo ca, bhante, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā nānatthā ceva nānābyañjanā ca? Idha, bhante, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā [V 2.0287] dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ catutthiṃ (?). Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya [T 4.0365] sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ [M 2.0486] mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena abyāpajjhena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), abyābajjhena (?) pharitvā viharati. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhante, appamāṇā cetovimutti.

'And what, venerable sir, is the way in which these states are different in both meaning and phrasing? Here, venerable sir, a bhikkhu dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness; likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, and to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will. He dwells with a mind accompanied by compassion... ...pe... with a mind accompanied by altruistic joy... ...pe... he dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity; likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, and to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will. This, venerable sir, is called the immeasurable liberation of mind.'

“Katamā ca, bhante, ākiñcaññā cetovimutti? Idha, bhante, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma, ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhante, ākiñcaññā cetovimutti.

“And what, venerable sir, is the liberation of mind through nothingness? Here, venerable sir, a monk, by completely transcending the dimension of the infinity of consciousness, thinking, ‘There is nothing whatsoever,’ enters and dwells in the dimension of nothingness. This, venerable sir, is called the liberation of mind through nothingness.

“Katamā ca, bhante, suññatā cetovimutti? Idha, bhante, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘suññamidaṃ attena vā [P 4.0297] attaniyena vā’ti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhante, suññatā cetovimutti.

“And what, venerable sir, is the liberation of mind through emptiness? Here, venerable sir, a monk, having gone to a forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects thus: ‘This is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.’ This, venerable sir, is called the liberation of mind through emptiness.

“Katamā ca, bhante, animittā cetovimutti? Idha, bhante, bhikkhu sabbanimittānaṃ amanasikārā animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhante, animittā cetovimutti. Ayaṃ kho, bhante, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā nānatthā ceva [T 4.0366] nānābyañjanā ca.

“And what, venerable sir, is the signless liberation of mind? Here, venerable sir, a monk, through non-attention to all signs, enters and dwells in the signless concentration of mind. This, venerable sir, is called the signless liberation of mind. This, venerable sir, is the way by which these states are different in meaning and also different in phrasing.

“Katamo ca, bhante, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nānaṃ? Rāgo, bhante, pamāṇakaraṇo, doso pamāṇakaraṇo, moho pamāṇakaraṇo. Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Yāvatā kho, bhante, appamāṇā cetovimuttiyo, akuppā tāsaṃ cetovimutti aggamakkhāyati. Sā kho pana akuppā cetovimutti suññā rāgena, suññā dosena, suññā mohena. Rāgo kho, bhante, kiñcanaṃ, doso kiñcanaṃ, moho kiñcanaṃ. Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Yāvatā kho[V 2.0288], bhante, ākiñcaññā cetovimuttiyo, akuppā tāsaṃ cetovimutti aggamakkhāyati. Sā kho [M 2.0487] pana akuppā cetovimutti suññā rāgena, suññā dosena, suññā mohena. Rāgo kho, bhante, nimittakaraṇo, doso nimittakaraṇo, moho nimittakaraṇo. Te khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Yāvatā kho, bhante, animittā cetovimuttiyo, akuppā tāsaṃ cetovimutti aggamakkhāyati. Sā kho pana akuppā cetovimutti suññā rāgena, suññā dosena, suññā mohena. Ayaṃ kho, bhante, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma [T 4.0367] ime dhammā ekatthā byañjanameva nāna”nti. “Lābhā te, gahapati, suladdhaṃ te, gahapati! Yassa te gambhīre buddhavacane paññācakkhu kamatī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“And what, venerable sir, is the way by which these states are of one meaning, though the phrasing differs? Lust, venerable sir, is a maker of measure; hatred is a maker of measure; delusion is a maker of measure. For a monk whose taints are destroyed, these have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, so that they are no more subject to future arising. Insofar, venerable sir, as there are immeasurable liberations of mind, the unshakeable liberation of mind is declared the highest among them. That unshakeable liberation of mind is empty of lust, empty of hatred, empty of delusion. Lust, venerable sir, is an impediment; hatred is an impediment; delusion is an impediment. For a monk whose taints are destroyed, these have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, so that they are no more subject to future arising. Insofar, venerable sir, as there are liberations of mind through nothingness, the unshakeable liberation of mind is declared the highest among them. That unshakeable liberation of mind is empty of lust, empty of hatred, empty of delusion. Lust, venerable sir, is a maker of signs; hatred is a maker of signs; delusion is a maker of signs. For a monk whose taints are destroyed, these have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, so that they are no more subject to future arising. Insofar, venerable sir, as there are signless liberations of mind, the unshakeable liberation of mind is declared the highest among them. That unshakeable liberation of mind is empty of lust, empty of hatred, empty of delusion. This, venerable sir, is the way by which these states are of one meaning, though the phrasing differs.” “It is a gain for you, householder, it is well gained by you, householder, that your eye of wisdom penetrates the profound word of the Buddha.”

8. Nigaṇṭhanāṭaputtasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta

350. Tena kho pana samayena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto nātaputto (sī.) macchikāsaṇḍaṃ [P 4.0298] anuppatto hoti mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhiṃ. Assosi kho citto gahapati – “nigaṇṭho kira nāṭaputto macchikāsaṇḍaṃ anuppatto mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhi”nti. Atha kho citto gahapati sambahulehi upāsakehi saddhiṃ yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhena nāṭaputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho cittaṃ gahapatiṃ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto etadavoca – “saddahasi tvaṃ, gahapati, samaṇassa gotamassa – atthi avitakko avicāro samādhi, atthi vitakkavicārānaṃ nirodho”ti?

350. At that time, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta had arrived at Macchikāsaṇḍa with a large assembly of Nigaṇṭhas. The householder Citta heard: “Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, it seems, has arrived at Macchikāsaṇḍa with a large assembly of Nigaṇṭhas.” Then the householder Citta, accompanied by many lay followers, went to where Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta was. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta. Having concluded this courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta said to the householder Citta: “Do you believe, householder, of the ascetic Gotama that there is concentration without applied thought and sustained thought, and that there is the cessation of applied thought and sustained thought?”

“Na khvāhaṃ ettha, bhante, bhagavato saddhāya gacchāmi. Atthi avitakko avicāro samādhi, atthi vitakkavicārānaṃ nirodho”ti. Evaṃ vutte, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto ulloketvā sakaṃ parisaṃ apaloketvā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), oloketvā (sī. aṭṭha. syā. aṭṭha.) etadavoca – “idaṃ bhavanto passantu, yāva ujuko cāyaṃ citto gahapati, yāva asaṭho cāyaṃ citto gahapati, yāva amāyāvī cāyaṃ citto gahapati, vātaṃ vā so jālena bādhetabbaṃ maññeyya, yo vitakkavicāre [T 4.0368] nirodhetabbaṃ maññeyya[M 2.0488], sakamuṭṭhinā vā so gaṅgāya sotaṃ āvāretabbaṃ maññeyya, yo vitakkavicāre nirodhetabbaṃ maññeyyā”ti.

“Venerable sir, regarding this, I do not proceed by faith in the Blessed One that there is concentration without applied thought and sustained thought, and that there is the cessation of applied thought and sustained thought.” When this was said, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, looking up at his own assembly, said this: “Behold, sirs, how upright this householder Citta is, how uncrafty this householder Citta is, how free from deceit this householder Citta is! One who would think that applied and sustained thought can be ceased might as well think to restrain the wind with a net, or to stop the current of the river Ganges with their own fist.”

“Taṃ [V 2.0289] kiṃ maññasi, bhante, katamaṃ nu kho paṇītataraṃ – ñāṇaṃ vā saddhā vā”ti? “Saddhāya kho, gahapati, ñāṇaṃyeva paṇītatara”nti. “Ahaṃ kho, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi[P 4.0299]. Ahaṃ kho, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Ahaṃ kho, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Ahaṃ kho, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Na so khvāhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ jānanto evaṃ passanto kassa aññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā saddhāya gamissāmi? Atthi avitakko avicāro samādhi, atthi vitakkavicārānaṃ nirodho”ti.

“What do you think, venerable sir, which is more excellent: knowledge or faith?” “Householder, knowledge is indeed more excellent than faith.” “Venerable sir, whenever I wish, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I enter and dwell in the first jhāna, which has applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. Venerable sir, whenever I wish, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought… I enter and dwell in the second jhāna. Venerable sir, whenever I wish, with the fading away of rapture… I enter and dwell in the third jhāna. Venerable sir, whenever I wish, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain… I enter and dwell in the fourth jhāna. I, venerable sir, knowing thus and seeing thus, for what other ascetic or brahmin should I go for faith that there is concentration without applied thought and sustained thought, and that there is the cessation of applied thought and sustained thought?”

Evaṃ vutte, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sakaṃ parisaṃ apaloketvā etadavoca – “idaṃ bhavanto passantu, yāva anujuko cāyaṃ citto gahapati, yāva saṭho cāyaṃ citto gahapati, yāva māyāvī cāyaṃ citto gahapatī”ti.

When this was said, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, looking toward his own assembly, said this: “Behold, sirs, how crooked this householder Citta is, how crafty this householder Citta is, how deceitful this householder Citta is!”

“Idāneva kho te idāneva ca pana (syā. kaṃ. ka.) mayaṃ, bhante, bhāsitaṃ – ‘evaṃ ājānāma [T 4.0369] idaṃ bhavanto passantu, yāva ujuko cāyaṃ citto gahapati, yāva asaṭho cāyaṃ citto gahapati, yāva amāyāvī cāyaṃ citto gahapatī’ti. Idāneva ca pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhāsitaṃ – ‘evaṃ ājānāma idaṃ bhavanto passantu, yāva anujuko cāyaṃ citto gahapati, yāva saṭho cāyaṃ citto gahapati, yāva māyāvī cāyaṃ citto gahapatī’ti. Sace te, bhante, purimaṃ saccaṃ, pacchimaṃ te micchā. Sace pana te, bhante, purimaṃ micchā, pacchimaṃ te saccaṃ. Ime kho pana, bhante, dasa sahadhammikā pañhā āgacchanti. Yadā nesaṃ atthaṃ ājāneyyāsi, atha maṃ paṭihareyyāsi saddhiṃ nigaṇṭhaparisāya. Eko pañho, eko uddeso, ekaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ. Dve pañhā, dve uddesā, dve veyyākaraṇāni. Tayo pañhā, tayo uddesā, tīṇi veyyākaraṇāni. Cattāro pañhā, cattāro uddesā, cattāri [M 2.0489] veyyākaraṇāni. Pañca pañhā, pañca uddesā, pañca veyyākaraṇāni. Cha pañhā, cha uddesā, cha veyyākaraṇāni. Satta pañhā, satta uddesā, satta veyyākaraṇāni[V 2.0290]. Aṭṭha pañhā, aṭṭha [P 4.0300] uddesā, aṭṭha veyyākaraṇāni. Nava pañhā, nava uddesā, nava veyyākaraṇāni. Dasa pañhā, dasa uddesā, dasa veyyākaraṇānī”ti. Atha kho citto gahapati nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ ime dasa sahadhammike pañhe āpucchitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmīti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Just now, venerable sir, we were expecting you to say this: ‘Venerable sirs, behold how upright this householder Citta is, how uncrafty this householder Citta is, how undeceitful this householder Citta is.’ But just now, venerable sir, you have said this: ‘Venerable sirs, behold how crooked this householder Citta is, how crafty this householder Citta is, how deceitful this householder Citta is.’ If, venerable sir, your former statement is true, then the latter is false. If, however, your former is false, then the latter is true. Now, venerable sir, these ten questions in accordance with the Dhamma arise. When you understand their meaning, then you should respond to me together with the assembly of Nigaṇṭhas. One question, one exposition, one explanation. Two questions, two expositions, two explanations. Three questions, three expositions, three explanations. Four questions, four expositions, four explanations. Five questions, five expositions, five explanations. Six questions, six expositions, six explanations. Seven questions, seven expositions, seven explanations. Eight questions, eight expositions, eight explanations. Nine questions, nine expositions, nine explanations. Ten questions, ten expositions, ten explanations.” Then the householder Citta, having posed these ten questions in accordance with the Dhamma to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, rose from his seat and departed. The eighth.

9. Acelakassapasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse to the Naked Ascetic Kassapa

351. Tena [T 4.0370] kho pana samayena acelo kassapo macchikāsaṇḍaṃ anuppatto hoti cittassa gahapatino purāṇagihisahāyo. Assosi kho citto gahapati – “acelo kira kassapo macchikāsaṇḍaṃ anuppatto amhākaṃ purāṇagihisahāyo”ti. Atha kho citto gahapati yena acelo kassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā acelena kassapena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho citto gahapati acelaṃ kassapaṃ etadavoca – “kīvaciraṃ pabbajitassa, bhante, kassapā”ti? “Tiṃsamattāni kho me, gahapati, vassāni pabbajitassā”ti. “Imehi pana te, bhante, tiṃsamattehi vassehi atthi koci uttarimanussadhammā uttarimanussadhammo (syā. kaṃ.) alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti? “Imehi kho me, gahapati, tiṃsamattehi vassehi pabbajitassa natthi koci uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato phāsuvihāro, aññatra naggeyyā ca muṇḍeyyā ca pāvaḷanipphoṭanāya cā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, citto gahapati acelaṃ kassapaṃ etadavoca – “acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Dhammassa svākkhātatā sabbatthapi evameva dissati yatra hi nāma tiṃsamattehi vassehi na koci [P 4.0301] uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato abhavissa phāsuvihāro, aññatra naggeyyā ca muṇḍeyyā ca pāvaḷanipphoṭanāya cā”ti!

351. Now at that time, the naked ascetic Kassapa, an old householder friend of Citta the householder, had arrived at Macchikāsaṇḍa. Citta the householder heard: ‘It seems the naked ascetic Kassapa, our old householder friend, has arrived at Macchikāsaṇḍa.’ Then Citta the householder approached the naked ascetic Kassapa; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the naked ascetic Kassapa. When they had concluded the greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Citta the householder said to the naked ascetic Kassapa: ‘Venerable Kassapa, how long has it been since you went forth?’ ‘Householder, it has been about thirty years since I went forth.’ ‘Venerable sir, in these thirty years, have you attained any superhuman state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding?’ ‘Householder, in these thirty years since I went forth, I have not attained any superhuman state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, or a comfortable abiding, apart from nakedness, a shaven head, and dusting off the sitting place.’ When this was said, Citta the householder said to the naked ascetic Kassapa: ‘It is amazing, sir, it is astonishing! How well-proclaimed this teaching is, that in thirty years there has been no attainment of any superhuman state, any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, or any comfortable abiding, apart from nakedness, a shaven head, and dusting off the sitting place!’

“Tuyhaṃ pana, gahapati, kīvaciraṃ [T 4.0371] upāsakattaṃ upagatassā”ti? “Mayhampi kho pana, bhante, tiṃsamattāni vassāni upāsakattaṃ upagatassā”ti. “Imehi pana te, gahapati, tiṃsamattehi vassehi atthi koci uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso [M 2.0490] adhigato phāsuvihāro”ti? “Gihinopi siyā, bhante. Ahañhi, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Ahañhi, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā [V 2.0291] …pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Ahañhi, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Ahañhi, bhante, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi, sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi. Sace kho panāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato bhagavatā (syā. kaṃ.) paṭhamataraṃ kālaṃ kareyyaṃ, anacchariyaṃ kho panetaṃ yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evaṃ byākareyya – ‘natthi taṃ saṃyojanaṃ yena saṃyojanena saṃyutto citto gahapati puna imaṃ lokaṃ āgaccheyyā’”ti. Evaṃ vutte, acelo kassapo cittaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho! Dhammassa svākkhātatā, yatra hi nāma gihī odātavasano gihī odātavasanā (sī. pī.) evarūpaṃ uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ adhigamissati adhigamissanti (sī. pī.) phāsuvihāraṃ. Labheyyāhaṃ, gahapati[P 4.0302], imasmiṃ dhammavinaye pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti.

“And you, householder, how long have you been a lay follower?” “Venerable sir, it has also been about thirty years for me since becoming a lay follower.” “In these thirty years, householder, have you attained any superhuman state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, a comfortable abiding?” “Venerable sir, it is possible even for a householder. For I, venerable sir, whenever I wish, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enter and abide in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by thought and examination, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. I, venerable sir, whenever I wish, with the stilling of thought and examination… enter and abide in the second jhāna. I, venerable sir, whenever I wish, with the fading away of rapture… enter and abide in the third jhāna. I, venerable sir, whenever I wish, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain… enter and abide in the fourth jhāna. If, venerable sir, I were to pass away before the Blessed One, it would not be surprising if the Blessed One were to declare of me thus: ‘There is no fetter by which the householder Citta is bound that would cause him to return to this world.’” When this was said, the naked ascetic Kassapa said to the householder Citta: “It is amazing, sir, it is astonishing! How well-proclaimed is the Dhamma, that a householder clad in white could attain such a superhuman state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, and a comfortable abiding. May I, householder, receive the going forth in this Dhamma and Discipline; may I receive the higher ordination!”

Atha kho citto gahapati [T 4.0372] acelaṃ kassapaṃ ādāya yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū etadavoca – “ayaṃ, bhante, acelo kassapo amhākaṃ purāṇagihisahāyo. Imaṃ therā pabbājentu upasampādentu. Ahamassa ussukkaṃ karissāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna”nti. Alattha kho acelo kassapo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno ca panāyasmā kassapo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā kassapo arahataṃ ahosīti. Navamaṃ.

Then the householder Citta, taking the naked ascetic Kassapa, approached the elder monks. Having approached, he said to the elder monks: "Venerable sirs, this naked ascetic Kassapa is an old friend from my former household life. May the elders grant him the going forth and the higher ordination. I will make an effort to provide his requisites: robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicines for the sick." The naked ascetic Kassapa obtained the going forth and the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline. Not long after his higher ordination, the Venerable Kassapa, dwelling alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute, soon realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having realized it, he dwelt therein. He understood: "Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being." And the Venerable Kassapa became one of the arahants.

10. Gilānadassanasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Visiting the Sick

352. Tena [M 2.0491] kho pana samayena citto gahapati ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho sambahulā ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu [V 2.0292] adhivatthā devatā saṅgamma samāgamma cittaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavocuṃ – “paṇidhehi, gahapati, anāgatamaddhānaṃ rājā assaṃ cakkavattī”ti.

352. Now at that time the householder Citta was sick, suffering, and gravely ill. Then many deities of the parks, deities of the forests, deities of the trees, and deities dwelling in medicinal plants, grass, and great trees, having gathered and come together, said to the householder Citta: “Make an aspiration, householder: ‘In a future time, may I be a wheel-turning monarch.’”

Evaṃ vutte, citto gahapati tā ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthā devatā etadavoca – “tampi aniccaṃ, tampi addhuvaṃ, tampi pahāya gamanīya”nti. Evaṃ [T 4.0373] vutte, cittassa gahapatino mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā [P 4.0303] cittaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavocuṃ – “satiṃ, ayyaputta, upaṭṭhapehi, mā vippalapī”ti. “Kiṃ tāhaṃ vadāmi yaṃ maṃ tumhe evaṃ vadetha – ‘satiṃ, ayyaputta, upaṭṭhapehi, mā vippalapī’”ti? “Evaṃ kho tvaṃ, ayyaputta, vadesi – ‘tampi aniccaṃ, tampi addhuvaṃ, tampi pahāya gamanīya’”nti. “Tathā hi pana maṃ ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthā devatā evamāhaṃsu – ‘paṇidhehi, gahapati, anāgatamaddhānaṃ rājā assaṃ cakkavattī’ti. Tāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘tampi aniccaṃ…pe… tampi pahāya gamanīya’”nti. “Kiṃ pana tā, ayyaputta, ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthā devatā atthavasaṃ sampassamānā evamāhaṃsu – ‘paṇidhehi, gahapati, anāgatamaddhānaṃ rājā assaṃ cakkavattī’”ti? “Tāsaṃ kho ārāmadevatānaṃ vanadevatānaṃ rukkhadevatānaṃ osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthānaṃ devatānaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘ayaṃ kho citto gahapati, sīlavā sīlavanto (ka.) kalyāṇadhammo. Sace paṇidahissati – anāgatamaddhānaṃ rājā assaṃ cakkavattī’ti, ‘tassa kho ayaṃ ijjhissati, sīlavato cetopaṇidhi visuddhattā dhammiko dhammikaṃ phalaṃ anupassatī’ti. Imaṃ kho tā ārāmadevatā vanadevatā rukkhadevatā osadhitiṇavanappatīsu adhivatthā devatā atthavasaṃ sampassamānā evamāhaṃsu – ‘paṇidhehi, gahapati, anāgatamaddhānaṃ rājā assaṃ [T 4.0374] cakkavattī’ti. Tāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘tampi aniccaṃ, tampi addhuvaṃ, tampi pahāya gamanīya’”nti.

When this was said, Citta the householder said to those deities of the parks, deities of the forests, deities of the trees, and deities dwelling in medicinal plants, grass, and great trees: “That too is impermanent, that too is not lasting, that too must be abandoned before one must go.” When this was said, Citta the householder’s friends, companions, relatives, and blood relations said to him: “Establish mindfulness, noble son, do not babble.” “What am I saying that makes you say to me: ‘Establish mindfulness, noble son, do not babble’?” “It is because you say, noble son: ‘That too is impermanent, that too is not lasting, that too must be abandoned before one must go.’” “Indeed, the deities of the parks, the deities of the forests, the deities of the trees, and the deities dwelling in medicinal plants, grass, and great trees said to me: ‘Make an aspiration, householder: “In a future time, may I be a wheel-turning monarch.”’ To them I say: ‘That too is impermanent… that too must be abandoned before one must go.’” “But for what reason, noble son, did those deities of the parks, deities of the forests, deities of the trees, and deities dwelling in medicinal plants, grass, and great trees, seeing what benefit, say to you: ‘Make an aspiration, householder: “In a future time, may I be a wheel-turning monarch”’?” “Those deities of the parks, deities of the forests, deities of the trees, and deities dwelling in medicinal plants, grass, and great trees thought thus: ‘This Citta the householder is virtuous, of good character. If he should make an aspiration—“In a future time, may I be a wheel-turning monarch”—this mental aspiration of his will be fulfilled because of its purity, as he is virtuous. A righteous person will see a righteous result.’ Seeing this benefit, those deities of the parks, deities of the forests, deities of the trees, and deities dwelling in medicinal plants, grass, and great trees said to me: ‘Make an aspiration, householder: “In a future time, may I be a wheel-turning monarch.”’ To them I say: ‘That too is impermanent, that too is not lasting, that too must be abandoned before one must go.’”

“Tena [M 2.0492] hi, ayyaputta, amhepi ovadāhī”ti. “Tasmā hi vo evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – buddhe [P 4.0304] aveccappasādena samannāgatā bhavissāma – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgatā bhavissāma – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena [V 2.0293] samannāgatā bhavissāma – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti. Yaṃ kho pana kiñci kule deyyadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ appaṭivibhattaṃ bhavissati sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehīti evañhi vo sikkhitabba”nti. Atha kho citto gahapati mittāmacce ñātisālohite buddhe ca dhamme ca saṅghe ca cāge ca samādapetvā kālamakāsīti. Dasamaṃ.

“In that case, noble son, please instruct us too.” “Therefore, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha—“Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant, perfectly self-enlightened, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, Well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.” We will be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma—“The Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One, directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be personally experienced by the wise.” We will be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha—“The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way, practicing the straight way, practicing the true way, practicing the proper way; that is, the four pairs of persons, the eight types of individuals—this Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.” And whatever gift-item there is in the family, all of it will be shared with those who are virtuous and of good character.’ Thus should you train yourselves.” Then, after establishing his friends, companions, relatives, and kin in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha, and in generosity, the householder Citta passed away.

Cittasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Citta is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this is:

Saṃyojanaṃ [T 4.0375] dve isidattā, mahako kāmabhūpi ca;

Godatto ca nigaṇṭho ca, acelena gilānadassananti.

The Fetters, two on Isidatta, Mahaka, and Kāmabhū; Godatta, and the Nigaṇṭha, with Acela, and Visiting the Sick.

8. Gāmaṇisaṃyuttaṃ

8. The Connected Discourses on Village Headmen

1. Caṇḍasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Caṇḍa

353. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 2.0294][M 2.0493]. Atha [T 4.0376][P 4.0305] kho caṇḍo gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho caṇḍo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacco caṇḍo caṇḍotveva yena midhekacco caṇḍoteva (sī. pī.) saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekacco sorato soratotveva yena midhekacco suratoteva (sī. pī.) saṅkhaṃ gacchatī”ti? “Idha, gāmaṇi, ekaccassa rāgo appahīno hoti. Rāgassa appahīnattā pare kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṃ pātukaroti. So caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Doso appahīno hoti. Dosassa appahīnattā pare kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṃ pātukaroti. So caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Moho appahīno hoti. Mohassa appahīnattā pare kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṃ pātukaroti. So caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Ayaṃ kho, gāmaṇi, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo yena midhekacco caṇḍo caṇḍotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati”.

353. At Sāvatthī. Then Caṇḍa the village headman approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Caṇḍa the village headman said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person in this world comes to be designated as “violent”? And, venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby a certain person in this world comes to be designated as “gentle”?' 'Here, village headman, for a certain person, lust is unabandoned. Because lust is unabandoned, others anger him; and when angered by others, he manifests his anger. He comes to be designated as “violent.” For him, hatred is unabandoned. Because hatred is unabandoned, others anger him; and when angered by others, he manifests his anger. He comes to be designated as “violent.” For him, delusion is unabandoned. Because delusion is unabandoned, others anger him; and when angered by others, he manifests his anger. He comes to be designated as “violent.” This, village headman, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby a certain person in this world comes to be designated as “violent.'”

“Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekaccassa rāgo pahīno hoti. Rāgassa pahīnattā pare na kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṃ na pātukaroti. So soratotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Doso pahīno hoti. Dosassa pahīnattā pare na kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṃ [T 4.0377] na pātukaroti. So soratotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Moho pahīno hoti. Mohassa pahīnattā pare na kopenti, parehi kopiyamāno kopaṃ na pātukaroti. So soratotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Ayaṃ kho, gāmaṇi, hetu ayaṃ paccayo yena midhekacco sorato soratotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchatī”ti.

Furthermore, village headman, for a certain person, lust is abandoned. Because lust is abandoned, others do not anger him; and when angered by others, he does not manifest anger. He comes to be designated as 'gentle.' For him, hatred is abandoned. Because hatred is abandoned, others do not anger him; and when angered by others, he does not manifest anger. He comes to be designated as 'gentle.' For him, delusion is abandoned. Because delusion is abandoned, others do not anger him; and when angered by others, he does not manifest anger. He comes to be designated as 'gentle.' This, village headman, is the cause, this is the condition, whereby a certain person in this world comes to be designated as 'gentle.'

Evaṃ [V 2.0295][P 4.0306] vutte, caṇḍo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā [M 2.0494] vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

When this was said, Caṇḍa the village headman said to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or point out the path to one who is lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness, thinking, “Those with eyes will see forms”; in the very same way, the Dhamma has been clarified by the Blessed One in numerous ways. I, venerable sir, go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward, for as long as life lasts.' First.

2. Tālapuṭasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Tālapuṭa

354. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho tālapuṭo tālaputto (sī. syā. kaṃ.) naṭagāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, pubbakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ naṭānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṃ hāseti rameti, so [T 4.0378] kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā pahāsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti. Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti? “Alaṃ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ. Mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī”ti. Dutiyampi kho tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, pubbakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ naṭānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṃ hāseti rameti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā pahāsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti. Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti? “Alaṃ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ. Mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī”ti. Tatiyampi kho tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, pubbakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ naṭānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṃ hāseti rameti, so [P 4.0307] kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā pahāsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti. Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti?

354. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrel sanctuary. Then Tālapuṭa, the chief of actors, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Tālapuṭa, the chief of actors, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I have heard this from former teachers and their ancestral teachers among the actors, who used to say: ‘Whatever actor, in the middle of a stage or in the middle of an assembly, makes people laugh and delights them with truth and falsehood, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the devas of Laughter.’ In this matter, what does the Blessed One say?” “Enough, Chief, let this be. Do not ask me this.” A second time, Tālapuṭa, the chief of actors, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I have heard this from former teachers and their ancestral teachers among the actors, who used to say: ‘Whatever actor, in the middle of a stage or in the middle of an assembly, makes people laugh and delights them with truth and falsehood, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the devas of Laughter.’ In this matter, what does the Blessed One say?” “Enough, Chief, let this be. Do not ask me this.” A third time, Tālapuṭa, the chief of actors, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I have heard this from former teachers and their ancestral teachers among the actors, who used to say: ‘Whatever actor, in the middle of a stage or in the middle of an assembly, makes people laugh and delights them with truth and falsehood, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the devas of Laughter.’ In this matter, what does the Blessed One say?”

“Addhā kho tyāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, na labhāmi nālatthaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) – ‘alaṃ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ, mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī’ti. Api ca tyāhaṃ byākarissāmi. Pubbe kho, gāmaṇi, sattā avītarāgā rāgabandhanabaddhā. Tesaṃ naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe ye dhammā rajanīyā te upasaṃharati bhiyyosomattāya. Pubbe kho, gāmaṇi, sattā avītadosā dosabandhanabaddhā. Tesaṃ naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe ye dhammā [M 2.0495] dosanīyā te [T 4.0379] upasaṃharati bhiyyosomattāya. Pubbe kho, gāmaṇi[V 2.0296], sattā avītamohā mohabandhanabaddhā. Tesaṃ naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe ye dhammā mohanīyā te upasaṃharati bhiyyosomattāya. So attanā matto pamatto pare madetvā pamādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā pahāso nāma nirayo tattha upapajjati. Sace kho panassa evaṃdiṭṭhi hoti – ‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṃ hāseti rameti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā pahāsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti, sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi. Micchādiṭṭhikassa kho panāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, purisapuggalassa dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā”ti.

“Indeed, Chief, I did not prevail upon you when I said, ‘Enough, Chief, let this be; do not ask me this.’ Nevertheless, I will explain it to you. Formerly, Chief, beings were not free from passion, bound by the fetter of passion. For them, an actor, in the middle of a stage or in the middle of an assembly, presents those things that are provocative of passion, for the sake of even greater passion. Formerly, Chief, beings were not free from aversion, bound by the fetter of aversion. For them, an actor, in the middle of a stage or in the middle of an assembly, presents those things that are provocative of aversion, for the sake of even greater aversion. Formerly, Chief, beings were not free from delusion, bound by the fetter of delusion. For them, an actor, in the middle of a stage or in the middle of an assembly, presents those things that are provocative of delusion, for the sake of even greater delusion. That actor, being himself intoxicated and heedless, and having made others intoxicated and heedless, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the hell named ‘Laughter.’ And if he holds such a view as this: ‘Whatever actor, in the middle of a stage or in the middle of an assembly, makes people laugh and delights them with truth and falsehood, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the devas of Laughter,’ that is his wrong view. For a person with wrong view, Chief, I declare one of two destinations: either hell or the animal realm.”

Evaṃ vutte, tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi, parodi, assūni pavattesi. “Etaṃ kho tyāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, nālatthaṃ – ‘alaṃ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī’”ti. “Nāhaṃ, bhante, etaṃ rodāmi yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha; api cāhaṃ, bhante, pubbakehi ācariyapācariyehi naṭehi dīgharattaṃ nikato vañcito paluddho – ‘yo so naṭo raṅgamajjhe [P 4.0308] samajjamajjhe saccālikena janaṃ hāseti rameti so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā pahāsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’”ti. “Abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā [T 4.0380] maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti. Alattha kho tālapuṭo naṭagāmaṇi bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno ca panāyasmā tālapuṭo…pe… arahataṃ ahosīti. Dutiyaṃ.

When this was said, Tālapuṭa, the chief of actors, cried and shed tears. “This is why, Chief, I did not prevail upon you when I said, ‘Enough, Chief, let this be; do not ask me this.’” “Venerable sir, I am not weeping on account of what the Blessed One has said to me. But, venerable sir, I have been deceived, cheated, and ruined for a long, long time by former teachers and their ancestral teachers among the actors, who said: ‘Whatever actor, in the middle of a stage or in the middle of an assembly, makes people laugh and delights them with truth and falsehood, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the devas of Laughter.’” “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or point out the way to one who was lost, or hold a lamp in the darkness so that those with sight might see forms; in the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by the Blessed One. I go to the Blessed One for refuge, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May I receive the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One, venerable sir; may I receive the higher ordination.” Tālapuṭa, the chief of actors, received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One; he received the higher ordination. And not long after his higher ordination, the Venerable Tālapuṭa became one of the arahants. The second.

3. Yodhājīvasuttaṃ

3. The Yodhājīva Sutta

355. Atha kho yodhājīvo gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho yodhājīvo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, pubbakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ yodhājīvānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo so yodhājīvo saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṃ [M 2.0496] ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti. Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti? “Alaṃ[V 2.0297], gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī”ti. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho yodhājīvo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, pubbakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ yodhājīvānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo so yodhājīvo saṅgāme [T 4.0381] ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṃ ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti. Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti?

355. Then the headman Yodhājīva approached the Blessed One; having approached... and so on... Seated to one side, the headman Yodhājīva said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, I have heard this from former teachers and instructors of warriors as they were speaking: "A warrior who strives and exerts himself in battle—if others strike him down and slay him while he is striving and exerting himself, with the breaking up of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of the devas named Parajita." What does the Blessed One say about this?' 'Enough, headman, let that be. Do not ask me that.' For a second time... and so on... For a third time, the headman Yodhājīva said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, I have heard this from former teachers and instructors of warriors as they were speaking: "A warrior who strives and exerts himself in battle—if others strike him down and slay him while he is striving and exerting himself, with the breaking up of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of the devas named Parajita." What does the Blessed One say about this?'

“Addhā [P 4.0309] kho tyāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, na labhāmi – ‘alaṃ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī’ti. Api ca tyāhaṃ byākarissāmi. Yo so, gāmaṇi, yodhājīvo saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tassa taṃ cittaṃ pubbe gahitaṃ hīnaṃ (sī. pī.) dukkaṭaṃ duppaṇihitaṃ – ‘ime sattā haññantu vā bajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesuṃ iti vā’ti. Tamenaṃ ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ pare hananti pariyāpādenti; so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajito nāma nirayo tattha upapajjatīti. Sace kho panassa evaṃ diṭṭhi hoti – ‘yo so yodhājīvo saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati tamenaṃ ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti, sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi. Micchādiṭṭhikassa kho panāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, purisapuggalassa dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā”ti.

“Indeed, headman, I did not prevail upon you when I said, ‘Enough, headman, let this be; do not ask me this.’ Nevertheless, I will answer you. When a warrior who makes a living by war strives and exerts himself in battle, his mind is previously seized, ill-done, and wrongly directed thus: 'May these beings be struck down, or bound, or cut off, or destroyed, or may they not exist at all.' If others then strike him down and slay him while he is striving and exerting himself, with the breaking up of the body, after death, he is reborn in the hell named Parajita. But if he holds such a view as this: 'A warrior who strives and exerts himself in battle—if others then strike him down and slay him while he is striving and exerting himself, with the breaking up of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of the devas named Parajita'—that is his wrong view. For a person with wrong view, headman, I declare one of two destinations: either hell or the animal realm.”

Evaṃ vutte, yodhājīvo gāmaṇi parodi, assūni pavattesi. “Etaṃ kho tyāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, nālatthaṃ – ‘alaṃ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī’”ti. “Nāhaṃ, bhante, etaṃ rodāmi yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha[T 4.0382]; apicāhaṃ, bhante, pubbakehi ācariyapācariyehi yodhājīvehi dīgharattaṃ nikato vañcito paluddho – ‘yo so yodhājīvo saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṃ ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’”ti. “Abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

When this was said, the headman Yodhājīva wept and shed tears. “This is why, headman, I did not succeed when I said to you: ‘Enough, headman, let that be; do not ask me this.’” “I am not weeping, Venerable Sir, because the Blessed One said this to me. But rather, Venerable Sir, I have been deceived, cheated, and deluded for a long time by former teachers and their teachers, the warriors, who said: ‘A warrior who strives and exerts himself in battle—if others strike him down and slay him as he strives and exerts himself, with the breaking up of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of the devas named Parajita.’” “Excellent, Venerable Sir!… From this day forward, may the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.” The Third.

4. Hatthārohasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Elephant Rider

356. Atha [V 2.0298][M 2.0497][P 4.0310] kho hatthāroho gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā…pe… ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gatanti. Catutthaṃ.

356. Then the headman, the elephant rider, approached the Blessed One. Having approached… (the text continues as in the preceding discourse)… From this day forward, may the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life. The Fourth.

5. Assārohasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Horse Rider

357. Atha kho assāroho gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho assāroho gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, pubbakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ assārohānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo so assāroho saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṃ ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti. Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti? “Alaṃ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī”ti. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho assāroho gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, pubbakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ assārohānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo so assāroho saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṃ ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ [T 4.0383] pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti. Idha bhagavā kimāhā”ti?

357. Then the headman, the horse rider, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the headman, the horse rider, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, I have heard this from former teachers and their teachers, horse riders who said: ‘That horse rider who strives and exerts himself in battle—if others kill him and slay him while he is striving and exerting himself, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of the devas named Parajita.’ What does the Blessed One say about this?” “Enough, headman, let that be. Do not ask me that.” A second time… and a third time the headman, the horse rider, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, I have heard this from former teachers and their teachers, horse riders who said: ‘That horse rider who strives and exerts himself in battle—if others kill him and slay him while he is striving and exerting himself, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of the devas named Parajita.’ What does the Blessed One say about this?”

“Addhā kho tyāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, na labhāmi – ‘alaṃ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī’ti. Api ca kho tyāhaṃ byākarissāmi. Yo so, gāmaṇi, assāroho saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati tassa [P 4.0311] taṃ cittaṃ pubbe gahitaṃ dukkaṭaṃ duppaṇihitaṃ – ‘ime sattā haññantu vā bajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā ahesuṃ iti vā’ti. Tamenaṃ ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajito nāma nirayo tattha upapajjati. Sace kho panassa evaṃ diṭṭhi hoti – ‘yo so assāroho saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṃ ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’ti, sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi. Micchādiṭṭhikassa kho panāhaṃ gāmaṇi, purisapuggalassa dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā”ti.

“Indeed, headman, I did not obtain from you what I wished when I said: ‘Enough, headman, let that be. Do not ask me that.’ Nevertheless, I will explain it to you. Headman, as for that horse rider who strives and exerts himself in battle, his mind has previously been badly grasped and wrongly directed thus: ‘May these beings be struck down, or bound, or annihilated, or destroyed, or may they not exist at all!’ If others then strike him down and slay him while he is striving and exerting himself, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the hell named Parajita. But if he holds such a view as this: ‘A horse rider who strives and exerts himself in battle—if others then strike him down and slay him while he is striving and exerting himself, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of the devas named Parajita’—that is his wrong view. For a person with wrong view, headman, I declare one of two destinations: either hell or the animal realm.”

Evaṃ [V 2.0299][M 2.0498] vutte, assāroho gāmaṇi parodi, assūni pavattesi. “Etaṃ kho tyāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, nālatthaṃ – ‘alaṃ, gāmaṇi, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī’”ti. “Nāhaṃ, bhante, etaṃ rodāmi yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha. Apicāhaṃ, bhante, pubbakehi ācariyapācariyehi assārohehi dīgharattaṃ nikato vañcito paluddho – ‘yo [T 4.0384] so assāroho saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṃ ussahantaṃ vāyamantaṃ pare hananti pariyāpādenti, so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā parajitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī’”ti. “Abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

When this was said, the headman, the horse rider, wept and shed tears. “This is why, headman, I did not succeed when I said to you: ‘Enough, headman, let that be; do not ask me this.’” “I am not weeping, Venerable Sir, because the Blessed One said this to me. But rather, Venerable Sir, I have been deceived, cheated, and deluded for a long time by former teachers and their teachers, the horse riders, who said: ‘That horse rider who strives and exerts himself in battle—if others kill him and slay him as he strives and exerts himself—with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the company of the devas named Parajita.’” “Excellent, Venerable Sir!… From this day forward, may the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.” The Fifth.

6. Asibandhakaputtasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse to Asibandhaka’s Son

358. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ viharati pāvārikambavane. Atha [P 4.0312] kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “brāhmaṇā, bhante, pacchā bhūmakā kāmaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā udakorohakā aggiparicārakā. Te mataṃ kālaṅkataṃ uyyāpenti nāma saññāpenti nāma saggaṃ nāma okkāmenti. Bhagavā pana, bhante, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pahoti tathā kātuṃ yathā sabbo loko kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyā”ti? “Tena hi, gāmaṇi, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsī”ti.

358. On one occasion, the Blessed One was staying at Nāḷandā in Pāvārika’s mango grove. Then the headman Asibandhakaputta approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the headman Asibandhakaputta said to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable Sir, there are brahmins of the western lands who carry water pots, wear garlands of moss, descend into the water, and tend the fire. They claim to send forth the departed, to make them known, and to cause them to ascend to heaven. But the Blessed One, Venerable Sir, an Arahant, a Fully Enlightened One, is surely able to act in such a way that the whole world, with the breakup of the body, after death, would be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world?’ ‘In that case, headman, I will question you in return on this very matter. Answer as you see fit.’

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, idhassa puriso pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhiko. Tamenaṃ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya – ‘ayaṃ puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjatū’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi[T 4.0385], api nu so puriso mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu [V 2.0300] vā thomanahetu vā pañjalikā anuparisakkanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, village headman? Suppose there is a man here who destroys life, takes what is not given, engages in sexual misconduct, speaks falsehood, speaks slanderously, speaks harshly, engages in idle chatter, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and holds wrong view. Then a great crowd of people might come together and assemble, and entreat him, praise him, and with joined palms repeatedly beseech him, saying: ‘May this man, with the breakup of the body, after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world!’ What do you think, village headman? Would that man, on account of the entreating, praising, or repeated beseeching with joined palms by that great crowd of people, with the breakup of the body, after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, puriso mahatiṃ puthusilaṃ gambhīre udakarahade pakkhipeyya. Tamenaṃ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya [M 2.0499] pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya – ‘ummujja, bho puthusile, uplava, bho puthusile[P 4.0313], thalamuplava, bho puthusile’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, api nu sā puthusilā mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu vā thomanahetu vā pañjalikā anuparisakkanahetu vā ummujjeyya vā uplaveyya vā thalaṃ vā uplaveyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Evameva kho, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhiko. Kiñcāpi taṃ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya – ‘ayaṃ puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjatū’”ti, atha kho so puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya.

“Just as, village headman, if a man were to throw a large, flat stone into a deep lake, and a great crowd of people were to gather, come together, and entreat, praise, and with joined palms repeatedly beseech it, saying, ‘Emerge, good flat stone! Float up, good flat stone! Come to the shore, good flat stone!’ What do you think, village headman? Would that flat stone emerge, float up, or come to the shore on account of the entreating, praising, or repeated beseeching of that great crowd of people?” “No, venerable sir.” “Even so, village headman, a person who destroys life, takes what is not given, engages in sexual misconduct, speaks falsehood, speaks slanderously, speaks harshly, engages in idle chatter, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and holds wrong view—even if a great crowd of people were to gather, come together, and entreat, praise, and with joined palms repeatedly beseech him, saying, ‘May this person, with the breakup of the body, after death, be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world!’—still, with the breakup of the body, after death, that person would be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, the lower realms, in hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, idhassa idha (ka.), idha cassa (?) puriso pāṇātipātā paṭivirato adinnādānā paṭivirato kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato musāvādā paṭivirato pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato [T 4.0386] samphappalāpā paṭivirato anabhijjhālu abyāpannacitto sammādiṭṭhiko. Tamenaṃ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya – ‘ayaṃ puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjatū’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, api nu so puriso mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu vā thomanahetu vā pañjalikā anuparisakkanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, village headman? Suppose there were a man here who abstains from destroying life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech, abstains from slanderous speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from idle chatter, is not covetous, has a mind without ill will, and holds right view. Then a great crowd of people might come together and assemble, and entreat him, praise him, and with joined palms repeatedly beseech him, saying: ‘May this man, with the breakup of the body, after death, be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, the lower realms, in hell!’ What do you think, village headman? Would that man, on account of the entreating, praising, or repeated beseeching with joined palms by that great crowd of people, with the breakup of the body, after death, be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, the lower realms, in hell?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, puriso sappikumbhaṃ vā telakumbhaṃ vā gambhīre udakarahade ogāhetvā bhindeyya. Tatra yāssa sakkharā vā kaṭhalā vā sā adhogāmī adhogāminī (?) assa; yañca khvassa tatra sappi vā telaṃ vā taṃ uddhaṃ gāmi [P 4.0314] assa. Tamenaṃ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya – ‘osīda, bho sappitela, saṃsīda[V 2.0301], bho sappitela, adho gaccha, bho sappitelā’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, api [M 2.0500] nu taṃ sappitelaṃ mahato janakāyassa āyācanahetu vā thomanahetu vā pañjalikā anuparisakkanahetu vā osīdeyya vā saṃsīdeyya vā adho vā gaccheyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Evameva kho, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso pāṇātipātā paṭivirato, adinnādānā paṭivirato, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato, musāvādā paṭivirato, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato[T 4.0387], samphappalāpā paṭivirato, anabhijjhālu, abyāpannacitto, sammādiṭṭhiko, kiñcāpi taṃ mahā janakāyo saṅgamma samāgamma āyāceyya thomeyya pañjaliko anuparisakkeyya – ‘ayaṃ puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjatū’ti, atha kho so puriso kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Just as, village headman, a man might take a pot of ghee or oil and, having submerged it in a deep lake, break it. There, whatever gravel or potsherds there were would go downwards, while whatever ghee or oil there was would go upwards. Then a great crowd of people might come together and assemble, and entreat it, praise it, and with joined palms repeatedly beseech it, saying: ‘Sink, good ghee and oil! Submerge, good ghee and oil! Go downwards, good ghee and oil!’ What do you think, village headman? Would that ghee and oil, on account of the entreating, praising, or repeated beseeching with joined palms by that great crowd of people, sink, submerge, or go downwards?” “No, venerable sir.” “Even so, village headman, a person who abstains from destroying life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech, abstains from slanderous speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from idle chatter, is not covetous, has a mind without ill will, and holds right view—even if a great crowd of people were to come together and assemble, and entreat him, praise him, and with joined palms repeatedly beseech him, saying: ‘May this person, with the breakup of the body, after death, be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, the lower realms, in hell!’—still, that person, with the breakup of the body, after death, would be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.” When this was said, the village headman Asibandhakaputta said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! … From this day forward, may the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.” The sixth.

7. Khettūpamasuttaṃ

7. The Simile of the Field

359. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ viharati pāvārikambavane. Atha kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “nanu, bhante, bhagavā sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharatī”ti? “Evaṃ, gāmaṇi, tathāgato sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharatī”ti. “Atha kiñcarahi, bhante, bhagavā ekaccānaṃ sakkaccaṃ dhammaṃ deseti, ekaccānaṃ no tathā sakkaccaṃ dhammaṃ desetī”ti? “Tena [P 4.0315] hi, gāmaṇi, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, idhassu idha (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kassakassa gahapatino tīṇi khettāni – ekaṃ khettaṃ aggaṃ, ekaṃ khettaṃ majjhimaṃ, ekaṃ khettaṃ hīnaṃ jaṅgalaṃ ūsaraṃ [T 4.0388] pāpabhūmi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, asu kassako gahapati bījāni patiṭṭhāpetukāmo kattha paṭhamaṃ patiṭṭhāpeyya, yaṃ vā aduṃ khettaṃ aggaṃ[V 2.0302], yaṃ vā aduṃ khettaṃ majjhimaṃ, yaṃ vā aduṃ khettaṃ hīnaṃ jaṅgalaṃ ūsaraṃ pāpabhūmī”ti? “Asu, bhante, kassako gahapati bījāni patiṭṭhāpetukāmo yaṃ aduṃ khettaṃ aggaṃ tattha patiṭṭhāpeyya[M 2.0501]. Tattha patiṭṭhāpetvā yaṃ aduṃ khettaṃ majjhimaṃ tattha patiṭṭhāpeyya. Tattha patiṭṭhāpetvā yaṃ aduṃ khettaṃ hīnaṃ jaṅgalaṃ ūsaraṃ pāpabhūmi tattha patiṭṭhāpeyyapi, nopi patiṭṭhāpeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Antamaso gobhattampi bhavissatī”ti.

359. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Nāḷandā in Pāvārika's mango grove. Then the headman Asibandhaka's son approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the headman Asibandhaka's son said to the Blessed One: "Is it not so, venerable sir, that the Blessed One dwells compassionate for the welfare of all living beings?" "That is so, headman, the Tathāgata dwells compassionate for the welfare of all living beings." "But then, venerable sir, why does the Blessed One teach the Dhamma carefully to some, but not so carefully to others?" "Well then, headman, I will question you in return. Answer as you see fit. What do you think, headman? Suppose a farmer householder has three fields—one excellent, one middling, and one that is inferior, rough, saline, and of poor soil. What do you think, headman? If that farmer householder wants to sow seeds, where would he first sow them—in the excellent field, the middling field, or the field that is inferior, rough, saline, and of poor soil?" "That farmer householder, venerable sir, wanting to sow seeds, would first sow them in the excellent field. Having sown there, he would then sow in the middling field. Having sown there, he might or might not sow in the field that is inferior, rough, saline, and of poor soil. For what reason? At the very least, it could serve as cattle fodder."

“Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yaṃ aduṃ khettaṃ aggaṃ; evameva mayhaṃ bhikkhubhikkhuniyo. Tesāhaṃ dhammaṃ desemi – ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ, sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsemi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ete hi, gāmaṇi, maṃdīpā maṃleṇā maṃtāṇā maṃsaraṇā viharanti. Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yaṃ aduṃ khettaṃ majjhimaṃ; evameva mayhaṃ upāsakaupāsikāyo. Tesaṃ pāhaṃ dhammaṃ desemi – ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ, sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsemi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ete hi, gāmaṇi, maṃdīpā maṃleṇā maṃtāṇā maṃsaraṇā viharanti. Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yaṃ aduṃ khettaṃ hīnaṃ jaṅgalaṃ [P 4.0316] ūsaraṃ pāpabhūmi; evameva mayhaṃ aññatitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇaparibbājakā[T 4.0389]. Tesaṃ pāhaṃ dhammaṃ desemi – ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsemi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Appeva nāma ekaṃ padampi ājāneyyuṃ taṃ nesaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.

Just as, headman, that field is excellent, so too are my monks and nuns. To them I teach the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing; I proclaim the holy life, which is entirely complete and pure. For what reason? Because, headman, they dwell with me as their island, their shelter, their protection, and their refuge. Just as, headman, that field is middling, so too are my male and female lay followers. To them I also teach the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing; I proclaim the holy life, which is entirely complete and pure. For what reason? Because, headman, they dwell with me as their island, their shelter, their protection, and their refuge. Just as, headman, that field is inferior, rough, saline, and of poor soil, so too are the ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers of other sects. To them I also teach the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing; I proclaim the holy life, which is entirely complete and pure. For what reason? If only they might understand even a single phrase, that would be for their long-term welfare and happiness."

“Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, purisassa tayo udakamaṇikā – eko udakamaṇiko acchiddo ahārī aparihārī, eko udakamaṇiko acchiddo hārī parihārī, eko udakamaṇiko chiddo hārī parihārī. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, asu puriso udakaṃ nikkhipitukāmo kattha paṭhamaṃ nikkhipeyya, yo vā so udakamaṇiko acchiddo ahārī aparihārī, yo vā so udakamaṇiko acchiddo hārī parihārī, yo vā so udakamaṇiko chiddo hārī parihārī”ti? “Asu, bhante, puriso udakaṃ nikkhipitukāmo, yo so udakamaṇiko acchiddo ahārī aparihārī tattha nikkhipeyya, tattha nikkhipitvā, yo so udakamaṇiko acchiddo hārī parihārī tattha nikkhipeyya, tattha nikkhipitvā, yo so udakamaṇiko chiddo hārī [V 2.0303] parihārī tattha nikkhipeyyapi, nopi nikkhipeyya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Antamaso bhaṇḍadhovanampi bhavissatī”ti.

Just as, headman, a man has three water pots: one water pot is uncracked, does not leak, and does not seep; one water pot is uncracked but leaks and seeps; and one water pot is cracked, leaks, and seeps. What do you think, headman? If this man wanted to store water, where would he store it first: in the water pot that is uncracked, does not leak, and does not seep; in the one that is uncracked but leaks and seeps; or in the one that is cracked, leaks, and seeps?" "Venerable sir, if that man wanted to store water, he would first store it in the water pot that is uncracked, does not leak, and does not seep. Having stored it there, he would then store it in the water pot that is uncracked but leaks and seeps. Having stored it there, he might or might not store it in the water pot that is cracked, leaks, and seeps. For what reason? At the very least, it will be useful for washing things."

“Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yo so udakamaṇiko acchiddo ahārī aparihārī; evameva mayhaṃ bhikkhubhikkhuniyo. Tesāhaṃ dhammaṃ desemi – ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ [M 2.0502] sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ[T 4.0390], kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsemi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ete hi, gāmaṇi, maṃdīpā maṃleṇā maṃtāṇā maṃsaraṇā viharanti. Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yo so udakamaṇiko acchiddo hārī parihārī; evameva mayhaṃ upāsakaupāsikāyo. Tesāhaṃ [P 4.0317] dhammaṃ desemi – ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsemi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ete hi, gāmaṇi, maṃdīpā maṃleṇā maṃtāṇā maṃsaraṇā viharanti. Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, yo so udakamaṇiko chiddo hārī parihārī; evameva mayhaṃ aññatitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇaparibbājakā. Tesāhaṃ dhammaṃ desemi – ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsemi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Appeva nāma ekaṃ padampi ājāneyyuṃ, taṃ nesaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“Just as, chieftain, that water pot is without a hole, not losing water, and not seeping water; so too are my monks and nuns. To them I teach the Dhamma—good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing. I proclaim the holy life that is utterly complete and pure. For what reason? Because, chieftain, they dwell with me as their island, me as their shelter, me as their protection, and me as their refuge. Just as, chieftain, that water pot is without a hole, carries water, and carries water from all around; so too are my laymen and laywomen. To them I teach the Dhamma—good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing. I proclaim the holy life that is utterly complete and pure. For what reason? Because, chieftain, they dwell with me as their island, me as their shelter, me as their protection, and me as their refuge. Just as, chieftain, that water pot has a hole, carries water, and carries water from all around; so too are the ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers of other sects. To them I teach the Dhamma—good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing. I proclaim the holy life that is utterly complete and pure. For what reason? So that they might understand even a single phrase, and that would be for their long-term welfare and happiness.” When this was said, Asibandhakaputta the chieftain said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! … From this day forward, may the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.” The seventh.

8. Saṅkhadhamasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Conch Blower

360. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ viharati pāvārikambavane. Atha kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi nigaṇṭhasāvako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho asibandhakaputtaṃ gāmaṇiṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kathaṃ nu kho, gāmaṇi, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto [T 4.0391] sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ desetī”ti? “Evaṃ kho, bhante, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti – ‘yo koci pāṇaṃ atipāteti, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci adinnaṃ ādiyati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko[V 2.0304], yo koci kāmesu micchā carati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci musā bhaṇati sabbo, so āpāyiko nerayiko. Yaṃbahulaṃ yaṃbahulaṃ viharati, tena tena nīyatī’ti. Evaṃ kho, bhante, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sāvakānaṃ dhammaṃ desetī”ti. “‘Yaṃbahulaṃ yaṃbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati, tena tena [P 4.0318] nīyati’, evaṃ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṃ”.

360. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Nāḷandā in Pāvārika’s mango grove. Then Asibandhakaputta the chieftain, a disciple of the Nigaṇṭhas, approached the Blessed One; having approached, he sat down to one side. The Blessed One said to Asibandhakaputta the chieftain, who was sitting to one side: “How, chieftain, does Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta teach the Dhamma to his disciples?” “Thus, venerable sir, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta teaches the Dhamma to his disciples: ‘Anyone who destroys life is destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell. Anyone who takes what is not given is destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell. Anyone who engages in sexual misconduct is destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell. Anyone who speaks falsely is destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell. As one frequently dwells, by that one is led.’ Thus, venerable sir, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta teaches the Dhamma to his disciples.” “‘As one frequently dwells, by that one is led,’ chieftain—if this is so, then according to the statement of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, no one would be destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell.”

“Taṃ [M 2.0503] kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso pāṇātipātī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṃ upādāya, katamo bahutaro samayo, yaṃ vā so pāṇamatipāteti, yaṃ vā so pāṇaṃ nātipātetī”ti? “Yo so, bhante, puriso pāṇātipātī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṃ upādāya, appataro so samayo yaṃ so pāṇamatipāteti, atha kho sveva bahutaro samayo yaṃ so pāṇaṃ nātipātetī”ti. “‘Yaṃbahulaṃ yaṃbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati tena tena nīyatī’ti, evaṃ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṃ”.

“What do you think, chieftain? Regarding a person who destroys life, taking occasion by night or by day, which is the greater time: the time when he destroys life, or the time when he does not destroy life?” “Venerable sir, for a person who destroys life, taking occasion by night or by day, the time when he destroys life is less; indeed, the time when he does not destroy life is far greater.” “‘As one frequently dwells, by that one is led,’ chieftain—if this is so, then according to the statement of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, no one would be destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso adinnādāyī rattiyā [T 4.0392] vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṃ upādāya, katamo bahutaro samayo, yaṃ vā so adinnaṃ ādiyati, yaṃ vā so adinnaṃ nādiyatī”ti. “Yo so, bhante, puriso adinnādāyī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṃ upādāya appataro so samayo, yaṃ so adinnaṃ ādiyati, atha kho sveva bahutaro samayo, yaṃ so adinnaṃ nādiyatī”ti. “‘Yaṃbahulaṃ yaṃbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati tena tena nīyatī’ti, evaṃ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṃ”.

“What do you think, chieftain? Regarding a person who takes what is not given, taking occasion by night or by day, which is the greater time: that when he takes what is not given, or that when he does not take what is not given?” “Venerable sir, regarding a person who takes what is not given, taking occasion by night or by day, the time when he takes what is not given is less. Indeed, much greater is the time when he does not take what is not given.” “‘As one frequently dwells, by that one is led,’ chieftain—if this is so, then according to the statement of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, no one would be destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso kāmesumicchācārī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṃ upādāya, katamo bahutaro samayo, yaṃ vā so kāmesu micchā carati, yaṃ vā so kāmesu micchā na caratī”ti? “Yo so, bhante, puriso kāmesumicchācārī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṃ upādāya, appataro so samayo yaṃ so kāmesu micchā carati, atha kho sveva bahutaro samayo, yaṃ so kāmesu micchā na caratī”ti. “‘Yaṃbahulaṃ [V 2.0305] yaṃbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati tena tena nīyatī’ti[P 4.0319], evaṃ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṃ”.

“What do you think, chieftain? Regarding a person who engages in sexual misconduct, taking occasion by night or by day, which is the greater time: when he engages in sexual misconduct or when he does not?” “Venerable sir, regarding a person who engages in sexual misconduct, taking occasion by night or by day, the time he engages in sexual misconduct is less, while the time he does not engage in it is far greater.” “‘As one frequently dwells, by that one is led,’ chieftain—if this is so, then according to the statement of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, no one would be destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell.”
