“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, yo so puriso musāvādī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṃ upādāya, katamo bahutaro samayo, yaṃ vā so musā bhaṇati, yaṃ vā so musā na bhaṇatī”ti? “Yo so, bhante[T 4.0393], puriso musāvādī rattiyā vā divasassa vā samayāsamayaṃ upādāya[M 2.0504], appataro so samayo, yaṃ so musā bhaṇati, atha kho sveva bahutaro samayo, yaṃ so musā na bhaṇatī”ti. “‘Yaṃbahulaṃ yaṃbahulañca, gāmaṇi, viharati tena tena nīyatī’ti, evaṃ sante na koci āpāyiko nerayiko bhavissati, yathā nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa vacanaṃ”.

“What do you think, Gāmaṇi? Regarding that person who is accustomed to speaking falsely, depending on the occasion, whether proper or improper, by night or by day, which is the greater period of time: when he speaks falsely, or when he does not speak falsely?” “Venerable Sir, regarding that person who is accustomed to speaking falsely, depending on the occasion, whether proper or improper, by night or by day, the period of time when he speaks falsely is shorter. But indeed, that very period of time when he does not speak falsely is greater.” “Gāmaṇi, if ‘one is led by that with which one dwells much,’ this being so, according to the word of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, no one would be one who arises in the plane of misery, one who arises in hell.”

“Idha, gāmaṇi, ekacco satthā evaṃvādī hoti evaṃdiṭṭhi evaṃdiṭṭhī (ka.) – ‘yo koci pāṇamatipāteti, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci adinnaṃ ādiyati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci kāmesu micchā carati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko, yo koci musā bhaṇati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayiko’ti. Tasmiṃ kho pana, gāmaṇi, satthari sāvako abhippasanno hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘mayhaṃ kho satthā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – yo koci pāṇamatipāteti, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayikoti. Atthi kho pana mayā pāṇo atipātito, ahampamhi āpāyiko nerayikoti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Taṃ, gāmaṇi, vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Mayhaṃ kho satthā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – yo koci adinnaṃ ādiyati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayikoti. Atthi kho pana mayā adinnaṃ ādinnaṃ ahampamhi āpāyiko nerayikoti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Taṃ, gāmaṇi, vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ [T 4.0394] appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Mayhaṃ kho satthā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – yo koci kāmesu micchā carati, sabbo so [P 4.0320] āpāyiko nerayiko’ti. Atthi kho pana mayā kāmesu micchā ciṇṇaṃ. ‘Ahampamhi āpāyiko nerayiko’ti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Taṃ, gāmaṇi, vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Mayhaṃ kho satthā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – yo koci musā bhaṇati, sabbo so āpāyiko nerayikoti. Atthi kho pana mayā musā bhaṇitaṃ. ‘Ahampamhi [V 2.0306] āpāyiko nerayiko’ti diṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhati. Taṃ, gāmaṇi, vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

“Here, Gāmaṇi, a certain teacher is one who speaks thus, one who holds such a view: ‘Whoever destroys a living being, all of them are ones who will arise in the plane of misery, ones who will arise in hell. Whoever takes what is not given, all of them are ones who will arise in the plane of misery, ones who will arise in hell. Whoever engages in sexual misconduct, all of them are ones who will arise in the plane of misery, ones who will arise in hell. Whoever speaks falsely, all of them are ones who will arise in the plane of misery, ones who will arise in hell.’ Now, Gāmaṇi, a disciple has great confidence in that teacher. It occurs to him thus: ‘My teacher is one who speaks thus, one who holds such a view: “Whoever destroys a living being, all of them are ones who will arise in the plane of misery, ones who will arise in hell.” Indeed, a living being has been destroyed by me. I, too, am one who will arise in the plane of misery, one who will arise in hell.’ Thus he acquires the view. Gāmaṇi, not having abandoned that speech, not having abandoned that mind, not having relinquished that view, he is deposited in hell just as if brought and placed there. ‘My teacher is one who speaks thus, one who holds such a view: “Whoever takes what is not given, all of them are ones who will arise in the plane of misery, ones who will arise in hell.” Indeed, what was not given has been taken by me. I, too, am one who will arise in the plane of misery, one who will arise in hell.’ Thus he acquires the view. Gāmaṇi, not having abandoned that speech, not having abandoned that mind, not having relinquished that view, he is deposited in hell just as if brought and placed there. ‘My teacher is one who speaks thus, one who holds such a view: “Whoever engages in sexual misconduct, all of them are ones who will arise in the plane of misery, ones who will arise in hell.” Indeed, I have engaged in sexual misconduct. I, too, am one who will arise in the plane of misery, one who will arise in hell.’ Thus he acquires the view. Gāmaṇi, not having abandoned that speech, not having abandoned that mind, not having relinquished that view, he is deposited in hell just as if brought and placed there. ‘My teacher is one who speaks thus, one who holds such a view: “Whoever speaks falsely, all of them are ones who will arise in the plane of misery, ones who will arise in hell.” Indeed, a falsehood has been spoken by me. I, too, am one who will arise in the plane of misery, one who will arise in hell.’ Thus he acquires the view. Gāmaṇi, not having abandoned that speech, not having abandoned that mind, not having relinquished that view, he is deposited in hell just as if brought and placed there.”

“Idha [M 2.0505] pana, gāmaṇi, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So anekapariyāyena pāṇātipātaṃ garahati vigarahati, ‘pāṇātipātā viramathā’ti cāha. Adinnādānaṃ garahati vigarahati, ‘adinnādānā viramathā’ti cāha. Kāmesumicchācāraṃ garahati, vigarahati ‘kāmesumicchācārā viramathā’ti cāha. Musāvādaṃ garahati vigarahati ‘musāvādā viramathā’ti cāha. Tasmiṃ kho pana, gāmaṇi, satthari sāvako abhippasanno hoti. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘bhagavā kho anekapariyāyena pāṇātipātaṃ garahati [T 4.0395] vigarahati, pāṇātipātā viramathāti cāha. Atthi kho pana mayā pāṇo atipātito yāvatako vā tāvatako vā. Yo kho pana mayā pāṇo atipātito yāvatako vā tāvatako vā, taṃ na suṭṭhu, taṃ na sādhu. Ahañceva ahañce (?) kho pana tappaccayā vippaṭisārī assaṃ. Na metaṃ pāpaṃ kammaṃ pāpakammaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) akataṃ bhavissatī’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya tañceva pāṇātipātaṃ pajahati. Āyatiñca pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti. Evametassa pāpassa kammassa pahānaṃ hoti. Evametassa pāpassa kammassa samatikkamo hoti.

“But here, Gāmaṇi, the Tathāgata arises in the world, an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Fortunate One, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One. He, in many ways, censures and strongly censures the destruction of life, and says, ‘Refrain from the destruction of life.’ He censures and strongly censures taking what is not given, and says, ‘Refrain from taking what is not given.’ He censures and strongly censures sexual misconduct, and says, ‘Refrain from sexual misconduct.’ He censures and strongly censures false speech, and says, ‘Refrain from false speech.’ Now, Gāmaṇi, a disciple has great confidence in that Teacher. He reflects thus: ‘The Blessed One, in many ways, censures and strongly censures the destruction of life, and says, “Refrain from the destruction of life.” Indeed, a living being has been destroyed by me, to whatever extent. That which was done by me was not good, it was not proper. I would indeed be remorseful on account of that, yet this evil kamma of mine will not become as if it were not done.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons that very destruction of life and in the future is one who refrains from the destruction of life. Thus there is the abandoning of this evil kamma. Thus there is the overcoming of this evil kamma.”

“‘Bhagavā kho anekapariyāyena adinnādānaṃ garahati vigarahati, adinnādānā viramathāti cāha. Atthi kho pana mayā adinnaṃ ādinnaṃ yāvatakaṃ vā tāvatakaṃ vā. Yaṃ kho pana mayā adinnaṃ ādinnaṃ yāvatakaṃ vā tāvatakaṃ vā taṃ na suṭṭhu, taṃ na sādhu. Ahañceva kho pana tappaccayā vippaṭisārī assaṃ, na metaṃ pāpaṃ kammaṃ akataṃ bhavissatī’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya tañceva adinnādānaṃ [P 4.0321] pajahati. Āyatiñca adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti. Evametassa pāpassa kammassa pahānaṃ hoti. Evametassa pāpassa kammassa samatikkamo hoti.

“‘The Blessed One, in many ways, censures and strongly censures taking what is not given, and says, “Refrain from taking what is not given.” Indeed, what was not given has been taken by me, to whatever extent. That which was done by me was not good, it was not proper. I would indeed be remorseful on account of that, yet this evil kamma of mine will not become as if it were not done.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons that very act of taking what is not given and in the future is one who refrains from taking what is not given. Thus there is the abandoning of this evil kamma. Thus there is the overcoming of this evil kamma.”

“‘Bhagavā kho pana anekapariyāyena kāmesumicchācāraṃ garahati vigarahati, kāmesumicchācārā viramathāti cāha. Atthi kho pana mayā kāmesu micchā ciṇṇaṃ yāvatakaṃ vā tāvatakaṃ vā. Yaṃ kho pana [T 4.0396] mayā kāmesu micchā ciṇṇaṃ yāvatakaṃ vā tāvatakaṃ vā taṃ [V 2.0307] na suṭṭhu, taṃ na sādhu. Ahañceva kho pana tappaccayā vippaṭisārī assaṃ, na [M 2.0506] metaṃ pāpaṃ kammaṃ akataṃ bhavissatī’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya tañceva kāmesumicchācāraṃ pajahati, āyatiñca kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti. Evametassa pāpassa kammassa pahānaṃ hoti. Evametassa pāpassa kammassa samatikkamo hoti.

“‘Indeed, the Blessed One in many ways condemns and disparages sexual misconduct, and says, “Refrain from sexual misconduct.” Now, there is sexual misconduct practiced by me, to whatever extent. Whatever sexual misconduct was practiced by me, to whatever extent, that was not good, that was not proper. Even if I were to feel remorse on account of that, this evil deed of mine would not become undone.’ Reflecting thus, he abandons that very sexual misconduct and in the future is abstinent from sexual misconduct. In this way, there is the abandoning of that evil deed. In this way, there is the overcoming of that evil deed.

“‘Bhagavā kho pana anekapariyāyena musāvādaṃ garahati vigarahati, musāvādā viramathāti cāha. Atthi kho pana mayā musā bhaṇitaṃ yāvatakaṃ vā tāvatakaṃ vā. Yaṃ kho pana mayā musā bhaṇitaṃ yāvatakaṃ vā tāvatakaṃ vā taṃ na suṭṭhu, taṃ na sādhu. Ahañceva kho pana tappaccayā vippaṭisārī assaṃ, na metaṃ pāpaṃ kammaṃ akataṃ bhavissatī’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya tañceva musāvādaṃ pajahati, āyatiñca musāvādā paṭivirato hoti. Evametassa pāpassa kammassa pahānaṃ hoti. Evametassa pāpassa kammassa samatikkamo hoti.

“‘Indeed, the Blessed One in many ways condemns and disparages false speech, and says, “Abstain from false speech.” Now, there is false speech spoken by me, to whatever extent. Whatever false speech was spoken by me, to whatever extent, that was not good, that was not proper. Even if I were to feel remorse on account of that, this evil deed of mine would not become undone.’ Reflecting thus, he abandons that very false speech and in the future is abstinent from false speech. In this way, there is the abandoning of that evil deed. In this way, there is the overcoming of that evil deed.

“So pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti. Adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti. Kāmesumicchācāraṃ pahāya kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti. Musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti. Pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Samphappalāpaṃ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti. Abhijjhaṃ pahāya [T 4.0397] anabhijjhālu hoti. Byāpādappadosaṃ [P 4.0322] pahāya abyāpannacitto hoti. Micchādiṭṭhiṃ pahāya sammādiṭṭhiko hoti.

“He, having abandoned the taking of life, is abstinent from the taking of life. Having abandoned taking what is not given, he is abstinent from taking what is not given. Having abandoned sexual misconduct, he is abstinent from sexual misconduct. Having abandoned false speech, he is abstinent from false speech. Having abandoned slanderous speech, he is abstinent from slanderous speech. Having abandoned harsh speech, he is abstinent from harsh speech. Having abandoned frivolous talk, he is abstinent from frivolous talk. Having abandoned covetousness, he is not covetous. Having abandoned ill will and malevolence, he is of a mind without ill will. Having abandoned wrong view, he is of right view.

“Sa kho so, gāmaṇi, ariyasāvako evaṃ vigatābhijjho vigatabyāpādo asammūḷho sampajāno paṭissato mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, balavā saṅkhadhamo appakasireneva catuddisā viññāpeyya; evameva kho, gāmaṇi, evaṃ bhāvitāya mettāya cetovimuttiyā evaṃ bahulīkatāya yaṃ pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ, na taṃ tatrāvasissati, na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhati.

“That noble disciple, village headman—thus without covetousness, without ill will, unconfused, clearly comprehending, and mindful—dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, and in every way, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness—extensive, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without distress. Just as, village headman, a strong conch-blower could easily make himself heard in the four directions, so too, village headman, when the liberation of mind by loving-kindness is thus developed and cultivated, any measured kamma does not remain there, does not persist there.

“Sa [M 2.0507] kho so, gāmaṇi, ariyasāvako evaṃ vigatābhijjho vigatabyāpādo asammūḷho sampajāno [V 2.0308] paṭissato karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe…. Upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Seyyathāpi, gāmaṇi, balavā saṅkhadhamo appakasireneva catuddisā viññāpeyya; evameva kho, gāmaṇi, evaṃ bhāvitāya upekkhāya cetovimuttiyā evaṃ bahulīkatāya yaṃ pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ [T 4.0398] na taṃ tatrāvasissati, na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhatī”ti. Evaṃ vutte, asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“That noble disciple, village headman—thus without covetousness, without ill will, unconfused, clearly comprehending, and mindful—dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by appreciative joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, and in every way, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—extensive, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without distress. Just as, village headman, a strong conch-blower could easily make himself heard in the four directions, so too, village headman, when the liberation of mind by equanimity is thus developed and cultivated, any measured kamma does not remain there, does not persist there.” When this was said, Asibandhakaputta the village headman said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir!… From this day forward, may the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.” The Eighth.

9. Kulasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Family

361. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena nāḷandā tadavasari[P 4.0323]. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ viharati pāvārikambavane.

361. On one occasion, while the Blessed One was wandering on tour in the Kosala country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, he arrived at Nāḷandā. There, the Blessed One was dwelling in Pāvārika’s mango grove in Nāḷandā.

Tena kho pana samayena nāḷandā dubbhikkhā hoti dvīhitikā setaṭṭhikā salākāvuttā. Tena kho pana samayena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto nāḷandāyaṃ paṭivasati mahatiyā nigaṇṭhaparisāya saddhiṃ. Atha kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi nigaṇṭhasāvako yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho asibandhakaputtaṃ gāmaṇiṃ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto etadavoca – “ehi tvaṃ, gāmaṇi, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropehi. Evaṃ te kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchissati – ‘asibandhakaputtena gāmaṇinā samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃmahiddhikassa evaṃmahānubhāvassa vādo āropito’”ti.

At that time, Nāḷandā was afflicted by famine, a time of scarcity when people were in doubt whether they would live or die, when there were white bones, and when people subsisted by means of tickets. At that same time, the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta was dwelling in Nāḷandā with a large assembly of Nigaṇṭhas. Then Asibandhakaputta the headman, a disciple of the Nigaṇṭhas, approached the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta. Having approached, he paid homage to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta and sat down to one side. To Asibandhakaputta the headman, who was seated to one side, the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta said this: “Come, headman, present a charge against the ascetic Gotama. In this way, a good report of your fame will spread: ‘A charge has been presented by Asibandhakaputta the headman against the ascetic Gotama, who is of such great psychic power and such great might!’”

“Kathaṃ panāhaṃ, bhante, samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃmahiddhikassa evaṃmahānubhāvassa vādaṃ āropessāmī”ti[V 2.0309]? “Ehi tvaṃ, gāmaṇi, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ [M 2.0508] vadehi – ‘nanu, bhante, bhagavā anekapariyāyena kulānaṃ [T 4.0399] anuddayaṃ anudayaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) vaṇṇeti, anurakkhaṃ vaṇṇeti, anukampaṃ vaṇṇetī’ti? Sace kho, gāmaṇi, samaṇo gotamo evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaroti – ‘evaṃ, gāmaṇi, tathāgato anekapariyāyena kulānaṃ anuddayaṃ vaṇṇeti, anurakkhaṃ vaṇṇeti, anukampaṃ vaṇṇetī’ti, tamenaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘atha kiñcarahi, bhante, bhagavā dubbhikkhe dvīhitike setaṭṭhike salākāvutte mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ cārikaṃ carati? Ucchedāya bhagavā kulānaṃ paṭipanno, anayāya bhagavā kulānaṃ paṭipanno, upaghātāya bhagavā kulānaṃ paṭipanno’ti! Imaṃ kho te, gāmaṇi, samaṇo gotamo ubhatokoṭikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho neva sakkhati sakkhiti (sī.) ma. ni. 2.83 uggilituṃ, neva sakkhati ogilitu”nti. “Evaṃ[P 4.0324], bhante”ti kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

“But how, venerable sir, can I present a charge against the ascetic Gotama, who is of such great psychic power and such great might?” “Come, headman, approach the ascetic Gotama and say this to him: ‘Venerable sir, does not the Blessed One in many ways praise kindness toward families, protection of families, and compassion for families?’ If, headman, the ascetic Gotama, when asked thus, answers: ‘Yes, headman, the Tathāgata in many ways praises kindness toward families, protection of families, and compassion for families,’ then you should say this to him: ‘Then why, venerable sir, does the Blessed One wander on tour with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus in a time of famine, when people are in doubt whether they will live or die, when there are white bones, and when people subsist by means of tickets? Is the Blessed One practicing for the annihilation of families? Is the Blessed One practicing for the destruction of families? Is the Blessed One practicing for the affliction of families?’ This, headman, is a two-horned question which, when put to the ascetic Gotama, he will be able neither to spit out nor to swallow it.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Asibandhakaputta the headman to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta. Then he rose from his seat, paid homage to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and went to the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Asibandhakaputta the headman said this to the Blessed One:

“Nanu, bhante, bhagavā anekapariyāyena kulānaṃ anuddayaṃ vaṇṇeti, anurakkhaṃ vaṇṇeti, anukampaṃ vaṇṇetī”ti? “Evaṃ, gāmaṇi, tathāgato anekapariyāyena kulānaṃ anuddayaṃ vaṇṇeti, anurakkhaṃ vaṇṇeti, anukampaṃ vaṇṇetī”ti. “Atha kiñcarahi, bhante, bhagavā dubbhikkhe dvīhitike setaṭṭhike salākāvutte mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ cārikaṃ [T 4.0400] carati? Ucchedāya bhagavā kulānaṃ paṭipanno, anayāya bhagavā kulānaṃ paṭipanno, upaghātāya bhagavā kulānaṃ paṭipanno”ti. “Ito so, gāmaṇi, ekanavutikappe ekanavuto kappo (syā. kaṃ.), ekanavutikappo (pī.) yamahaṃ anussarāmi, nābhijānāmi kiñci kulaṃ pakkabhikkhānuppadānamattena upahatapubbaṃ. Atha kho yāni tāni kulāni aḍḍhāni mahaddhanāni mahābhogāni pahūtajātarūparajatāni pahūtavittūpakaraṇāni pahūtadhanadhaññāni, sabbāni tāni dānasambhūtāni ceva saccasambhūtāni ca sāmaññasambhūtāni ca. Aṭṭha kho, gāmaṇi, hetū, aṭṭha paccayā kulānaṃ upaghātāya. Rājato vā kulāni upaghātaṃ gacchanti, corato vā kulāni upaghātaṃ gacchanti, aggito vā kulāni upaghātaṃ gacchanti[M 2.0509], udakato vā kulāni upaghātaṃ gacchanti, nihitaṃ vā ṭhānā vigacchati nihitaṃ vā nādhigacchanti (sī. pī.), duppayuttā vā kammantā vipajjanti, kule vā kulaṅgāroti kulānaṃ vā kulaṅgāro (sī.) uppajjati, yo te bhoge vikirati [P 4.0325] vidhamati viddhaṃseti, aniccatāye aṭṭhamīti. Ime kho, gāmaṇi, aṭṭha hetū, aṭṭha paccayā kulānaṃ upaghātāya[V 2.0310]. Imesu kho, gāmaṇi, aṭṭhasu hetūsu, aṭṭhasu paccayesu saṃvijjamānesu yo maṃ evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ucchedāya bhagavā kulānaṃ paṭipanno, anayāya bhagavā kulānaṃ paṭipanno, upaghātāya bhagavā kulānaṃ paṭipanno’ti, taṃ, gāmaṇi, vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye”ti. Evaṃ [T 4.0401] vutte, asibandhakaputto gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Navamaṃ.

“Venerable sir, does not the Blessed One in many ways praise kindness toward families, protection of families, and compassion for families?” “Yes, headman, the Tathāgata in many ways praises kindness toward families, protection of families, and compassion for families.” “Then why, venerable sir, does the Blessed One wander on tour with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus in a time of famine, when people are in doubt whether they will live or die, when there are white bones, and when people subsist by means of tickets? Is the Blessed One practicing for the annihilation of families? Is the Blessed One practicing for the destruction of families? Is the Blessed One practicing for the affliction of families?” “Headman, as far back as I can recollect for ninety-one eons, I am not aware of any family ever having been ruined by the mere giving of cooked almsfood. On the contrary, those families that are affluent, with great wealth, with great possessions, with abundant gold and silver, with abundant assets and property, with abundant money and grain—all these have arisen from giving, from truthfulness, and from the state of being a noble recluse. Headman, there are eight causes, eight conditions for the ruin of families. Families are ruined by kings, by thieves, by fire, or by water; or their hidden treasure is lost from its place; or their badly undertaken works fail; or a waster—a ‘family charcoal’—arises in the family, who scatters, squanders, and destroys their wealth; and impermanence is the eighth. These, headman, are the eight causes, the eight conditions for the ruin of families. When these eight causes and eight conditions exist, headman, if anyone should say of me: ‘The Blessed One is practicing for the annihilation of families, for the destruction of families, for the affliction of families,’ then, headman, without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view, he is set down in hell just as something is set down after being brought.” When this was said, Asibandhakaputta the headman said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! ... May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life, from this day forward.”

10. Maṇicūḷakasuttaṃ

10. The Maṇicūḷaka Sutta

362. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena rājantepure rājaparisāya sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – “kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ, sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ, paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajata”nti!

362. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Now on that occasion, in the royal palace, among the royal assembly who were seated and assembled, this discussion arose: “Gold and silver are allowable for the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans; the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans consent to gold and silver; the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans accept gold and silver.”

Tena kho pana samayena maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti. Atha kho maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi taṃ parisaṃ etadavoca – “mā ayyo ayyā (sī. pī.) evaṃ avacuttha. Na kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ, na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ, nappaṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ, nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatā”ti. Asakkhi kho maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi taṃ parisaṃ saññāpetuṃ. Atha kho maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [P 4.0326] nisinno kho maṇicūḷako gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha, bhante, rājantepure rājaparisāya sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – ‘kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ, sādiyanti samaṇā [T 4.0402] sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ, paṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajata’nti. Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhante, taṃ parisaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘mā ayyo evaṃ avacuttha. Na kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ [V 2.0311] jātarūparajataṃ, na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ, nappaṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā [M 2.0510] jātarūparajataṃ, nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatā’ti. Asakkhiṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, taṃ parisaṃ saññāpetuṃ. Kaccāhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva bhagavato homi, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhāmi, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaromi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī”ti?

Now on that occasion, the headman Maṇicūḷaka was seated in that assembly. Then the headman Maṇicūḷaka said this to that assembly: 'Sirs, do not speak thus. Gold and silver are not allowable for the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans; the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans do not consent to gold and silver; the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans do not accept gold and silver. The ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans have laid aside gems and gold; they have rejected gold and silver.' The headman Maṇicūḷaka was able to convince that assembly. Then the headman Maṇicūḷaka approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the headman Maṇicūḷaka said this to the Blessed One: 'Here, venerable sir, in the royal palace, among the royal assembly who were seated and assembled, this discussion arose: "Gold and silver are allowable for the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans; the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans consent to gold and silver; the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans accept gold and silver." When this was said, venerable sir, I said this to that assembly: "Sirs, do not speak thus. Gold and silver are not allowable for the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans; the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans do not consent to gold and silver; the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans do not accept gold and silver. The ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans have laid aside gems and gold; they have rejected gold and silver." Venerable sir, I was able to convince that assembly. Venerable sir, in answering thus, do I speak in accordance with what was said by the Blessed One, do I not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is not true, do I explain the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and does no reasoned, consequential statement of mine arrive at a censurable point?'

“Taggha tvaṃ, gāmaṇi, evaṃ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva me hosi, na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhasi, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākarosi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati. Na hi, gāmaṇi, kappati samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ jātarūparajataṃ, na sādiyanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ, nappaṭiggaṇhanti samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jātarūparajataṃ, nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā apetajātarūparajatā. Yassa kho, gāmaṇi, jātarūparajataṃ kappati, pañcapi tassa kāmaguṇā kappanti. Yassa pañca kāmaguṇā kappanti ( ) (tassapi jātarūparajataṃ kappati,) (syā. kaṃ.), ekaṃsenetaṃ[T 4.0403], gāmaṇi, dhāreyyāsi assamaṇadhammo asakyaputtiyadhammoti. Api cāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, evaṃ vadāmi – tiṇaṃ tiṇatthikena pariyesitabbaṃ, dāru dārutthikena pariyesitabbaṃ, sakaṭaṃ sakaṭatthikena pariyesitabbaṃ, puriso purisatthikena [P 4.0327] pariyesitabbo pariyesitabbo”ti (?). Natvevāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, kenaci pariyāyena ‘jātarūparajataṃ sāditabbaṃ pariyesitabba’nti vadāmī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Indeed, headman, in answering thus you speak in accordance with what was said by me, and you do not misrepresent me with what is not true. You explain the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and no reasoned, consequential statement of yours arrives at a censurable point. For, headman, gold and silver are not allowable for the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans. The ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans do not consent to gold and silver; the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans do not accept gold and silver. The ascetics who are sons of the Sakyans have laid aside gems and gold; they have rejected gold and silver. Headman, for whomever gold and silver are allowable, for him the five strands of sensual pleasure are also allowable. For whomever the five strands of sensual pleasure are allowable, you should regard this unequivocally, headman, as not the practice of an ascetic, not the practice of a son of the Sakyans. Moreover, headman, I say this: grass is to be sought by one who needs grass, wood by one who needs wood, a cart by one who needs a cart, and a man by one who needs a man. But in no way whatsoever, headman, do I say that gold and silver are to be consented to or to be sought.”

11. Bhadrakasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse to Bhadraka

363. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā mallesu viharati uruvelakappaṃ nāma mallānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho bhadrako gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho bhadrako gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desetū”ti. “Ahañce ahañca (syā. kaṃ. ka.) te, gāmaṇi, atītamaddhānaṃ ārabbha [M 2.0511] dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca deseyyaṃ – ‘evaṃ ahosi atītamaddhāna’nti, tatra te siyā kaṅkhā, siyā vimati. Ahaṃ ce ahañca (syā. kaṃ. ka.) te, gāmaṇi, anāgatamaddhānaṃ ārabbha dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca deseyyaṃ – ‘evaṃ bhavissati anāgatamaddhāna’nti, tatrāpi te siyā kaṅkhā, siyā vimati. Api cāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, idheva nisinno [V 2.0312] ettheva te nisinnassa dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desessāmi. Taṃ suṇāhi[T 4.0404], sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho bhadrako gāmaṇi bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

363. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Mallas, in a town of the Mallas named Uruvelakappa. Then the headman Bhadraka approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the headman Bhadraka said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the origin and the cessation of suffering.' 'If I were to teach you, headman, the origin and cessation of suffering by referring to the past—"Thus it was in the past"—you might have doubt or uncertainty about that. If I were to teach you, headman, the origin and cessation of suffering by referring to the future—"Thus it will be in the future"—you might have doubt or uncertainty about that as well. But I, headman, sitting right here, will teach the origin and cessation of suffering to you as you are sitting right here. Listen to it and attend carefully; I will speak.' 'Yes, venerable sir,' replied the headman Bhadraka to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, atthi te uruvelakappe manussā yesaṃ te vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti? “Atthi me, bhante, uruvelakappe manussā yesaṃ me vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti. “Atthi pana te, gāmaṇi, uruvelakappe manussā yesaṃ te [P 4.0328] vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā nuppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti? “Atthi me, bhante, uruvelakappe manussā yesaṃ me vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā nuppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti. “Ko nu kho, gāmaṇi, hetu, ko paccayo yena te ekaccānaṃ uruvelakappiyānaṃ manussānaṃ vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti? “Yesaṃ me, bhante, uruvelakappiyānaṃ manussānaṃ vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, atthi me tesu chandarāgo[T 4.0405]. Yesaṃ pana, bhante, uruvelakappiyānaṃ manussānaṃ vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā nuppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, natthi me tesu chandarāgo”ti. “Iminā tvaṃ, gāmaṇi, dhammena diṭṭhena viditena akālikena pattena pariyogāḷhena atītānāgate nayaṃ nehi – ‘yaṃ kho kiñci atītamaddhānaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjamānaṃ uppajji uppajjati (sabbattha) sabbaṃ taṃ chandamūlakaṃ chandanidānaṃ. Chando hi mūlaṃ dukkhassa. Yampi hi kiñci anāgatamaddhānaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjamānaṃ uppajjissati, sabbaṃ taṃ chandamūlakaṃ chandanidānaṃ. Chando hi mūlaṃ dukkhassā’”ti[M 2.0512]. “Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāva subhāsitaṃ cidaṃ subhāsitamidaṃ (sī. pī.), bhante, bhagavatā yaṅkiñci atītamaddhānaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjamānaṃ uppajjati, sabbantaṃ chandamūlakaṃ chandanidānaṃ, chando hi mūlaṃ dukkhassāti, yaṅkiñci anāgatamaddhānaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjamānaṃ uppajjissati sabbantaṃ chandamūlakaṃ chandanidānaṃ, chando hi mūlaṃ dukkhassā”ti (syā. kaṃ.) – ‘yaṃ kiñci dukkhaṃ uppajjamānaṃ [P 4.0329] uppajjati, sabbaṃ taṃ chandamūlakaṃ chandanidānaṃ. Chando hi mūlaṃ dukkhassā’ti. “yaṅkiñci atītamaddhānaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjamānaṃ uppajjati, sabbantaṃ chandamūlakaṃ chandanidānaṃ, chando hi mūlaṃ dūkkhassāti, yaṅkiñci anāgatamaddhānaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjamānaṃ uppajjissati, sabbantaṃ chandamūlakaṃ chandanidānaṃ, chando hi mūlaṃ dukkhassā”ti (syā. kaṃ) Atthi me, bhante, ciravāsī nāma kumāro bahi āvasathe āvesane (?) paṭivasati. So khvāhaṃ, bhante, kālasseva vuṭṭhāya purisaṃ uyyojemi uyyojesiṃ (ka.) – ‘gaccha, bhaṇe, ciravāsiṃ kumāraṃ jānāhī’ti. Yāvakīvañca, bhante, so puriso nāgacchati, tassa me hoteva aññathattaṃ – ‘mā heva ciravāsissa kumārassa kiñci ābādhayitthā’”ti ābādhayethāti (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.).

“What do you think, headman? Are there people in Uruvelakappa such that, if they were executed, imprisoned, suffered loss of property, or were censured, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair would arise in you?” “Yes, venerable sir, there are people in Uruvelakappa such that, if they were executed, imprisoned, suffered loss of property, or were censured, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair would arise in me.” “But are there people in Uruvelakappa, headman, such that, if they were executed, imprisoned, suffered loss of property, or were censured, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair would not arise in you?” “Yes, venerable sir, there are people in Uruvelakappa such that, if they were executed, imprisoned, suffered loss of property, or were censured, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair would not arise in me.” “What, headman, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby for some people of Uruvelakappa, if they were executed, imprisoned, suffered loss of property, or were censured, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair would arise in you?” “Venerable sir, for those people of Uruvelakappa for whom, if they were executed, imprisoned, suffered loss of property, or were censured, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair would arise in me—I have desire and passion for them. But for those people of Uruvelakappa for whom, if they were executed, imprisoned, suffered loss of property, or were censured, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair would not arise in me—I have no desire and passion for them.” “By this principle which is seen, known, immediate, attained, and penetrated, headman, you should apply this inference to the past and future: ‘Whatever suffering arose in the past, all of it was rooted in desire, with desire as its source. For desire is the root of suffering. And whatever suffering will arise in the future, all of it will be rooted in desire, with desire as its source. For desire is the root of suffering.’” “It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is marvelous, venerable sir! How well this has been spoken by the Blessed One: ‘Whatever suffering arises, all of it is rooted in desire, with desire as its source. For desire is the root of suffering.’ Venerable sir, I have a son named Ciravāsī who lives in a lodging outside the town. Rising early, venerable sir, I send a man, saying, ‘Go, friend, find out about the boy Ciravāsī.’ And as long as that man does not return, I become anxious, thinking, ‘May nothing afflict the boy Ciravāsī!’”

“Taṃ [V 2.0313] kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, ciravāsissa kumārassa vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti[T 4.0406]? “Ciravāsissa me, bhante, kumārassa vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṃ, kiṃ pana me nuppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti. “Imināpi kho etaṃ, gāmaṇi, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ kiñci dukkhaṃ uppajjamānaṃ uppajjati, sabbaṃ taṃ chandamūlakaṃ chandanidānaṃ. Chando hi mūlaṃ dukkhassā’”ti.

“What do you think, headman? If the boy Ciravāsī were executed, imprisoned, suffered loss of property, or were censured, would sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair arise in you?” “Venerable sir, if the boy Ciravāsī were executed, imprisoned, suffered loss of property, or were censured, there would be an alteration even of my life. How then could sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair not arise in me?” “By this method also, headman, it should be understood: ‘Whatever suffering arises, all of it is rooted in desire, with desire as its source. For desire is the root of suffering.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, yadā te ciravāsimātā ciravāsissa mātā (sī. pī.) adiṭṭhā ahosi, assutā ahosi, te ciravāsimātuyā chando vā rāgo vā pemaṃ vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Dassanaṃ vā te, gāmaṇi, āgamma savanaṃ vā evaṃ te ahosi – ‘ciravāsimātuyā chando vā rāgo vā pemaṃ vā’”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, headman? When Ciravāsī's mother was unseen and unheard of by you, did you have desire, passion, or affection for her?” “No, venerable sir.” “Was it on account of seeing or hearing her, headman, that you came to have desire, passion, or affection for Ciravāsī's mother?” “Yes, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, ciravāsimātuyā te vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti? “Ciravāsimātuyā [P 4.0330] me, bhante, vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṃ, kiṃ pana me nuppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti! “Imināpi kho etaṃ, gāmaṇi, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ – ‘yaṃ kiñci dukkhaṃ uppajjamānaṃ uppajjati, sabbaṃ taṃ chandamūlakaṃ chandanidānaṃ. Chando hi mūlaṃ dukkhassā’”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

“What do you think, headman? If Ciravāsī's mother were to be killed, imprisoned, suffer loss of property, or be censured, would sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair arise in you?” “Venerable sir, if Ciravāsī's mother were to be killed, imprisoned, suffer loss of property, or be censured, there would be an alteration even of my life; how then could sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair not arise in me?” “By this method also, headman, it should be understood: ‘Whatever suffering arises, all of it is rooted in desire, with desire as its source. For desire is the root of suffering.’”

12. Rāsiyasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse to Rāsiya

364. Atha [T 4.0407][M 2.0513] kho rāsiyo gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rāsiyo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaṃ tapaṃ garahati, sabbaṃ tapassiṃ lūkhajīviṃ ekaṃsena upavadati upakkosatī’ti upakkosati upavadatīti (dī. ni. 1.381). Ye te, bhante, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaṃ tapaṃ garahati, sabbaṃ tapassiṃ lūkhajīviṃ ekaṃsena upavadati upakkosatī’ti, kacci te, bhante, bhagavato vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī”ti? “Ye [V 2.0314] te, gāmaṇi, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaṃ tapaṃ garahati, sabbaṃ tapassiṃ lūkhajīviṃ ekaṃsena upavadati upakkosatī’ti, na me te vuttavādino, abbhācikkhanti ca pana maṃ te asatā tucchā abhūtena”.

364. Then the headman Rāsiya went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down to one side. Seated thus, the headman Rāsiya said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I have heard it said: ‘The ascetic Gotama criticizes all asceticism; he categorically condemns and reviles every ascetic who leads a harsh life.’ Venerable sir, those who say this—are they reporting the Blessed One’s own words? Do they not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is untrue? Do they declare what is in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no reasonable consequence of their assertion would provide grounds for criticism?” “Headman, those who say: ‘The ascetic Gotama criticizes all asceticism; he categorically condemns and reviles every ascetic who leads a harsh life’—they are not reporting my own words. They misrepresent me with what is nonexistent, empty, and false.”

“Dveme, gāmaṇi, antā pabbajitena na sevitabbā – yo cāyaṃ kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyogo hīno gammo pothujjaniko anariyo anatthasaṃhito, yo cāyaṃ attakilamathānuyogo dukkho anariyo anatthasaṃhito. Ete te, gāmaṇi, ubho ante anupagamma majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā [P 4.0331] – cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Katamā ca sā, gāmaṇi, majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā – cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho sā, gāmaṇi, majjhimā paṭipadā [T 4.0408] tathāgatena abhisambuddhā – cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

“Headman, these two extremes should not be cultivated by one who has gone forth. What two? There is the devotion to indulgence in sensual pleasures, which is base, vulgar, worldly, ignoble, and unbeneficial; and there is the devotion to self-mortification, which is painful, ignoble, and unbeneficial. Without approaching either of these two extremes, the Tathāgata has awakened to the middle path, which produces vision, produces knowledge, and leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. And what, headman, is that middle path awakened to by the Tathāgata, which produces vision, produces knowledge, and leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view… right concentration. This, headman, is that middle path awakened to by the Tathāgata, which produces vision, produces knowledge, and leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.

“Tayo kho me, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogino santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame tayo? Idha, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati, sāhasena adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti. Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena. Adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti. Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati [M 2.0514] sāhasena. Adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti.

“Headman, there are these three kinds of enjoyers of sensual pleasures existing in the world. What are the three? Here, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth unrighteously and by force. Having sought wealth unrighteously and by force, he does not make himself happy and pleased, does not share it, and does not perform meritorious deeds. Again, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth unrighteously and by force. Having sought wealth unrighteously and by force, he makes himself happy and pleased, but does not share it and does not perform meritorious deeds. Again, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth unrighteously and by force. Having sought wealth unrighteously and by force, he makes himself happy and pleased, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds.

“Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi. Dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi na [P 4.0332] attānaṃ sukheti, na pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karoti. Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi. Dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karoti. Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati, sāhasenapi asāhasenapi[V 2.0315]. Dhammādhammena bhoge [T 4.0409] pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti.

“Again, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with and without force. Having sought wealth in this way, he does not make himself happy and pleased, does not share it, and does not perform meritorious deeds. Again, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with and without force. Having sought wealth in this way, he makes himself happy and pleased, but does not share it and does not perform meritorious deeds. Again, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with and without force. Having sought wealth in this way, he makes himself happy and pleased, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds.

“Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena. Dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena na attānaṃ sukheti, na pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karoti. Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena. Dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karoti. Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena. Dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti. Te ca bhoge gadhito gathito (sī.) mucchito ajjhopanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati. Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena. Dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena [P 4.0333] attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti. Te ca bhoge agadhito amucchito anajjhopanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.

“Again, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth righteously and without force. Having sought wealth righteously and without force, he does not make himself happy and pleased, does not share it, and does not perform meritorious deeds. Again, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth righteously and without force. Having sought wealth righteously and without force, he makes himself happy and pleased, but does not share it and does not perform meritorious deeds. Again, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth righteously and without force. Having sought wealth righteously and without force, he makes himself happy and pleased, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds. And he enjoys that wealth being greedy for it, infatuated with it, and attached to it, not seeing the danger and without the wisdom of escape from it. Again, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth righteously and without force. Having sought wealth righteously and without force, he makes himself happy and pleased, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds. And he enjoys that wealth without being greedy for it, without being infatuated with it, and without being attached to it, seeing the danger and with the wisdom of escape from it.

“Tatra[M 2.0515], gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena, adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena na attānaṃ sukheti, na pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karoti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho. Katamehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho? Adhammena [T 4.0410] bhoge pariyesati sāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. Na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇetīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karotīti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī imehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

Headman, among them, that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth unrighteously and with violence, and having sought wealth unrighteously and with violence, neither makes himself happy and pleased, nor shares, nor performs meritorious deeds: this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is blameworthy on three grounds. On what three grounds is he blameworthy? ‘He seeks wealth unrighteously and with violence’—on this first ground he is blameworthy. ‘He neither makes himself happy nor pleased’—on this second ground he is blameworthy. ‘He neither shares nor performs meritorious deeds’—on this third ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is blameworthy on these three grounds.

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena, adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karoti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho, ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Katamehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho? Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. Na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karotīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Katamena ekena ṭhānena [V 2.0316] pāsaṃso? Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetīti, iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho, iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso.

Headman, among them, that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth unrighteously and with violence, and having sought wealth unrighteously and with violence, makes himself happy and pleased, but neither shares nor performs meritorious deeds: this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is blameworthy on two grounds and praiseworthy on one ground. On what two grounds is he blameworthy? ‘He seeks wealth unrighteously and with violence’—on this first ground he is blameworthy. ‘He neither shares nor performs meritorious deeds’—on this second ground he is blameworthy. On what one ground is he praiseworthy? ‘He makes himself happy and pleased’—on this one ground he is praiseworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is blameworthy on these two grounds and praiseworthy on this one ground.

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena, adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena [P 4.0334] attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī ekena ṭhānena gārayho, dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso. Katamena ekena ṭhānena gārayho? Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenāti, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Katamehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso? Attānaṃ [T 4.0411] sukheti pīṇetīti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Saṃvibhajati puññāni karotīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho, imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso.

Headman, among them, that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth unrighteously and with violence, and having sought wealth unrighteously and with violence, makes himself happy and pleased, shares, and performs meritorious deeds: this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is blameworthy on one ground and praiseworthy on two grounds. On what one ground is he blameworthy? ‘He seeks wealth unrighteously and with violence’—on this one ground he is blameworthy. On what two grounds is he praiseworthy? ‘He makes himself happy and pleased’—on this first ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He shares and performs meritorious deeds’—on this second ground he is praiseworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is blameworthy on this one ground and praiseworthy on these two grounds.

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi, dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi na attānaṃ sukheti, na pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na [M 2.0516] puññāni karoti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso, tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho. Katamena ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso? Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenāti, iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Katamehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho? Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. Na attānaṃ sukheti, na pīṇetīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karotīti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso, imehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

Headman, among them, that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with violence and without violence, and having sought wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with violence and without violence, neither makes himself happy and pleased, nor shares, nor performs meritorious deeds: this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is praiseworthy on one ground and blameworthy on three grounds. On what one ground is he praiseworthy? ‘He seeks wealth righteously and without violence’—on this one ground he is praiseworthy. On what three grounds is he blameworthy? ‘He seeks wealth unrighteously and with violence’—on this first ground he is blameworthy. ‘He neither makes himself happy nor pleased’—on this second ground he is blameworthy. ‘He neither shares nor performs meritorious deeds’—on this third ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is praiseworthy on this one ground and blameworthy on these three grounds.

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi, dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karoti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso, dvīhi [T 4.0412] ṭhānehi gārayho. Katamehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso? Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso[P 4.0335]. Katamehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho? Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. Na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karotīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena [V 2.0317] gārayho. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso, imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

Headman, among them, that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with violence and without violence, and having sought wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with violence and without violence, makes himself happy and pleased, but neither shares nor performs meritorious deeds: this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is praiseworthy on two grounds and blameworthy on two grounds. On what two grounds is he praiseworthy? ‘He seeks wealth righteously and without violence’—on this first ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He makes himself happy and pleased’—on this second ground he is praiseworthy. On what two grounds is he blameworthy? ‘He seeks wealth unrighteously and with violence’—on this first ground he is blameworthy. ‘He neither shares nor performs meritorious deeds’—on this second ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is praiseworthy on these two grounds and blameworthy on these two grounds.

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi, dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso, ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Katamehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso? Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Saṃvibhajati puññāni karotīti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Katamena ekena ṭhānena gārayho? Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenāti[M 2.0517], iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī imehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.

Headman, among them, that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with violence and without violence, and having sought wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with violence and without violence, makes himself happy and pleased, shares, and performs meritorious deeds: this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is praiseworthy on three grounds and blameworthy on one ground. On what three grounds is he praiseworthy? ‘He seeks wealth righteously and without violence’—on this first ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He makes himself happy and pleased’—on this second ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He shares and performs meritorious deeds’—on this third ground he is praiseworthy. On what one ground is he blameworthy? ‘He seeks wealth unrighteously and with violence’—on this one ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, Headman, is praiseworthy on these three grounds and blameworthy on this one ground.

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena[T 4.0413], dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena, na attānaṃ sukheti, na pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karoti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso, dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho. Katamena ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso? Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenāti, iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Katamehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho? Na attānaṃ sukheti, na pīṇetīti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. Na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karotīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso, imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

Among these, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth rightly and non-violently; having sought wealth rightly and non-violently, he does not make himself happy or satisfied, does not share it, and does not perform meritorious deeds. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, headman, is praiseworthy on one ground and blameworthy on two grounds. On which one ground is he praiseworthy? ‘He seeks wealth rightly and non-violently’; on this one ground he is praiseworthy. On which two grounds is he blameworthy? ‘He does not make himself happy or satisfied’; on this first ground he is blameworthy. ‘He does not share it or perform meritorious deeds’; on this second ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, headman, is praiseworthy on this one ground and blameworthy on these two grounds.

“Tatra[P 4.0336], gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karoti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso, ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Katamehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso? Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Katamena ekena ṭhānena gārayho[V 2.0318]? Na saṃvibhajati, na puññāni karotīti, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.

“Among these, headman, this enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth rightly and non-violently; having sought wealth rightly and non-violently, he makes himself happy and satisfied, but does not share it or perform meritorious deeds. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, headman, is praiseworthy on two grounds and blameworthy on one ground. On which two grounds is he praiseworthy? ‘He seeks wealth rightly and non-violently’—on this first ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He makes himself happy and satisfied’—on this second ground he is praiseworthy. On which one ground is he blameworthy? ‘He does not share it or perform meritorious deeds’—on this one ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, headman, is praiseworthy on these two grounds and blameworthy on this one ground.”

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena[T 4.0414], dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti, te ca bhoge gadhito mucchito ajjhopanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso, ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Katamehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso? Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Saṃvibhajati puññāni karotīti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso[M 2.0518]. Katamena ekena ṭhānena gārayho? Te ca bhoge gadhito mucchito ajjhopanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjatīti, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī imehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.

Among these, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth rightly and non-violently; having sought wealth rightly and non-violently, he makes himself happy and satisfied, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds. And he enjoys that wealth while being greedy, infatuated, and engrossed, not seeing the danger and without the wisdom of escape. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, headman, is praiseworthy on three grounds and blameworthy on one ground. On which three grounds is he praiseworthy? ‘He seeks wealth rightly and non-violently’; on this first ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He makes himself happy and satisfied’; on this second ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He shares it and performs meritorious deeds’; on this third ground he is praiseworthy. On which one ground is he blameworthy? ‘He enjoys that wealth while being greedy, infatuated, and engrossed, not seeing the danger and without the wisdom of escape’; on this one ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, headman, is praiseworthy on these three grounds and blameworthy on this one ground.

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti. Te [P 4.0337] ca bhoge agadhito amucchito anajjhopanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī catūhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso. Katamehi catūhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso? Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenāti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Saṃvibhajati puññāni karotīti, iminā tatiyena [T 4.0415] ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Te ca bhoge agadhito amucchito anajjhopanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjatīti, iminā catutthena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, kāmabhogī imehi catūhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso.

Among these, headman, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth rightly and non-violently; having sought wealth rightly and non-violently, he makes himself happy and satisfied, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds. And he enjoys that wealth without being greedy, infatuated, or engrossed, seeing the danger and with the wisdom of escape. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, headman, is praiseworthy on four grounds. On which four grounds is he praiseworthy? ‘He seeks wealth rightly and non-violently’; on this first ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He makes himself happy and satisfied’; on this second ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He shares it and performs meritorious deeds’; on this third ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He enjoys that wealth without being greedy, infatuated, or engrossed, seeing the danger and with the wisdom of escape’; on this fourth ground he is praiseworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, headman, is praiseworthy on these four grounds.

“Tayome, gāmaṇi, tapassino lūkhajīvino santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame tayo? Idha, gāmaṇi, ekacco tapassī lūkhajīvī saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti – ‘appeva nāma kusalaṃ dhammaṃ adhigaccheyyaṃ, appeva nāma uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ [V 2.0319] sacchikareyya’nti. So attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, kusalañca dhammaṃ nādhigacchati, uttari ca manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ na sacchikaroti.

“Headman, there are these three ascetics living a rough life who are found in the world. What three? Here, headman, a certain ascetic, living a rough life, has gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith, thinking: ‘If only I might attain a wholesome state; if only I might realize a state superior to the human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones!’ He heats and torments himself, but he does not attain a wholesome state, nor does he realize a state superior to the human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.”

“Idha pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco tapassī lūkhajīvī saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti – ‘appeva nāma kusalaṃ dhammaṃ adhigaccheyyaṃ, appeva nāma uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikareyya’nti. So attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, kusalañhi kho dhammaṃ adhigacchati, uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ na sacchikaroti.

“Furthermore, headman, a certain ascetic, living a rough life, has gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith, thinking: ‘If only I might attain a wholesome state; if only I might realize a state superior to the human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.’ He heats and torments himself, and he does indeed attain a wholesome state, but he does not realize a state superior to the human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.”

“Idha [M 2.0519][P 4.0338] pana, gāmaṇi, ekacco tapassī lūkhajīvī saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti – ‘appeva nāma kusalaṃ dhammaṃ adhigaccheyyaṃ, appeva nāma uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikareyya’nti. So attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti[T 4.0416], kusalañca dhammaṃ adhigacchati, uttari ca manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikaroti.

“Furthermore, headman, a certain ascetic, living a rough life, has gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith, thinking: ‘If only I might attain a wholesome state; if only I might realize a state superior to the human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.’ He heats and torments himself, and he attains a wholesome state and realizes a state superior to the human state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.”

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ tapassī lūkhajīvī attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, kusalañca dhammaṃ nādhigacchati, uttari ca manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ na sacchikaroti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, tapassī lūkhajīvī tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho. Katamehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho? Attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpetīti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. Kusalañca dhammaṃ nādhigacchatīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Uttari ca manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ na sacchikarotīti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, tapassī lūkhajīvī, imehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

“Therein, headman, as to that ascetic who lives a rough life, who heats and torments himself, but does not attain a wholesome state, and does not realize a state superior to the human, a special distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones—this ascetic, headman, who lives a rough life is blameworthy on three grounds. On which three grounds is he blameworthy? That he heats and torments himself—on this first ground he is blameworthy. That he does not attain a wholesome state—on this second ground he is blameworthy. That he does not realize a state superior to the human, a special distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones—on this third ground he is blameworthy. This ascetic, headman, who lives a rough life, is blameworthy on these three grounds.”

“Tatra, gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ tapassī lūkhajīvī attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, kusalañhi kho dhammaṃ adhigacchati, uttari ca manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ na sacchikaroti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, tapassī lūkhajīvī dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho, ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Katamehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho? Attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpetīti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. Uttari ca manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ na sacchikarotīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Katamena ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso? Kusalañhi kho dhammaṃ adhigacchatīti, iminā [V 2.0320] ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, tapassī lūkhajīvī imehi [T 4.0417] dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho, iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso.

“Therein, headman, as to that ascetic who lives a rough life, who heats and torments himself, and indeed attains a wholesome state, but does not realize a state superior to the human, a special distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones—this ascetic, headman, who lives a rough life is blameworthy on two grounds and praiseworthy on one ground. On which two grounds is he blameworthy? That he heats and torments himself—on this first ground he is blameworthy. That he does not realize a state superior to the human, a special distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones—on this second ground he is blameworthy. On which one ground is he praiseworthy? That he indeed attains a wholesome state—on this one ground he is praiseworthy. This ascetic, headman, who lives a rough life, is blameworthy on these two grounds and praiseworthy on this one ground.”

“Tatra[P 4.0339], gāmaṇi, yvāyaṃ tapassī lūkhajīvī attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, kusalañca dhammaṃ adhigacchati, uttari ca manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikaroti. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, tapassī lūkhajīvī ekena ṭhānena gārayho, dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso. Katamena ekena ṭhānena gārayho? Attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpetīti, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Katamehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso? Kusalañca dhammaṃ adhigacchatīti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Uttari ca manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikarotīti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso[M 2.0520]. Ayaṃ, gāmaṇi, tapassī lūkhajīvī iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho, imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso.

“Therein, headman, as to that ascetic who lives a rough life, who heats and torments himself, yet attains a wholesome state and realizes a state superior to the human, a special distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones—this ascetic, headman, who lives a rough life is blameworthy on one ground and praiseworthy on two grounds. On which one ground is he blameworthy? That he heats and torments himself—on this one ground he is blameworthy. On which two grounds is he praiseworthy? That he attains a wholesome state—on this first ground he is praiseworthy. That he realizes a state superior to the human, a special distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones—on this second ground he is praiseworthy. This ascetic, headman, who lives a rough life, is blameworthy on this one ground and praiseworthy on these two grounds.”

“Tisso imā, gāmaṇi, sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṃ veditabbā viññūhi. Katamā tisso? Yaṃ ratto rāgādhikaraṇaṃ attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti. Rāge pahīne nevattabyābādhāya ceteti, na parabyābādhāya ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti. Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṃ veditabbā viññūhi. Yaṃ duṭṭho dosādhikaraṇaṃ attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi [T 4.0418] ceteti. Dose pahīne nevattabyābādhāya ceteti, na parabyābādhāya ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti. Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā [P 4.0340] akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṃ veditabbā viññūhi. Yaṃ mūḷho mohādhikaraṇaṃ attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti. Mohe pahīne nevattabyābādhāya ceteti, na parabyābādhāya ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti. Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṃ veditabbā viññūhi. Imā kho, gāmaṇi, tisso sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṃ veditabbā viññūhī”ti.

“Headman, there are these three purgations that are visible here and now, without fever, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced personally by the wise. What three? When one is lustful, based on lust, one intends for one's own affliction, for others' affliction, and for the affliction of both. When lust is abandoned, one does not intend for one's own affliction, for others' affliction, or for the affliction of both. This is a purgation that is visible here and now, without fever, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced personally by the wise. When one is hateful, based on hate, one intends for one's own affliction, for others' affliction, and for the affliction of both. When hate is abandoned, one does not intend for one's own affliction, for others' affliction, or for the affliction of both. This is a purgation that is visible here and now, without fever, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced personally by the wise. When one is deluded, based on delusion, one intends for one's own affliction, for others' affliction, and for the affliction of both. When delusion is abandoned, one does not intend for one's own affliction, for others' affliction, or for the affliction of both. This is a purgation that is visible here and now, without fever, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced personally by the wise. These, headman, are the three purgations that are visible here and now, without fever, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced personally by the wise.”

Evaṃ vutte, rāsiyo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Dvādasamaṃ.

When this was said, Rāsiya the headman said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! … From this day forward, may the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.” Twelfth.

13. Pāṭaliyasuttaṃ

13. The Discourse with Pāṭaliya

365. Ekaṃ [V 2.0321] samayaṃ bhagavā koliyesu viharati uttaraṃ nāma uttarakaṃ nāma (sī.) koliyānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho pāṭaliyo gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho pāṭaliyo gāmaṇi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘samaṇo gotamo māyaṃ jānātī’ti. Ye te, bhante, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo māyaṃ jānātī’ti, kacci te, bhante, bhagavato [M 2.0521] vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ [T 4.0419] ṭhānaṃ āgacchati? Anabbhācikkhitukāmā hi mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavanta”nti. “Ye te, gāmaṇi, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo māyaṃ jānātī’ti, vuttavādino ceva me, te na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatīti, saccaṃyeva [P 4.0341] kira, bho, mayaṃ tesaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ na saddahāma – ‘samaṇo gotamo māyaṃ jānātīti, samaṇo khalu bho gotamo māyāvī’ti. Yo nu kho, gāmaṇi, evaṃ vadeti – ‘ahaṃ māyaṃ jānāmī’ti, so evaṃ vadeti – ‘ahaṃ māyāvī’ti. Tatheva taṃ bhagavā hoti, tatheva taṃ sugata hotī”ti. Tena hi, gāmaṇi, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi; yathā te khameyya, tathā taṃ byākareyyāsi –

365. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Koliyans, in a Koliyan town named Uttara. Then Pāṭaliya the headman approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Pāṭaliya the headman said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, I have heard this: “The ascetic Gotama knows deceit.” Those, venerable sir, who say thus: “The ascetic Gotama knows deceit,” are they speakers of what has been said by the Blessed One? Do they not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is untrue? Do they explain in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no reasonable consequence of their assertion gives ground for criticism? For we do not wish, venerable sir, to misrepresent the Blessed One.' 'Headman, those who say thus: “The ascetic Gotama knows deceit,” are speakers of what has been said by me. They do not misrepresent me with what is untrue. They explain in accordance with the Dhamma, and no reasonable consequence of their assertion gives ground for criticism.' 'So it is true then! We did not believe those ascetics and brahmins who said, “The ascetic Gotama knows deceit.” So then, the ascetic Gotama is indeed deceitful!' 'Headman, does one who says, “I know deceit,” thereby say, “I am deceitful”?' 'It is just so, Blessed One! It is just so, Sugata!' 'Well then, headman, I will question you in return on this very point. Answer as you see fit.'

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, jānāsi tvaṃ koliyānaṃ lambacūḷake bhaṭe”ti? “Jānāmahaṃ, bhante, koliyānaṃ lambacūḷake bhaṭe”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, kimatthiyā koliyānaṃ lambacūḷakā bhaṭā”ti? “Ye ca, bhante, koliyānaṃ corā te ca paṭisedhetuṃ, yāni ca koliyānaṃ dūteyyāni tāni ca vahātuṃ tāni ca pahātuṃ (syā. kaṃ.), tāni ca yātuṃ (katthaci), tāni cāvahātuṃ (?), etadatthiyā, bhante, koliyānaṃ lambacūḷakā bhaṭā”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gāmaṇi, jānāsi tvaṃ koliyānaṃ lambacūḷake bhaṭe sīlavante vā te dussīle vā”ti? “Jānāmahaṃ, bhante, koliyānaṃ lambacūḷake bhaṭe dussīle pāpadhamme[T 4.0420]; ye ca loke dussīlā pāpadhammā koliyānaṃ lambacūḷakā bhaṭā tesaṃ aññatarā”ti. “Yo nu kho, gāmaṇi, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘pāṭaliyo gāmaṇi jānāti koliyānaṃ lambacūḷake bhaṭe dussīle pāpadhamme, pāṭaliyopi gāmaṇi dussīlo pāpadhammo’ti, sammā nu kho so vadamāno vadeyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante! Aññe, bhante, koliyānaṃ lambacūḷakā bhaṭā, aññohamasmi. Aññathādhammā koliyānaṃ lambacūḷakā bhaṭā, aññathādhammohamasmī”ti. “Tvañhi [V 2.0322][P 4.0342] nāma, gāmaṇi, lacchasi – ‘pāṭaliyo gāmaṇi jānāti koliyānaṃ lambacūḷake bhaṭe dussīle pāpadhamme, na ca pāṭaliyo gāmaṇi dussīlo pāpadhammo’ti, kasmā tathāgato na lacchati – ‘tathāgato māyaṃ jānāti, na ca tathāgato māyāvī’ti? Māyaṃ cāhaṃ, gāmaṇi, pajānāmi, māyāya [M 2.0522] ca vipākaṃ, yathāpaṭipanno ca māyāvī kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati tañca pajānāmi”.

What do you think, headman? Do you know the Lambacūḷaka retainers of the Koliyans?' 'I know them, venerable sir, the Lambacūḷaka retainers of the Koliyans.' 'What do you think, headman? For what purpose do the Koliyans have the Lambacūḷaka retainers?' 'To repel the thieves of the Koliyans, venerable sir, and to carry their messages—for this purpose, venerable sir, the Koliyans have the Lambacūḷaka retainers.' 'What do you think, headman?
