Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samādhibalaṃ bhāveti…pe… ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paññābalaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo…pe….

And what, monks, is the path leading to the Unconditioned? Here, monks, a monk develops the power of faith, which is based on seclusion… This, monks, is called the path leading to the Unconditioned… And what, monks, is the path leading to the Unconditioned? Here, monks, a monk develops the power of energy… This, monks, is called the path leading to the Unconditioned… And what, monks, is the path leading to the Unconditioned? Here, monks, a monk develops the power of mindfulness… This, monks, is called the path leading to the Unconditioned… And what, monks, is the path leading to the Unconditioned? Here, monks, a monk develops the power of concentration… This, monks, is called the path leading to the Unconditioned… And what, monks, is the path leading to the Unconditioned? Here, monks, a monk develops the power of wisdom, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and resulting in relinquishment. This, monks, is called the path leading to the Unconditioned…

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo…pe… katamo [T 4.0449] ca, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo…pe….

And what, monks, is the path leading to the Unconditioned? Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness… he develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena… he develops the enlightenment factor of energy… he develops the enlightenment factor of rapture… he develops the enlightenment factor of tranquility… he develops the enlightenment factor of concentration… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and resulting in relinquishment. This, monks, is called the path leading to the Unconditioned…

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo…pe… katamo [P 4.0368] ca, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammāsaṅkappaṃ bhāveti [V 2.0341] …pe… sammāvācaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammākammantaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāājīvaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāvāyāmaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsatiṃ bhāveti…pe… asaṅkhatañca vo bhikkhave, desessāmi asaṅkhatagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, asaṅkhataṃ…pe…? Katamo ca, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ[M 2.0541]. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatagāmimaggo. Iti kho, bhikkhave, desitaṃ vo mayā asaṅkhataṃ, desito asaṅkhatagāmimaggo. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya, kataṃ vo taṃ mayā. Etāni, bhikkhave, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni. Jhāyatha, bhikkhave, mā pamādattha; mā pacchā [T 4.0450] vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And what, Bhikkhus, is the path leading to the Unconditioned? Here, Bhikkhus, a monk develops right view based on seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, culminating in relinquishment. This, Bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the Unconditioned… and so on… And what, Bhikkhus, is the path leading to the Unconditioned? Here, Bhikkhus, a monk develops right intention… and so on… right speech… and so on… right action… and so on… right livelihood… and so on… right effort… and so on… right mindfulness… and so on… Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the Unconditioned and the path leading to the Unconditioned. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the Unconditioned?… and so on… And what, Bhikkhus, is the path leading to the Unconditioned? Here, Bhikkhus, a monk develops right concentration based on seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, culminating in relinquishment. This, Bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the Unconditioned. Thus, Bhikkhus, the Unconditioned has been taught to you by me, and the path leading to the Unconditioned has been taught. That which should be done by a teacher for his disciples, seeking their welfare, being compassionate, out of compassion, that has been done for you by me. These, Bhikkhus, are the roots of trees; these are empty dwellings. Meditate, Bhikkhus, do not be negligent; do not be remorseful later. This is our instruction to you.” The first.

2. Anatasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the State Without Craving

378. “Anatañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, anatagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, anataṃ…pe…”. (Yathā asaṅkhataṃ tathā vitthāretabbaṃ). Dutiyaṃ.

378. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the state without craving and the path leading to the state without craving. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the state without craving?… and so on…” (To be elaborated as for the Unconditioned.) The second.

3-32. Anāsavādisuttaṃ

3-32. The Discourses on the Taintless and so forth

379-408. “Anāsavañca [P 4.0369] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anāsavagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, anāsavaṃ…pe… saccañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi saccagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, saccaṃ…pe… pārañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi pāragāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, pāraṃ…pe… nipuṇañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi nipuṇagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, nipuṇaṃ…pe… sududdasañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi sududdasagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, sududdasaṃ…pe… ajajjarañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi ajajjaragāmiñca [V 2.0342] maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, ajajjaraṃ…pe… dhuvañca [P 4.0370] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi dhuvagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhuvaṃ…pe… apalokitañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi apalokitagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, apalokitaṃ…pe… anidassanañca [T 4.0451] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anidassanagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, anidassanaṃ…pe… nippapañcañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi nippapañcagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, nippapañcaṃ…pe…?

“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the taintless and the path leading to the taintless. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the taintless?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the truth and the path leading to the truth. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the truth?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the far shore and the path leading to the far shore. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the far shore?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the subtle and the path leading to the subtle. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the subtle?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the very hard to see and the path leading to the very hard to see. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the very hard to see?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unaging and the path leading to the unaging. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the unaging?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the stable and the path leading to the stable. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the stable?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unperishable and the path leading to the unperishable. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the unperishable?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the invisible and the path leading to the invisible. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the invisible?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the non-proliferated and the path leading to the non-proliferated. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-proliferated?… and so on…”

“Santañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi santagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, santaṃ…pe… amatañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi amatagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, amataṃ…pe… paṇītañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi paṇītagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, paṇītaṃ…pe… sivañca vo, bhikkhave[M 2.0542], desessāmi sivagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, sivaṃ…pe… khemañca [P 4.0371] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi khemagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, khemaṃ…pe… taṇhākkhayañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi taṇhākkhayagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, taṇhākkhayaṃ…pe…?

“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the peaceful and the path leading to the peaceful. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the peaceful?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the deathless and the path leading to the deathless. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the deathless?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the sublime and the path leading to the sublime. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the sublime?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the blissful and the path leading to the blissful. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the blissful?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the secure and the path leading to the secure. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the secure?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the destruction of craving and the path leading to the destruction of craving. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the destruction of craving?… and so on…”

“Acchariyañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi acchariyagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, acchariyaṃ…pe… abbhutañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi abbhutagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, abbhutaṃ…pe… anītikañca [T 4.0452] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anītikagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, anītikaṃ…pe… anītikadhammañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anītikadhammagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, anītikadhammaṃ…pe… nibbānañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi nibbānagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, nibbānaṃ…pe… abyāpajjhañca abyāpajjhañca (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi abyāpajjhagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, abyāpajjhaṃ…pe… virāgañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi virāgagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, virāgo…pe…?

“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the marvelous and the path leading to the marvelous. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the marvelous?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the wonderful and the path leading to the wonderful. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the wonderful?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unafflicted and the path leading to the unafflicted. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the unafflicted?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unafflicted state and the path leading to the unafflicted state. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the unafflicted state?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you Nibbāna and the path leading to Nibbāna. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is Nibbāna?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you the untroubled and the path leading to the untroubled. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is the untroubled?… and so on… Bhikkhus, I will teach you dispassion and the path leading to dispassion. Listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, is dispassion?… and so on…”

“Suddhiñca [V 2.0343][P 4.0372] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi suddhigāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, suddhi…pe… muttiñca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi muttigāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, mutti…pe… anālayañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anālayagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, anālayo…pe… dīpañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi dīpagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, dīpaṃ…pe… leṇañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi leṇagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, leṇaṃ…pe… tāṇañca [T 4.0453] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi tāṇagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, tāṇaṃ…pe… saraṇañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi saraṇagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, saraṇaṃ…pe…anusāsanī”ti? Bāttiṃsatimaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I will teach you purity and the path leading to purity. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is purity? … (The same formula is repeated for:) liberation … non-attachment … the island … the shelter … protection … and the refuge. The thirty-second.”

33. Parāyanasuttaṃ

33. The Discourse on the Ultimate Resort

409. “Parāyanañca [P 4.0373] parāyaṇañca (pī. sī. aṭṭha.) vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi parāyanagāmiñca maggaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, parāyanaṃ? Yo, bhikkhave, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo [M 2.0543] mohakkhayo – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, parāyanaṃ. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, parāyanagāmī maggo? Kāyagatāsati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, parāyanagāmimaggo. Iti kho, bhikkhave, desitaṃ vo mayā parāyanaṃ, desito parāyanagāmimaggo. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya, kataṃ vo taṃ mayā. Etāni, bhikkhave, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni. Jhāyatha, bhikkhave, mā pamādattha; mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī”ti. (Yathā asaṅkhataṃ tathā vitthāretabbaṃ). Tettiṃsatimaṃ.

409. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the ultimate resort and the path leading to the ultimate resort. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the ultimate resort? The destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion—this, bhikkhus, is called the ultimate resort. And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the ultimate resort? Mindfulness directed to the body. This, bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the ultimate resort. Thus, bhikkhus, I have taught you the ultimate resort, and I have taught the path leading to the ultimate resort. Whatever should be done by a teacher for his disciples out of compassion, seeking their welfare, that has been done by me for you. Here, bhikkhus, are the roots of trees; here are empty dwellings. Meditate, bhikkhus, do not be negligent; do not be remorseful later. This is our instruction to you. The thirty-third.”

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Asaṅkhataṃ anataṃ anāsavaṃ, saccañca pāraṃ nipuṇaṃ sududdasaṃ;

Ajajjaraṃ dhuvaṃ apalokitaṃ, anidassanaṃ nippapañca santaṃ.

The unconditioned, without craving, the taintless, the truth, the far shore, the subtle, the very difficult to see; the unaging, the stable, the imperishable, the unmanifest, free from proliferation, the peaceful.

Amataṃ [V 2.0344] paṇītañca sivañca khemaṃ, taṇhākkhayo acchariyañca abbhutaṃ;

Anītikaṃ anītikadhammaṃ, nibbānametaṃ sugatena desitaṃ.

The deathless, the sublime, the blissful, the secure, the destruction of craving, the wondrous, the marvelous; without affliction, the state without affliction—this is Nibbāna, taught by the Well-Gone One.

Abyāpajjho [T 4.0454] virāgo ca, suddhi mutti anālayo;

Dīpo leṇañca tāṇañca, saraṇañca parāyananti.

Non-affliction, dispassion, purity, liberation, non-attachment; the island, the shelter, the protection, the refuge, and the ultimate resort.

Asaṅkhatasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Unconditioned is completed.

10. Abyākatasaṃyuttaṃ

10. The Connected Discourses on the Undeclared

1. Khemāsuttaṃ

1. Discourse with Khemā

410. Ekaṃ [T 4.0455][M 2.0544][V 2.0345][P 4.0374] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena khemā bhikkhunī kosalesu cārikaṃ caramānā antarā ca sāvatthiṃ antarā ca sāketaṃ toraṇavatthusmiṃ vāsaṃ upagatā hoti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo sāketā sāvatthiṃ gacchanto, antarā ca sāketaṃ antarā ca sāvatthiṃ toraṇavatthusmiṃ ekarattivāsaṃ upagacchi. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, toraṇavatthusmiṃ tathārūpaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā jāna yamahaṃ ajja payirupāseyya”nti.

410. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time the bhikkhunī Khemā, while traveling on a walking tour among the Kosalans, had taken up residence at Toraṇavatthu between Sāvatthī and Sāketa. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, while traveling from Sāketa to Sāvatthī, took up residence for one night at Toraṇavatthu between Sāketa and Sāvatthī. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed a certain man: “Come, good man, find out about such an ascetic or brahmin at Toraṇavatthu whom I might attend upon today.”

“Evaṃ, devā”ti kho so puriso rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā kevalakappaṃ toraṇavatthuṃ āhiṇḍanto anvāhiṇḍanto (sī.) nāddasa tathārūpaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā yaṃ rājā pasenadi kosalo payirupāseyya. Addasā kho so puriso khemaṃ bhikkhuniṃ toraṇavatthusmiṃ vāsaṃ upagataṃ. Disvāna yena rājā pasenadi kosalo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ etadavoca –

“Very well, your majesty,” that man replied to King Pasenadi of Kosala. Wandering through the entirety of Toraṇavatthu, he did not see such an ascetic or brahmin whom King Pasenadi of Kosala might attend upon. But that man did see the bhikkhunī Khemā who had taken up residence at Toraṇavatthu. Having seen her, he approached King Pasenadi of Kosala; having approached, he said this to King Pasenadi of Kosala:

“Natthi kho, deva, toraṇavatthusmiṃ tathārūpo samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yaṃ devo payirupāseyya. Atthi ca kho, deva, khemā nāma bhikkhunī, tassa bhagavato sāvikā arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Tassā kho pana ayyāya [T 4.0456] evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato [P 4.0375] – ‘paṇḍitā, viyattā medhāvinī bahussutā cittakathā kalyāṇapaṭibhānā’ti. Taṃ devo payirupāsatū”ti.

“Your majesty, there is no such ascetic or brahmin at Toraṇavatthu whom your majesty might attend upon. But there is, your majesty, a bhikkhunī named Khemā, a female disciple of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. And of that venerable lady, such a fine report has spread: ‘She is wise, accomplished, intelligent, very learned, an eloquent speaker, and of excellent ready wit.’ Let your majesty attend upon her.”

Atha [V 2.0346] kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena khemā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā khemaṃ bhikkhuniṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ [M 2.0545] nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo khemaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, ayye, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ panayye, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ nu kho, ayye, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ panayye, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti. “Etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the bhikkhunī Khemā; having approached and paid homage to the bhikkhunī Khemā, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the bhikkhunī Khemā: “Venerable lady, does the Tathāgata exist after death?” “Great king, this has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death.’” “Then, venerable lady, does the Tathāgata not exist after death?” “This too, great king, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death.’” “Venerable lady, does the Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death?” “This has been left undeclared by the Blessed One, great king: ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’” “Then, venerable lady, does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?” “This too, great king, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

“‘Kiṃ nu kho, ayye, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭhā samānā – ‘abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā – hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ panayye, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭhā samānā – ‘etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, ayye, hoti ca [T 4.0457] na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭhā samānā – ‘abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā – hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ panayye, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭhā samānā – ‘etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi. ‘Ko nu kho[P 4.0376], ayye, hetu, ko paccayo yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā’”ti?

“Venerable lady, when asked, ‘Does the Tathāgata exist after death?’ you say, ‘Great king, this has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: “The Tathāgata exists after death.”’ When asked, ‘Then, venerable lady, does the Tathāgata not exist after death?’ you say, ‘This too, great king, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: “The Tathāgata does not exist after death.”’ When asked, ‘Venerable lady, does the Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death?’ you say, ‘This has been left undeclared by the Blessed One, great king: “The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.”’ When asked, ‘Then, venerable lady, does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?’ you say, ‘This too, great king, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: “The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.”’ What, venerable lady, is the cause, what is the condition, why this has been left undeclared by the Blessed One?”

“Tena hi, mahārāja, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, atthi te koci gaṇako vā muddiko vā saṅkhāyako vā yo pahoti gaṅgāya vālukaṃ vālikaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.) gaṇetuṃ – ettakā ettikā (sī.) vālukā iti vā, ettakāni vālukasatāni iti vā, ettakāni vālukasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni vālukasatasahassāni iti vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, ayye”. “Atthi pana te koci gaṇako vā muddiko vā saṅkhāyako vā yo pahoti mahāsamudde [M 2.0546] udakaṃ gaṇetuṃ – ettakāni udakāḷhakāni iti vā, ettakāni udakāḷhakasatāni [V 2.0347] iti vā, ettakāni udakāḷhakasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni udakāḷhakasatasahassāni iti vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, ayye”. “Taṃ kissa hetu”? “Mahāyye, samuddo gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho”ti. “Evameva kho, mahārāja, yena rūpe tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno [T 4.0458] paññāpeyya taṃ rūpaṃ tathāgatassa pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ. Rūpasaṅkhāyavimutto kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti.

“Well then, great king, I will question you in return on this very matter. Answer as you see fit. What do you think, great king? Is there any accountant, calculator, or reckoner of yours who is able to count the sand in the Ganges: ‘There are this many grains of sand,’ or ‘this many hundreds of grains of sand,’ or ‘this many thousands of grains of sand,’ or ‘this many hundreds of thousands of grains of sand’?” “Certainly not, venerable lady.” “Is there any accountant, calculator, or reckoner of yours who is able to measure the water in the great ocean: ‘There are this many āḷhakas of water,’ or ‘this many hundreds of āḷhakas of water,’ or ‘this many thousands of āḷhakas of water,’ or ‘this many hundreds of thousands of āḷhakas of water’?” “Certainly not, venerable lady.” “For what reason?” “Venerable lady, the great ocean is deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom.” “Even so, great king, that form by which one describing the Tathāgata might describe him, that form has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise again in the future. The Tathāgata, great king, is liberated from reckoning by form; he is deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom, just like the great ocean. ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ does not apply.

“Yāya vedanāya tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya, [P 4.0377] sā vedanā tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Vedanāsaṅkhāyavimutto, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti.

“By whatever feeling one might designate the Tathāgata, that feeling has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future. The Tathāgata, great king, is freed from reckoning in terms of feeling; he is deep, immeasurable, hard to fathom, like the great ocean. ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ does not apply.

“Yāya saññā tathāgataṃ…pe… yehi saṅkhārehi tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya, te saṅkhārā tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Saṅkhārasaṅkhāyavimutto kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti[T 4.0459], ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti.

“By whatever perception one might designate the Tathāgata… or by whatever volitional formations one might designate the Tathāgata, those volitional formations have been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and are of a nature not to arise in the future. Great king, the Tathāgata is freed from reckoning in terms of volitional formations; he is deep, immeasurable, hard to fathom, like the great ocean. ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ does not apply.

“Yena viññāṇe tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya taṃ viññāṇaṃ tathāgatassa pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ [M 2.0547] anuppādadhammaṃ. Viññāṇasaṅkhāyavimutto kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upetī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo khemāya bhikkhuniyā [V 2.0348] bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā khemaṃ bhikkhuniṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

“By whatever consciousness one might designate the Tathāgata, that consciousness has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future. Freed from reckoning in terms of consciousness, great king, the Tathāgata is deep, immeasurable, hard to fathom, like the great ocean. ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ does not apply. ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ does not apply.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, having delighted in and rejoiced at the words of the bhikkhunī Khemā, rose from his seat, paid homage to the bhikkhunī Khemā, circumambulated her with his right side toward her, and departed.

Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aparena samayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, bhante, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ [P 4.0378] kho etaṃ, mahārāja, mayā – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ pana, bhante, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṃ mayā – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ nu kho, bhante, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti[T 4.0460]? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, mahārāja, mayā – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ pana, bhante, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṃ mayā – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ nu kho, bhante, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti iti puṭṭho samāno – ‘abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, mahārāja, mayā – hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi…pe…. “‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭho samāno – “‘etampi kho, mahārāja, abyākataṃ mayā – neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi. Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti?

Then, on a later occasion, King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, does the Tathāgata exist after death?” “This, great king, has been undeclared by me: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death.’” “Then, venerable sir, does the Tathāgata not exist after death?” “This too, great king, has been undeclared by me: ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death.’” “Venerable sir, does the Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death?” “This, great king, has been undeclared by me: ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’” “Then, venerable sir, does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?” “This too, great king, has been undeclared by me: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’” “Venerable sir, when asked, ‘Does the Tathāgata exist after death?’, you say, ‘This, great king, has been undeclared by me: “The Tathāgata exists after death.”’ … When asked, ‘Then, venerable sir, does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?’, you say, ‘This too, great king, has been undeclared by me: “The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.”’ What, venerable sir, is the reason, what is the cause, why this has been undeclared by the Blessed One?”

“Tena hi, mahārāja, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, atthi te koci gaṇako vā muddiko vā saṅkhāyako vā yo pahoti gaṅgāya vālukaṃ gaṇetuṃ [M 2.0548] – ettakā vālukā iti vā…pe… ettakāni vālukasatasahassāni iti vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Atthi pana te koci gaṇako vā muddiko vā saṅkhāyako vā yo pahoti mahāsamudde udakaṃ gaṇetuṃ – ettakāni udakāḷhakāni iti vā…pe… ettakāni udakāḷhakasatasahassāni iti vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Taṃ kissa hetu”? “Mahā, bhante, samuddo gambhīro [T 4.0461] appameyyo duppariyogāho. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yena rūpena tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya, taṃ rūpaṃ tathāgatassa pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ [P 4.0379] anuppādadhammaṃ. Rūpasaṅkhāyavimutto [V 2.0349] kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti. Yāya vedanāya…pe… yāya saññāya…pe… yehi saṅkhārehi…pe…”.

“Then, great king, I will question you in return. Answer as you see fit. What do you think, great king—is there any accountant, calculator, or reckoner who is able to count the sand of the Ganges, saying: ‘There are this many grains of sand,’ or ‘There are this many hundreds of thousands of grains of sand’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Is there any accountant, calculator, or reckoner who is able to measure the water in the great ocean, saying: ‘There are this many āḷhakas of water,’ or ‘There are this many hundreds of thousands of āḷhakas of water’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Why is that?” “Because, venerable sir, the great ocean is deep, immeasurable, and hard to fathom. In the same way, great king, by whatever form one might designate the Tathāgata, that form has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future. Freed from reckoning in terms of form, great king, the Tathāgata is deep, immeasurable, hard to fathom, like the great ocean. ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’ does not apply; … ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ does not apply. By whatever feeling… by whatever perception… by whatever volitional formations…”

“Yena viññāṇena tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya, taṃ viññāṇaṃ tathāgatassa pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ. Viññāṇasaṅkhāyavimutto kho, mahārāja, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upeti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi na upetī”ti.

“By whichever consciousness one might designate the Tathāgata, that consciousness has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future. Freed from being reckoned by consciousness, great king, the Tathāgata is deep, immeasurable, hard to fathom, like the great ocean. ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’ does not apply; ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death’ does not apply; ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ does not apply; ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ does not apply.”

“Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yatra hi nāma satthu ceva satthuno ceva (sī.) sāvikāya ca atthena attho byañjanena byañjanaṃ saṃsandissati[T 4.0462], samessati, na virodhayissati vihāyissati (sī. syā. kaṃ.), vigāyissati (ka.) yadidaṃ aggapadasmiṃ. Ekamidāhaṃ, bhante, samayaṃ khemaṃ bhikkhuniṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ apucchiṃ. Sāpi me ayyā etehi padehi etehi byañjanehi etamatthaṃ byākāsi, seyyathāpi bhagavā. Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yatra hi nāma satthu ceva sāvikāya ca atthena attho byañjanena byañjanaṃ saṃsandissati, samessati, na virodhayissati yadidaṃ aggapadasmiṃ. Handa dāni mayaṃ, bhante, gacchāma. Bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā”ti. “Yassa dāni tvaṃ, mahārāja, kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavato [M 2.0549] bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā [P 4.0380] anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmīti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is amazing, venerable sir! How the meaning coincides with the meaning and the phrasing with the phrasing of the Teacher and the female disciple; they agree and do not contradict in this supreme principle. Once, venerable sir, I approached the bhikkhunī Khemā and asked her about this matter. That noble lady also explained this matter to me with these same words and these same phrases, just as the Blessed One has. It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is amazing, venerable sir! How the meaning coincides with the meaning and the phrasing with the phrasing of the Teacher and the female disciple; they agree and do not contradict in this supreme principle. And now, venerable sir, we shall depart. We have many duties and much to do.” “Now, great king, is the time for whatever you think fit.” Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, having delighted in and rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to his right, and departed. The First.

2. Anurādhasuttaṃ

2. The Anurādha Sutta

411. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā anurādho bhagavato avidūre araññakuṭikāyaṃ viharati. Atha kho sambahulā aññatitthiyā paribbājakā yenāyasmā anurādho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā anurādhena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu[V 2.0350]. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā āyasmantaṃ anurādhaṃ etadavocuṃ – “yo so, āvuso anurādha, tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṃ tathāgato imesu catūsu ṭhānesu paññāpayamāno [T 4.0463] paññāpeti – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā”ti? “Yo so, āvuso, tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṃ tathāgato aññatra imehi catūhi ṭhānehi paññāpayamāno paññāpeti – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā āyasmantaṃ anurādhaṃ etadavocuṃ – “so cāyaṃ yo cāyaṃ (sī.) bhikkhu navo bhavissati acirapabbajito, thero vā pana bālo abyatto”ti. Atha kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā āyasmantaṃ anurādhaṃ navavādena ca bālavādena ca apasādetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃsu.

411. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Now on that occasion the Venerable Anurādha was dwelling not far from the Blessed One in a forest hut. Then a number of wanderers of other sects approached the Venerable Anurādha; having approached, they exchanged greetings with the Venerable Anurādha. When they had concluded their courteous and memorable talk, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those wanderers of other sects said this to the Venerable Anurādha: “Friend Anurādha, that Tathāgata—the supreme man, the ultimate man, who has attained the ultimate attainment—when designating him, the Tathāgata designates him in one of these four positions: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’” “Friends, that Tathāgata—the supreme man, the ultimate man, who has attained the ultimate attainment—when designating him, the Tathāgata designates him apart from these four positions: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’” When this was said, those wanderers of other sects said this to the Venerable Anurādha: “This monk must be a novice, not long ordained; or if he is an elder, he is foolish and incompetent.” Then those wanderers of other sects, having disparaged the Venerable Anurādha with accusations of being a novice and a fool, rose from their seats and departed.

Atha [P 4.0381] kho āyasmato anurādhassa acirapakkantesu aññatitthiyesu paribbājakesu etadahosi – “sace kho maṃ te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā uttariṃ puccheyyuṃ, kathaṃ byākaramāno nu khvāhaṃ tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ vuttavādī ceva bhagavato assaṃ, na [M 2.0550] ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkheyyaṃ, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākareyyaṃ, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgaccheyyā”ti? Atha [T 4.0464] kho āyasmā anurādho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā anurādho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idhāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato avidūre araññakuṭikāyaṃ viharāmi. Atha kho, bhante, sambahulā aññatitthiyā paribbājakā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā mayā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho, bhante, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā maṃ etadavocuṃ – “yo so, āvuso anurādha, tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṃ tathāgato imesu catūsu ṭhānesu paññāpayamāno paññāpeti – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā”ti? Evaṃ vuttāhaṃ, bhante, te aññatitthiye paribbājake etadavocaṃ – “yo so, āvuso[V 2.0351], tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṃ tathāgato aññatra imehi catūhi ṭhānehi paññāpayamāno paññāpeti – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā”ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhante, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā maṃ etadavocuṃ – “so cāyaṃ bhikkhu navo bhavissati acirapabbajito thero vā pana bālo abyatto”ti. Atha kho maṃ, bhante, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā navavādena ca bālavādena ca [T 4.0465] apasādetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃsu. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, acirapakkantesu tesu aññatitthiyesu [P 4.0382] paribbājakesu etadahosi – “sace kho maṃ te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā uttariṃ puccheyyuṃ, kathaṃ byākaramāno nu khvāhaṃ tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ vuttavādī ceva bhagavato assaṃ, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkheyyaṃ, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākareyyaṃ, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgaccheyyā”ti?

Then, not long after those wanderers of other sects had departed, this thought occurred to the Venerable Anurādha: 'If those wanderers of other sects were to question me further, how should I answer them so that I would be one who speaks what was spoken by the Blessed One, and would not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is not true, and would explain the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and so that no reasonable, consequential statement would lead to a censurable position?' Then the Venerable Anurādha approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Anurādha said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, I am dwelling here in a forest hut not far from the Blessed One. Then, Venerable Sir, a number of wanderers of other sects approached where I was; having approached, they exchanged greetings with me. When they had concluded their courteous and memorable talk, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Venerable Sir, those wanderers of other sects said this to me: “Friend Anurādha, that Tathāgata—the supreme man, the ultimate man, who has attained the ultimate attainment—when designating him, the Tathāgata designates him in one of these four positions: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or… ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’?” When this was said, Venerable Sir, I said this to those wanderers of other sects: “Friends, that Tathāgata—the supreme man, the ultimate man, who has attained the ultimate attainment—when designating him, the Tathāgata designates him apart from these four positions: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or… ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’” When this was said, Venerable Sir, those wanderers of other sects said this to me: “This monk must be a novice, not long ordained; or if he is an elder, he is foolish and incompetent.” Then, Venerable Sir, those wanderers of other sects, having disparaged me with accusations of being a novice and a fool, rose from their seats and departed. Then, Venerable Sir, not long after those wanderers of other sects had departed, this thought occurred to me: “If those wanderers of other sects were to question me further, how should I answer them so that I would be one who speaks what was spoken by the Blessed One, and would not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is not true, and would explain the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and so that no reasonable, consequential statement would lead to a censurable position?”'

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, anurādha, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“What do you think, Anurādha, is form permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, Venerable Sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“That which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, Venerable Sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“Now, that which is impermanent, suffering, and of a nature to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Indeed not, Venerable Sir.”

“Vedanā niccā vā aniccā vā”ti?…Pe… saññā [M 2.0551] …pe… saṅkhārā…pe… “viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti?

“Is feeling permanent or impermanent?… Is perception… Are formations… Is consciousness permanent or impermanent?”

“Aniccaṃ, bhante”.

“Impermanent, Venerable Sir.”

“Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vā”ti?

“That which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

“Dukkhaṃ, bhante”.

“Suffering, Venerable Sir.”

“Yaṃ [V 2.0352] panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?

“Now, that which is impermanent, suffering, and of a nature to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

“No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Indeed not, Venerable Sir.”

“Tasmātiha, anurādha, yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na [T 4.0466] meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yā kāci vedanā atītānāgatapaccuppannā…pe… yā kāci saññā…pe… ye keci saṅkhārā…pe… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na [P 4.0383] meso attā’ti evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evaṃ passaṃ, anurādha, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati. Nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.

“Therefore, Anurādha, whatever form there is—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all that form should be seen as it really is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling there is—past, future, or present… Whatever perception… Whatever formations… Whatever consciousness there is—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all that consciousness should be seen as it really is with right wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus, Anurādha, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. In the liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘Liberated!’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, anurādha, rūpaṃ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanaṃ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Saññaṃ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Saṅkhāre tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Viññāṇaṃ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, anurādha, rūpasmiṃ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Aññatra rūpā tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Vedanāya…pe… aññatra vedanāya…pe… saññāya…pe… [T 4.0467] aññatra saññāya…pe… saṅkhāresu…pe… aññatra saṅkhārehi…pe… viññāṇasmiṃ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Aññatra viññāṇā tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, Anurādha, do you regard form as the Tathāgata?” “No, venerable sir.” “Do you regard feeling as the Tathāgata?” “No, venerable sir.” “Do you regard perception as the Tathāgata?” “No, venerable sir.” “Do you regard volitional formations as the Tathāgata?” “No, venerable sir.” “Do you regard consciousness as the Tathāgata?” “No, venerable sir.” “What do you think, Anurādha, do you regard the Tathāgata as in form?” “No, venerable sir.” “Do you regard the Tathāgata as apart from form?” “No, venerable sir.” “...in feeling... apart from feeling... in perception... apart from perception... in volitional formations... apart from volitional formations... do you regard the Tathāgata as in consciousness?” “No, venerable sir.” “Do you regard the Tathāgata as apart from consciousness?” “No, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ [V 2.0353] kiṃ maññasi, anurādha, rūpaṃ, vedanaṃ, saññaṃ, saṅkhāre, viññāṇaṃ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No [P 4.0384] hetaṃ, bhante”. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, anurādha, ayaṃ so arūpī avedano asaññī asaṅkhāro aviññāṇo tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Ettha ca te, anurādha, diṭṭheva [M 2.0552] dhamme saccato thetato tathāgate anupalabbhiyamāne tathāgato anupalabbhiyamāno (syā. ka.), tathāgate anupalabbhamāne (?) kallaṃ nu te taṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ veyyākaraṇāya (sī.) – yo so, āvuso, tathāgato uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto, taṃ tathāgato aññatra imehi catūhi ṭhānehi paññāpayamāno paññāpeti – “‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Sādhu sādhu, anurādha! Pubbe cāhaṃ, anurādha, etarahi ca dukkhañceva paññāpemi dukkhassa ca nirodha”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

“What do you think, Anurādha, do you regard form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness as the Tathāgata?” “No, venerable sir.” “What do you think, Anurādha, do you regard one who is without form, without feeling, without perception, without volitional formations, and without consciousness as the Tathāgata?” “No, venerable sir.” “Since, Anurādha, a Tathāgata is not apprehended by you as true and actual even in this very life, is it proper for you to declare: ‘Friends, the Tathāgata—the supreme person, the highest person, who has attained the supreme attainment—is described apart from these four propositions: “The Tathāgata exists after death,” ... or “The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death”’?” “No, venerable sir.” “Good, good, Anurādha! Both formerly and now, Anurādha, I proclaim only suffering and the cessation of suffering.”

3. Paṭhamasāriputtakoṭṭhikasuttaṃ

3. The First Discourse with Sāriputta and Koṭṭhika

412. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ca sāriputto, āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko bārāṇasiyaṃ viharanti isipatane migadāye. Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko [T 4.0468] sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca –

412. At one time, the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika were dwelling at Bārāṇasī in the Deer Park at Isipatana. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika arose from seclusion and approached the Venerable Sāriputta. He exchanged greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta, and after concluding their courteous and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ panāvuso, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi [P 4.0385] kho, āvuso, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ panāvuso, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

“What now, friend Sāriputta, does a Tathāgata exist after death?” “Friend, this has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘A Tathāgata exists after death.’” “Then, friend, does a Tathāgata not exist after death?” “This too, friend, has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘A Tathāgata does not exist after death.’” “What now, friend, does a Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death?” “Friend, this has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘A Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’” “Then, friend, does a Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?” “This too, friend, has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

“‘Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭho samāno, ‘abyākataṃ [V 2.0354] kho etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā – hoti tathāgato [M 2.0553] paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi…pe… ‘kiṃ panāvuso, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭho samāno – ‘etampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi. Ko nu kho, āvuso, hetu, ko paccayo yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti?

“Friend, when asked, ‘What now, does a Tathāgata exist after death?’ you say, ‘Friend, this has not been declared by the Blessed One: “A Tathāgata exists after death.”’ … And when asked, ‘Then, friend, does a Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?’ you say, ‘This too, friend, has not been declared by the Blessed One: “A Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.”’ What, friend, is the reason, what is the cause, why this has not been declared by the Blessed One?”

“Hoti [T 4.0469] tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti kho, āvuso, rūpagatametaṃ. Na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, rūpagatametaṃ. Hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, rūpagatametaṃ. Neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, rūpagatametaṃ. Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti kho, āvuso, vedanāgatametaṃ. Na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, vedanāgatametaṃ. Hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, vedanāgatametaṃ. Neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, vedanāgatametaṃ. Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti kho, āvuso, saññāgatametaṃ. Na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, saññāgatametaṃ. Hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, saññāgatametaṃ. Neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, saññāgatametaṃ. Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti kho, āvuso, saṅkhāragatametaṃ[P 4.0386]. Na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, saṅkhāragatametaṃ. Hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, saṅkhāragatametaṃ. Neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, saṅkhāragatametaṃ. Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti kho, āvuso, viññāṇagatametaṃ. Na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, viññāṇagatametaṃ. Hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, viññāṇagatametaṃ. Neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti, viññāṇagatametaṃ. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, hetu ayaṃ paccayo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Friend, the view ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ pertains to form. The view ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’ pertains to form. The view ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ pertains to form. The view ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ pertains to form. Friend, the view ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ pertains to feeling. The view ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’ pertains to feeling. The view ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ pertains to feeling. The view ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ pertains to feeling. Friend, the view ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ pertains to perception. The view ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’ pertains to perception. The view ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ pertains to perception. The view ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ pertains to perception. Friend, the view ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ pertains to volitional formations. The view ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’ pertains to volitional formations. The view ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ pertains to volitional formations. The view ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ pertains to volitional formations. Friend, the view ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ pertains to consciousness. The view ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’ pertains to consciousness. The view ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ pertains to consciousness. The view ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ pertains to consciousness. This, friend, is the cause, this is the reason, why this has not been declared by the Blessed One. The Third.

4. Dutiyasāriputtakoṭṭhikasuttaṃ

4. The Second Sāriputta-Koṭṭhika Discourse

413. Ekaṃ [T 4.0470] samayaṃ āyasmā ca sāriputto, āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko bārāṇasiyaṃ viharanti isipatane migadāye…pe… (sāyeva [M 2.0554] pucchā) “ko nu kho, āvuso, hetu, ko paccayo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti? “Rūpaṃ kho, āvuso, ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, rūpasamudayaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, rūpanirodhaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ[V 2.0355], rūpanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti; ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti; ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti; ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, viññāṇasamudayaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, viññāṇanirodhaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti; ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ [P 4.0387] maraṇā’tipissa hoti; ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti; ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”tipissa hoti.

413. On one occasion, the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika were dwelling in Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana… (the same question) “What, friend, is the cause, what is the reason, why this has not been declared by the Blessed One?” “Friend, for one who does not know and see form as it really is, who does not know and see the origin of form as it really is, who does not know and see the cessation of form as it really is, who does not know and see the path of practice leading to the cessation of form as it really is, it occurs to him thus: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death.’ It occurs to him thus: ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death.’ It occurs to him thus: ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’ It occurs to him thus: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ For one who does not know and see feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as it really is, who does not know and see the origin of consciousness as it really is, who does not know and see the cessation of consciousness as it really is, who does not know and see the path of practice leading to the cessation of consciousness as it really is, it occurs to him thus: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death.’ It occurs to him thus: ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death.’ It occurs to him thus: ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’ It occurs to him thus: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

“Rūpañca kho, āvuso, jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, rūpasamudayaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, rūpanirodhaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, rūpanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ [T 4.0471] maraṇā’tipissa na hoti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti. Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, viññāṇasamudayaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, viññāṇanirodhaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti; ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti; ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti; ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, hetu ayaṃ paccayo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Friend, for one who knows and sees form as it really is, who knows and sees the origin of form as it really is, who knows and sees the cessation of form as it really is, who knows and sees the path of practice leading to the cessation of form as it really is, the view ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ does not occur to him… the view ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ does not occur to him. For one who knows and sees feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as it really is, who knows and sees the origin of consciousness as it really is, who knows and sees the cessation of consciousness as it really is, who knows and sees the path of practice leading to the cessation of consciousness as it really is, the view ‘the Tathāgata exists after death’ does not occur to him; the view ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’ does not occur to him; the view ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ does not occur to him; the view ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ does not occur to him. This, friend, is the cause, this is the reason, why this has not been declared by the Blessed One. The Fourth.

5. Tatiyasāriputtakoṭṭhikasuttaṃ

5. The Third Sāriputta-Koṭṭhika Discourse

414. Ekaṃ [M 2.0555] samayaṃ āyasmā ca sāriputto, āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko bārāṇasiyaṃ viharanti isipatane migadāye…pe… (sāyeva pucchā) “ko nu kho, āvuso, hetu ko paccayo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti? “Rūpe kho, āvuso, avigatarāgassa avigatacchandassa [V 2.0356] avigatapemassa avigatapipāsassa avigatapariḷāhassa avigatataṇhassa ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti. Vedanāya…pe… saññāya…pe… saṅkhāresu…pe… viññāṇe avigatarāgassa avigatacchandassa avigatapemassa avigatapipāsassa avigatapariḷāhassa avigatataṇhassa ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ [T 4.0472] maraṇā’tipissa hoti…pe… ‘neva [P 4.0388] hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti. Rūpe ca kho, āvuso, vigatarāgassa…pe… vedanāya…pe… saññāya…pe… saṅkhāresu…pe… viññāṇe vigatarāgassa vigatacchandassa vigatapemassa vigatapipāsassa vigatapariḷāhassa vigatataṇhassa ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

414. At one time, the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika were dwelling in Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana… (the same question is asked) “What, friend, is the cause, what is the reason, why this was left undeclared by the Blessed One?” “Friend, for one for whom passion, desire, affection, thirst, feverishness, and craving for form have not departed, it occurs to them: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’… or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ For one for whom passion, desire, affection, thirst, feverishness, and craving for feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness have not departed, it occurs to them: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’… or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ But, friend, for one for whom passion, desire, affection, thirst, feverishness, and craving for form have departed… for feeling… for perception… for volitional formations… for consciousness, it does not occur to them: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’… or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ This, friend, is the cause, this is the reason, why this was left undeclared by the Blessed One.” The fifth.

6. Catutthasāriputtakoṭṭhikasuttaṃ

6. The Fourth Sāriputta-Koṭṭhika Discourse

415. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ca sāriputto, āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko bārāṇasiyaṃ viharanti isipatane migadāye. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākoṭṭhikena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ mahākoṭṭhikaṃ etadavoca – “‘kiṃ nu kho, āvuso koṭṭhika, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti…pe… ‘kiṃ panāvuso, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti iti puṭṭho samāno – ‘etampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato [M 2.0556] paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi”. “Ko nu kho, āvuso, hetu, ko paccayo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti?

415. At one time, the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika were dwelling at Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta arose from seclusion and approached the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika. Having approached, he exchanged courteous and memorable greetings with the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika. When this courteous and memorable talk was finished, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika: “‘Friend Koṭṭhika, does the Tathāgata exist after death?’… ‘Does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?’—when you are asked this, you say: ‘This, too, friend, has not been declared by the Blessed One: the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ What, friend, is the cause, what is the reason, why this has not been declared by the Blessed One?”

“Rūpārāmassa [T 4.0473] kho, āvuso, rūparatassa rūpasammuditassa rūpanirodhaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato [P 4.0389] paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti; ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti; ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti; ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti. Vedanārāmassa kho, āvuso, vedanāratassa vedanāsammuditassa, vedanānirodhaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ [V 2.0357] maraṇā’tipissa hoti…pe… saññārāmassa kho, āvuso…pe… saṅkhārārāmassa kho āvuso…pe… viññāṇārāmassa kho, āvuso, viññāṇaratassa viññāṇasammuditassa viññāṇanirodhaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti”.

“Friend, for one who delights in form, is fond of form, and is gladdened by form, who does not know or see the cessation of form as it really is, it occurs to him: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ For one who delights in feeling, is fond of feeling, and is gladdened by feeling, who does not know or see the cessation of feeling as it really is, it occurs to him: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’… For one who delights in perception… For one who delights in volitional formations… For one who delights in consciousness, is fond of consciousness, and is gladdened by consciousness, who does not know or see the cessation of consciousness as it really is, it occurs to him: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’… or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

“Na rūpārāmassa kho, āvuso, na rūparatassa na rūpasammuditassa, rūpanirodhaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti. Na vedanārāmassa kho, āvuso…pe… na saññārāmassa kho, āvuso…pe… na saṅkhārārāmassa kho, āvuso…pe… na viññāṇārāmassa kho, āvuso, na viññāṇaratassa na viññāṇasammuditassa, viññāṇanirodhaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti…pe… [T 4.0474] ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti.

“Friend, for one who does not delight in form, is not fond of form, and is not gladdened by form, who knows and sees the cessation of form as it really is, it does not occur to him: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’… nor does it occur to him: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’. For one who does not delight in feeling… For one who does not delight in perception… For one who does not delight in volitional formations… For one who does not delight in consciousness, is not fond of consciousness, and is not gladdened by consciousness, who knows and sees the cessation of consciousness as it really is, it does not occur to him: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’… nor does it occur to him: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’. This, friend, is the cause, this is the reason, why this has not been declared by the Blessed One.”

“Siyā panāvuso, aññopi pariyāyo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti? “Siyā, āvuso. Bhavārāmassa kho, āvuso, bhavaratassa bhavasammuditassa, bhavanirodhaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti. Na [M 2.0557] bhavārāmassa [P 4.0390] kho, āvuso, na bhavaratassa na bhavasammuditassa, bhavanirodhaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti. Ayampi kho, āvuso, pariyāyo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti.

“Friend, might there be another way by which this has been undeclared by the Blessed One?” “There might be, friend. For one who delights in becoming, is fond of becoming, and is gladdened by becoming, who does not know or see the cessation of becoming as it really is, it occurs to him: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’… or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ For one who does not delight in becoming, is not fond of becoming, and is not gladdened by becoming, who knows and sees the cessation of becoming as it really is, it does not occur to him: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’… nor does it occur to him: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’. This, too, friend, is a way by which this has been undeclared by the Blessed One.”

“Siyā panāvuso, aññopi pariyāyo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti? “Siyā, āvuso. Upādānārāmassa kho, āvuso, upādānaratassa upādānasammuditassa, upādānanirodhaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti. Na upādānārāmassa kho, āvuso, na upādānaratassa na upādānasammuditassa, upādānanirodhaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti [T 4.0475] tathāgato [V 2.0358] paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti…pe… ‘neva, hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti. Ayampi kho āvuso, pariyāyo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti.

“Friend, might there be another reason by which this has been left undeclared by the Blessed One?” “There might be, friend. Indeed, friend, for one who delights in clinging, is fond of clinging, is gladdened by clinging, not knowing and not seeing the cessation of clinging as it really is, it occurs to him: ‘A being exists after death’… and it occurs to him: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ Indeed, friend, for one who does not delight in clinging, is not fond of clinging, is not gladdened by clinging, knowing and seeing the cessation of clinging as it really is, it does not occur to him: ‘A being exists after death’… and it does not occur to him: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ This, friend, is indeed the reason by which this has been left undeclared by the Blessed One.”

“Siyā panāvuso, aññopi pariyāyo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti? “Siyā, āvuso. Taṇhārāmassa kho, āvuso, taṇhāratassa taṇhāsammuditassa, taṇhānirodhaṃ ajānato apassato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa hoti. Na taṇhārāmassa kho, āvuso, na taṇhāratassa na taṇhāsammuditassa, taṇhānirodhaṃ jānato passato yathābhūtaṃ, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti…pe. [P 4.0391]… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipissa na hoti. Ayampi kho, āvuso, pariyāyo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti.

“Friend, might there be another reason by which this has been left undeclared by the Blessed One?” “There might be, friend. Indeed, friend, for one who delights in craving, is fond of craving, is gladdened by craving, not knowing and not seeing the cessation of craving as it really is, it occurs to him: ‘A being exists after death’… and it occurs to him: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ Indeed, friend, for one who does not delight in craving, is not fond of craving, is not gladdened by craving, knowing and seeing the cessation of craving as it really is, it does not occur to him: ‘A being exists after death’… and it does not occur to him: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ This, friend, is indeed the reason by which this has been left undeclared by the Blessed One.”

“Siyā panāvuso, aññopi pariyāyo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ bhagavatā”ti? “Ettha dāni, āvuso sāriputta, ito uttari kiṃ icchasi? Taṇhāsaṅkhayavimuttassa, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhuno vaṭṭaṃ vattaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) vaddhaṃ (pī.) natthi paññāpanāyā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Friend, might there be another reason by which this has been left undeclared by the Blessed One?” “Now in this matter, friend Sāriputta, what more do you wish for beyond this? Friend Sāriputta, for a monk who is liberated through the destruction of craving, there is no round of existence for designation.”

7. Moggallānasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse with Moggallāna

416. Atha [M 2.0558] kho vacchagotto paribbājako yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahāmoggallānena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako āyasmantaṃ [T 4.0476] mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca –

416. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having concluded this pleasant and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said this to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna:

“Kiṃ nu kho, bho moggallāna, sassato loko”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – ‘sassato loko’”ti. “Kiṃ pana, bho moggallāna, asassato loko”ti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘asassato loko’”ti. “Kiṃ nu kho, bho moggallāna, antavā loko”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – ‘antavā loko’”ti. “Kiṃ pana, bho moggallāna, anantavā loko”ti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘anantavā loko’”ti. “Kiṃ [P 4.0392] nu kho, bho moggallāna, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ [V 2.0359] sarīra”nti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’”nti. “Kiṃ pana, bho moggallāna, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra”nti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’”nti. “Kiṃ nu kho, bho moggallāna, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ pana, bho moggallāna, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ nu kho, bho moggallāna, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ pana, bho moggallāna, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

“How is it, Master Moggallāna, is the world eternal?” “This, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The world is eternal.’” “Then how is it, Master Moggallāna, is the world not eternal?” “This too, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The world is not eternal.’” “How is it, Master Moggallāna, is the world finite?” “This, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The world is finite.’” “Then how is it, Master Moggallāna, is the world infinite?” “This too, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The world is infinite.’” “How is it, Master Moggallāna, is the life-principle the same as the body?” “This, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The life-principle is the same as the body.’” “Then how is it, Master Moggallāna, is the life-principle one thing and the body another?” “This too, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The life-principle is one thing and the body another.’” “How is it, Master Moggallāna, does a being exist after death?” “This, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘A being exists after death.’” “Then how is it, Master Moggallāna, does a being not exist after death?” “This too, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘A being does not exist after death.’” “How is it, Master Moggallāna, does a being both exist and not exist after death?” “This, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘A being both exists and does not exist after death.’” “Then how is it, Master Moggallāna, does a being neither exist nor not exist after death?” “This too, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

“Ko [T 4.0477] nu kho, bho moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo, yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ puṭṭhānaṃ evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti vā, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti vā, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ [M 2.0559] maraṇāti vā, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā? Ko [P 4.0393] pana, bho moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo, yena samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃ puṭṭhassa na evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – sassato lokotipi, asassato lokotipi, antavā lokotipi, anantavā lokotipi, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīrantipi, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīrantipi, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇātipi, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇātipi, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇātipi, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇātipī”ti?

“What, Master Moggallāna, is the cause, what is the condition, why for the wanderers of other sects, when asked thus, there is this kind of explanation: ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal,’ or ‘The world is finite,’ or ‘The world is infinite,’ or ‘The life-principle is the same as the body,’ or ‘The life-principle is one thing and the body another,’ or ‘A being exists after death,’ or ‘A being does not exist after death,’ or ‘A being both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death’? And what, Master Moggallāna, is the cause, what is the condition, why for the ascetic Gotama, when asked thus, there is not this kind of explanation: that the world is eternal, that the world is not eternal, that the world is finite, that the world is infinite, that the life-principle is the same as the body, that the life-principle is one thing and the body another, that a being exists after death, that a being does not exist after death, that a being both exists and does not exist after death, or that a being neither exists nor does not exist after death?”

“Aññatitthiyā kho, vaccha, paribbājakā cakkhuṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassanti…pe… jivhaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassanti…pe… manaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassanti. Tasmā aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ puṭṭhānaṃ evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – sassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā.
