Tathāgato ca kho, vaccha, arahaṃ [V 2.0360] sammāsambuddho cakkhuṃ [T 4.0478] ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati…pe… jivhaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati…pe… manaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Tasmā tathāgatassa evaṃ puṭṭhassa na evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – sassato lokotipi…pe… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇātipī”ti.

“Indeed, Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard the eye thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’ …and so on… They regard the tongue thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’ …and so on… They regard the mind thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’ Therefore, when wanderers of other sects are asked thus, their explanation is thus: ‘The world is eternal,’ or …and so on … ‘a being neither is nor is not after death.’ But the Tathāgata, Vaccha, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, regards the eye thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ …and so on… He regards the tongue thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ …and so on… He regards the mind thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Therefore, when the Tathāgata is asked thus, his explanation is not thus: ‘The world is eternal,’ and so on… ‘a being neither is nor is not after death.’”

Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, sassato loko”ti? Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, mayā – ‘sassato loko’ti…pe…. “Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ mayā – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged joyful greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded the joyful and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable Gotama, is the world eternal?’ ‘Vaccha, this has not been declared by me: “The world is eternal.”’ …and so on… ‘Then, Venerable Gotama, does a being neither exist nor not exist after death?’ ‘This too, Vaccha, has not been declared by me: “A being neither is nor is not after death.”’

“Ko [M 2.0560][P 4.0394] nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo, yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ puṭṭhānaṃ evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā? Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo, yena bhoto gotamassa evaṃ puṭṭhassa na evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’tipi…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipī”ti?

“What, Venerable Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby for the wanderers of other sects, when asked thus, their explanation is thus: ‘The world is eternal,’ or …and so on… ‘a being neither is nor is not after death’? What, then, Venerable Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby for the Venerable Gotama, when asked thus, the explanation is not thus: ‘The world is eternal,’ and so on… ‘a being neither is nor is not after death’?”

“Aññatitthiyā kho, vaccha, paribbājakā cakkhuṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi[T 4.0479], eso me attā’ti samanupassanti…pe… jivhaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassanti…pe… manaṃ ‘etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassanti. Tasmā aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ puṭṭhānaṃ evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā. Tathāgato ca kho, vaccha, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho cakkhuṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati…pe… jivhaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati…pe… manaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Tasmā [V 2.0361] tathāgatassa evaṃ puṭṭhassa na evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’tipi, ‘asassato loko’tipi, ‘antavā loko’tipi, ‘anantavā loko’tipi, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’ntipi, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’ntipi, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipī”ti.

“Indeed, Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard the eye thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’ …and so on… They regard the tongue thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’ …and so on… They regard the mind thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’ Therefore, when wanderers of other sects are asked thus, their explanation is thus: ‘The world is eternal,’ or …and so on… ‘a being neither is nor is not after death.’ But the Tathāgata, Vaccha, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, regards the eye thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ …and so on… He regards the tongue thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ …and so on… He regards the mind thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Therefore, for the Tathāgata, when asked thus, the explanation is not thus: ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘the world is not eternal,’ or ‘the world is finite,’ or ‘the world is infinite,’ or ‘the life-principle and the body are the same,’ or ‘the life-principle is one thing and the body another,’ or ‘a being exists after death,’ or ‘a being does not exist after death,’ or ‘a being both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘a being neither is nor is not after death.’”

“Acchariyaṃ, bho gotama, abbhutaṃ, bho gotama! Yatra hi nāma satthu ca satthussa ca (sī. pī.), satthu ceva (khemāsutte) sāvakassa ca atthena attho byañjanena byañjanaṃ saṃsandissati samessati na virodhayissati, yadidaṃ aggapadasmiṃ. Idānāhaṃ, bho gotama, samaṇaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ upasaṅkamitvā [P 4.0395] etamatthaṃ apucchiṃ. Samaṇopi me moggallāno etehi padehi etehi byañjanehi [T 4.0480] tamatthaṃ byākāsi, seyyathāpi bhavaṃ gotamo. Acchariyaṃ, bho gotama, abbhutaṃ, bho gotama[M 2.0561]! Yatra hi nāma satthu ca sāvakassa ca atthena attho byañjanena byañjanaṃ saṃsandissati samessati na virodhayissati, yadidaṃ aggapadasmi”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“Wonderful, Venerable Gotama, marvelous, Venerable Gotama! How indeed the meaning and the phrasing of the Teacher and the disciple align, agree, and do not conflict, in regard to this supreme principle. Just now, Venerable Gotama, I approached the ascetic Mahāmoggallāna and asked him about this matter. The ascetic Moggallāna also explained that matter to me with these very words and these very phrases, just as the Venerable Gotama has. Wonderful, Venerable Gotama, marvelous, Venerable Gotama! How indeed the meaning and the phrasing of the Teacher and the disciple align, agree, and do not conflict, in regard to this supreme principle.” Seventh.

8. Vacchagottasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse to Vacchagotta

417. Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, sassato loko”ti? Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, mayā – ‘sassato loko’ti…pe…. “Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ mayā – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

417. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One and exchanged joyful greetings with him. After concluding a joyful and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Gotama, is the world eternal?” “This, Vaccha, has been undeclared by me: ‘The world is eternal.’” …and so on… “Then, Venerable Gotama, does a being neither exist nor not exist after death?” “This too, Vaccha, has been undeclared by me: ‘A being neither is nor is not after death.’”

“Ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ puṭṭhānaṃ evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā? Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo, yena bhoto gotamassa [V 2.0362] evaṃ puṭṭhassa na evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’tipi…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipī”ti?

“Venerable Gotama, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby wanderers of other sects, when questioned thus, give such an explanation as: ‘The world is eternal’… or ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’? And what, Venerable Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby the Venerable Gotama, when questioned thus, does not give such an explanation as: ‘The world is eternal’… or ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’?”

“Aññatitthiyā kho, vaccha, paribbājakā rūpaṃ attato samanupassanti, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ[T 4.0481]. Vedanaṃ attato samanupassanti…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassanti, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Tasmā aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ [P 4.0396] evaṃ puṭṭhānaṃ evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā. Tathāgato ca kho, vaccha, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho na rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā rūpaṃ, na rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Na vedanaṃ attato samanupassati…pe… na saññaṃ…pe… na saṅkhāre…pe… na viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, na [M 2.0562] viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā viññāṇaṃ, na viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Tasmā tathāgatassa evaṃ puṭṭhassa na evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’tipi…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipī”ti.

“Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard form as self, or self as possessing form, or form in self, or self in form. They regard feeling as self… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness in self, or self in consciousness. Therefore, when wanderers of other sects are questioned thus, they give such an explanation as: ‘The world is eternal’ or… ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ But the Tathāgata, Vaccha, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, does not regard form as self, nor self as possessing form, nor form in self, nor self in form. He does not regard feeling as self… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as self, nor self as possessing consciousness, nor consciousness in self, nor self in consciousness. Therefore, when the Tathāgata is questioned thus, he does not give such an explanation as: ‘The world is eternal’ or… ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako uṭṭhāyāsanā yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahāmoggallānena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, bho moggallāna, sassato loko”ti? Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – ‘sassato loko’ti…pe…. “Kiṃ pana, bho moggallāna, ‘neva [T 4.0482] hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having concluded the courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: “Venerable Moggallāna, is the world eternal?” “This, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The world is eternal.’” … “Then, Venerable Moggallāna, is it that ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’?” “This too, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

“Ko nu kho, bho moggallāna, hetu, ko paccayo, yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ puṭṭhānaṃ evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā? Ko pana, bho moggallāna, hetu, ko paccayo yena samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃ puṭṭhassa na evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’tipi…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipī”ti?

“Venerable Moggallāna, what is the cause, what is the condition, whereby wanderers of other sects, when questioned thus, give such an explanation as: ‘The world is eternal,’ or… ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’? And what, Venerable Moggallāna, is the cause, what is the condition, whereby the ascetic Gotama, when questioned thus, does not give such an explanation as: ‘The world is eternal,’ or… ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’?”

“Aññatitthiyā [V 2.0363][P 4.0397] kho, vaccha, paribbājakā rūpaṃ attato samanupassanti, rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā rūpaṃ, rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Vedanaṃ attato samanupassanti…pe… saññaṃ…pe… saṅkhāre…pe… viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassanti, viññāṇavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, attani vā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Tasmā aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ puṭṭhānaṃ evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā. Tathāgato ca kho, vaccha, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho na rūpaṃ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṃ vā attānaṃ, na attani vā rūpaṃ, na rūpasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Na vedanaṃ attato samanupassati…pe… na [M 2.0563] saññaṃ…pe… na saṅkhāre…pe… na viññāṇaṃ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṃ [T 4.0483] vā attānaṃ, na attani vā viññāṇaṃ, na viññāṇasmiṃ vā attānaṃ. Tasmā tathāgatassa evaṃ puṭṭhassa na evaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti – ‘sassato loko’tipi, ‘asassato loko’tipi, ‘antavā loko’tipi, ‘anantavā loko’tipi, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’ntipi, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’ntipi, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipī”ti.

“Vaccha, wanderers of other sects regard form as self, or self as possessing form, or form in self, or self in form. They regard feeling as self… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness in self, or self in consciousness. Therefore, when wanderers of other sects are questioned thus, they give such an explanation as: ‘The world is eternal,’ or… ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ But the Tathāgata, Vaccha, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, does not regard form as self, nor self as possessing form, nor form in self, nor self in form. He does not regard feeling as self… perception… volitional formations… consciousness as self, nor self as possessing consciousness, nor consciousness in self, nor self in consciousness. Therefore, when the Tathāgata is questioned thus, he does not give such an explanation as: ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal,’ or ‘The world is finite,’ or ‘The world is infinite,’ or ‘The soul is the same as the body,’ or ‘The soul is one thing and the body another,’ or ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

“Acchariyaṃ, bho moggallāna, abbhutaṃ, bho moggallāna! Yatra hi nāma satthu ca sāvakassa ca atthena attho byañjanena byañjanaṃ saṃsandissati, samessati, na virodhayissati, yadidaṃ aggapadasmiṃ. Idānāhaṃ, bho moggallāna, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ apucchiṃ. Samaṇopi me gotamo etehi padehi etehi byañjanehi etamatthaṃ byākāsi, seyyathāpi bhavaṃ moggallāno. Acchariyaṃ, bho moggallāna, abbhutaṃ, bho moggallāna! Yatra hi nāma satthu ca sāvakassa ca atthena attho byañjanena byañjanaṃ saṃsandissati samessati na virodhayissati, yadidaṃ aggapadasmi”nti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Marvelous, venerable Moggallāna, astonishing, venerable Moggallāna! That for the Teacher and the disciple, meaning corresponds with meaning and phrasing with phrasing; that they agree and do not contradict, regarding this foremost point. Just now, venerable Moggallāna, I approached the ascetic Gotama and asked him about this matter. The ascetic Gotama also explained this matter to me with these words and these phrases, just as the venerable Moggallāna has. Marvelous, venerable Moggallāna, astonishing, venerable Moggallāna! That for the Teacher and the disciple, meaning corresponds with meaning and phrasing with phrasing; that they agree and do not contradict, regarding this foremost point.” Eighth.

9. Kutūhalasālāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse at the Hall of Curiosity

418. Atha [P 4.0398] kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

418. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went to the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded this courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One:

“Purimāni[V 2.0364], bho gotama[T 4.0484], divasāni purimatarāni sambahulānaṃ nānātitthiyānaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ kutūhalasālāyaṃ sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – ‘ayaṃ kho pūraṇo kassapo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa. Sopi sāvakaṃ abbhatītaṃ kālaṅkataṃ upapattīsu byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno’ti. Yopissa [M 2.0564] sāvako uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto tampi sāvakaṃ abbhatītaṃ kālaṅkataṃ upapattīsu byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno’”ti.

“Venerable Gotama, on former days, and on even more former days, this conversation arose among many ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers of various other sects who were sitting together and assembled in the hall of debate: ‘This Pūraṇa Kassapa has a following, has a group, is a teacher of a group, is well-known, famous, a founder of a sect, and is regarded as a saint by many people. He declares of a disciple who has passed on, who is deceased, regarding his rebirths: “So-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place; so-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place.” And of that disciple of his who is a supreme person, a highest person, who has attained the supreme attainment, he also declares of that disciple who has passed on, who is deceased, regarding his rebirths: “So-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place; so-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place.”’

“Ayampi kho makkhali gosālo…pe… ayampi kho nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto…pe… ayampi kho sañcayo sañjayo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) belaṭṭhaputto…pe… ayampi kho pakudho pakuddho (pī.) kaccāno…pe… ayampi kho ajito kesakambalo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa. Sopi sāvakaṃ abbhatītaṃ kālaṅkataṃ upapattīsu byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno’ti. Yopissa sāvako uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto tampi sāvakaṃ abbhatītaṃ kālaṅkataṃ [P 4.0399] upapattīsu byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno’”ti.

“This Makkhali Gosāla also… this Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta also… this Sañcaya Belaṭṭhaputta also… this Pakudha Kaccāna also… this Ajita Kesakambala also has a following, has a group, is a teacher of a group, is well-known, famous, a founder of a sect, and is regarded as a saint by many people. He too declares of a disciple who has passed on, who is deceased, regarding his rebirths: ‘So-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place; so-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place.’ And of that disciple of his who is a supreme person, a highest person, who has attained the supreme attainment, he also declares of that disciple who has passed on, who is deceased, regarding his rebirths: ‘So-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place; so-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place.’”

“Ayampi kho samaṇo gotamo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa. Sopi sāvakaṃ abbhatītaṃ kālaṅkataṃ upapattīsu byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra [T 4.0485] upapanno’ti. Yopissa yo ca khvassa (pī.) sāvako uttamapuriso paramapuriso paramapattipatto tañca sāvakaṃ abbhatītaṃ kālaṅkataṃ upapattīsu na byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno’ti. Api ca kho naṃ evaṃ byākaroti – ‘acchecchi taṇhaṃ, vivattayi saṃyojanaṃ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bho gotama, ahu deva kaṅkhā, ahu vicikicchā – ‘kathaṃ nāma kathañhi nāma (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) kathaṃ kathaṃ nāma (chakkaṅguttare pañcamavagge dutiyasutte) samaṇassa gotamassa dhammo abhiññeyyo’”ti dhammābhiññeyyāti (pī. ka.) dhammo… aññeyyo (chakkaṅguttare)?

“This ascetic Gotama also has a following, has a group, is a teacher of a group, is well-known, famous, a founder of a sect, and is regarded as a saint by many people. He too declares of a disciple who has passed on, who is deceased, regarding his rebirths: ‘So-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place; so-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place.’ But of that disciple of his who is a supreme person, a highest person, who has attained the supreme attainment, he does not declare of that disciple who has passed on, who is deceased, regarding his rebirths: ‘So-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place; so-and-so has been reborn in such-and-such a place.’ Rather, he declares of him thus: ‘He has cut off craving, turned away from the fetters, and by the right overcoming of conceit, has made an end of suffering.’ For me, venerable Gotama, there was indeed doubt, there was indeed uncertainty: ‘How, indeed, is the Dhamma of the ascetic Gotama to be known by direct knowledge?’”

“Alañhi te, vaccha, kaṅkhituṃ, alaṃ vicikicchituṃ. Kaṅkhanīye ca pana te ṭhāne vicikicchā uppannā. Saupādānassa khvāhaṃ, vaccha, upapattiṃ paññāpemi no anupādānassa. Seyyathāpi[V 2.0365], vaccha, aggi saupādāno jalati, no anupādāno; evameva khvāhaṃ, vaccha, saupādānassa upapattiṃ paññāpemi, no anupādānassā”ti.

“Indeed, Vaccha, it is fitting for you to doubt, fitting to be uncertain. For uncertainty has arisen in you in a matter fit for doubt. I, Vaccha, declare rebirth for one with clinging, not for one without clinging. Just as, Vaccha, a fire with fuel burns, and not without fuel; so too, Vaccha, I declare rebirth for one with clinging, not for one without clinging.”

“Yasmiṃ[M 2.0565], bho gotama, samaye acci vātena khittā dūrampi gacchati, imassa pana bhavaṃ gotamo kiṃ upādānasmiṃ paññāpetī”ti? “Yasmiṃ kho, vaccha, samaye acci vātena khittā dūrampi gacchati, tamahaṃ vātūpādānaṃ paññāpemi. Vāto hissa, vaccha, tasmiṃ samaye upādānaṃ hotī”ti. “Yasmiñca [P 4.0400] pana, bho gotama, samaye imañca kāyaṃ nikkhipati, satto ca aññataraṃ kāyaṃ anupapanno hoti, imassa pana bhavaṃ gotamo kiṃ upādānasmiṃ paññāpetī”ti? “Yasmiṃ kho, vaccha, samaye imañca kāyaṃ nikkhipati, satto ca aññataraṃ kāyaṃ anupapanno hoti, tamahaṃ taṇhūpādānaṃ vadāmi. Taṇhā hissa, vaccha, tasmiṃ samaye upādānaṃ hotī”ti hotīti…pe… (ka.). Navamaṃ.

“Venerable Gotama, at the time when a flame, thrown by the wind, goes even afar, what does the venerable Gotama declare to be its fuel in this case?” “Vaccha, at the time when a flame, thrown by the wind, goes even afar, I declare that to have wind as its fuel. For, Vaccha, at that time the wind is its fuel.” “And, venerable Gotama, at the time when one lays down this body and a being has not yet arrived at another body, what does the venerable Gotama declare to be its fuel in this case?” “Vaccha, at the time when one lays down this body and a being has not yet arrived at another body, I say that has craving as its fuel. For, Vaccha, at that time craving is its fuel.” Ninth.

10. Ānandasuttaṃ

10. The Ānanda Sutta

419. Atha [T 4.0486] kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, atthattā”ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi. “Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, natthattā”ti? Dutiyampi kho bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi. Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

419. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. When this courteous and memorable talk was finished, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Gotama, is there a self?” When this was said, the Blessed One remained silent. “Then, Venerable Gotama, is there no self?” A second time, the Blessed One remained silent. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta rose from his seat and departed.

Atha kho āyasmā ānando acirapakkante vacchagotte paribbājake bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, bhante, bhagavā vacchagottassa paribbājakassa pañhaṃ puṭṭho na byākāsī”ti? “Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘atthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘atthattā’ti byākareyyaṃ, ye te, ānanda, samaṇabrāhmaṇā sassatavādā tesametaṃ saddhiṃ tesametaṃ laddhi (sī.) abhavissa. Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘natthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘natthattā’ti byākareyyaṃ, ye te, ānanda, samaṇabrāhmaṇā [P 4.0401] ucchedavādā tesametaṃ saddhiṃ abhavissa. Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘atthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘atthattā’ti byākareyyaṃ, api [V 2.0366] nu me taṃ, ānanda, anulomaṃ abhavissa ñāṇassa uppādāya – ‘sabbe dhammā anattā’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa [M 2.0566] ‘natthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘natthattā’ti byākareyyaṃ[T 4.0487], sammūḷhassa, ānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa bhiyyo sammohāya abhavissa – ‘ahuvā me nūna pubbe attā, so etarahi natthī’”ti. Dasamaṃ.

Then, not long after the wanderer Vacchagotta had departed, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, for what reason did the Blessed One not answer the question asked by the wanderer Vacchagotta?” “If, Ānanda, when asked by the wanderer Vacchagotta, ‘Is there a self?’ I were to answer, ‘There is a self,’ this would be in accordance with the doctrine of those ascetics and brahmins who are eternalists. If, Ānanda, when asked by the wanderer Vacchagotta, ‘Is there no self?’ I were to answer, ‘There is no self,’ this would be in accordance with the doctrine of those ascetics and brahmins who are annihilationists. If, Ānanda, when asked by the wanderer Vacchagotta, ‘Is there a self?’ I were to answer, ‘There is a self,’ would that be in conformity with the arising of the knowledge that ‘all phenomena are not-self’?” “No, venerable sir.” “If, Ānanda, when asked by the wanderer Vacchagotta, ‘Is there no self?’ I were to answer, ‘There is no self,’ it would lead to the further confusion of the already confused Vacchagotta, who would think: ‘Surely, I formerly had a self, and now it does not exist.’” The tenth.

11. Sabhiyakaccānasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse with Sabhiya Kaccāna

420. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā sabhiyo kaccāno ñātike viharati giñjakāvasathe. Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yenāyasmā sabhiyo kaccāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sabhiyena kaccānena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako āyasmantaṃ sabhiyaṃ kaccānaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho bho, kaccāna, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ pana, bho kaccāna, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

420. On one occasion, the Venerable Sabhiya Kaccāna was dwelling at Ñātika in the Brick Hall. Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Venerable Sabhiya Kaccāna. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Sabhiya Kaccāna. When this courteous and memorable talk was finished, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Venerable Sabhiya Kaccāna: “Venerable Kaccāna, does the Tathāgata exist after death?” “Vaccha, this has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death.’” “Then, Venerable Kaccāna, does the Tathāgata not exist after death?” “This too, Vaccha, has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death.’”

“Kiṃ nu kho, bho kaccāna, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti. “Kiṃ [P 4.0402] pana, bho kaccāna, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti? “Etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’”ti.

“Venerable Kaccāna, does the Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death?” “This, Vaccha, has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’” “Then, Venerable Kaccāna, does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?” “This too, Vaccha, has not been declared by the Blessed One: ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”

“‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho kaccāna, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno – ‘abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi[T 4.0488]. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho kaccāna, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno – ‘abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha, bhagavatā – na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho kaccāna, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno – ‘abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, vaccha[V 2.0367], bhagavatā – hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho kaccāna, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno – ‘etampi kho, vaccha, abyākataṃ bhagavatā – neva hoti na [M 2.0567] na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vadesi. Ko nu kho, bho kaccāna, hetu, ko paccayo, yenetaṃ abyākataṃ samaṇena gotamenā”ti? “Yo ca, vaccha, hetu, yo ca paccayo paññāpanāya rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā, so ca hetu, so ca paccayo sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjheyya. Kena naṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā”ti. “Kīvaciraṃ pabbajitosi, bho kaccānā”ti? “Naciraṃ, āvuso, tīṇi vassānī”ti. “Yassapa’ssa, āvuso, etamettakena ettakameva taṃpa’ssa bahu, ko pana vādo evaṃ ko pana vādo eva (sī. pī.) abhikkante”ti! Ekādasamaṃ.

“Venerable Kaccāna, when asked, ‘Does the Tathāgata exist after death?’ you say, ‘This, Vaccha, has not been declared by the Blessed One: The Tathāgata exists after death.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Kaccāna, does the Tathāgata not exist after death?’ you say, ‘This, Vaccha, has not been declared by the Blessed One: The Tathāgata does not exist after death.’ When asked, ‘Venerable Kaccāna, does the Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death?’ you say, ‘This, Vaccha, has not been declared by the Blessed One: The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’ When asked, ‘Then, Venerable Kaccāna, does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death?’ you say, ‘This too, Vaccha, has not been declared by the Blessed One: The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ What, Venerable Kaccāna, is the cause, what is the condition, for this not having been declared by the ascetic Gotama?” “Vaccha, the cause and condition for the designation of one as ‘having form’ or ‘formless,’ ‘percipient’ or ‘non-percipient,’ or ‘neither percipient nor non-percipient’—if that cause and that condition were to cease completely, in all respects, and without remainder, by what could one designate him as ‘having form’ or ‘formless,’ ‘percipient’ or ‘non-percipient,’ or ‘neither percipient nor non-percipient’?” “How long have you been ordained, Venerable Kaccāna?” “Not long, friend, three years.” “Friend, for one to have gained so much in such a short time is itself a great gain; what then is to be said of one who is so advanced?” The eleventh.

Abyākatasaṃyuttaṃ [P 4.0403] samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Undeclared is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this:

Khemātherī [T 4.0489] anurādho, sāriputtoti koṭṭhiko;

Moggallāno ca vaccho ca, kutūhalasālānando;

Sabhiyo ekādasamanti;

Therī Khemā, Anurādha, Sāriputta, and Koṭṭhika; Moggallāna and Vaccha, Kutūhalasālā, Ānanda; and Sabhiya is the eleventh.

Saḷāyatanavaggo catuttho.

The Chapter on the Six Sense Bases, the Fourth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this:

Saḷāyatanavedanā, mātugāmo jambukhādako;

Sāmaṇḍako moggallāno, citto gāmaṇi saṅkhataṃ;

Abyākatanti dasadhāti.

The Six Sense Bases, Feeling, the Woman, Jambukhādaka; Sāmaṇḍaka, Moggallāna, Citta, the Village Headman, the Conditioned; and the Undeclared—thus there are ten.

Saḷāyatanavaggasaṃyuttapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāḷi of the Connected Discourses on the Chapter of the Six Sense Bases is concluded.
